- [X] Tests cover representative shipped scaffold files and current =.orgasmic= files.

** Description
Build the daemon's serialized write surface and read model: append tx and sessions, rewrite direct-edit files through flocked RPC, maintain an in-memory projection, and expose localhost REST plus WebSocket streams.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [X] Daemon startup rebuilds the materialized index from project and home files before serving normal reads.
- [X] Working-file parse failures keep last-good indexed state and report file plus line.
- [X] Tx append uses property-drawer-only Org headings and append-only file handles.
- [X] API and CLI share stable request IDs for retriable mutations.
- [X] REST and WS surfaces cover board/project/task/run/manager/tmux/daemon/auth/question/recovery and graph endpoints.
- [X] WebSocket streams emit board, task, run, manager, graph, and daemon events needed by the UI.

** Evidence

The CLI's =src/home.rs= is now a thin re-export. Net test count unchanged (3 tests moved from cli to core).
- [2026-05-21 Thu 21:35] Implemented the daemon's serialized writer (crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/writer.rs) as a single tokio task fed by an mpsc channel. Wraps orgasmic-core::tx::TxWriter (which already handles the macOS append-mode pitfall per CLAUDE.md) and orgasmic-core::session::SessionWriter; direct-edit graph rewrites take an advisory fs2 flock per dec_WH9PD and use a tmp+rename for atomicity. Idempotency cache keyed on request_id closes AC #4.
- [2026-05-21 Thu 21:35] Implemented the in-memory materialized index (crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/index.rs) with board+projects+tx projections. =Index::rebuild= runs at boot before the daemon serves normal reads (AC #1). On per-file parse failure, the prior project entry is retained and the error surfaces through =/graph/parse-errors= (AC #2). Tested by =index::tests::parse_failure_keeps_last_good=.

** Description
Lift the HAR-style runtime boundary into orgasmic: a typed =WorkerDriver= trait, concrete driver skeletons, one active run per task/kind, event capture into JSONL sessions, and supervisor ownership guards.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [X] Driver trait covers acquire, attach, release, event stream, transition_state, and babysitter actions.
- [X] Supervisor enforces one active run per =(task_id, kind)= tuple.
- [X] Driver events are persisted through the session writer with inspectable JSONL.
- [X] Runtime identity includes run id, runtime id, and boot id.
- [X] Babysitter runs use separate JSONL sessions, summarized implementer event chunks, and only poke/restart/escalate/record tools.
- [X] Continuation runs include =:PREVIOUS_RUN:=, prior session JSONL path, current worktree diff summary, and original acceptance criteria.

** Evidence
- [2026-05-21 Thu 22:05] Implemented =WorkerDriver= trait in =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/trait.rs= covering acquire, attach (default = =NotReattachable=, opted into per driver), event stream (=mpsc::Receiver<DriverEvent>=), =transition_state=, babysitter actions, and =release=. Trait is single-surface — RunKind discriminates implementer vs babysitter so the same trait carries both modes (arch_A53QX constraint).
- [2026-05-21 Thu 22:05] Four concrete drivers implementing the trait: =claude_acp.rs= (ACP wire shape, simulated mode when no endpoint configured), =codex_appserver.rs= (codex appserver wire shape, URL validation, simulated mode), =hermes.rs= (Hermes ACP variant, session-token required when endpoint set), =tmux_tui.rs= (real tmux spawn when tmux is on PATH; inert mode fallback). All four enforce the babysitter / implementer tool boundary inside =DriverControl=.

** Description
Add graph RPCs and projection behavior for decisions, architecture nodes, task edges, stale propagation, snapshots, ADR regeneration, and scoped reconciliation.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [X] Graph nodes can be created, revised, validated, superseded, finalized, snapshotted, and restored through daemon APIs.
- [X] Semantic hashes exclude prose-only edits and drive forward stale propagation.
- [X] ADR files regenerate from decisions marked =:ADR_WORTHY: t= with stable numbering.
- [X] Reconciliation scopes stale architecture before stale tasks before stale code.
- [X] =apply_revision= is atomic across hash update, stale propagation, and tx append.
- [X] Reconcile/finalize rejects pending decisions, trace inconsistency, file-deletion/supersede mismatches, and invalid cross-scope references.
- [X] Reconcile-complete validates every cross-scope =:REFERENCES:=, =:EXTENDS:=, =:OVERRIDES:=, and =:HOSTED_IN:= edge against arch_MPAQT: dangling pointers to deleted or superseded nodes are rejected, and any project-scope =:OVERRIDES:= of a removed global term blocks completion.
- [X] Glossary writes reject implementation details such as code paths, type signatures, and function names.

** Evidence

** Description
Lift =CodexAppserverDriver= from simulated mode to a real JSON-RPC bridge against a running =codex app-server= process. Today the driver only emits =Ready= + =RunComplete= on release when =endpoint= is missing; when an endpoint is configured the wire layer is still stubbed.

Target: when =config.endpoint= names a reachable codex app-server (HTTP or WebSocket per existing =url_like= validator), the driver opens the JSON-RPC channel, forwards the spawn payload (model, reasoning_effort, prompt-bundle text, continuation context), and translates the app-server's streamed messages into =DriverEvent::TextChunk= / =ToolCall= / =RunComplete= / =Error= variants. =transition_state= and =release= map to app-server control messages. Tool-call gating per =DriverControl='s worker-vs-babysitter rules is preserved.

Closes the arch_A53QX partial-status item "claude_acp/codex_appserver/hermes drivers default to simulated mode" for the codex_appserver driver. Sibling tasks TASK-KJJRF (Claude ACP) and TASK-AAW76 (Hermes) close the other two.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] When =config.endpoint= is empty or absent, the driver continues to behave as today (simulated mode emits =Ready= + =RunComplete= on release) so the existing supervisor-lease / JSONL tests stay green.
- [ ] When =config.endpoint= names a reachable codex app-server, the driver opens the JSON-RPC channel and forwards spawn payload (model, reasoning_effort, prompt-bundle, continuation context) using the app-server's documented JSON-RPC schema.
- [ ] Streamed app-server messages are translated into =DriverEvent= variants and flushed through the existing =mpsc::Sender<DriverEvent>= without reordering. Sequence numbers monotonic per stream.
- [ ] =transition_state(new_state, reason)= and =release= map to app-server control messages (or graceful shutdown if no equivalent exists) and produce the appropriate =DriverEvent::Transition= / =Release=.
- [ ] Worker vs babysitter tool boundary preserved: =WorkerTool= and =BabysitterTool= sets continue to gate inbound tool invocations.
- [ ] New test exercises the bridge against a recorded fixture or a local =codex app-server= when one is on =PATH=; skipped (logged to stderr) when not available, matching the =tmux_tui::tests::real_tmux_session_lifecycle= pattern.
- [ ] =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= clean, =cargo fmt --check= clean, =git diff --check= clean.
- [ ] Workspace MSRV (1.78) preserved — no =Option::is_none_or=, =File::unlock=, etc. (see CLAUDE.md Pitfalls).

** Description
Promote =POST /grill=, =POST /architect=, =POST /plan=, and =POST /reconcile= from tx-only stubs (today they only emit =<stage>.requested= via =post_stage=) to real driver-backed agent acquisitions. Each stage selects the matching agent template (=griller=, =architector=, =planner=, plus =glossarist= where applicable), compiles its prompt bundle for the target stage, acquires a driver run via the supervisor, and emits the existing =<stage>.requested= tx PLUS a follow-on =<stage>.completed= tx when the run releases.

Adds stage-completion plumbing the manager can cascade on per arch_R3EPE ("stage-complete endpoints let the manager cascade from grilling to architecture to planning to implementation").

Blocked by TASK-F6D3T because both touch =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs= and TASK-F6D3T owns the persona-injection extension to tmux_tui that this task also relies on.

- [ ] On driver release with success, a =<stage>.completed= tx is emitted and the WS event stream announces stage completion (board / manager topic).
- [ ] On driver release with failure, a =<stage>.failed= tx is emitted with the failure reason; no =<stage>.completed= event.

:TEST_CMD:         cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon
:DEPENDS_ON:       TASK-M1MZ4
:END:

** Description
arch_MPAQT constraint "apply_revision is atomic across hash update, stale propagation, and tx write succeed or fail together" is not honoured. Today the revise handler rewrites the file, refreshes the index, propagates stale, then writes tx — failures between steps leave partial effects.

Implementation: introduce a =WriterHandle::transaction= primitive that batches multiple file rewrites + a tx append behind a single serialized commit point. The transaction prepares all rewrites to a staging area (e.g., =target.tmp= files), syncs them, atomically renames into place, then appends tx. On error before commit, all staging is discarded; after commit, the changes are durable.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] =WriterHandle::transaction= API accepts a batch of =FileRewrite= + =TxAppend= and commits all-or-nothing.
- [ ] =/decisions/:id/revise= and =/architecture/:id/revise= use the transaction; an injected failure between stale propagation and tx append leaves no on-disk effect.
- [ ] New integration test covers the failure rollback path.
- [ ] cargo test/clippy/fmt/diff clean; MSRV 1.78.

** Description
TASK-XB874 audit identified that arch_BVH7M's "modified historical tx files block daemon start" constraint is not enforced. Today, =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/index.rs::rebuild= scans historical tx files and collects parse errors into the per-file =parse_errors= map, but =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/lib.rs::Daemon::run= continues booting normally even when historical-tx parse errors exist.

The intent of the constraint: working files (=sprint.org=, =backlog.org=, etc.) tolerate parse failures by keeping the last-good index — but historical tx files (=.orgasmic/tx/YYYY-MM.org= and =$ORGASMIC_HOME/state/tx/YYYY-MM.org=) are append-only audit logs that should never change retroactively. If one fails to parse, that's evidence of corruption or unauthorized retroactive edits, and the daemon refuses to start until the operator either reverts the edit or explicitly reseals.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [X] During =Index::rebuild=, classify per-file parse errors as either =working-file= (existing tolerant behavior) or =historical-tx= (new strict behavior).
- [X] When any historical-tx parse error is found during rebuild, =Daemon::run= refuses to bind / serve requests and returns a structured error naming the offending file and the line, with a hint about reverting / sealing.
- [X] Existing working-file last-good fallback behavior is preserved (=parse_failure_keeps_last_good= still passes).
- [X] New test in =crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/integration.rs= covers: (a) a corrupted historical tx file blocks daemon start with a specific error, (b) a corrupted working file does NOT block start (last-good fallback).
- [X] =cargo test --workspace= green, =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= clean, =cargo fmt --check= clean, =git diff --check= clean.
- [X] MSRV 1.78 preserved.

- [2026-05-22 Fri 11:05] Added startup gate in =Daemon::run= that checks the rebuilt snapshot before writer/watcher/listener startup; on a historical-tx parse error, returns =HistoricalTxStartupError { path, line, message }= with display text including revert/git/reseal guidance.
- [2026-05-22 Fri 11:05] New integration tests in =crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/integration.rs=: =corrupted_historical_tx_blocks_daemon_start= and =corrupted_working_file_does_not_block_start=.

:CODEX_COMMIT:     2183138
:END:

** Description
Implement the schema and daemon changes that the 2026-05-23 UI grilling session locked in. Five model additions, one model realign, one new tx type, one new projection, one new slot. All landed in a single sprint task so the new UI sessions (3 onwards) can build against the new model without serialization tricks.

The five model additions:
1. *Task lifecycle realign* (dec_MKC0A). Collapse per-kind state machines to a single 6-stage lifecycle on the task heading: BACKLOG / EXPLORE / PLAN / IMPLEMENT / REVIEW / SHIP / DONE plus BLOCKED / CANCELLED. Update =shipped/schema/state-machine.org=, =crates/orgasmic-core/src/schema.rs::TaskState=, =crates/orgasmic-core/src/org.rs::TODO_KEYWORDS=. Migrate the existing 45 sprint headings to the new keywords (most map directly: =DONE=→=DONE=; =READY=→=BACKLOG= or =IMPLEMENT= depending on task; =analyzing/implementing/testing/fixing/merging=→folded into =IMPLEMENT= stage).
2. *Run sub-state* (dec_RECYG). Per-kind sub-states (=analyzing=, =implementing=, =testing=, =fixing=, =merging=, =planning=, =drafted=, =findings_recorded=, =reviewing=, =approved=, =requested_changes=) move off the task heading and onto the run record as a string field with three namespaces: =agent.<verb>=, =human.<verb>=, =ci.<verb>=. Add a =RunState= field on =RunSummary= and serialize through =DriverEvent= lifecycle.
3. *Subtasks* (dec_JW11K). Add =:PARENT_TASK:= property to =TaskHeading=. ID format =TASK-NNN.M=. Daemon's materialized index rolls up =subtasks: BTreeMap<TaskId, Vec<TaskId>>= from back-edges; index rejects orphan subtasks at boot/refresh. Subtask creation via =POST /tasks/:id/subtasks=. UI never directly mutates the org file.
4. *Comments + activity projection* (dec_A4V2N). New tx type =comment= per =shipped/schema/tx.org=: properties TX_ID, TIME, TYPE=comment, ACTOR, PROJECT, TASK, RUN_ID (optional), ARTIFACTS (optional), IN_REPLY_TO (optional), BODY (escaped markdown). New endpoint =POST /tasks/:id/comments= (writer routes through =POST /tx= internally). New projection in =index.rs=: =activity_index: BTreeMap<TaskId, Vec<TxEntry>>=; rebuilt on boot, incrementally updated on each =comment= or =manager.action= tx append. New endpoint =GET /tasks/:id/activity= returns chronologically-merged comments + state-transition tx + run lifecycle events from the JSONL session.
5. *Ownership lock model* (dec_CX17K, dec_JW9TJ). Add =:STAGE_AGENT_BACKLOG:= through =:STAGE_AGENT_DONE:= properties to =shipped/project-scaffold/project.org= and parse them in =ProjectFile= view. On a stage transition (whether DnD-via-tx or supervisor-driven), the daemon consults the stage-agent map and auto-spawns a run if a template is configured (empty = human-only). Supervisor reports =owner= on the run record: =human= when no active run, =agent.<kind>= when active. Add =POST /runs/:id/release= endpoint that cancels the active run and returns ownership to =human= (used by the UI's "Release agent" affordance).
6. *Activity slot for agent prompt compiler* (dec_A4V2N). Register =task.activity= slot namespace in =shipped/schema/slots.org=; extend =crates/orgasmic-core/src/slots.rs::is_dynamic_skill_slot= to recognize it; loader fills from the same =activity_index= projection. Existing agent templates can opt in with ={{task.activity}}=; not required for v0.0.1 dogfood.

For each existing task, apply the following operations (where applicable):

3. *Synthesized agent-completion comment*. For each =DONE= task, write one =comment= tx entry to =.orgasmic/tx/2026-05.org= with:

** Description
TASK-YFAER added the =:STAGE_AGENT_*:= property group on =project.org= + scaffold and emits =EventPayload::AutoSpawnRequested { task_id, kind, agent_template }= from the api/writer path on stage transitions whose target stage has a configured agent. Codex deliberately deferred the async consumer that actually calls =Supervisor::acquire_task= because invoking the supervisor synchronously from the writer/index path was out of scope for a single sequential implementer round.

This task wires the consumer: subscribe to =AutoSpawnRequested= events in the daemon's event bus (next to the existing typed-event consumers added by TASK-YRK91), call =supervisor.acquire_task(task_id, agent_template, default_overrides)=, and emit a new =run.auto_spawned= tx (or reuse =run.created= with a =:ORIGIN: auto_spawn= property if cleaner). The consumer must be idempotent against re-emission (e.g., daemon-restart re-fires of pending events) using the same =(task_id, kind)= lease check the supervisor already enforces; duplicate =AutoSpawnRequested= for an already-leased task should be a no-op, not an error.

:PRIORITY:         P2
:MERGE_SHA:        ce5ff70

:WORKER:   implementer-claude
:IMPLEMENTS:       arch_R3EPE arch_C87Z9

:READ_SCOPE:       .orgasmic/decisions.org .orgasmic/architecture.org shipped/manager/persona.org CLAUDE.md docs/adr/*.org crates/**
:TEST_CMD:         cargo test --workspace
:END:

** Description
The manager handoff discipline (=shipped/manager/persona.org= rules 3+4 / =CLAUDE.md= "Manager role — dispatch-only, killable at any time") requires the manager to append a =manager.dispatch_started= tx before launching any background work that outlives a single manager reply (codex implementer, reviewer agent, etc.), so a future recall can find orphaned dispatches when a manager is killed mid-session.

Today this sequence is hand-coded by the manager each time:
1. =git worktree add /tmp/orgasmic-worktrees/task-NNN -b task-NNN-<slug>=
2. Write =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-NNN-brief.md=
3. =nohup codex exec ... < brief.md > stdout.log 2>&1 &=
4. Append =manager.dispatch_started= tx with =:TASK:=, =:WORKTREE:=, =:CODEX_BRIEF_PATH:=, =:STARTED_AT:=, =:CODEX_PID:=

This task wraps that sequence as one atomic CLI subcommand: =orgasmic manager dispatch --task TASK-NNN --kind implementer --brief /path/to/brief.md --model gpt-5.5 --effort xhigh= (with reasonable defaults).

Behavior:
- Validates the task ID exists in sprint.org and is in a dispatchable lifecycle stage (BACKLOG / IMPLEMENT / REVIEW depending on =--kind=).
- Creates the worktree at the conventional path.
- Spawns codex with the standard flags from the CLAUDE.md contract.
- Appends the =manager.dispatch_started= tx via the daemon writer (atomic — if the writer rejects, the worktree is removed and codex is killed).
- Prints the inner codex PID and the watcher command for the manager to install.

Companion subcommand =orgasmic manager dispatch-close --task TASK-NNN --status done|aborted= for the integration step: records =implementer.done= / =manager.dispatch_aborted= tx and removes the worktree.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] =orgasmic manager dispatch --task TASK-NNN --kind implementer --brief <path>= creates worktree, spawns codex, appends pre-flight tx, all atomically.
- [ ] On any step failure, cleans up: removes worktree, kills codex if spawned, deletes pre-flight tx if appended (best-effort; manager tx is append-only so deletion fails gracefully and the manager can record =manager.dispatch_aborted= instead).
- [ ] =orgasmic manager dispatch-close --task TASK-NNN --status done= records =implementer.done= tx, removes worktree, optionally deletes the branch.
- [ ] =orgasmic manager dispatch-status= lists all open =manager.dispatch_started= tx without a close, with worktree state + codex PID liveness.
- [ ] New tx types (or `:KIND:` properties on existing tx) registered in =shipped/schema/tx.org=.
- [ ] Integration test exercises spawn → check status → close-done path end-to-end against a stub-driver codex (or a simulated dispatch).
- [ ] All workspace tests green; clippy =--workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= clean; fmt clean; =git diff --check= clean.

** Description
Two correctness gaps in the dispatched CLI:

- *F-1 (medium bug, reviewer):* =dispatch-status= PID derivation (=manager.rs:955= =find_codex_pid=) treats any =codex exec= process containing the task id as a match. Reproduced live: with a stale implementer dispatch tx-0141 still recorded as open, =dispatch-status= reported its =CODEX_PID= as 31247, but ps showed 31247 was the reviewer dispatch's codex (different =--output-last-message= path). Result: =--orphans-only= can incorrectly suppress real orphans when a same-task reviewer/fix dispatch is running.
- *F-A (medium bug, manager-discovered via dogfood):* =dispatch= validation rejects =--kind reviewer= when the task is in lifecycle stage =done=. The manager workflow per persona rule 2 is: merge → implementer.done tx → flip subtask DONE → dispatch reviewer. So reviewer dispatch from DONE is the *normal* case, not an exception. Brief's "REVIEW | IMPLEMENT" allowlist was wrong; should be "REVIEW | IMPLEMENT | DONE" for reviewer kind (or add a =--force= / =--allow-stage= escape hatch).

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-1 fix.* =find_codex_pid= (or its replacement) matches the exact =--output-last-message= path derived from the open dispatch's =:CODEX_BRIEF_PATH:= property, not a task-substring on the command line. Brief filename → last filename pattern: =task-NNN-brief.md= ↔ =task-NNN-last.txt= (or whatever convention the dispatch CLI established — read =cmd_dispatch= for the actual last-path derivation). If exact match fails, fall back to "pid unknown" rather than weakly attributing.
- [ ] Add a regression test in =crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/dispatch.rs= that spawns two stub-codex processes for the same task id (one implementer, one reviewer) with different =--output-last-message= paths, then asserts =dispatch-status= attributes each to the right dispatch.
- [ ] *F-A fix.* =cmd_dispatch= validation for =--kind reviewer= accepts stages =REVIEW=, =IMPLEMENT=, AND =DONE=. Optionally also =SHIP= (between DONE and shipped). Update the error message to match. Document the rationale in the validation helper (persona rule 2: reviewer follows implementer.done flip).
- [ ] Add a regression test that =cmd_dispatch= accepts reviewer-from-DONE without =--force=.
- [ ] =cargo test --workspace + cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings + cargo fmt --check + git diff --check= all clean. MSRV 1.78.

** Evidence
- [2026-05-23 Sat 21:02] Shipped in bundled coupled commit =803a4c3= on =task-045.fixes-impl=; merged no-ff as =c6a47a5= (with TASK-FB8CK.2). Codex gpt-5.5 xhigh, ~12 min wall, 191,661 tokens (shared with TASK-FB8CK.2), session 019e55f7-2974-7ff2-9887-83f335efc02a.
- F-A: =cmd_dispatch= validation now accepts reviewer kind from stages =REVIEW=, =IMPLEMENT=, =DONE=, =SHIP= (was REVIEW|IMPLEMENT only). Reject still applies to =BACKLOG / EXPLORE / PLAN / CANCELLED=. Code comment cites persona rule 2 + the manager workflow ordering.
- F-1: =find_codex_pid= now derives the exact =--output-last-message= path from open dispatch's =:CODEX_BRIEF_PATH:= property and matches that exact path against running =codex exec= command lines. No task-substring fallback. Returns =None= when not found rather than weakly attributing. Live verified: =dispatch-status= no longer false-positives across same-task dispatches.
- Regression tests in =tests/dispatch.rs= (+292/-? LOC across both subtasks): two stub-codex processes for same task id with different output paths attribute correctly; reviewer-from-DONE dispatch accepted via dry-run.
- Verification: =cargo test --workspace= + =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= + =cargo fmt --check= + =git diff --check= all clean. MSRV 1.78 preserved.
- Manager rebuilt =target/debug/orgasmic= post-merge; live smoke =orgasmic manager dispatch --task TASK-FB8CK --kind reviewer --dry-run= now prints the full plan instead of rejecting on stage.

** Notes
Tiny scope per finding (~30-80 LOC change in manager.rs + 50 LOC of tests). Both fixes ship in one bundled commit since they share the same file.

** Description
- *F-2 (medium correctness, reviewer):* =DispatchCloseArgs= and =close_done_request= write a fixed extras subset (commit/session/tokens/wall/reason). CLI-produced =reviewer.done= records therefore cannot carry the reviewer-outcome metadata the manager has been recording by hand (=:VERDICT:=, =:BLOCKS_SHIP:=, =:FINDINGS_TOTAL:=, =:FINDINGS_BY_SEVERITY:=, =:FINDINGS_BY_KIND:=, =:REPORT_PATH:=, =:REVIEWED_DIFF:=, =:RECOMMENDED_SUBTASKS:=). Also =--merge-sha= is required for both kinds even though reviewer.done has no merge.
- *F-3 (low docs, reviewer):* =shipped/schema/tx.org= documents =reviewer.done= as sharing the =implementer.done= property set, making =:MERGE_SHA:= and =:BRANCH:= look required for read-only reviewer closes. Recent real =reviewer.done= tx omit them.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-2 fix.* Add a repeatable =--property KEY=VALUE= passthrough to =dispatch-close= so any =:KEY: value= property can be appended to the close tx extras. Validate KEY is uppercase-snake. The hand-coded reviewer-outcome properties (=VERDICT/BLOCKS_SHIP/FINDINGS_*/REPORT_PATH/REVIEWED_DIFF/RECOMMENDED_SUBTASKS=) all become CLI-recordable.
- [ ] *F-2 follow-up.* Make =--merge-sha= kind-aware: required for =implementer.done= closes, optional for =reviewer.done= and =manager.dispatch_aborted=. Replace with =--reviewed-diff= as the reviewer-specific structured input (still recordable via =--property= but elevated to a flag for ergonomics).
- [ ] *F-3 fix.* Split =shipped/schema/tx.org= per-type required vs optional lists. =implementer.done= keeps =:MERGE_SHA:= + =:BRANCH:= required + the optional metadata. =reviewer.done= has its own block with =:CLOSED_TX:= + =:VERDICT:= + =:REPORT_PATH:= required; =:BLOCKS_SHIP:= + =:FINDINGS_*:= + =:REVIEWED_DIFF:= + =:RECOMMENDED_SUBTASKS:= optional. Common base (=:TX_ID:= / =:TIME:= / =:TYPE:= / =:ACTOR:= / =:MACHINE:= / =:PROJECT:= / =:TASK:= / =:CLOSED_TX:=) stays shared.
- [ ] Update integration test to exercise =dispatch-close --status done --kind reviewer-derived --property VERDICT=clean --property FINDINGS_TOTAL=0= and assert the appended tx carries those extras.
- [ ] =cargo test --workspace + cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings + cargo fmt --check + git diff --check= all clean. MSRV 1.78.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-2 (medium a11y) — Manager popover dialog semantics.* When =size === 'focus'=, root carries =role="dialog"= + =aria-modal="true"= + =aria-labelledby= pointing at a heading element; focus trapped within the popover; background is inert (or focus-trap library equivalent). Opening peek→workbench or peek→focus moves keyboard focus to the first actionable control inside the popover (currently nothing receives focus). Collapsing restores focus to the original trigger. Peek-bar trigger button carries =aria-expanded={size !== 'peek'}= + =aria-controls={id-of-content-region}=.
- [ ] *F-2 (medium a11y) — Global Escape disambiguation.* The Escape keydown handler in =ManagerPopover= must not collapse the popover when focus is inside a text input/textarea/contenteditable, OR when another radix overlay is open (radix Sheets/Popovers manage their own Escape). Simplest path: bail out of the collapse handler if =document.activeElement= is editable or if a higher-priority radix overlay has the focus root.
- [ ] *F-3 (low a11y) — Mobile bell trigger.* The mobile branch in =NotificationBell= (the =onClick={open}= path, not the radix PopoverTrigger) must set =aria-expanded={open}= + =aria-controls= referencing the Sheet content's id. Sheet content gets a stable id and =aria-labelledby= referencing the "Needs you" header. Keep desktop branch unchanged.

Used by =ManagerPopover= + =ManagerPeekBar= + =ManagerWorkbench= drag handles.

- [X] No regressions to the existing manager keyboard shortcuts (=Cmd/Ctrl+\`= toggle, Esc collapse to peek) outside the F-2 disambiguation case.

** Description
Replaces the seven remaining UI placeholders that survived UI Session 4 and lands the routing substrate that the polish-phase 2 endgame depends on. Today =GraphView=, =OrgView=, and =SettingsView= are the only entry points for Decisions, Architecture, Glossary, ADR, Snapshots, Activity, and stage-agent configuration. Per dec_PA23Y, dec_TQZTE, dec_E394G there should be six first-class pages with list rows + back-stack modal + (where applicable) per-page react-flow graph, in addition to the cross-domain Graph that already shipped in Session 4. Per dec_JSX48 the routing substrate becomes TanStack Router with path-for-nav + query-for-modals. =OrgView= ships a CodeMirror-with-org-mode editor (replacing the bare textarea). =SettingsView= grows a stage-agent map editor over the =STAGE_AGENT_*= property group on =project.org=.

This is a large but architecturally well-scoped session: every surface has a clear list-rows + modal-with-back-stack pattern, an existing fetcher (=fetchDecisions/Architecture/Glossary/Adrs/Snapshots= already in =ui/src/lib/api.ts=), and a decided UX (dec_PA23Y..046). The new abstraction is =NodeListView=/=NodeGraphView=/=NodeModal= parameterised by node-kind per dec_PA23Y's user note.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *Decisions page* (=ui/src/components/DecisionsView.tsx=) lands as the default landing page for any selected project per dec_PA23Y / dec_JSX48 (the cross-domain Graph stays as a separate page). Two-view toggle on top right: =[List] [Graph]= (default List). List rows (numeric sort by dec_NNN ID): mono ID + title + first sentence of =** Decision= (truncated to one line) + topic/glossary chips. Click row or press Enter opens the back-stack modal. Filter bar above the list: topic filter and free-text search across title + body. URL state drives the modal open state via TanStack Router's =useSearch=.
  - Graph subview = per-page react-flow + dagre top-down view of decisions only. Nodes teal; edges from =:DECIDES:= property; ADR halo when =:ADR_WORTHY: t=. Click single = 1-hop highlight; double-click or Enter on focused node = open modal; right-click = context menu with "Open modal" + "Open in cross-domain Graph". Per-project viewport persisted under =decisions-viewport:<projectId>= localStorage key (mirrors TASK-EBWZ9.3's =graph-viewport:<projectId>= pattern).
- [ ] *Architecture page* (=ui/src/components/ArchitectureView.tsx=) lands as the second primary nav item per dec_PA23Y's "same component family parameterised by node-kind". List rows: mono =arch_NNN= + title + first interface line (truncated; reads the first =** Interface= bullet from the body — body parsing tolerated through the existing =get_architecture_node= response if it carries it, otherwise show a fallback "interface unknown" muted line and don't block on it). Chip area: depends-on count chip ("→3") and motivating-decisions chip ("dec_GRDFB"). Modal sections: Interface bullets, Constraints, =:DECIDES:=-back-edge motivating decisions (clickable into modal back-stack), =:DEPENDS_ON:= chips (clickable). Graph subview = left-to-right react-flow + dagre, =:DEPENDS_ON:= as primary edges, =:DECIDES:= back-edges as dotted secondary edges. Per-project viewport persisted under =architecture-viewport:<projectId>=.

IDs hidden everywhere in the UI; the canonical name is the primary key. List rows: bold canonical name + first sentence of definition (truncated) + ↔N "relates to" chip (count of =:RELATES_TO:= entries). Sort by canonical name. Filter bar: free-text on canonical + definition. Modal: definition body + Avoid list + Relates-to chips (back-stack open into other glossary modals or into decisions / arch modals that reference them) + source-file link.

Modal sections: full body markdown rendered (via the existing approach — if no markdown-renderer lib is in scope, use a minimal mono =<pre>= showing the body verbatim with line-breaks preserved; do **not** add a markdown lib in this dispatch), "Generated from dec_NNN" chip, source-file link.

Filter bar: Type (multi-select across tx =:TYPE:= values — manager.tick, manager.dispatch_started, implementer.done, reviewer.done, comment, snapshot, adr.*, decision.*, architecture.*, glossary.*), Actor (multi), Date range (preset chips Today/7d/30d + custom), Task (single combobox of task IDs). Lists the six writable stages (BACKLOG, EXPLORE, PLAN, IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, SHIP — DONE is purely terminal; BLOCKED/CANCELLED are bookkeeping stages so skip them; also list them as read-only "—" rows if it keeps the table tidy). ** Description
Addresses reviewer findings F-1 (high), F-2 (medium), F-3 (medium), and F-8 (high) from =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-047-review-report.md=. The TanStack Router migration shipped the path-based routes but the per-page filter state, the modal drawer-stack, and the manager-size query param did not adopt TanStack's =useSearch= / =navigate= contract — instead they kept legacy =useQueryState= writes, =window.history.pushState= calls, or component-local =useState=. This breaks the dec_JSX48 "path + query hybrid, browser-back follows previous filter" contract and prevents deep-linking from reflecting the actual session state.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-1 fix.* =NodeModal= drawer-stack management goes through TanStack Router's =useSearch= + =navigate({ search })= instead of =window.location.search= + =window.history.pushState= / =replaceState=. Chip-click inside a modal body pushes a new id onto =?drawer_stack=...= via =navigate=; clicking Back / closing modal pops via =navigate=; browser back/forward respects the stack (TanStack tracks history per its router instance).
- [ ] *F-2 fix.* Esc on a stacked modal pops *one frame* via the same router seam — only deletes the whole stack when the stack is already empty (closing the bottom frame returns to the underlying route). Match the dec_JSX48 user-note browser-back contract: "close modal → previous page → previous filter".
- [ ] *F-3 fix.* =NodeModal= header renders a breadcrumb of opened nodes (e.g., =dec_GRDFB > arch_R3EPE > arch_R3EPE details=). Clicking any crumb pops the stack down to that depth. Single Back icon remains for the one-step pop. The breadcrumb hides on viewports below =sm= (mobile sheet has limited header space) and falls back to "Back" + count.
- [ ] *F-8 fix.* Migrate the search-state holdouts to TanStack:
  - =DecisionsView= filter bar (topic filter, free-text query) reads from =useSearch()= and writes via =navigate({ search })=. Drop the =useQueryState= calls. Same shape for =ArchitectureView= (free-text per TASK-ZYPJC.4) and =ActivityView= (Type / Actor / Date / Task filters; date-range needs a JSON-safe shape).
  - =ManagerPopover= consumes =?manager=peek|workbench|focus= from =useSearch=. The =sessionStorage= persistence stays as a fallback for "last size when no query param", but the URL is authoritative on initial render. Writing the URL on size change is OK — debounce if needed to avoid history spam during drag.
  - Update the route's =validateSearch= schema so type-safe accessors exist.
- [ ] *Manager popover regression check.* Cmd+\` toggle and Esc collapse must still work; drag handles must not race the URL writes (debounce or write only on settle).
- [ ] *No new deps.* TanStack Router is already installed; no =@tanstack/react-router-zod= or similar add-on. Use TanStack's built-in =validateSearch= (function form).
- [ ] =cd ui && npm run build= passes (tsc --noEmit + vite build).
- [ ] =git diff --check= clean.

** Description
Addresses reviewer findings F-4 (medium perf), F-11 (medium design), F-13 (medium design). =NodeModal= currently runs all per-kind fetchers (decisions / architecture / glossary / ADR / three orgFile reads) on every page even when the modal is closed — wasteful network + auth-noise; glossary IDs leak through to modal header chrome and the mobile Sheet description even though dec_E394G requires the canonical name as the primary key in UI; ADR promote/demote actions live only in the row kebab menu and the source decision in the row renders as a passive badge instead of a clickable chip linking into the source decision modal.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-4 fix.* Detail loaders inside =NodeModal= are gated on =open=. When the modal is closed (no =?<kind>= path segment + no top-of-stack id), no fetchers run. When opening from a list page, the matching list response is reused if it already contains the needed fields — only fetch a detail endpoint (=GET /architecture/:id= / =GET /glossary/:id= / =GET /adr/:id=) when the body needs fields that the list summary lacks.
- [ ] *F-11 fix.* Glossary modal hides the raw =:ID:= everywhere user-facing: header shows canonical name only; mobile Sheet description shows canonical name; the back-stack chip uses canonical name. The id stays in the URL =?drawer_stack=glossary-NNN= but is not rendered as a code span anywhere in the UI.
- [ ] *F-13 fix part 1.* ADR row's "Generated from dec_NNN" is a clickable chip that pushes =dec_NNN= onto the drawer stack (opens the source decision modal). Keep the kebab menu for Promote/Demote at the row level.
- [ ] *F-13 fix part 2.* ADR modal header carries Promote + Demote buttons (mirror the row kebab actions). Disabled states: Promote disabled when status is already =accepted=; Demote disabled when status is already =proposed= or =deprecated=. Both fire the existing =postAdrPromote= / =postAdrPromote= helpers with sonner toast feedback.
- [ ] =cd ui && npm run build= passes.
- [ ] =git diff --check= clean.

** Description
Addresses reviewer findings F-5 (medium bug), F-6 (medium design), F-7 (medium design). =NodeGraph= secondary edges from architecture nodes try to draw =decision -> architecture= edges even though the graph node set only contains architecture ids — those edges reference missing source nodes and React Flow throws missing-node warnings. The per-page graph only implements double-click to open a modal; dec_PA23Y also requires single-click 1-hop highlight, Enter on the focused node, and a right-click context menu. The dec_NZ9PS mobile matrix is only partially applied: the graph subview remains an inline fixed-height canvas instead of opening as a full-screen Sheet below =md=, and list-row chips/actions stay visible below =sm= instead of degrading.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-5 fix.* =NodeGraph= for architecture only emits secondary =:DECIDES:= back-edges when both endpoints exist in the rendered node set. Currently the source is a decision id not in the architecture node set — change the secondary edge to architecture → motivating-decision id only when that decision id is also in the node set (which it never is in the architecture-only subview); for the architecture subview, surface the motivating decision as a row chip in the side panel instead of a graph edge. No React Flow missing-node warnings.
- [ ] *F-6 fix.* Per-page graph interactions:
  - Single click on a node → 1-hop highlight (TASK-EBWZ9.3 cross-domain Graph pattern). Re-uses the same opacity-25% / opacity-100% logic.
  - Enter key on focused node → opens the modal (the existing double-click behaviour).
  - Right-click on a node → ContextMenu (radix) with "Open modal" + "Open in cross-domain Graph" entries. The latter navigates to =/projects/$projectId/graph= with =?focus=$nodeId= so the cross-domain graph can fitView on that node (cross-domain GraphView accepts =?focus= if it's wired; if not, just navigate without the param — flag in evidence).
- [ ] *F-7 fix part 1.* Below =md=, the per-page graph subview opens as a full-screen Sheet (slides up from bottom) instead of rendering inline. The List/Graph toggle on mobile becomes a button that opens the Sheet. Mirrors TASK-EBWZ9.5's mobile Sheet pattern for the cross-domain graph detail.
- [ ] *F-7 fix part 2.* Below =sm=, list-row chips that are not load-bearing (=kind=, =priority=, ADR badge for non-promoted decisions, snapshot label) hide. =useIsMobile()= hook already exists; reuse it. Row IDs + titles + status pills + Restore/Action buttons stay visible.
- [ ] =cd ui && npm run build= passes; no React Flow missing-node warnings in console.
- [ ] =git diff --check= clean.

Edge case: =NodeGraph='s callback passes the **bare** id (e.g. =dec_GRDFB=) while =GraphView= keys nodes as =${type}:${rawId}= (e.g. =decision:dec_GRDFB=) — pick a consistent representation. Recommended fix: namespace at the emit side (=NodeGraph.openCrossDomainGraph= maps its =GraphKind= to the matching =NodeType= prefix before passing through). Bonus tiny polish if zero-cost: also highlight the focused node visually (e.g., temporary ring/outline) so the user sees what was focused.

Or (b) add a new =GET /projects/:id/tasks/:task_id/body= endpoint that returns =Vec<{ section: String, lines: Vec<String> }>= and let the frontend section-split itself. Pick whichever you find cleaner; (a) is probably less wire-overhead. Body parsing: the task heading subtree in sprint.org contains second-level =** Description=, =** Acceptance Criteria=, =** Evidence=, =** Notes=, =** Worklog=, =** Reviewer pass= sections — collect lines between them. Acceptance items inside =** Acceptance Criteria= are =- [X] ...= / =- [ ] ...= bullets; preserve those as-is (frontend renders them as a checklist with the check state from the marker). Frontend: render in =MainPane= replacing the placeholder. Each section gets a small heading + body. =Description= and =Notes= = paragraph-rendered (split on blank lines). =Acceptance Criteria= = checklist (checked vs unchecked). =Evidence= = rendered as a bullet list. =Worklog= = collapsed by default if present (use shadcn Accordion or a simple summary/details block) since these can be long. ** Description
Bundle of three small UI follow-ups from the TASK-DK0Y2 reviewer pass. All three live in =ui/src/=, share no overlap with the daemon-side TASK-DK0Y2.2, and can be implemented in one coupled commit.

*F-1 (medium bug):* =GraphView= still runs two viewport ops when =?focus= is set with no saved viewport. React Flow receives =fitView={!viewportSeed.viewport}= and fits the whole graph on mount; the focus effect schedules a second =fitView({ nodes: [{ id: focus }] })=. Result: full-graph flash, or viewport race if RF's initial fit completes after the focus fit. Fix: gate the initial full-graph fit on =!focus= AND trigger the focused fit from a single flow-ready path (=onInit=-only or a single explicit ready-state effect) so exactly one viewport action wins when focus is present.

*F-4 (low design):* The bonus lazy-load uses =<Suspense fallback={null}>= in =router.tsx:366-392=, so the first task click or hard reload at =/tasks?task=...= updates the URL but shows nothing until the TaskDialog chunk resolves. The data-loading skeleton inside TaskDialog only appears AFTER the chunk is fetched. Fix: light dialog/skeleton fallback (e.g., a stub =<Dialog>= with empty =<DialogContent>= showing the existing TaskDialog loading skeleton, or a small inline placeholder), OR prefetch the chunk from TasksPage row intent (=onMouseEnter= / =onFocus= on the row).

*F-5 (low bug):* =tasksRoute.validateSearch= only preserves =task=, but =TasksPage= still owns =layout= via the legacy =useQueryState('layout')=. Opening or closing a task through TanStack navigation rebuilds search from the route search shape, dropping =?layout=kanban= from the URL even though the page still treats it as URL state. Fix: either (a) add =layout?: 'list' | 'kanban'= to =TasksSearch= validateSearch and preserve it through the open/close reducers, OR (b) migrate TasksPage layout fully onto the route search API (kill the =useQueryState= usage). (a) is smaller; (b) is more consistent with dec_JSX48.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-1:* Loading =/projects/.../graph?focus=decision:dec_GRDFB= does NOT flash a full-graph fit first — exactly one viewport action happens and it's the focused fit. If =?focus= is absent the existing fit-on-init behavior is preserved unchanged.
- [ ] *F-1:* Verify by reading the code: `fitView` prop on =<ReactFlow>= is conditional on `!focus`, AND the focus effect runs once per focus value (no double-fitView for the same focus).
- [ ] *F-4:* First click on a Tasks row shows SOME UI surface (skeleton dialog, fallback shell, or pre-fetched ready dialog) before the chunk-load completes — not a frozen-looking nothing.
- [ ] *F-5:* Setting =?layout=kanban= then opening a task (=?task=TASK-NNN=) preserves both params in the URL after the modal opens. Closing the modal preserves =?layout=. Hard reload at =/tasks?layout=kanban&task=TASK-NNN= opens both correctly.

** Description
Bundle of two daemon-side correctness fixes from the TASK-DK0Y2 reviewer pass. Both live in =crates/orgasmic-daemon/=, share no overlap with the UI-side TASK-DK0Y2.1.

*F-2 (medium correctness):* =get_task= (=api.rs:208-222=) finds the task in the materialized snapshot, then =TaskDetail::from_summary= rereads and reparses =summary.source_file= from disk. If =.orgasmic/sprint.org= is temporarily malformed, moved, or otherwise in a state where the index is serving its last-good projection, the task list can still show the task while opening the dialog returns a 500 from the fresh parse. Fix: either (a) parse/cache task bodies during project indexing (=ProjectIndex= gets a =task_bodies: BTreeMap<TaskId, TaskBody>= alongside =tasks=), OR (b) on fresh-parse failure during =TaskDetail::from_summary=, degrade to an empty body with a parse diagnostic in the response (e.g., =parse_warning: Option<String>= field) instead of failing the whole detail endpoint. Pick (a) if the body parse is cheap and worth the memory; pick (b) if you'd rather keep =ProjectIndex= lean. Either way: NO endpoint-500 when the list is serving last-good.

*F-3 (low correctness):* =parse_task_body= (=index.rs:975-1004= + =1006-1027=) only reads named child sections, so free body text BEFORE the first =**= subsection is silently lost. Inside =** Acceptance Criteria=, any non-empty non-bullet line is converted into an unchecked checklist item, so explanatory prose before the actual =- [ ]= bullets renders as an unchecked "criterion". Fix: (i) fold pre-section task body into =description= when no explicit =** Description= subsection exists (or surface as a separate =preamble: Option<String>= field — your call); (ii) inside =** Acceptance Criteria=, only emit checklist items from lines that actually start with =- [X]= / =- [x]= / =- [ ]= / =- [-]= (rule on the marker prefix); non-bullet prose should be preserved separately (e.g. a =prose: Vec<String>= field on the section) OR concatenated into a leading =description-style= block above the list.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-2:* If =.orgasmic/sprint.org= is malformed (intentionally introduce a parse error mid-file for a manual test, but no need to commit it), =GET /projects/:id/tasks/:task_id= for a task whose summary IS in the last-good index does NOT return 500. It returns either the parsed body (if disk is still readable) or a TaskDetail with empty/None body fields + an optional parse-warning surface.
- [ ] *F-2:* Add at least one daemon test simulating the last-good case (project index has a task; disk parse fails or returns different shape). Test asserts no 5xx.
- [ ] *F-3:* Task body with free prose before the first =** Description= subsection: prose is captured (either folded into =description= or surfaced separately, your choice) — not silently dropped.
- [ ] *F-3:* Task body with =** Acceptance Criteria= containing a non-bullet line BEFORE the first =- [X]/[ ]= bullet: the non-bullet line is NOT emitted as an unchecked checklist item. Existing checklist parse is unchanged. Add at least one parser test for this case.

** Description
CLI polish round driven by the TASK-DK0Y2 end-to-end dogfood. The new =orgasmic manager dispatch= / =dispatch-close= surface worked across implementer + reviewer + fix-implementer phases with zero hand-coded tx for 4 of the 5 close operations — but **four specific gaps** required manual hand-edits or surfaced reviewer-recommended polish. Close them now so every future dispatch is fully mechanical.

Plus a fifth gap (daemon watcher reload investigation) that is daemon-side rather than CLI-side; filed as TASK-FB8CK.4 separately so its scope doesn't bleed into this CLI dispatch.

The four gaps in this scope:

*Gap 1 — auto-transition lifecycle stage on dispatch / close.* Today =dispatch --kind implementer= validates the heading is in =Backlog= or =Implement= state but does NOT write back. Manager has to hand-edit =* BACKLOG TASK-NNN= → =* IMPLEMENT TASK-NNN= (and =:STATE: backlog= → =:STATE: implement=) in a separate commit. Same gap on close: =dispatch-close --kind implementer --status done= leaves the heading at IMPLEMENT; manager hand-edits to REVIEW; on reviewer close it should hand-edit to DONE. Lifecycle correctness matters for the kanban — surfaced this session by the user when the Tasks page IMPLEMENT/REVIEW columns showed empty during in-flight work.

Transition matrix:
- =dispatch --kind implementer= on a task at BACKLOG → IMPLEMENT
- =dispatch --kind implementer= on a task at IMPLEMENT (already there) → no-op (idempotent)
- =dispatch-close --kind implementer --status done= → IMPLEMENT → REVIEW
- =dispatch-close --kind implementer --status aborted= → IMPLEMENT → BACKLOG (revert)
- =dispatch --kind reviewer= on a task at REVIEW → no-op
- =dispatch --kind reviewer= on a task at IMPLEMENT / DONE / SHIP → REVIEW (broader matrix per existing validator)
- =dispatch-close --kind reviewer --status done= with =VERDICT=clean= and no recommended subtasks → REVIEW → DONE
- =dispatch-close --kind reviewer --status done= with findings + recommended subtasks → REVIEW (stay; manager will dispatch fix-impl next)
- =dispatch-close --kind reviewer --status aborted= → REVIEW → IMPLEMENT (revert to pre-review state) OR leave alone (acceptable — pick simpler)
- For *fix-implementer* dispatches (=:PARENT_TASK:= set on subtask): =dispatch-close --status done= on a fix-subtask flips subtask BACKLOG → DONE directly (one-round-of-fixes discipline; no separate REVIEW). The CLI can detect this via the heading's =:PARENT_TASK:= property.

Atomicity: the heading edit + tx append must succeed-together-or-fail-together. Existing pre-flight pattern (validate → worktree → tx → spawn) extends to (validate → worktree → tx → heading-edit → spawn); on heading-edit fail, roll back tx (or accept tx-as-source-of-truth and surface heading-edit failure as a warning — pick the simpler robust path).

*Gap 2 — READY keyword reconciliation.* TASK-YFAER narrowed the lifecycle allowlist to 9 keywords (BACKLOG/EXPLORE/PLAN/IMPLEMENT/REVIEW/SHIP/DONE/BLOCKED/CANCELLED). But =crates/orgasmic-cli/src/project.rs= scaffold still emits =* READY TASK-XXX= for new task headings, which the org parser drops (treats READY as part of title) and the dispatch CLI rejects with "missing lifecycle TODO keyword". Two valid fixes:
- (a) Add READY to the TODO_KEYWORDS allowlist + state-machine. Backwards-friendly but pollutes the narrowed vocabulary.
- (b) Update the scaffold to emit =* BACKLOG=. Cleaner, matches the post-TASK-YFAER vocabulary.

**Pick (b).** Find every place in =crates/orgasmic-cli/src/project.rs= (and any related project-init code) that emits =READY= and change to =BACKLOG=. Update any scaffold tests in the same crate that assert =* READY= in fixtures.

*Gap 3 — multi-task dispatch.* =--task= currently accepts ONE task slug. Bundled fix dispatches (TASK-DK0Y2.{1,2} pattern, also seen in TASK-EBWZ9.{1..5} / TASK-ZYPJC.{1..4}) need to write =:TASK: TASK-A TASK-B ...= on the pre-flight tx AND append N matching =implementer.done= tx on close. Today the manager hand-codes the N-th tx. Fix:
- =dispatch=: accept =--task TASK-A --task TASK-B= (repeated) OR =--task TASK-A,TASK-B= (comma-separated). Prefer **repeated arg** (clap idiom; less shell-quoting drama). Validate all tasks exist + all are in a dispatchable state. Pre-flight tx writes =:TASK:= as space-separated slugs.
- =dispatch-close=: accept the same repeated/comma form. On close, append N =implementer.done= tx (one per task) sharing =:MERGE_SHA:= + =:CODEX_COMMIT:= + =:CODEX_SESSION:= + =:WALL:= + =:TOKENS:= + =:CLOSED_TX:= + =:BRANCH:= — single tx-write transaction that appends N records (atomic via the existing fs append + advisory flock).
- =dispatch-status=: detect bundled-task close (currently flagged "accept-as-v1" limitation in TASK-FB8CK dogfood notes); a dispatch is "closed" when any one of its tasks has a matching =implementer.done=/=reviewer.done= tx since the manager.dispatch_started timestamp.

*Gap 4 — dispatch-close cleanup ordering / error recovery.* Reviewer flagged: close tx appended BEFORE worktree-remove + branch-delete. If cleanup fails after tx, durable state says "closed" while local state has a dangling worktree/branch. No retry path. Fix: rearrange cleanup logic and add a =:CLEANUP_STATUS:= property to the close tx:
- Run worktree-remove + branch-delete FIRST (best-effort).
- Then append the close tx with =:CLEANUP_STATUS: ok= (both succeeded), =:CLEANUP_STATUS: worktree_failed= (worktree-remove failed), =:CLEANUP_STATUS: branch_failed=, or =:CLEANUP_STATUS: partial=. Include error message in =:CLEANUP_ERROR:= optional property.
- Add =orgasmic manager dispatch-status --cleanup-failed= filter that lists open / closed dispatches whose =:CLEANUP_STATUS:= is non-ok, so the manager can run a retry pass.

Alternative simpler approach if the above seems heavy: keep tx-append-before-cleanup ordering but wrap cleanup in =.with_context()= and emit a =manager.cleanup_failed= follow-up tx if cleanup errors after the close tx is written. Both approaches are acceptable; pick whichever is cleaner to test.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *Gap 1 (dispatch transition):* =orgasmic manager dispatch --task TASK-X --kind implementer= on a task heading at =* BACKLOG TASK-X ...= AND =:STATE: backlog= writes the heading to =* IMPLEMENT TASK-X ...= AND =:STATE: implement= atomically with the pre-flight tx append. Verify by reading sprint.org immediately after dispatch.
- [ ] *Gap 1 (close transition — implementer done):* =dispatch-close --task TASK-X --kind implementer --status done= on a task NOT having =:PARENT_TASK:= flips heading IMPLEMENT → REVIEW. If the task has =:PARENT_TASK:= set (fix-subtask), flip directly to DONE (one-round-of-fixes).
- [ ] *Gap 1 (close transition — reviewer done):* =dispatch-close --task TASK-X --kind reviewer --status done --property VERDICT=clean --property RECOMMENDED_SUBTASKS=""= flips REVIEW → DONE. If =--property VERDICT=has-issues...= and =--property RECOMMENDED_SUBTASKS="TASK-X.1 TASK-X.2"= (non-empty), leave at REVIEW.
- [ ] *Gap 1 (idempotency):* re-dispatching on a task already at IMPLEMENT is a no-op (no tx, no heading change, no error — the existing CLI may not need this if it errors on "already dispatched", which is also acceptable, but the heading-flip must not fail on idempotent retry).
- [ ] *Gap 1 (atomicity):* if heading-edit fails (e.g., sprint.org is read-only), the pre-flight tx must NOT be appended (or must be rolled back / followed by a cancel tx). No durable "tx says started, heading says still backlog" state.
- [ ] *Gap 2 (READY → BACKLOG scaffold):* =crates/orgasmic-cli/src/project.rs= and any related init code emit =* BACKLOG TASK-NNN= for new headings, not =* READY=. =orgasmic init= on a fresh project produces sprint.org that the dispatch CLI accepts without manual edits. Existing scaffold tests updated.
- [ ] *Gap 3 (multi-task dispatch):* =orgasmic manager dispatch --task TASK-A --task TASK-B --kind implementer --brief ...= validates both tasks exist + both in dispatchable state, creates one worktree (the WRITE_SCOPE is union), writes ONE pre-flight tx with =:TASK: TASK-A TASK-B=. =dispatch --kind reviewer= same.
- [ ] *Gap 3 (multi-task close):* =dispatch-close --task TASK-A --task TASK-B --status done --merge-sha XXX ...= appends N =implementer.done= tx (one per task), all sharing the merge metadata + =:CLOSED_TX:= pointing to the same pre-flight tx. Hand-coding the N-th tx is no longer needed.
- [ ] *Gap 3 (dispatch-status):* bundled-task closes are correctly resolved (no false "open" reports when one of the bundled tasks has a matching close tx).
- [ ] *Gap 4 (cleanup status):* close tx carries =:CLEANUP_STATUS: ok= when both worktree-remove and branch-delete succeed; =worktree_failed= / =branch_failed= / =partial= otherwise. =:CLEANUP_ERROR:= populated with a one-line error message when status is non-ok. =orgasmic manager dispatch-status --cleanup-failed= (or equivalent filter) lists non-ok closes.
- [ ] Tests: at least one new integration test per gap (Gap 1: dispatch-flip-then-close-flip round-trip on a task fixture; Gap 2: scaffold emits BACKLOG; Gap 3: two-task dispatch + close writes 1 pre-flight + 2 close tx; Gap 4: simulate worktree-remove failure → close tx records =CLEANUP_STATUS: worktree_failed=).
- [ ] =cargo test --workspace= + =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= + =cargo fmt --check= + =git diff --check= all clean. MSRV 1.78 preserved.

** Notes
This is a Rust-workspace dispatch; no UI changes. Estimated 400-600 LOC across =manager.rs= + =project.rs= + tests. Single coupled commit per the prior TASK-FB8CK / TASK-FB8CK.{1,2} pattern.

Lifecycle correctness for THIS dispatch itself: manager will (manually, since auto-transition doesn't exist yet) flip TASK-FB8CK.3 BACKLOG → IMPLEMENT at dispatch, then IMPLEMENT → REVIEW at implementer.done, then REVIEW → DONE on reviewer-clean. ** Description
Bundled polish round closing the 3 reviewer findings on TASK-FB8CK.3 + the already-known =:PARENT_TASK:= heuristic gap. All four live in =crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs= + tests; landed as ONE coupled commit per the reviewer's explicit bundle recommendation.

*F-1 (medium bug):* =build_dispatch_plan= overlap check only rejects when an open dispatch contains ALL requested tasks. Open =TASK-A= + new =dispatch --task TASK-A --task TASK-B= passes validation because =latest_open_dispatch_for_tasks= misses the partial overlap. Two live dispatches end up owning =TASK-A=. Fix: reject any open record whose =:TASK:= set INTERSECTS the requested task set. Regression test: open A, then attempt to dispatch A+B → must error with a clear "already open for TASK-A" message.

*F-2 (medium correctness):* =cmd_dispatch= flips the heading lifecycle (e.g., BACKLOG → IMPLEMENT) BEFORE spawning codex. If =spawn_codex= fails, the code appends =manager.dispatch_aborted= + cleans up the worktree, but never restores the heading — leaving a durably-aborted task stuck at IMPLEMENT. Fix: capture pre-dispatch stages (per task in the bundle), and on spawn-fail rollback path restore them via the same heading-writer helpers. If the restore itself fails, append a warning to stderr but keep the abort tx as durable record.

*F-3 (medium correctness):* =dispatch-close= for a bundled dispatch appends N close tx via N separate /tx requests. First-append-succeeds + later-append-fails leaves the tx log with a partial bundle close AND the worktree is already cleaned up (per gap 4's cleanup-before-tx ordering). =scan_open_dispatches= correctly requires all bundled tasks to mark the dispatch closed — so =dispatch-status= shows it as plain "open" with NO PARTIAL_CLOSED warning. Fix: pick one — (a) make bundled close appends a single daemon-side batch/transaction (write all N records inside ONE /tx POST or with a daemon-side multi-write API); OR (b) make =dispatch-close= idempotent in the partial case (subsequent calls only append the missing close tx for tasks that don't yet have one), AND surface =PARTIAL_CLOSED=<closed>/<total>= in =dispatch-status= output with the missing task ids. **Pick (b)** — idempotent + visible-in-status. Simpler than batch tx semantics, gives the manager an explicit retry path.

*Heuristic gap (already-known, from TASK-FB8CK.3 close-dogfood):* =:PARENT_TASK:= conflates "reviewer-finding fix subtask" (skip review, one-round-of-fixes) with "polish/follow-up subtask" (normal cycle, gets reviewer pass). Reviewer recommends: add =:FIX_SUBTASK: t= boolean property to fix-subtask headings; the auto-transition keys off that property instead of =:PARENT_TASK:= presence. Manager sets =:FIX_SUBTASK: t= when filing reviewer-finding fixes; polish-subtasks (like TASK-FB8CK.3, TASK-FB8CK.5) omit the property.

Add a schema doc to =shipped/schema/state-machine.org= or =shipped/manager/persona.org= naming when the manager should set =:FIX_SUBTASK: t=.

** Description
**Symptom**: direct edits to =.orgasmic/sprint.org= (via Claude Code's Edit tool, the new TASK-FB8CK.3 CLI auto-flip writer, or any other path that's not a daemon tx-route write) do NOT trigger a daemon project-index refresh. =/projects/:id/tasks/:task_id= continues to serve the pre-edit lifecycle stage until either (a) someone POSTs to =/tx= (the dispatch CLI's pre-flight tx-file write triggers this side effect), or (b) the daemon is restarted. The Tasks-page kanban displays stale state, undermining the lifecycle-stage discipline shipped in TASK-FB8CK.3.

**Observed 3× this session**: (1) manual =BACKLOG → IMPLEMENT= flip via Edit tool for TASK-DK0Y2 mid-dispatch — daemon stale until restart; (2) post-TASK-DK0Y2 merge — sprint.org changes weren't reflected until daemon rebuild + restart; (3) TASK-FB8CK.5 auto-flip via the new CLI write path — daemon stale until restart (verified live moments before this task was filed).

**Watcher code state (current)**: The =RecommendedWatcher= IS spawned (=crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/watcher.rs:80-89=). Per-project =.orgasmic/= directory IS watched recursively via =WatcherCommand::WatchProject= sent from =Daemon::run= for each project in the initial board snapshot (=lib.rs:170-174=). =flush()= canonicalizes both sides of the path comparison (=watcher.rs:230, 237=, mirrors the CLAUDE.md macOS pitfall). =record_event= filters to =.org=-extension files only (=watcher.rs:218=). So the watcher LOOKS like it should fire on sprint.org changes — but empirically it doesn't.

**Hypotheses to investigate** (codex picks ones to verify):

1. **Atomic-write event-shape mismatch.** Editors (and likely Claude Code's Edit tool, and the new CLI's =set_title_line= writer) often use a write-temp-file-then-rename pattern, which produces =EventKind::Create=, =EventKind::Modify(Name(_))=, possibly =EventKind::Remove= on the temp file rather than a direct =EventKind::Modify(Data)= on sprint.org. The =record_event= filter (=watcher.rs:206-216=) accepts =Create/Modify/Remove/Any/Other=. So this *should* be covered — but verify. Add debug tracing on each raw event, reproduce the edit, see what arrives.

2. **Path canonicalization mismatch on macOS.** On macOS, FSEvents may report =/System/Volumes/Data/Users/...= or =/private/Users/...= paths. The watcher's =canonical()= helper (=watcher.rs:202-204=) calls =fs::canonicalize= (resolves all symlinks). The snapshot =entry.path= used in =touched_projects= is canonicalized inside =flush= (=watcher.rs:247=). But the initial =WatchProject= passes =entry.path.clone()= raw (=lib.rs:171=). If the raw path doesn't match the FSEvent-reported canonical form, the watch handle might be registered on a path that FSEvents never reports against. Investigate.

3. **Notify watch handle silently dropped.** The watcher =watch()= return is checked (=watcher.rs:145-148= warns on error), but daemon logs don't appear to write to disk (=~/.orgasmic/logs/= is empty). Run with =RUST_LOG=debug= or capture stderr to see if =watch project failed= ever fires.

4. **=record_event= filter dropping non-=.org= temp files.** Editors writing to =sprint.org.tmp= or =sprint.org.swp= or =.#sprint.org= produce non-=.org= extensions; the filter at line 218 drops them. The atomic rename's final event (CREATE/MODIFY of sprint.org) should still fire — unless the rename event lacks the extension or arrives only on the source side. Trace it.

5. **=record_event= path-tracking gap.** =record_event= uses =path.extension()= to filter. If FSEvents reports parent-directory events (no extension), they're dropped. Verify the event paths carry sprint.org specifically, not just =.orgasmic/=.

**Approach**: write a focused reproduction first — an integration test that simulates the Edit-tool write pattern AND the new CLI's =set_title_line= write pattern. Read =crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs= for the latter (it's the most relevant new-write path). Add tracing or a test bus subscriber to capture what events arrive. Then fix the gap.

Assert =index.refresh_project= is NOT called within (debounce + 100ms) on the failing path — to capture the bug.

The existing =fs_event_triggers_project_refresh= test (=watcher.rs:304=) probably uses a simpler write that doesn't hit the bug — extend it OR add a sibling test that exercises the bug path.
- [ ] If the bug is in =record_event='s filter, document the new accepted event shapes in a code comment.
- [ ] =cargo test --workspace= clean (with the new test). =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= clean. =cargo fmt --check= clean. =git diff --check= clean. MSRV 1.78 preserved. No new deps.

** Description
Information-architecture restructure of the app shell per dec_CGVRW + dec_HYD58 + dec_H9P38. The current AppShell (ui/src/components/AppShell.tsx, ~500 lines) has Decisions/Architecture/Tasks/Glossary as primary nav with a sub-section "More" disclosure carrying Project, Runs, Org, ADR, Snapshots, Activity, Graph, Status, Settings (9 items). The Board page is a separate /board route surfaced via the index redirect when no last-project is stored. The user direction is to demote Board to a project-switcher affordance in the sidebar drawer, narrow primary nav to exactly 4 items + 4 spoiler items, and move Status + Settings entirely out of the sidebar into top-header icons (LED click → Status; gear → Settings). Manager popover (ManagerPopover) is already shipped per TASK-EBWZ9 and stays as-is; this task does not touch it.

*Three coupled surfaces:*

*(A) Project selector in the sidebar (dec_CGVRW).* The sidebar's first item becomes a project switcher dropdown. Selecting a project navigates to /projects/$projectId/decisions (the new default landing page) and persists to localStorage.orgasmic.active_project + localStorage.orgasmic.lastProject. The dropdown shows the currently active project (project_id + branch chip) with a small caret that opens a popover listing every registered project. A search/filter input appears once the project count exceeds ~6. The sidebar footer carries two actions: "+ Add project" (small dialog: validates a path; auto-fills project_id / repo_url / branch from .orgasmic/project.org and git config) and "Manage projects" (large modal whose contents are the existing BoardView Card grid — preserve the BoardView component as-is and mount it inside a shadcn Dialog with sm:max-w-none + h-[85vh]; Card click closes the modal AND switches the active project). Single-project users never see the Manage modal because the dropdown collapses to just the active project + the two footer actions. Empty state (no projects): dropdown disabled; footer shows "+ Add your first project" prominently.

*(B) Primary nav narrowed + spoiler (dec_HYD58).* PRIMARY = [Decisions, Architecture, Tasks, Glossary]. SPOILER ("More") = [ADR, Graph, Snapshots, Activity]. Removed from sidebar entirely: Project (overview was redundant with header; if kept route, link goes via the project-id chip click), Runs (low-value standalone page; live runs surface inside Activity per dec_CGVRW-era IA), Org (Org editor demoted; access via shipped/manager surface if needed — keep the route reachable by URL but not nav), Status (header LED is the entry point), Settings (header gear is the entry point). The spoiler starts EXPANDED on desktop (matches current behavior); collapsed on mobile.

*(C) Top header (dec_H9P38).* Right side of the header sticks with the current LED + bell + theme + gear pattern (which already partially exists). Make the LED a real click target navigating to /projects/$projectId/status (replaces "WS live" badge entirely; that's already done). Make the gear click target navigate to /projects/$projectId/settings (already done). Mobile (<md): theme + gear collapse into the existing ⋯ MobileOverflow dropdown (already done; expand it to also expose Status in the overflow list since the LED stays visible). *(D) Index redirect (cleanup).* /board route is preserved (URL still works) but no longer the default. The root redirect should always go to /projects/$projectId/decisions; if no last-project is stored, open the "+ Add project" dialog as a startup state on /projects/none/decisions or a synthetic /welcome route (codex picks the cleanest; lean toward keeping /board as the no-project fallback route renamed to render the Manage modal full-screen).

** Description
Five reviewer findings from TASK-B2P1Z bundled as a single fix-implementer round per one-round-of-fixes discipline. P1 because F-1 is a HIGH security finding that blocks-ship.

*F-1 (HIGH security) — Org injection in board.org writes.* =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs:225-238= + =crates/orgasmic-core/src/projects.rs:98-103,181-190= accept caller-provided =project_id=, =repo_url=, =default_branch=, path and render them directly into Org headings/property drawers. Re-parse-after-write only validates syntax, not absence of injected properties/headings. A bearer-auth caller can inject =:STATUS: active\n:PRIORITY: corrupted\n* INJECTED HEADING=-style payloads via newlines/control chars.

*F-2 (MEDIUM correctness) — Concurrent POST /projects races board.org.* =orgasmic-core/src/projects.rs:163-175= + =api.rs:256-263= do read-modify-write without locking. Two concurrent POSTs both read old board, append different entries, later write overwrites earlier (lost entry). Same-ID race bypasses duplicate check.

*F-3 (LOW security) — Filesystem paths leaked in error envelope.* =api.rs:298-304,318-324,5435-5438= pass raw filesystem context into JSON error responses (=write /Users/.../state/board.org=, canonical project paths). UI displays inline → developer strings as user-facing copy + path-disclosure smell.

*F-4 (LOW a11y) — Error callout has no live-region semantics.* =ProjectAddDialog.tsx:130-155= renders error callout without =role="alert"= / =aria-live=. Screen readers don't announce errors.

*F-5 (LOW design) — Cancel disabled during submit.* =ProjectAddDialog.tsx:157-168= disables both Submit AND Cancel. User can't back out via visible Cancel control.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-1*: =register_project= + =init_project= validate every caller-provided string before rendering. Strict grammar for =project_id= (=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+=, no whitespace/control chars/newlines, max length ~64). =repo_url= + =default_branch= reject newlines/control chars, max length cap. Path rejects newlines/null bytes. Integration tests: newline injection in each field reliably rejected (400 or 422) with no file write.
- [ ] *F-2*: Board read-modify-write serialized. Use =fs2::FileExt::lock_exclusive(&file)= (per CLAUDE.md trait-vs-stable pitfall; do NOT use =std::fs::File::lock= which is MSRV 1.89). Wrap read/duplicate-check/write/reparse in lock. Integration test: two concurrent POSTs with distinct IDs both land; same-ID race produces exactly one 201 + one 409.
- [ ] *F-3*: Public error messages stable, generic, path-free (e.g., "failed to read project.org", "failed to update project board"). Detailed errors logged server-side via =tracing= with original cause. UI receives the safe message.
- [ ] *F-4*: =ProjectAddDialog= error callout gets =role="alert"= AND =aria-live="polite"=. Optionally =aria-describedby= from form/inputs to the error region.
- [ ] *F-5*: Cancel button stays enabled (=disabled=false=) during submit. Clicking Cancel during pending request closes the dialog.
- [ ] All 210 tests still pass; new tests added per F-1 + F-2 (estimate +6-10). clippy/fmt/diff clean. MSRV 1.78. =cd ui && npm run build= clean, main =index= chunk under +1 kB over 361.63 kB.
- [ ] No new deps in =Cargo.toml= or =package.json=.

** Description
Live evidence from the [[2026-05-24]] TASK-B2P1Z chrome smoke: the running daemon (PID 97809, ~15h uptime) predated the TASK-B2P1Z merges, so the first =POST /projects= attempt returned =405 Allow: GET, HEAD= and the dialog rendered "405 Open Manage" — confusing for a real user who'd hit the same case after pulling latest without restarting their daemon.

This is a class problem: any merge that adds/changes daemon-facing routes (api.rs, projects.rs, watcher.rs, drivers, supervisor, writer, RPC) needs a daemon restart, but the developer has no surface telling them. =orgasmic doctor= already exists as the catch-all DX/diagnostics command (per polish-phase-1 plans in goal.org). Add a check:

1. Read the running daemon's =/daemon/status= (=boot_id=, =started_at=, optionally =git_sha=).
2. Read the on-disk binary at =$ORGASMIC_HOME/bin/orgasmic= mtime (or =stat=).
3. Read =git log --since=<daemon start> --oneline -- crates/orgasmic-daemon/ crates/orgasmic-core/= for merges since boot.
4. If binary mtime > daemon start_at OR there are daemon-code commits since boot, emit a yellow warning: =⚠ running daemon predates recent merges; restart recommended (orgasmic restart)=. Print the offending SHAs.

Optionally surface in =orgasmic status= too (since users hit that more often than =doctor=).

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] =orgasmic doctor= acquires daemon status + binary mtime + recent commits and emits the warning when stale.
- [ ] Warning includes: daemon uptime, binary build time, count of daemon-code commits since boot, first 3 SHAs + subjects.
- [ ] Clean state (no stale): silent or single ✓ line.
- [ ] Daemon down: skip the check, emit "daemon not running" once (don't double-warn).
- [ ] Bracket-aware: don't false-positive on doc-only commits under =crates/orgasmic-daemon/= (e.g., commits that only touch =*.md=). Acceptable to be conservative — first cut can flag any commit under those paths and refine later.
- [ ] Integration test: spawn an older binary, fake a newer mtime + git commit, assert =doctor= emits the warning. (Use =tempfile= for the binary stub.)
- [ ] All tests pass; clippy/fmt/diff clean. No new deps. MSRV 1.78.

*F-1 (MEDIUM test) — Path-free assertions miss the actual leaked path.* =tests/integration.rs:115-134= rejects only =/tmp=, =/private/=, =os error=. Fixture root from =tempfile::tempdir()= can be elsewhere (=/var/folders/...=, custom =TMPDIR=). A leak of =ctx.project_root= without those tokens still passes.

*F-3 (MEDIUM bug) — Content loaders classify NotFound by string matching.* =content_load_error= decides 404 only when =error.to_string()= contains =not found through loader rule= (=api.rs:351-361=). If the file disappears between =resolve_loader= and =read_to_string=, the underlying =io::ErrorKind::NotFound= becomes a generic 500.

*F-4 (MEDIUM design) — Loader-backed errors lose structured =path= field.* Helpers log only =error = %error= (=api.rs:346-361=); the path is embedded in the =anyhow= context from =content.rs:407-504=. Sanitized body, but server diagnostics lose consistent =path= field.

*F-5 (MEDIUM test) — Decisions/Architecture/Glossary/ADR tests all hit =/org/file=.* (=tests/integration.rs:479-508=) only proves =get_org_file= / =read_artifact= (=api.rs:3542-3552=). They do not exercise the route families registered at =api.rs:112-132=.

*F-6 (LOW test) — Tests don't assert JSON envelope shape.* =assert_path_free_error= checks raw text contains, not =error= field of =\{"error": ...\}=.

*F-7 (LOW design) — Raw org-file errors not artifact-aware.* =get_org_file= passes generic =org file= to =read_artifact= (=api.rs:3542-3552=). All raw-file misses say =org file not found= regardless of which file.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-1*: Pass the project root + home root into =assert_path_free_error= and assert body does not contain those exact paths or their canonical forms. Keep =/tmp= + =/private/= + =os error= as extra smoke coverage. Make fixture-path assertion load-bearing.
- [ ] *F-2*: Add failing-path tests for at least one list route AND one load route per family =/agent-templates=, =/prompts=, =/skills=. e.g., a =.org= directory where a file is expected, or unreadable user content. Assert status + path-free invariant (extended per F-1).
- [ ] *F-3*: Replace string-based content-loader error classification. Either propagate a typed content load error carrying =kind=, =path=, =source=, OR inspect the =anyhow= chain for =std::io::Error= and map =ErrorKind::NotFound= → =ApiError::not_found= and everything else → =ApiError::internal=. Add a regression test: file present at resolve-time, race-deleted before read (use a deterministic shim or =tempfile= manipulation).
- [ ] *F-4*: Content loader errors log =path = %p.display(), error = %e= structured fields consistent with =file_read_error=. Either via the typed-error route (F-3) or by re-extracting path from anyhow context.
- [ ] *F-5*: Keep one raw org-file missing-read test. Add targeted tests for the loader-backed route families claimed in the inventory. For genuine index-only routes that never hit filesystem errors (=/contradictions=, =/tasks/:id/activity=), assert their not-found/empty-state response is path-free + properly typed.
- [ ] *F-6*: Tests parse response as JSON and assert =error= field is present + non-empty. Use endpoint-specific predicates (=contains("not found") && !contains("read ")= or =starts_with("failed to")=). Preserves copy-edit flex without losing envelope contract.
- [ ] *F-7*: Derive artifact label from validated relative path in =get_org_file= before calling =read_artifact=. Map =decisions.org= → ="decisions file"=, =architecture.org= → ="architecture file"=, =glossary.org= → ="glossary file"=, ADR paths → ="ADR file"=, fall back to ="org file"= for unknown allowed files.
