*F-1 (HIGH bug) — =orgasmic doctor= emits no daemon-down signal.* Stale check skips when =daemon_status= returns =None= (=doctor.rs:83,122=); =daemon_status()= collapses connection failures, token read failures, 401s, decode failures into =None= (=doctor.rs:130=); =cmd_doctor= only prints =diagnose()= findings (=main.rs:674=); no other check emits =daemon not running=. Acceptance breach: criterion says daemon-down should skip stale AND emit =daemon not running= once.

*F-2 (MEDIUM design) — Decision fn reads wall clock.* =check_daemon_staleness()= calls =SystemTime::now()= internally for uptime (=doctor.rs:203=). Non-deterministic; prevents precise unit coverage of boundary cases.

*F-3 (LOW bug) — Sub-minute uptime renders as seconds.* =human_duration()= falls through to =format!("{secs}s")= for <60s (=doctor.rs:260=). Focus list called out =<1m= explicitly.

*F-4 (MEDIUM test) — Integration test misses the git-backed warning path.* Only test (=tests/doctor.rs:23=) creates a newer binary symlink and asserts =0 daemon-code commits=. Git path is only unit-tested (=doctor.rs:364=). Acceptance says integration test must spawn older binary + fake newer mtime + git commit + assert warning.

*F-5 (MEDIUM test) — Daemon-down + unauthorized not tested through acquisition layer.* Only daemon-down test calls =check_daemon_staleness(None, ...)= directly (=doctor.rs:405=). Doesn't prove connection-refused / missing-token / 401 are correctly classified by =daemon_status()= (=doctor.rs:130=).

*F-6 (LOW design) — Commit truncation loses remaining-count.* Lists first three, then bare =...= (=doctor.rs:226,229=). Focus area asked for =...and N more=.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-1*: Make daemon status acquisition return a small status enum (=Running(DaemonStatus)=, =Unavailable=, =Unauthorized=) OR add one separate daemon-liveness doctor finding. Keep stale check silent on unavailable/unauthorized status, but emit exactly ONE non-stale warning (=daemon not running= on connection refused; =daemon auth token mismatch= on 401, or a single combined message — pick one deliberately). NOT a double-warn with the stale check.
- [ ] *F-2*: Pass =now: SystemTime= into =check_daemon_staleness()= (or split rendering so uptime is supplied by caller). Unit tests assert exact uptime strings for =<1m=, =59s=, =1m=, =1h 4m=, =2d 3h=, =30d 5h= without sleeping or racing the clock.
- [ ] *F-3*: =human_duration()= returns =<1m= for =secs < 60=. Add direct tests for the listed boundaries.

** Description
Four reviewer findings from TASK-M88ZM bundled as one fix-implementer round per one-round-of-fixes discipline. F-1 is HIGH (blocks-ship for production use of the new driver). Report at =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-056-review-report.md=.

*F-1 (HIGH bug) — Natural cursor-agent completion recorded as interrupted.* =cursor_agent.rs:748= maps real =result= event to =DriverEvent::RunComplete=, then =run_cursor_agent_stdio= at =:402= waits for the child and returns, dropping the event sender. Supervisor at =supervisor.rs:339= treats stream-close as =Interrupted=; stage outcome at =api.rs:2363= treats interrupted as failure. Reviewer's live smoke confirmed real CLI emits =system/init=, =user=, =assistant=, =result= then exits — every successful Cursor run races to interrupted.

*F-2 (MEDIUM bug) — Tool events bypass WorkerTool/BabysitterTool policy.* =cursor_agent.rs:653= and =:706= emit =DriverEvent::ToolCall= for arbitrary Cursor tool names; unit test at =:1124= asserts a ="shell"= ToolCall even though trait contract restricts implementer tool calls to =WorkerTool= and babysitter calls to =BabysitterTool=. =translate_value= at =:543= has no top-level =tool_use= arm — cursor's =tool_use= events get downgraded to system text chunks.

*F-3 (LOW bug) — Unsupported endpoint values silently use stdio.* =validate()= at =:82= validates =api_key_env= and =sandbox= but never rejects non-empty endpoint values other than ="stdio"=. =configured_endpoint()= treats any non-empty string as real mode — typo =stdlo= or HTTP URL spawns local stdio bridge.

*F-4 (LOW test) — Real-wire tests don't prove terminal uniqueness or partial chunking.* =tests/cursor_agent.rs:109= stops after first terminal event without asserting exactly one terminal, no post-terminal events, no duplicate release-created terminal. Driver always passes =--stream-partial-output= but no fixture proves cumulative partials become sensible deltas.

** Description
Two reviewer findings from TASK-YVZ9V bundled as one fix-implementer round per one-round-of-fixes discipline. Both share a single root cause: the new AutoSpawn candidate-discovery path (=auto_spawn_worker_dirs= + =read_dir= loop in =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs:2732-2768=) diverges from the existing =load_stage_worker= loader semantics.

F-1 HIGH (correctness): candidate discovery walks only =workers/= directories; =load_stage_worker= falls back to legacy =agent-templates/{id}.org=. A project whose stage-mapped worker only exists as a legacy agent template can have its unpinned task silently routed to some other eligible worker, violating the stage-mapped-worker preference.

F-2 MEDIUM (correctness): candidate slice is built from =std::fs::read_dir= (unstable iteration order on macOS/Linux). =auto_select_worker= is deterministic only relative to its input slice, so two equally-eligible fully-specified workers can produce different winners across platforms.

Report at =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-059-review-report.md=.

Daemon looks up worker via eligibility (or =--worker= override flag); composes prompt bundle (persona + skills + conventions + brief); calls =supervisor.acquire(driver_for(worker.driver), AcquireRequest{...})=; returns dispatch result. Driver-emitted DriverEvents drive lifecycle transitions through supervisor → tx pipeline. ** Description
Surfaced by manager during TASK-G0C5R + TASK-DFEDX parallel dispatches (and visible already on TASK-RF3J1.1 retrospectively): the daemon =/runs= classifier flags subprocess-stream-json + cursor-agent runs as =interrupted= with reason "driver subprocess-stream-json/cursor-agent could not prove a live runtime handle" even when (a) the subprocess is alive and actively working, OR (b) the run has already terminated naturally with =RunComplete= written to the session jsonl.

Root cause hypothesis: the supervisor's =runtime_id= registration for spawned subprocesses doesn't track the cursor-agent subprocess properly (or expires too aggressively), AND/OR the run-classifier doesn't consult the session jsonl terminal events before falling back to runtime-handle liveness.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reproduce: spawn a cursor-agent dispatch, observe =/runs= response shows =live= (not =interrupted=) while the subprocess is alive.
- [ ] Post-RunComplete: =/runs= shows the run as =finished= (or whatever terminal classification is correct), not =interrupted=.
- [ ] Run-classifier consults session jsonl terminal events as primary signal; runtime-handle liveness as secondary.

** Description
TASK-RF3J1 dispatch endpoint accepts =last_path= as part of =DispatchRequest= but does not WRITE to it on =RunComplete=. Result: TASK-G0C5R + TASK-DFEDX (and TASK-RF3J1.1 itself) finished with =run_complete= in session jsonl but no =last.txt= on disk, breaking the manager's watcher convention (`until [ -s '$last_path' ]`).

Additionally: cursor-agent in =--sandbox enabled --force= mode does NOT commit the worktree even though the brief asks it to. Symptom: cursor-agent finishes with =run_complete=, leaves uncommitted changes in the worktree, watcher times out waiting for last.txt. Manager has to inspect session jsonl, run cargo gates manually, and =git commit -m "$summary"= on behalf.

Fix two surfaces:
1. *last.txt writer*: dispatch endpoint registers a =RunComplete= subscriber that writes the assistant's terminal summary to =last_path=. Source: session jsonl =run_complete= event's =event.summary= (or the last assistant text_chunk if summary missing).
2. *Auto-commit*: when an implementer dispatch's terminal event is =RunComplete= AND the worktree has uncommitted changes AND verification gates pass (cargo test/clippy/fmt/diff), append an =implementer.commit_pending= tx so manager can confirm. (Don't auto-commit silently — too risky; just signal.) Alternatively: ship a small =manager dispatch-finalize --task TASK-NNN= subcommand that does verify+commit+merge in one shot.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *last.txt writer*: dispatch RunComplete writes assistant summary to =last_path=; integration test asserts the file content. Watcher convention =until [ -s '$last_path' ]= works.
- [ ] *Implementer-commit-signal*: either auto-tx =implementer.commit_pending= on RunComplete with uncommitted worktree, OR new =manager dispatch-finalize --task TASK-NNN= subcommand that runs verify+commit+merge.
- [ ] Regression tests for both surfaces; the existing TASK-RF3J1 e2e tests still pass.
- [ ] =cargo test --workspace + cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings + cargo fmt --check + git diff --check= all green. MSRV 1.78. No new deps.

** Description
6 findings from TASK-CPA74 reviewer (verdict has-issues no-blocks-ship). 3 MEDIUM affect fresh-user UX; 3 LOW polish. All foldable into one docs round.

*F-1 (MEDIUM correctness)* — README instructs =orgasmic serve --port 8739= but =orgasmic init= writes =bind_port: 4848= in =$ORGASMIC_HOME/config.yaml= per =home.rs:120-123=. The CLI's =read_bind_port= (=daemon_client.rs:189-216=) reads config default, so post-serve =orgasmic status= / =doctor= hit :4848 while daemon is on :8739. Vite hardcodes :8739 so UI flow works; documented status step does not. Fix: add a one-liner after =orgasmic init= to set =bind_port: 8739= in config.yaml (or =export ORGASMIC_DAEMON_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8739=). Add Troubleshooting note that CLI + Vite must agree.

*F-2 (MEDIUM correctness)* — First use step 3 (=orgasmic status=) runs BEFORE step 4 (=orgasmic serve=). On fresh install, =DaemonClient::from_home= requires a bearer token at =$ORGASMIC_HOME/user/auth/token=, which is created only by first successful =orgasmic serve= boot (=auth.rs:18-34=). Step 3 errors with "bearer token not found ... run orgasmic serve once to generate it". Fix: move =orgasmic status= to step 5 (after =orgasmic serve=), OR add a note that step 3 is expected to fail until after step 4 on first run.

*F-3 (MEDIUM design / AC source)* — README cites Node version from =ui/package-lock.json= (Vite 6's =engines=). Brief AC said "Node from =ui/package.json= engines". =ui/package.json= has no =engines= field. Two acceptable fixes: (a) add =engines: { node: "^18.0.0 || ^20.0.0 || >=22.0.0" }= to =ui/package.json= and point README there (cleaner; future-proof), OR (b) reword README: "Vite 6 requires Node ^18 || ^20 || >=22 (see =vite= in =ui/package-lock.json=; no top-level =engines= in =ui/package.json= yet)." Recommend (a) since it's small.

*F-4 (LOW correctness)* — Troubleshooting "Daemon won't start" → "confirm =$ORGASMIC_HOME/user/auth/token= exists". On a failed first start, the token CORRECTLY doesn't exist; checking it doesn't help diagnose. Fix: lead with =orgasmic doctor=; note token appears AFTER first successful =orgasmic serve=.

*F-5 (LOW design)* — PATH one-liner hardcodes =~/.orgasmic= instead of respecting custom =$ORGASMIC_HOME=. Fix: use =$ORGASMIC_HOME/bin:$PATH= with a note on =export ORGASMIC_HOME=... for non-default.

*F-6 (LOW docs)* — Troubleshooting missing port-conflict bullets (:8739 + :5180). Fix: add =lsof -i :8739= advice + Vite =--port= override + update tunnel YAML accordingly.

** Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] *F-2*: First use ordering puts =orgasmic status= AFTER =orgasmic serve= (or adds expected-error caveat).
- [ ] *F-3*: Either =ui/package.json= gets an =engines= field, OR README wording acknowledges =engines= is absent and cites the lockfile honestly.

Reproduce: dispatch a reviewer kind after a recent implementer close on the same task — the reviewer's dispatch_started is silently skipped.

Observed evidence:

Root cause hypothesis: TASK-RF3J1.6 F-7's =implementer.commit_pending= subscriber may be intercepting or racing with the =record_dispatch_started= writer. Verify whether =record_dispatch_started= even exists / is called in the post-TASK-WQFPG layout of =api.rs::post_task_dispatch=. ** Description
Surfaced live during the TASK-WQFPG.1 dispatch this session (cursor-agent =run-20260525T050115-...= on =task-062.1-impl=): the cursor-agent subprocess ran to clean completion + self-commit, but =/private/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-062.1-last.txt= and =/private/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-062.1-stdout.log= were NEVER populated, despite =run.created= tx recording both paths in =:LAST_PATH:= and =:STDOUT_PATH:=.

This is a regression from the TASK-RF3J1.6 era. The TASK-RF3J1 cluster narrative explicitly noted: "F-7 ships the dispatch RunComplete last.txt writer + =implementer.commit_pending= tx signal (gated by =dispatch.auto_commit_signal= config; default true), closing the manager-on-behalf-commit overhead loop AND restoring the watcher convention." So the writer SHOULD be wired — but is silently no-op for cursor-agent dispatches in the post-TASK-RF3J1.6 + post-TASK-FXXC0 daemon.

Earlier dispatches in this session DID populate these files (TASK-WQFPG implementer, TASK-G0C5R/TASK-DFEDX/TASK-CPA74 reviewer rounds at =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-*-last.txt= are full of content). TASK-WQFPG.1 was the FIRST cursor-agent dispatch after the TASK-FXXC0 daemon-rebuild + restart at 01:23. So the regression entered between TASK-WQFPG's merge (=4e96cc0=) and HEAD.

Suspected causes (ordered by likelihood):
1. TASK-FXXC0's reshape of =post_task_dispatch= moved the manager.dispatch_started tx write into the daemon, but may have orphaned the supervisor-side RunComplete observer that TASK-RF3J1.6 wired to write last.txt. The new handler creates the run.created tx with =:LAST_PATH:= populated, but the supervisor-side writer may need a separate registration that the new handler doesn't perform.
2. Cursor-agent specific: the cursor-agent driver might not emit a RunComplete event the same way claude-acp / codex-appserver do; the writer expects a particular event shape and skips silently otherwise.
3. The =dispatch.auto_commit_signal= config might be defaulting to false post-TASK-FXXC0 (config defaults can drift on schema changes).

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reproduce the gap: dispatch a cursor-agent implementer (TASK-KM5K1 itself counts — dogfood the fix on the next dispatch); verify that =last.txt= and =stdout.log= are NOT populated on the current daemon.
- [ ] Root-cause the gap: identify which of the three suspected causes (supervisor-side observer missing, cursor-agent event shape, config default drift) is responsible. Trace via =tracing::debug!= adds if needed; remove the debugs before final commit.
- [ ] Fix: ensure that any cursor-agent dispatch via =POST /projects/.../tasks/.../dispatch= produces a populated =last.txt= (subprocess final stdout — the cursor-agent =result= event message) AND =stdout.log= (full subprocess stdout). The =implementer.commit_pending= tx signal should ALSO fire on RunComplete per the TASK-RF3J1.6 F-7 contract.
- [ ] Regression test in =crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/dispatch_endpoint.rs=: dispatch a simulated implementer run (using the existing mock-driver test scaffolding), assert that after RunComplete the =:LAST_PATH:= file exists with non-empty content AND =:STDOUT_PATH:= file exists with non-empty content. Test should reliably reproduce TASK-KM5K1's gap if the supervisor wiring regresses again.
- [ ] =cargo test --workspace + cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings + cargo fmt --check + git diff --check= all green. MSRV 1.78. No new deps.

** Description

*F-1 (MEDIUM correctness)* — =GET /managers/recent-actions= ignores project scope. Handler scans all tx records in the daemon index with no =project= filter; in a multi-project daemon, workbench cards leak other projects' manager activity. Fix: thread =?project=<id>= query param (or derive from session context); filter =record.entry.project= match; thread =projectId= from =ManagerPopover= into =fetchManagerRecentActions= call.

*F-2 (MEDIUM correctness)* — Manager action =body= field always empty string. =get_manager_recent_actions= returns =body: String::new()= unconditionally; UI's "Show full action body" disclosure (=ManagerWorkbench.tsx:219-225=) is dead code. Fix: populate =body= from =extra= =BODY= when present; mirror =activity_body()= logic for manager tx types. OR drop the disclosure entirely if no useful body source.

*F-3 (LOW test)* — Integration test for recent-actions doesn't cover =limit= default (5), cap at 50, or =body= shape. Test only validates filtering + chronological selection. Fix: extend =get_manager_recent_actions_returns_recent_manager_tx= with cases for omitted-limit → 5, =limit=999= → 50 cap, and project-scoping isolation (after F-1 fix).

*F-4 (LOW a11y)* — =ManagerActionCard= cards lack =article= landmark / =aria-label=. Screen-reader users get unstructured content. Fix: wrap each card in =<article aria-label={...}>= with descriptive label (tx type + relative time + actor).

*F-5 (LOW cosmetic)* — =NodeListView= sticky filter header has =border-b= on inner =Card= instead of outer wrapper per brief. Behavior equivalent. Optional fix: move border to wrapper for brief alignment.

** Description
Bundle of three small daemon-dispatch-hardening fixes surfaced live during the TASK-KM5K1.1 dispatch (=run-20260525T063458=). All three concern the live cursor-agent dispatch loop and overlap on =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs= — bundling them as one cluster avoids three back-to-back single-file dispatches contending for the same write region.

*Item 1 — cursor-agent stream taxonomy gap.* The TASK-KM5K1.1 dispatch emitted 530+ =text_chunk= events ALL with =stream: system= (cursor-agent "thinking deltas"); zero events with =stream: assistant=. TASK-KM5K1.1's =dispatch_last_summary_from_session= precedence fix is correct, but on the live cursor-agent path it still produces empty last.txt summaries because no assistant chunks ever arrive. Either the cursor-agent driver needs to emit a synthetic =run_complete= event when the subprocess exits (preferred — keeps the daemon extractor honest), OR the driver re-classifies its terminal text chunk as =stream: assistant=, OR =dispatch_last_summary_from_session= grows a system-thinking fallback (least preferred — pollutes the summary with raw thinking).

*Item 2 — completion watcher no-terminal-event timeout.* =spawn_dispatch_completion_watcher= currently polls indefinitely after the subprocess exits if no terminal session marker (=Lifecycle::Release= / =run_complete= / failure outcome) was emitted in the session. Falls back only on the 86,400s safety cap, which means a clean-exit-no-terminal cursor-agent run can leave the daemon-side watcher spinning for 24h before artifacts get written. Need: short post-exit grace period (e.g., 30s — long enough to let in-flight session writes flush) after the supervisor classifies the run as ended, then proceed with artifact write from whatever envelopes are present, even if no terminal event arrived.

*Item 3 — tx writer trailing whitespace on empty :REASON: values.* When =record_dispatch_started= (or any tx writer) is called with an empty =:REASON:= string, the serializer emits =:REASON:       \n= (trailing spaces). Pre-existing: =.orgasmic/tx/2026-05.org= lines 5450, 5496, 5604, 5669 all show the pattern. Breaks =git diff --check= on every cluster-close commit; manager hand-strips before commit. Cosmetic but discipline-affecting. Fix: when serializing tx property values, trim trailing whitespace OR skip the property line entirely if the value is empty.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *Item 1 (cursor-agent stream taxonomy)*: pick ONE of the three approaches above (synthetic run_complete preferred). After the fix, a real cursor-agent dispatch (verify by running this very dispatch's brief through =orgasmic manager dispatch=) produces a non-empty =:LAST_PATH:= file. Add a focused dispatch_endpoint test that emulates the cursor-agent "all system thinking deltas, no terminal" shape and asserts the chosen fix produces non-empty last.txt content.
- [ ] *Item 2 (watcher post-exit grace)*: =spawn_dispatch_completion_watcher= must short-circuit within N seconds (recommend 30s) of supervisor-observed subprocess exit when no terminal event has arrived. Add a regression test that drives the watcher to a no-terminal-event clean exit and asserts the watcher returns within the grace window (NOT 86,400s).
- [ ] *Item 3 (tx writer trailing whitespace)*: after dispatch with =--reason ""= (or with no =--reason= flag), the resulting tx entry must not have trailing whitespace on the :REASON: line (either omit the line, emit =:REASON: \n= with no trailing space, or emit just =:REASON:\n=). Add a focused unit test that constructs a tx entry with empty :REASON: and asserts no trailing whitespace via =assert!(!line.ends_with(' '))=. Verify =git diff --check= clean after a fresh dispatch.
- [ ] =cargo test --workspace + clippy + fmt + diff= all green. MSRV 1.78.
- [ ] Tests cover all three items; net test count grows by at least 3.

** Notes
Bundled rather than three separate dispatches because all three touch =api.rs= in overlapping regions; parallelism would require careful brief partitioning and risk merge conflicts. Single bundled brief is cheaper. NOT a :FIX_SUBTASK: (these are not reviewer findings on a prior dispatch); will go through full IMPLEMENT → REVIEW → DONE lifecycle. Reviewer pass after merge per persona rule 2.

** Description
Bundle of three daemon-dispatch-polish fixes. All surfaced live this session (TASK-M5JTN reviewer F-2 + TASK-M5JTN.1 stuck-dispatch incident + TASK-PYW86 chrome smoke side finding). Bundled rather than three separate dispatches because all overlap on the daemon dispatch/run lifecycle code paths and a single coherent change is cheaper than three sequential round-trips.

*Item 1 — cursor-agent driver synthetic run_complete on subprocess exit (was TASK-M5JTN.2 / supersedes it).* TASK-M5JTN reviewer F-2: Item 1's path (c) "system fallback after assistant accumulation" produces noisy last.txt on live implementer-cursor dispatches (composer-2.5-fast emits 500+ raw thinking deltas with =stream: system= and no terminal event). Path (a) — the cursor-agent driver synthesizes a =DriverEvent::RunComplete { summary }= on clean subprocess exit when no real terminal was emitted — is the architecturally correct fix. Reviewer confirmed feasibility: =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/cursor.rs= already has =terminal_emitted=, =emit_run_complete_once=, =translate_result=; =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/subprocess_stream_json.rs= currently emits nothing on successful exit when =!terminal_emitted()= (lines 276-286).

*Item 2 — daemon run-lifecycle classifier early-exit detection (was TASK-T3NWN candidate).* Surfaced live this session during the first TASK-M5JTN.1 dispatch attempt. When cursor-agent subprocess dies after only 2 envelopes (=lifecycle::acquire= + =driver_event::ready=) — e.g., spawned with a bad CLI invocation race — the daemon's run-lifecycle classifier leaves the run stuck "active" and refuses =/runs/.../release= with =active run= error. Required daemon restart to clear the lock. Need: detect this early-exit pattern (subprocess exited + only N envelopes with no work envelope) within a short window (~10s) and auto-release the lease so subsequent dispatches don't 409 Conflict.

*Item 3 — hung task-detail endpoint (was TASK-NGDNP candidate).* Surfaced during TASK-PYW86 chrome smoke (two turns ago): =GET /projects/:valid_project_id/tasks/:invalid_task_id= hangs (>4s timeout, no response). Compare =GET /projects/<missing>/tasks/<id>= returns 404 in ~7s. Likely the task-detail handler does a synchronous file read (or task-graph lookup) with no NotFound short-circuit on the invalid task_id path. Need: return 404 quickly for unknown task ids on valid projects.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *Item 1 (synthetic run_complete)*:
  - In =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/subprocess_stream_json.rs= (or =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/cursor.rs=, depending on architectural fit), synthesize a =DriverEvent::RunComplete { summary }= when: (i) subprocess exits with status 0, (ii) no terminal session marker (=RunComplete=, =Lifecycle::Release=) has been emitted, (iii) some content was accumulated during the run. Summary = accumulated assistant text if available, otherwise the trailing N system chunks (consistent with =dispatch_last_summary_from_session= precedence).
  - The synthetic emission MUST NOT fire when a real terminal event has already arrived. Use the existing =terminal_emitted= flag.
  - Live dispatch (or test emulating the live shape) of an implementer-cursor run with no real terminal event produces a non-empty =last.txt= where the content is the SUMMARY (distilled), not raw concatenated thinking deltas.
  - Add a focused integration test in =crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/dispatch_endpoint.rs= OR =crates/orgasmic-drivers/tests/= that emulates the cursor-agent "system-only, no terminal" shape, runs through the full driver-mode pipeline, and asserts the synthetic =RunComplete= is emitted with the expected summary.
  - Optional: with path (a) shipped, the system-text fallback in =dispatch_last_summary_from_session= becomes potentially-removable. If safely removable (no other driver depends on it), remove and document. Otherwise leave in place as defense-in-depth and note why.

- [ ] *Item 2 (early-exit classifier)*:
  - In =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs= (or =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs=, depending on where the lifecycle classifier lives), detect the early-exit pattern: subprocess exited + only acquire + ready envelopes (or only N≤2 envelopes with no work-related events) within a short observation window (~10s). When detected, auto-release the lease (the same code path that =/runs/.../release= would invoke).
  - The detection must NOT fire on legitimately-fast successful runs that just happen to emit few envelopes (e.g., a dispatched task that completes in 1s and emits a clean run_complete). Use the early-exit AC: presence of acquire + ready but NOT a single "work" event (text_chunk, tool_call, or terminal).
  - After the fix, a stuck-active run from this pattern auto-clears within ~10s of subprocess exit; subsequent dispatches don't 409 Conflict.
  - Add a focused integration test that simulates the early-exit shape (mock driver emits acquire + ready then subprocess "exits" via simulated supervisor signal) and asserts the run auto-releases within bounded timeout, with no 409 on a subsequent dispatch.

- [ ] *Item 3 (hung task-detail endpoint)*:
  - In =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs= task-detail handler (search for the route registered at =GET /projects/:project_id/tasks/:task_id=), short-circuit with a 404 NotFound when the task_id doesn't exist in the project's task index. The check must complete quickly (no synchronous file read on the task path before the existence check).
  - Match the response shape of the existing project-not-found case: short JSON envelope (=404 {"error":"task not found"}= or similar — keep path-free per TASK-PYW86 envelope hardening).
  - Add a focused integration test in =dispatch_endpoint.rs= (or wherever the task-detail handler tests live) that issues =GET /projects/<valid>/tasks/<invalid>= and asserts: (a) response is 404 within bounded timeout (e.g., <1s), (b) response envelope contains no filesystem paths, (c) response envelope is JSON with an "error" field.

- [ ] *Cross-cutting*:
  - =cargo test --workspace + clippy + fmt + diff= all green. MSRV 1.78.
  - No new dependencies.
  - Net test count grows by at least 3 (one per item).

** Description
The =orgasmic manager dispatch= CLI currently prints a watch hint like:

#+begin_src
dispatched: TASK-XXX implementer pid=50864 run_id=run-... worker=...
watch: until [ -s '/private/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-XXX-last.txt' ] || ! ps -p 50864 > /dev/null; do sleep 8; done
#+end_src

The =pid=50864= here is the OUTER wrapper PID — the cursor-agent CLI launcher that forks the worker-server process and then exits within seconds. The watch hint relies on =ps -p 50864= to detect "dispatch is done", but this is wrong: =ps -p 50864= goes false within seconds while the actual cursor-agent worker-server process (e.g., PID 37147) keeps running for the full dispatch duration (10 min to 1h+).

Live observed this turn on TASK-J95T2 reviewer dispatch and TASK-J95T2.1 implementer dispatch: my manager watcher script exited early because it polled the wrong PID. I worked around by also polling =pgrep -f "cursor-agent/versions.*worker-server"= and adding a 5s post-exit drain. This works but should be the CLI's responsibility, not the manager's.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The =orgasmic manager dispatch= CLI output prints a watch hint that correctly reflects the dispatch's true liveness. Pick ONE approach:
  - *(a) Inner-PID approach*: have the daemon's =POST /projects/:project_id/tasks/:task_id/dispatch= response include the cursor-agent worker-server PID (not just the wrapper PID), and the CLI prints that PID in the watch hint. Requires daemon-side: poll =/proc= (or =ps= on macOS) for the wrapper's child process within a short window after spawn (~5s) and stash the descendant PID in the run record. Caveat: depends on knowing the worker-server is always a direct child of the wrapper.
  - *(b) Run-state-poll approach*: change the watch hint to poll the daemon's API (e.g., =/runs/:run_id/status=) for run released, rather than polling a PID. Requires daemon-side: ensure such an endpoint exists and is bearer-authed appropriately. CLI side: print a watch hint that uses =curl= with the bearer token. More robust (no PID fragility) but the watch hint becomes longer.
  - *(c) Process-pattern approach*: print a watch hint that uses =pgrep -f= matching the worker pattern + session id or run id. E.g., =until [ -s last.txt ] || ! pgrep -f "cursor-agent.*<session_id>" > /dev/null; do sleep 8; done=. Requires cursor-agent's argv to actually include the session id; verify by inspecting =ps -o command= for an active dispatch first.
- [ ] After the fix, a typical manager watcher script using the new watch hint exits when the dispatch actually completes (not when the outer wrapper dies). Verify by dispatching TASK-CNZGR itself (dogfood — the dispatch that ships this fix should be the first to benefit from it).
- [ ] Add a unit test in =crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/= (or integration test in =dispatch_endpoint.rs= depending on approach chosen) that asserts the dispatch CLI output contains a sensible watch hint (e.g., approach (a): contains an inner-PID format; approach (b): contains the daemon URL + run_id; approach (c): contains a process-pattern).
- [ ] =cargo test --workspace + clippy + fmt + diff= all green. MSRV 1.78.

** Notes
NOT :FIX_SUBTASK: t — full IMPLEMENT → REVIEW → DONE lifecycle. P3 because the manager's pgrep workaround works; this is DX polish, not a blocker. The daemon-side approach (a) is the cleanest long-term and matches the existing pattern of the dispatch handler tracking subprocess lifecycle (TASK-M5JTN + TASK-J95T2 work). Recommended choice: (a) inner-PID.

** Evidence

- Implementation: new =supervisor::resolve_dispatch_watch_pid= polls direct children via =pgrep -P= for up to 5s, prefers =worker-server= children, falls back to wrapper PID. Only applied to =cli_dispatch= spawns (early-exit watcher still uses wrapper PID — implementer reverted an attempt to switch that because it broke real cursor-agent auto-spawn). =manager.rs= unchanged — it already prints =response.pid=.
- Tests: 361 → 363. Workspace clean (cargo test + clippy + fmt + diff). MSRV 1.78.
- Reviewer: cursor-agent (reviewer-cursor, composer-2.5-fast), ~5min wall. Verdict =has-issues, no-blocks-ship= (5 findings). Report at =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-075-review-report.md=. Findings: F-1 MEDIUM (500ms fallback latches non-worker-server intermediate child — LIVE-DEMONSTRATED by the reviewer dispatch itself: printed =pid=36632= didn't match wrapper 36202 or worker-server 37731), F-2 MEDIUM (tests don't exercise worker-server preference path), F-3 LOW (doc comment overstates early-exit watcher behavior), F-4 LOW (fallback to dead wrapper PID inherent), F-5 LOW (5s sync HTTP latency).

Note: the FIRST TASK-CNZGR.1 dispatch attempt SIGKILL'd (cursor-agent crashed at seq 2, before any work — unclear cause; possibly OS pressure). The TASK-CNZGR reviewer dispatch ITSELF live-demonstrated F-1: printed =pid=36632= didn't correspond to any live process when I checked moments later; the real cursor-agent processes were wrapper PID 36202 and worker-server PID 37731. The 500ms fallback path latched a non-worker-server intermediate child that exited shortly after, recreating the original liveness bug class for that one dispatch.

Reviewer report at =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-075-review-report.md=.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-1 — strict worker-server gate for full 5s window on cursor-agent wrappers*: In =supervisor::poll_direct_child_pid= (=crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs:891-909=), when =wrapper_looks_like_cursor_agent(parent_pid)= is true, KEEP polling for =worker-server= children for the entire 5s window. Remove the 500ms accept-any-child gate for cursor-agent wrappers. The accept-any-child fallback should only apply to non-cursor wrappers (and explicit test hooks). Rationale: the original bug class was a wrapper exiting fast while worker-server kept running. Accepting any descendant defeats the fix when an intermediate launcher exists.
- [ ] *F-2 — add test that exercises the worker-server preference path*: Both current tests use generic =sleep 300= children with no =worker-server= in the command, so they hit the accept-any-child branch, not =prefer_worker_server_child=. Add a test where a fake shim spawns a child whose =ps -o command= output contains =worker-server= (alongside a concurrent generic sibling) and assert the worker-server child is chosen. Test must FAIL on a build that removes the =worker-server= string match.

Poll briefly for a direct child so dispatch watch hints and early-exit watchers track the real worker PID." But the early-exit watcher (TASK-J95T2) intentionally uses the wrapper PID, NOT the resolved worker PID. Fix the comment to say "watch hints / DispatchResponse.pid only; early-exit watcher remains on the wrapper PID by design (TASK-J95T2)".

** Description
The =acp-stdio= driver mode spawns =codex app-server= as a subprocess (auto-spawn shipped in TASK-RF3J1.1 via HAR pattern) but never drives it over JSON-RPC. As a result every dispatch routed through =implementer-codex-stdio= / =reviewer-codex-stdio= idles: codex app-server reads nothing from stdin, never receives =initialize= / =thread/start= / =turn/start=, and the orgasmic daemon eventually marks the run as stuck (TASK-J95T2 early-exit classifier was added precisely because this gap kept jamming the supervisor pipeline). Workaround for the last ~3 weeks: route every dispatch through the working =implementer-cursor= / =reviewer-cursor= path (cursor-agent CLI + subprocess-stream-json driver).

Closing this gap unlocks two things:

1. *On-rail codex dispatches*: =--worker implementer-codex-stdio= becomes a usable choice in =orgasmic manager dispatch=; reviewer-codex-stdio can run reviewer passes. Removes the "cursor-agent only" footgun.
2. *UI real-time agent chat* (TASK-C7ZG5 follow-up): user direction this session — "user can via task dialog (ui) click the current agent status to open the chat with the running agent and in real time monitor the session via the same chat interface as manager uses in har app for acp driver type". The chat UX only makes sense over a real ACP wire, so this task is its enabler.

Concrete code-level diagnosis (the implementer brief expands on each):

- =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/acp_stdio.rs= today is just a compose-adapter wrapper that hands work to =SubprocessStreamJsonDriver=. It spawns the binary correctly but =SubprocessStreamJsonDriver::run_subprocess_stream_json= treats stdout as line-delimited stream-json and calls =adapter.parse_stdout_line(&line)= for each line. The =HarnessEventAdapter::parse_stdout_line= default deserialises one JSON value per line and delegates to =parse_event= — so codex notifications WOULD route through =CodexAdapter::parse_event= correctly if codex were already in a session. But nothing sends the JSON-RPC requests (=initialize=, =thread/start=, =turn/start=) that get codex into that state, and the adapter's control surface (=transition_state=, =babysitter_action=, =release=) emits =WireMessage::JsonRpc { method, params }= values that the subprocess driver also has no codepath to send.
- =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/acp_ws.rs::run_acp_ws= is the closest analog: it implements exactly this JSON-RPC client lifecycle (request_response → on_ws_thread_started → ws_turn_start_params → loop driving =parse_event= against incoming notifications + handling control wire-messages). It just happens to do so over a WebSocket. The natural refactor is either: (a) factor =request_response= / =handle_outcome= / =RpcIds= into a transport-agnostic helper that both =acp_ws.rs= and a new =acp_stdio.rs= runtime can drive, or (b) duplicate the loop in =acp_stdio.rs= and reach for the shared helper later — implementer's call based on how clean the abstraction comes out.

Note: =codex app-server= speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC on its stdio (HAR convention), not LSP-style Content-Length framing. Confirm by spawning it locally — but assume newline-delimited unless evidence otherwise.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] =acp-stdio= mode drives a real JSON-RPC client lifecycle when the harness adapter's =compose_request= returns a =HarnessRequest::Subprocess= (today's path) AND the adapter's =stdio_initial_payload= surface is enough to seed the session:
  - sends an =initialize= request, waits for response,
  - sends =thread/start= with the params from the adapter's session_init shape (or a new adapter method — see "Open implementation choices" below) and routes the result through =adapter.on_ws_thread_started(endpoint, response)= so =CodexAdapter= can record the thread id and emit =Ready=,
  - sends =turn/start= with =adapter.ws_turn_start_params()= and feeds the result through =adapter.on_ws_response("turn/start", value)=,
  - loops reading notifications from stdout (one JSON-RPC value per line) and feeds each through =adapter.parse_event(value)=,
  - dispatches control =WireMessage::JsonRpc { method, params }= writes to stdin (one JSON-RPC envelope per line) when =transition_state= / =babysitter_action= / =release= produce them,
  - detects terminal events (=adapter.terminal_emitted() = true= after =turn/completed= / =thread/closed=) and shuts down cleanly.
- [ ] The "endpoint" parameter for =on_ws_thread_started= is replaced with a transport-neutral identifier (e.g., the path-or-binary the subprocess was spawned as) so the same =CodexAdapter::on_ws_thread_started= works for both acp-ws and acp-stdio without lying about the URL. If renaming the trait param crosses too many call sites, document the carry-over in the brief.
- [ ] A new fixture-style integration test in =crates/orgasmic-drivers/tests/driver_modes.rs= (or a sibling) that pairs an =AcpStdioDriver= against a mocked codex peer (e.g., a child process running a tiny Rust helper or a python one-liner that reads JSON-RPC requests from stdin and writes scripted responses + notifications) and asserts the same envelope shape the existing acp-ws fixture asserts: =Ready { simulated: false, thread_id: ... }= → =TextChunk { Assistant, "hello" }= → =ToolCall { transition_state }= → =RunComplete=. Gate the test on the helper being available; gracefully skip otherwise (mirroring =codex_available()= in =adapters/codex.rs::tests=). Real-binary verification with =codex app-server= itself is allowed but not required (codex CLI may not be on CI). If the helper-process approach is too fiddly, an in-process =tokio::io::DuplexStream= mock that gets handed to a refactored "run_acp_stdio over arbitrary AsyncRead/AsyncWrite" function is also acceptable — implementer's call.
- [ ] Existing tests stay green: =cargo test --workspace= (currently 365), =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings=, =cargo fmt --check=, =git diff --check= all green. MSRV 1.78. Pay attention to the CLAUDE.md MSRV pitfall list: =fs2::FileExt::lock_exclusive=, no =Option::is_none_or=, etc.
- [ ] Live-validate locally if =codex= is on PATH: dispatch this task itself or any subsequent task with =--worker implementer-codex-stdio= (post-merge) and observe a working session: the run reaches =run.created= → emits Ready + at least one TextChunk → terminates with RunComplete or RunFail (whichever codex returns for a small no-op prompt). If codex isn't on PATH, document the constraint in the Evidence section and rely on the mock-peer fixture for correctness.

Don't touch tmux. Don't add UI bits — the TASK-C7ZG5 follow-up (UI agent-chat overlay) is a separate dispatch.

** Description
Closes 3 of 5 TASK-HY0QT reviewer findings (F-1, F-2, F-3). F-4 + F-5 reviewer-deferred (can piggyback if cheap; otherwise ship deferred).

The TASK-HY0QT implementation introduced =run_acp_stdio= as a parallel runtime to =SubprocessStreamJsonDriver=, but in doing so dropped two subprocess-lifecycle properties that TASK-J95T2 specifically went to the trouble of shipping for the cursor-agent / claude-stream-json path:

- *F-1 missing exit synthesis*: =run_acp_stdio= ends the runtime loop and calls =child.wait()= but never invokes =finalize_subprocess_exit= (or an analog). If =codex app-server= dies before emitting =turn/completed= / =thread/closed= — crash, OOM, SIGKILL, network hiccup, whatever — the supervisor sees an open run with no terminal event. This is exactly the failure mode TASK-J95T2's =cursor::distill_subprocess_exit_summary= + synthetic =RunComplete= path was built to prevent on the cursor-agent side.
- *F-2 no kill on channel drop*: When all =AcpStdioControl= senders drop (supervisor crash, early-detach, abrupt session shutdown), =commands.recv()= returns =None= and the runtime breaks WITHOUT calling =child.kill()=. The legacy =SubprocessStreamJsonDriver= treats channel-close as a release signal and kills the child before finalising. Without that, a dropped session can leave a detached =codex app-server= orphan.
- *F-3 control-plane untested*: The new fixture =acp_stdio_codex_jsonrpc_handshake_mock_peer= exercises the read-side handshake (=initialize= → =thread/start= → =Ready= → notification stream → =RunComplete=) but never calls =session.control.release(...)= / =transition_state(...)= / =babysitter_action(...)= to assert that =HarnessControlOutcome.wire_messages= (e.g., codex =turn/interrupt=, =turn/steer=) get serialised to stdin as JSON-RPC envelopes. This was one of the three stacked failures the TASK-HY0QT brief identified pre-merge (failure mode B: wire-message control plane was silent); the write path is implemented via shared =handle_outcome= but has no regression test on the stdio side.

Reviewer report at =/tmp/orgasmic-codex/task-077-review-report.md=.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-1 — port TASK-J95T2 exit synthesis into run_acp_stdio*: After the main =select!= loop in =run_acp_stdio= exits (stdout EOF, transport error, channel close), wire the equivalent of =SubprocessStreamJsonDriver::finalize_subprocess_exit= behaviour: if =adapter.terminal_emitted()= is false AND assistant text can be distilled (track distillation by recording =DriverEvent::TextChunk= emissions through the loop like =SubprocessExitSummary::record= does), call =adapter.emit_run_complete_once(&events, Some(summary)).await= when exit status is success; otherwise emit a fatal =DriverError= with the exit status. Use the existing =cursor::distill_subprocess_exit_summary= for the distillation (or wrap it in a transport-neutral helper if the symbol name is misleading — implementer's call).
- [ ] *F-2 — kill child on channel drop*: When =commands.recv()= returns =None= in the main loop, set a =released= flag, call =child.kill().await=, then fall through to the same exit-synthesis path as F-1. Pattern matches =SubprocessStreamJsonDriver= lines 340-360.
- [ ] *F-3 — mock-peer control-plane test*: Extend =acp_stdio_codex_jsonrpc_handshake_mock_peer= (or add a sibling test) where the mock peer scripts a response to a =turn/interrupt= (or any other JSON-RPC method codex's adapter emits via =wire_messages=) on stdin, the test calls =session.control.release("done").await=, and asserts the method appears on the peer's stdin before =RunComplete= is emitted. If the helper-process shell approach is too brittle for stdin-reading, prefer the in-process =tokio::io::DuplexStream= mock mentioned in the TASK-HY0QT brief.
- [ ] (Optional, piggyback if cheap) *F-4 — assert ToolCall ordering + intervening notifications in the stdio fixture*: extend the mock peer to emit an =item/tool/call= or similar before =turn/completed=, OR send a notification between =thread/start= request and response, and assert the events arrive in the expected order through the supervisor. WS-side coverage already exists in =codex_turn_start_terminal_notification_does_not_emit_followup_error=.
- [ ] (Optional, piggyback if cheap) *F-5 — eliminate double-call of stdio_session_init*: =compose_stdio_request= probes =stdio_session_init(...).is_ok()= to choose the JSON-RPC upgrade path; =uses_jsonrpc_stdio= calls the same method again. Refactor to a single call — e.g., have =compose_stdio_request= return =(HarnessRequest, Option<Value>)= or stash the init value on the compose adapter. Idempotent today for =CodexAdapter= but easy to diverge with a future adapter.
- [ ] =cargo test --workspace + clippy + fmt + diff= all green. MSRV 1.78. Pay attention to the CLAUDE.md MSRV pitfalls (=fs2::FileExt::lock_exclusive=, no =Option::is_none_or=, etc).

** Description
Surface the existing manager-popover chat transcript from inside the task drawer so the user can click the "current agent" badge on a task heading and watch the running agent's session stream in real time, without leaving the task UI. This was the user-stated UX motivation for closing TASK-HY0QT: "user can via task dialog (ui) click the current agent status to open the chat with the running agent and in real time monitor the session via the same chat interface as manager uses in har app for acp driver type".

This dispatch is also a deliberate live-codex dogfood of TASK-HY0QT: the dispatch itself routes via =--worker implementer-codex-stdio= (codex CLI v0.133.0 on PATH at =~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.4.1/bin/codex=, =acp-stdio= driver landed in =cbdf079= and hardened in =6ecc820=). A clean run with =Ready= → ≥1 =TextChunk= → =RunComplete= envelopes in the session JSONL plus actual code landing = TASK-HY0QT live-validated. If the handshake stalls or the babysitter detects a stall, manager rolls back via the TASK-FB8CK.5 spawn-fail path and re-dispatches via =implementer-cursor=.

*Heavy lifting is already done.* The chat component =ui/src/components/manager/ManagerChatTranscript.tsx= is driver-agnostic: it takes ={ runId, initialSource? }=, calls =fetchRun(runId)= for the session source, subscribes to the daemon's =/ws?topic=run= event stream via =useEventStream=, parses the JSONL into role-tagged bubbles, and handles =text= / =tool_call= / =run_fail= / =driver_error= / lifecycle / note envelopes (=ManagerChatTranscript.tsx:58-128=). It is currently used from =ManagerWorkbench.tsx:167= and =ManagerPopover.tsx:136=. The remaining work is plumbing it into =TaskDialog.tsx=.

*Existing surfaces (read these first):*
- =ui/src/components/TaskDialog.tsx:178-186= — the existing Owner badge. This is the click target. Today it just renders =task.owner= as a static badge.
- =ui/src/components/manager/ManagerChatTranscript.tsx:142-188= — the component to reuse. No changes required to its surface unless this task needs a small prop addition (see Acceptance Criteria F-2).
- =ui/src/lib/types.ts:44-56= — =TaskSummary= type. Does NOT currently carry =run_id=. This needs to be plumbed.
- =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs::apply_task_owners= (around line 193, 304, 565) — the function that populates =task.owner= from =supervisor.runs=. It already has the run in hand; just needs to attach =run_id= to the returned summary.
- =ui/src/components/ui/sheet.tsx= — shadcn Sheet primitive available.
- =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/ws.rs= — =GET /ws?topic=run= is the wire the chat already subscribes to (per =ManagerChatTranscript= imports). Should not need changes.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-1 — plumb =run_id= into =TaskSummary= when an agent is active.* Daemon side: extend =apply_task_owners= (and the =TaskSummary= struct in =orgasmic-core= if that's where it lives) so that when a task has =owner = "agent.*"= (i.e., a run is currently leased to it), the matching =supervisor.runs= entry's =run_id= is attached to the returned summary. Default null when no active run. UI side: add =run_id?: string | null= to =TaskSummary= in =ui/src/lib/types.ts:44=. No breaking changes to any other consumer.

- [ ] *F-2 — click-to-open chat overlay from the Owner badge.* In =TaskDialog.tsx=, when =task.owner= starts with =agent.= AND =task.run_id= is present, the Owner badge (currently lines 178-186) becomes a button (or wrap in =<button>=). Clicking it opens a shadcn =Sheet= sliding from the right (=side="right"=, narrow-medium width, e.g. =sm:max-w-md= or =sm:max-w-lg=). Sheet content: =<ManagerChatTranscript runId={task.run_id} />=. Sheet header: terse run identifier (task ID + short run_id slug + a small lucide icon, e.g. =MessageSquare=). Sheet should be dismissible via Esc and the standard shadcn close button; the underlying TaskDialog stays mounted behind it (use Sheet, not Dialog-inside-Dialog).

  When =task.owner = "human"= or =task.run_id= is null, the Owner badge stays as today (non-interactive). Do NOT gate on driver type — the chat component handles any driver's session JSONL envelopes; restricting to acp-stdio / acp-ws would shrink the feature unnecessarily and the user's spec calls out ACP as the primary motivator but not the only valid case.

- [ ] *F-3 — accessibility + UX polish.* The clickable Owner badge must have an accessible label (e.g., =aria-label={`View live agent chat for ${task.id}`}=) and a tooltip/affordance hint that it's clickable (e.g., subtle =cursor-pointer= + =hover:ring-1 hover:ring-ring/40= or similar — match the existing dialog's interactive-element styling). Keyboard: Enter / Space opens the Sheet. Focus management: opening the Sheet moves focus into it; closing returns focus to the Owner badge.

- [ ] *F-4 — empty state and error state.* =ManagerChatTranscript= already renders "No transcript events for this run yet." when source is empty, and a destructive banner on fetch error. If the run finishes while the Sheet is open, the transcript should still update via the WS event stream (which it does by design — no action needed; just verify). If =fetchRun(run_id)= returns 404 (run completed and was GC'd), the destructive banner is acceptable but the Sheet should remain dismissible.

- [ ] *F-5 — no regressions in existing manager-popover usage.* =ManagerWorkbench.tsx:167= and =ManagerPopover.tsx:136= must continue to work unchanged. If F-2 needs a prop addition to =ManagerChatTranscript= (e.g., a header slot), default it so existing call sites compile.

MSRV 1.78 — pay attention to the CLAUDE.md MSRV pitfall list (=fs2::FileExt::lock_exclusive=, no =Option::is_none_or= etc.). UI: =cd ui && npm run typecheck && npm run build= clean (no new TypeScript errors). No lint warnings introduced by the new code (=npm run lint= if defined).

- [ ] *Live verification* (optional but encouraged — manager will dogfood it post-merge): after the daemon is rebuilt + restarted with this change, dispatch any small task via =--worker implementer-codex-stdio= (or =implementer-cursor=, doesn't matter — the UI is driver-agnostic), open the task in the UI's task drawer, click the Owner badge while the run is active, observe the live chat transcript update. If this is left to the manager post-merge, document the constraint in the Evidence section.

** Description
Live-codex dogfood of TASK-HY0QT during the TASK-C7ZG5 dispatch surfaced two real gaps in the acp-stdio path that the mock-peer fixture didn't exercise:

1. *Codex's =require_escalated= sandbox-approval protocol is unhandled.* When codex sends an =exec_approval_request= / =apply_patch_approval_request= JSON-RPC notification (e.g., for a =cargo test --workspace= that wants to bind localhost sockets), the orgasmic acp-stdio driver has zero code path to respond. Codex sits indefinitely waiting for a grant that never comes. Discovered live during TASK-C7ZG5 implementer dispatch =run-20260526T072438-...= which stalled at =seq=350-351= with no follow-up events for ~23 minutes. =grep approval|sandbox|escalat= across =acp_stdio.rs= / =acp_ws.rs= / =jsonrpc.rs= / =adapters/codex.rs= returns zero matches — the acp-ws path will hit the same issue when someone runs codex over it.

2. *Babysitter-stall-detector is not spawned for acp-stdio runs.* The =implementer-codex-stdio= worker spec declares =:BABYSITTER_WORKER: babysitter-stall-detector= but no =<run_id>.babysitter.jsonl= file was ever created during the TASK-C7ZG5 codex dispatch — meaning the babysitter wasn't invoked. The supervisor wires babysitters into the subprocess-stream-json (cursor) path but apparently not the acp-stdio path.

User design call (this session, 2026-05-26): driver-primary detection + auto-approval per an allowlist; babysitter as fallback for residual stall modes. Allowlist with task-level override (worker spec defines defaults; task heading can override).

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-1 SandboxAllowlist struct.* New =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/sandbox.rs= module exporting =SandboxAllowlist { allow_exec: bool, allow_patch: bool, allow_network: bool, allow_writes_outside_cwd: bool }= plus =Default= trait returning all-true (trust-all baseline matches the headless dispatch model). Plus a resolution helper =fn resolve(task: Option<&SandboxAllowlist>, worker: Option<&SandboxAllowlist>) -> SandboxAllowlist= that returns task > worker > default.
- [ ] *F-2 worker-spec property.* =shipped/workers/implementer-codex-stdio.org=, =reviewer-codex-stdio.org=, and =implementer-codex-appserver.org= gain a =:SANDBOX_PERMISSIONS:= property serialised as a CSV-of-key=value pairs (=allow_exec=true,allow_patch=true,allow_network=true,allow_writes_outside_cwd=true= as the worker-level default). Worker loader in =crates/orgasmic-core/= parses it into =SandboxAllowlist=.
- [ ] *F-3 task heading override.* Task heading parser in =crates/orgasmic-core/src/sprint.rs= (or wherever task properties are parsed) accepts an optional =:SANDBOX_PERMISSIONS:= property with the same CSV format. Tested with a unit test that loads a task heading with override + asserts =resolve()= picks task > worker.
- [ ] *F-4 HarnessEventAdapter::try_handle_approval.* New trait method on =HarnessEventAdapter=: =async fn try_handle_approval(&mut self, method: &str, params: &Value, allowlist: &SandboxAllowlist) -> Option<ApprovalResponse>= where =ApprovalResponse = Approved | Denied=. Default impl returns None. =CodexAdapter= implements it to recognize codex's approval-request methods (=exec_approval_request=, =apply_patch_approval_request=; check codex JSON-RPC protocol docs / source for exact names — there may be others like file-write or network ones) and match against allowlist; non-codex adapters keep the None default.

** Description
Surfaced live during the TASK-CNZGR.1 first dispatch attempt (session 2026-05-25): cursor-agent crashed with SIGKILL before doing real work, leaving a session with =acquire= + =ready= + =driver_error= envelopes. TASK-J95T2's early-exit classifier =session_is_early_exit_no_work= (=crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs:1137=) returned =false= because =session_has_work_envelope= (line 1112) counts ANY non-ready =DriverEvent= as "work" — including =driver_error=. So auto-release didn't fire. Direct =POST /runs/.../release= returned =active run= error; required full daemon restart to clear.

Cause: =session_has_work_envelope= treats all =driver_event type=!=ready= as work envelopes. =driver_error= envelopes are terminal failures (the driver itself died / errored before doing useful work) and should not count as "work received".

Fix shape (small, ~10-30 LOC):
1. Either exclude =driver_error= from =session_has_work_envelope= so the early-exit classifier triggers on =acquire + ready + driver_error= sessions, OR
2. Add =driver_error= to =session_has_terminal_event= (line 1125) so the classifier short-circuits earlier in the chain.

Option 1 is more surgical (no behavior change when there ARE work envelopes alongside driver_error; auto-release still fires when only acquire+ready+driver_error happened). Option 2 is broader (treats driver_error as terminal everywhere, which may have wider blast radius if other code checks =session_has_terminal_event=). Implementer's call.

The early-exit classifier should then drive the standard run.failed path with the driver_error's error message as the failure reason.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-1 driver_error excluded from "work" envelopes* OR *promoted to terminal*: change in =session_has_work_envelope= or =session_has_terminal_event= per implementer choice. Comment explaining the choice.
- [ ] *F-2 unit test*: synthesize a =[acquire, ready, driver_error]= envelope sequence in =supervisor.rs= tests. Assert =session_is_early_exit_no_work= returns =true= (so the classifier triggers auto-release). Mirrors the live TASK-CNZGR.1 SIGKILL scenario.
- [ ] *F-3 the run actually transitions to failed* (not stuck active) when the classifier triggers on a driver_error session. If there's an existing higher-level supervisor test asserting this path, extend it; if not, add a focused unit test.
- [ ] All gates green: =cargo test --workspace=, =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings=, =cargo fmt --check=, =git diff --check=. MSRV 1.78.

** Description
Deferred-MEDIUM finding from TASK-KFGDS reviewer pass: when the implementer run terminates, the spawned babysitter should also release. Currently =RunRecord= (=crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs:148-162=) stores a =babysitter_target: Option<String>= field that's set on BABYSITTER runs (pointing back at their parent implementer run_id) but NOT a companion =babysitter_run_id= on IMPLEMENTER runs. So when the implementer's =release()= fires (=supervisor.rs:814=), the supervisor doesn't know which babysitter run is its companion and the babysitter run continues writing to its .babysitter.jsonl indefinitely.

This was a known gap on the original cursor/subprocess-stream-json path too; TASK-KFGDS.1's babysitter spawn just extended the pattern to acp-stdio without fixing the cascade-release. With babysitters now spawning on every CLI dispatch (post-TASK-KFGDS.1), orphan babysitter runs accumulate on every clean implementer.done. Worth fixing.

Fix shape (small, ~30-60 LOC):
1. Add =babysitter_run_id: Option<String>= to =RunRecord= (set when supervisor auto-spawns the babysitter after implementer acquire).
2. In =Supervisor::release= when =rec.kind == RunKind::Implementer= AND =rec.babysitter_run_id.is_some()=, cascade-release the babysitter via the same release path.
3. Regression test: spawn implementer + auto-babysitter; release implementer; assert babysitter run is also released (= no longer in supervisor.runs).

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *F-1 RunRecord companion field*: add =babysitter_run_id: Option<String>= to =RunRecord=. Set it at babysitter auto-spawn site (search for where =AcquireRequest.babysitter: Some(...)= triggers the babysitter spawn — that's where the new babysitter run gets its run_id; record it on the parent implementer's RunRecord).
- [ ] *F-2 cascade release*: extend =Supervisor::release= so that when an Implementer run releases AND has a non-null =babysitter_run_id=, it also calls release on the babysitter run (with a reason like ="cascade from implementer <run_id>"=). Order: release implementer first, then babysitter (avoid the babysitter writing a "lost parent" event mid-cascade). Idempotency: if the babysitter is already released (e.g., user manually released), don't error.
- [ ] *F-3 regression test*: in =supervisor.rs= tests, synthesize an implementer acquire with =babysitter: Some(BabysitterAutoSpawn { ... })=. Assert that AFTER spawn, =supervisor.runs= contains both runs AND the implementer's RunRecord has =babysitter_run_id == Some(<bs run id>)=. Then call =release()= on the implementer. Assert: (a) implementer is released, (b) babysitter is also released (gone from =supervisor.runs= OR has =terminal_outcome.is_some()=).
- [ ] All gates green: =cargo test --workspace=, =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings=, =cargo fmt --check=, =git diff --check=. MSRV 1.78.

** Notes
- *NOT* =:FIX_SUBTASK: t= — full IMPLEMENT → REVIEW → DONE lifecycle. Small scope but earns a proper reviewer pass.

- *Out-of-scope*: don't restructure RunKind / RunRecord beyond adding the field. Don't change the babysitter spawn LOGIC; just track the resulting run_id. Don't touch =acp_stdio.rs= or driver code.

** Description
TASK-FWBYB shipped =orgasmic doctor=' staleness check (binary mtime vs daemon-code merge SHA + uptime; multi-line =Finding::Warn=). TASK-FWBYB.1 hardened it (=DaemonLiveness= enum + exactly-one liveness signal when daemon not-Running). The check is real, validated end-to-end, and silent when daemon is fresh.

Open follow-up (cited in goal.org and TASK-FWBYB notes): users running their normal =orgasmic status= command don't see the staleness warning — only =orgasmic doctor= surfaces it. =orgasmic status= is the more common liveness check (one-line output: boot_id + uptime + projects + parse_errors + tx count). Surfacing the staleness Warn there means users notice "you're running a stale daemon binary" without needing to remember to run doctor.

Fix shape (small, ~30-100 LOC):
1. =crates/orgasmic-cli/src/status.rs= currently renders the daemon-status JSON envelope from =/daemon/status= (bearer-authed via =DaemonClient=).
2. After rendering the normal status output, call into =doctor.rs='s existing =check_daemon_staleness= (or equivalent function — read =doctor.rs= for the exact name) using the same =SystemTime::now()= + git-log path as TASK-FWBYB.1. If the check returns =Finding::Warn=, render it as a trailing block (e.g., =WARN: daemon binary appears stale: <message>=).
3. Skip the staleness check entirely if =DaemonLiveness= is not =Running= (= same TASK-FWBYB.1 F-1 invariant: don't double-warn when daemon is down).
4. New integration test in =crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/= (or wherever status has tests) that seeds a tempdir git repo + stale binary mtime + running daemon fixture and asserts =orgasmic status= output contains the WARN line.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] *AC-1 status emits staleness Warn when daemon is Running AND check fires*: =orgasmic status= output includes a trailing =WARN: ...= block matching the same format =orgasmic doctor= uses, when the daemon-code-since-binary-mtime check fires. Format: multi-line Warn (binary path + most-recent merge SHA + commits-since-boot count), same as doctor.
- [ ] *AC-2 status is silent when daemon is fresh*: =orgasmic status= does NOT emit the WARN block when binary mtime is newer than all daemon-code merges since boot. No extra noise on the happy path.
- [ ] *AC-3 status skips check when daemon not-Running*: same =DaemonLiveness::Running= gate as TASK-FWBYB.1 F-1. When daemon is unreachable / unauthorized, the existing status error path stays untouched; do NOT add a staleness check on top of it (no double-warn).
- [ ] *AC-4 integration test*: =cargo test -p orgasmic-cli= covers (i) status-with-stale-binary outputs WARN, (ii) status-with-fresh-binary does NOT, (iii) status-with-daemon-down does NOT call the staleness check. Reuse the test seeds from TASK-FWBYB.1 if they're in a shared test-helper module; otherwise duplicate the tempdir-git fixture pattern.
- [ ] *AC-5 no helper duplication*: do NOT copy-paste the doctor staleness logic into status.rs. Extract =check_daemon_staleness= (or rename if private) to be callable from both =doctor.rs= and =status.rs=. If it currently lives in =doctor.rs= as a private fn, lift it to =pub(crate)= or move to a shared module under =crates/orgasmic-cli/src/=. Choose the minimum-disruption refactor.
- [ ] All gates green: =cargo test --workspace=, =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings=, =cargo fmt --check=, =git diff --check=. MSRV 1.78. No new deps.

** Description
Validate =implementer-claude-tmux= end-to-end on real =claude= TUI and harden any gaps surfaced. Today the worker spec at =shipped/workers/implementer-claude-tmux.org= is boilerplate, and =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/tmux.rs= has scaffolding-grade fixtures (hard-coded =agent_template_id: "tmux-tui-default"= at lines 396/646; =inert= gate at line 89 mirrors the simulated-mode pattern that bit TASK-EXFTV). This driver has never been dogfooded against a real claude TUI dispatch.

Pattern reference: the sibling HAR app (=../har/=) drives claude interactively through tmux with a compose surface below the pane — port that pattern for orgasmic's worker side first (TASK-GMR53 handles the manager side).

Driver flow under test (autonomous worker):
1. =acquire= → =spawn_tmux_session= creates =tmux new-session -d -s orgasmic-claude-<run_id>=.
2. Send the compiled prompt bundle to the pane (=tmux send-keys -t <session> 'claude' Enter; sleep; tmux send-keys -t <session> '<prompt>' Enter=).
3. Pane output captured as =DriverEvent::TextChunk= envelopes via periodic =tmux capture-pane -p=.
4. Terminal signal: claude TUI emits a recognizable end-of-turn marker (= "esc to interrupt" prompt disappearing, or a sentinel the brief asks claude to echo). Driver converts to =RunComplete=.
5. Cleanup: =tmux kill-session -t <session>= on release.

Suspected gaps to investigate + close (the live dogfood will surface the actual list):
- =inert= gate over-fires (same shape as TASK-EXFTV claude-acp endpoint-gate bug).
- =agent_template_id= hard-coding ignores the worker's =:DEFAULT_MODEL:= / =:DEFAULT_EFFORT:= properties.
- No model/effort plumbing: claude TUI needs =--model= flag, but the driver doesn't pass it.
- Terminal detection heuristic (end-of-turn marker) may not exist yet — needs design.
- Worker spec is boilerplate: add =:DEFAULT_MODEL: claude-sonnet-4-6=, =:DEFAULT_EFFORT: high=, real persona body, dispatch-flow docs.

Per dec_X6Q0S refinement, =WRITES= is for append/replace file or projection content; these are in-memory broadcast bus publishes (=events.rs::publish=) that the WebSocket bridge (=ws.rs=) consumes. Should be =CALLS= (to a first-class event-bus/broadcaster leaf if one exists, or directly).

Fixes:
1. Remove the =arch_A53QX.4 -> file:sessions SPAWNS= edge. Replace with =WRITES= to file:sessions (the supervisor writes session JSONL).
2. Add a SPAWNS edge from the manager-tick path leaf (=arch_R3EPE.1= or similar) → =arch_A53QX.1= (supervisor acquire). If supervisor.acquire's spawn role is on a different leaf, route the edge there.
3. Retag the three =WRITES -> socket:events= edges as =CALLS= to the event-bus leaf if =arch_C87Z9= already has one (likely =arch_C87Z9.2 WebSocket event broadcaster=), OR as =CALLS= directly to the broadcaster if no separate event-bus leaf exists.

** Description
TASK-GMR53 reviewer F-2 MEDIUM: the daemon's real path may send either an append-only delta or the entire current capture as a plain text frame, but the UI always writes every text frame as append-only terminal data. For full-screen TUI redraws, scrollback truncation, clears, or any non-prefix pane change, the server falls back to sending a full capture and the client appends that full screen below the previous screen — turning the manager pane into repeated snapshots rather than a live terminal view.

Fix: make the WS frame contract explicit. Either structured JSON frames =\{type: 'delta' | 'full', text\}= (binary text frames stay plain text for the delta case, JSON for full), OR adopt a real PTY-attach stream (xterm.js + pty bytes through). Lighter-touch path: =\{type, text\}= JSON frames; client clears/homes xterm on =full= before writing.

** Description
TASK-HJBXF live-dogfood found: =claude= TUI takes ~2-5s to render its banner + input field after =tmux new-session= spawns it. The driver's current code calls =paste_text_into_pane= immediately after =spawn_tmux_session= returns, which races claude's startup → prompt enters the void → claude sits at empty cursor forever.

Two viable fixes:
1. *Wait-for-input-prompt heuristic*: capture-pane periodically (~250ms) after spawn; detect claude's prompt indicator (=❯ = at the start of a line, or => = for older claude versions) → only then paste. Add ~10s timeout fallback (if no prompt detected, log warning + paste anyway).
2. *Sleep-after-spawn*: simpler but less robust — =sleep 3-5s= after spawn before paste. Works for claude today but brittle if claude TUI startup gets slower or faster.

Reference HAR app (=../har/=) likely solves this — read =../har/crates/har-drivers/src/modes/tmux.rs= or equivalent for the proven pattern.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Driver waits for claude's input field to be ready before pasting prompt.
- [ ] If no input field detected after timeout (~10s default), log warning + paste anyway (don't block forever).
- [ ] Inline test: mock-peer that takes >1s to render its prompt; driver still successfully pastes.
- [ ] Real-wire smoke test (gated on =which tmux && which claude=) confirms the fix.
- [ ] All gates green.

** Evidence
- *Implementer pass merged as =823be91= (codex =dae58c3=, ~18 min wall, clean codex dispatch — no rescue needed for the codex side).* +164/-1 LOC across 2 files. New helper =wait_for_input_ready(session, timeout)= polls =capture_pane= every 250ms until prompt indicator (line starting with =❯= or => = followed by whitespace) appears OR =DriverError::InputNotReady(timeout)= fires. Acquire path calls it ONLY when =spawn_plan.command == "claude"=. On timeout, logs warning + pastes anyway. Real-world detail caught by codex: claude v2.1.153 uses NBSP (U+00A0) after =❯=, not ASCII space → detection uses generic =char::is_whitespace=. Inline tests: =wait_for_input_ready_returns_ok_when_mock_pane_has_prompt= + =wait_for_input_ready_returns_input_not_ready_on_timeout= + =pane_has_input_prompt_detects_claude_indicators= + =real_claude_input_ready_smoke= (gated on which tmux + claude). Configurable knob =TmuxTuiConfig.input_ready_timeout= default 10s.
- *Manager 2-line follow-up patch (this commit) restores 800ms settle-sleep for NON-claude commands.* Codex's diff inadvertently dropped the existing =tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(800)).await= that gated the paste path for the entire acquire loop, replacing it with a claude-only =wait_for_input_ready= branch. =real_tmux_prompt_bundle_is_consumed= (which uses =cat= as a mock TUI without a =❯= prompt) became flaky → race-dependent ordering between Ready emission and TextChunk emission from cat's instant stdout echo. Fix: when =command != "claude"=, sleep 800ms before paste (mirrors pre-TASK-HJBXF.1 behavior). 57/57 driver lib tests pass post-patch.
- *Gates on merged main =823be91= + manager patch:* cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers --lib (57 passed) ✓; cargo test --workspace ✓ (1 failure pre-patch — see manager note); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings ✓; cargo fmt --check ✓; git diff --check ✓.
- *Lesson learned*: =cargo test 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "exit: $?"= captures tail's exit code, NOT cargo's. Use =set -o pipefail= or check =${PIPESTATUS[0]}= for the leftmost-pipe exit code in future gate runs. Logged for housekeeping.
- *Unblocks TASK-HJBXF.2* (second live-dogfood); next manager action.

** Description
Real-tmux integration tests (=real_tmux_prompt_bundle_is_consumed=, =real_tmux_session_lifecycle=, etc.) leave orphan tmux sessions named =orgasmic-run-prompt-real-<uuid>= after the test completes. The test calls =s.control.release("done")= but evidently the release path doesn't fully kill the tmux session under test isolation, OR the test ends before async cleanup completes.

Manager housekeeping during the TASK-HJBXF.2 dogfood found 3 such orphans accumulated from various test runs.

Fix: either (a) ensure =DriverSession::Drop= or explicit cleanup tears down the tmux session synchronously, or (b) use =std::process::Command::new("tmux").args(["kill-session", "-t", session_name])= as a final guard in each test's cleanup block.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Real-tmux tests don't leave orphan sessions after =cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers --lib modes::tmux= run.
- [x] Mock-peer + non-tmux tests unaffected.
- [x] All gates green.

** Evidence
- *Date*: [2026-06-05 Fri].
- *Fix shape*: added a =SessionGuard(String)= Drop-guard struct to the tmux test module that calls the existing =kill_tmux_session_sync= on drop. Each real-tmux test that spawns a session now binds =let _guard = SessionGuard(tmux_session_name(&s.identity));= (or the explicit session name for =real_claude_input_ready_smoke=) immediately after spawn — so the session is killed unconditionally on success, assert-failure unwind, or panic. Tests covered: =real_tmux_session_lifecycle=, =real_claude_input_ready_smoke=, =real_tmux_eot_marker_emits_run_complete=, =real_tmux_early_exit_before_eot_is_failure=, =real_tmux_prompt_bundle_is_consumed= (the named orphan source), =real_tmux_attach_proves_existing_session=. =real_tmux_control_drop_without_release_kills_session= left unguarded by design (it asserts the driver's own Drop cleanup). =kill-session= is a no-op when the session already exited.
- *Gates*: =cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers= EXIT=0 (all real_tmux tests RAN — tmux was on PATH — and passed); =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= EXIT=0; =cargo fmt --check= EXIT=0; =git diff --check= EXIT=0.
- *Orphan proof*: post-run =pgrep -fl "worker-server|sleep 3600"= → none; =tmux ls= shows no leftover =orgasmic-test=/=run-real=/=run-prompt-real=/=run-attach=/=run-mock-eot=/=run-early-exit=/=input-ready= sessions (only the pre-existing daemon session + an unrelated June-3 run session remain).

** Description
TASK-QSBDB reviewer F-1 HIGH security: =command_has_shell_control= at =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/cursor.rs:993= rejects =;=, =|=, =&=, newlines, backticks, =$(=, but does NOT reject shell redirection (=<=, =>=) or process substitution. Commands like =git -C <worktree> diff >/etc/orgasmic-leak= or =grep --path <worktree> pattern < /etc/passwd= pass the first-token + path checks while the shell performs I/O OUTSIDE the worktree before running the allowed binary.

This violates the TASK-QSBDB negative-policy guarantee that cursor still cannot read arbitrary host paths or write outside the write_scope.

- [ ] Negative test in driver_modes.rs asserting redirection on allowed commands is blocked.
- [ ] All gates green.

** Description

Since =candidate_paths= treats keys like =cwd= as path candidates, a tool call with an UNSAFE target path PLUS a SAFE =cwd= still passes the policy.

Separately, =path_is_under= does lexical normalization only (no =fs::canonicalize=), so symlinks under the worktree or =/tmp/orgasmic-codex= resolve to arbitrary host paths while still passing the prefix check.

- [ ] Negative tests: unsafe target + safe cwd; symlink traversal under allowed roots.
- [ ] All gates green.

** Description
The CLI dispatcher (=crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs=) hard-codes =DispatchKind= to =Implementer | Reviewer=. TASK-EZ0ST shipped the architector persona, agent template, prompt template, and convention bundle — but the dispatch wiring was never extended. As a result =orgasmic manager dispatch --kind architector ...= fails clap validation, and TASK-ENXWA (first real architector run) cannot be dispatched cleanly.

Add an =Architector= variant to =DispatchKind= and thread it through every branching site so an architector dispatch behaves correctly end-to-end (worktree path, branch name, lifecycle stage transitions, dispatch_started tx KIND field, close tx type, dispatchable-stage gate).

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] =DispatchKind= enum gains =Architector= variant with =as_str() -> "architector"=.
- [ ] =default_worktree(task, Architector)= returns =/tmp/orgasmic-worktrees/<slug>-arch= (or similar non-colliding path; must differ from both implementer and reviewer defaults).
- [ ] =default_branch(task, Architector)= returns =<slug>-arch=.
- [ ] =lifecycle_stage_for_kind(Architector)= maps to a sensible architector stage. Two acceptable conventions: (a) re-use =LifecycleStage::Implement= since architector authors content same as implementer just on different files, OR (b) introduce a new =LifecycleStage= variant if the existing state-machine vocabulary supports it. Implementer's choice — justify in the PR.
- [ ] Close-tx-type mapping in =close_tx_type_for_kind=: =Architector= -> =architector.done=.
- [ ] =dispatchable_stage(Architector, stage)= mirrors implementer (BACKLOG or current architector-stage). Document the gate inline.
- [ ] Sprint state transitions: dispatch flips BACKLOG -> architector-stage (whatever choice was made above); close-done flips -> DONE.
- [ ] Existing dispatch CLI tests pass + at least one new test covers the architector path (worktree path, branch, kind round-trip).
- [ ] =cargo test -p orgasmic-cli= green; =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= clean; =cargo fmt --check= clean; MSRV 1.78.
- [ ] No changes to daemon supervisor or codex worker code — architector dispatch must work via the existing =--worker architector= path with the agent template loaded by =shipped/agent-templates/architector.org= (already shipped via TASK-EZ0ST).

** Notes
- *Tiny surface*: ~7 match-arm sites in =crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs= (enum, as_str, lifecycle stage map at ~L1118, close-tx-type map at ~L803, sprint-state transition map at ~L1135 + ~L1140, dispatchable-stage gate at ~L1290, default_worktree at ~L1374, default_branch at ~L1384). Plus tests.

- *Out of scope*: griller/planner DispatchKind variants (file separately if needed); architector persona changes; architecture.org content changes.
