* DONE TASK-RCP69 Pre-apply raw-body escape mode: persisting untrusted text (logs, stderr) must be the easy path, not a guard bounce :daemon:core:api:dx:hardening:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID:               TASK-RCP69
:PRIORITY:         P3
:WORKER:           implementer-cursor
:WRITE_SCOPE:      crates/orgasmic-core/src/org.rs crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/
:READ_SCOPE:       crates/orgasmic-core/src/org.rs crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/body_write_guard.rs
:TEST_CMD:         cargo test -p orgasmic-core -p orgasmic-daemon
:END:

** Description
From the round-4 architecture critique §2 (kernel adopted, framing rejected).
The TASK-HC7PW/TASK-HC7PW.1 guard fails closed on phantom-heading payloads: a body
write containing a column-0 =* line= bounces with =BodyHeadingInjection=.
Correct as the invariant — but it leaves no convenient path for the
legitimate case the critic names: persisting raw untrusted text (a worker's
stderr, a crash dump, a pasted log) whose lines happen to start with =*= or
=#+=. Today every caller must know to wrap/escape by hand or the write
bounces; the safe path should be the easy path.

Add an opt-in raw-content mode at the body-write API boundary (e.g.
=body_format: raw= on the body-edit ops): the daemon wraps the payload in
=#+begin_example ... #+end_example= and applies org comma-escaping to
embedded =*=/=#+= lines BEFORE splicing, so the payload round-trips
losslessly as verbatim content and can never alter structure.

The structural-invariance guard stays exactly as is. The critic proposed
pre-apply escaping INSTEAD of the post-apply check — rejected: silently
transforming default writes would mask genuine injection bugs and surprise
callers. Escaping is a convenience callers opt into for designated raw
content; the fail-closed guard remains the gate behind it.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Raw mode: payload with column-0 =* X= / =#+end_example= lines is
  accepted, wrapped, comma-escaped, round-trips byte-stable, and re-parses
  with zero structural change (guard still passes).
- [ ] Adversarial content cannot escape the wrapper (a payload containing its
  own =#+end_example= line is escaped, not interpreted as the block end).
- [ ] Default mode unchanged: unescaped phantom-heading payload still bounces
  with =BodyHeadingInjection= (existing body_write_guard suite green).

** Description
Operator direction [2026-06-11]: assume parallel work by several devs on the
same repo — different modules, WRITE_SCOPEs never overlap, but each dev runs
their own daemon on their own clone and =.orgasmic/= syncs through git. That
is multi-master: dec_SSJVD's revisit trigger ("the day two daemons must merge
graphs") fires the day a second dev joins, which for a coordination tool is
the adoption path, not an edge case. Per-clone sequencing (TASK-GBT5W) cannot
see the other clone's allocations — both daemons will hand out the same next
TASK-NNN. Same-file appends at least conflict textually at merge; a
sprint.org-vs-backlog.org pair merges SILENTLY → duplicate ID → ambiguous
DEPENDS_ON / dispatch / lifecycle targets. And every week of adoption embeds
more TASK-NNN references in prose and commit messages — re-keying later is
exactly the rewrite-every-reference cost conceded in the round-4 critique.
Decide now, while it is cheap.

Design the identity scheme and deliver the ADR draft. Leading option
(manager assessment — validate, don't rubber-stamp):
- *Stable key*: ULID per task in the property drawer (=:UID:= or a
  repurposed =:ID:=), generated at filing, collision-proof with zero
  coordination. Invisible in prose; costs one drawer line; anchors
  mechanical re-aliasing and disambiguates if the alias layer is ever
  violated.
- *Readable alias (the human surface)*: OPERATOR CONSTRAINT [2026-06-11]:
  NO checked-in actor registry — the =.orgasmic/actors.org= roster concept
  is rejected. No registration ceremony, no people-administration file in
  repo state; identity must ride what git already has, or not exist at
  all. Two candidate shapes remain; the ADR weighs them:
  1. /Plain TASK-NNN + merge-time repair/ (doctrine-consistent with
     dec_MK7AH detect-and-reconcile): each clone allocates max+1 locally;
     cross-clone duplicates are RARE (only filings concurrent between
     syncs), detection is certain (post-pull doctor lint over alias
     uniqueness), repair is mechanical (the ULID anchors each heading; the
     younger filing is renumbered and all in-repo references — DEPENDS_ON,
     org-file prose — rewritten in the same repair commit). Cost: an ID
     can change shortly after filing, inside a short window where few
     external references exist. Zero onboarding friction; IDs stay short.
  2. /Derived namespace, roster-less/: actor slug derived from existing
     git identity (=user.email= local-part, optionally +2-char hash) —
     nothing registered anywhere. Prevents instead of repairs; cost:
     longer IDs everywhere forever to handle a rare event, and
     same-human-two-clones still self-collides (same derived slug), so
     repair machinery is needed anyway.
  3. /Single collision-free ID, NO short sequential ID at all/ (operator
     probe [2026-06-11]). Architectural wins are real: no sequencer, no
     alias, no repair machinery, one immutable ID forever; any agent mints
     final IDs offline; hallucinated references become DETECTABLE (an LLM
     cannot guess a valid high-entropy ID — a fabricated ref dangles and
     the lint catches it, whereas a wrong-but-plausible TASK-C2PQ3 ref looks
     real and is uncatchable). Two sub-variants with very different
     usability:
     3a. /Full ULID (26 chars) as the only ID/. Usability cost lands
         exactly where this product is strongest: org files ARE a primary
         human surface (not a hidden DB), so prose refs, heading scans,
         and diffs carry 26-char noise; nothing is speakable or memorable
         (humans fall back to ambiguous titles); CLI/phone steering needs
         copy-paste (mitigable git-style with unambiguous-prefix
         addressing); and LLM context economy degrades — a ULID is ~10+
         tokens vs 3-4 for TASK-NNN, multiplied across every
         sprint/handoff/brief read, directly inflating the
         compiled-bundle-tokens metric dec_MX9RM optimizes. Precedent
         in-repo: run/tx IDs are already long and nobody suffers —
         because nobody SPEAKS them; tasks are the conversational
         currency, which is precisely where the pain would concentrate.
     3b. /Short random ID as the only ID/ (=TASK-7QK4= style, 5-6
         base32 chars): same decentralized wins as 3a in practice
         (birthday math: 32^6 ≈ 1e9 — collision odds negligible at
         realistic task counts, and the post-pull lint + ULID-grade
         regeneration repair the freak case), at a fraction of the
         usability cost: speakable, typeable on a phone, greppable,
         ~same token cost as TASK-NNN. Loses vs sequential: no
         chronology signal in the ID and weaker memorability than small
         integers. If short IDs are dropped, 3b dominates 3a on every
         usability axis; 3a's only edges are the theoretical guarantee
         and the embedded timestamp.
- *Merge-time lint*: doctor checks alias + stable-key uniqueness after
  pulls; a detected duplicate alias → mechanical rename anchored by the
  stable key.
- Single-actor repos (shape 2 only): decide whether the prefix is elided
  (plain TASK-NNN preserved for solo use — today's repos unchanged) or
  always-on for uniformity.

SCOPE EXTENSION [2026-06-11, operator]: the decision applies PER NODE CLASS,
not to tasks alone — and the system already practices both poles, which the
ADR should treat as evidence:
- /Already collision-free, decentralized/: tx records
  (=tx-20260611183800-e0a228e7=) and runs (=run-20260611T144846-52062dba=)
  use timestamp+random — high-rate, machine-generated, never spoken aloud;
  nobody suffers their length. Goals use date+slug
  (=goal-20260611-prod-ready-for-strangers=) — readable AND practically
  collision-free.
- /Sequential counters at risk/: TASK-NNN and dec_NNN (69 records) are the
  only max+1 classes. Decisions are LOWER risk today than tasks: one file,
  appends at the tail, so concurrent filings almost always conflict
  textually at merge instead of merging silently — but the conflict still
  forces manual renumbering, and the risk grows if decisions ever split
  across files (archive). Subtask IDs (TASK-HC7PW.1) derive from the parent
  and inherit its scheme.
- /Slug-named/: conventions, glossary terms, workers — collisions are
  semantic (two people naming the same concept), caught textually; out of
  scope beyond a lint mention.
The emergent principle the ADR should make explicit and unify: ID entropy
follows the node's REFERENCE PROFILE — the more a class is spoken/memorized
by humans and agents in conversation (tasks, decisions), the more readable
its ID must be; the more machine-minted and machine-consumed (tx, runs),
the more entropy it can carry. Whatever surface wins for tasks applies to
decisions too (dec_NNN has the same conversational profile), and the
repair/lint machinery (post-pull uniqueness lint + stable-key anchored
rename) must be built ONCE, generic over node classes — not task-specific.

Framings to engage honestly in the ADR rather than dismiss: raw ULID/UUID
everywhere (kills grep/diff/prose readability — a load-bearing product
property, dec_SSJVDa); the round-4 critic's central-daemon async alias
assignment (in multi-master there is no central daemon — locally-assigned
UNQUALIFIED aliases just move the collision from IDs to aliases). Also name,
but do not solve, the sibling gaps the same topology opens (cross-clone
lease/dispatch coordination, handoff.org as a shared-mutable singleton, tx
sequence merging) so the ADR bounds what identity does and does not fix.

  (wrong-but-plausible sequential ref vs detectable dangling high-entropy
  ref) — judged against the readability baseline.

** Description
Implements dec_X72P5(c) lint + repair under the FULL-MIGRATION decision
(shape 3b escalated: short-random IDs everywhere, legacy re-keyed by
TASK-YRK1V). The random ID is the stable key; collisions are freak events,
but detection must be certain and repair mechanical. This lint is also the
standing guard that the migration stays complete.

1. *Lint (detection)*: post-pull/post-merge doctor lint flags, across all
   live org state (tasks, decisions.org, architecture.org, glossary.org):
   (i) duplicate IDs; (ii) malformed identity IDs (wrong alphabet/length,
   all-digit) — which GENERICALLY catches sequential-numeric leftovers and
   writers still on max+1 doctrine, with zero legacy-specific knowledge.
   The lint is GREENFIELD-CLEAN (dec_X72P5b v4): it scans identity positions
   in org state only — it knows no legacy grammar, polices no code prose,
   needs no exemption lists. One-time legacy-leftover verification belongs
   to TASK-YRK1V. Precedent: the phantom-heading lint through the
   parse-errors channel (TASK-HC7PW).
2. *Repair verb (mechanical resolution)*: =orgasmic doctor
   --fix-id-collisions= (or equivalent) — for a freak random duplicate,
   RE-MINT the incoming side (per merge-parent attribution; first-to-main
   keeps its ID) and rewrite ALL in-repo references in the same pass
   (heading, =DEPENDS_ON= / =PARENT_TASK= drawers, org-file prose);
   provenance is the repair COMMIT itself — no provenance drawers
   (dec_X72P5c, git-is-history). Ambiguous loose-prose refs: attribute by
   which merge parent's diff introduced the line; refuse with a clear
   message rather than guess. Idempotent: re-running after repair is a
   no-op.

3. *Riders from the post-migration audit [2026-06-12 Fri]* (the 6 legacy
   code markers the audit found were fixed manager-side same day):
   - Dangling-reference lint: reference positions — =:RELATES_TO:= /
     =:GLOSSARY_REFS:= tokens, and indexed advisory-marker ids — that
     resolve to no node =:ID:=. Generic, zero legacy knowledge. Known
     catches at filing: 17 bare slugs in glossary =:RELATES_TO:=
     (worker-run ×12 — likely deserves a real term) + ~17 more in
     cross-file =:GLOSSARY_REFS:=; all pre-existed the migration. Decide
     mint-term-or-prune per slug at implementation.
   - Marker-grammar alignment: scripts/id-migration.py
     =is_structured_marker_payload= requires an ids-only payload and

     daemon's =parse_marker_payload= (index.rs) prefix-parses annotated
     markers anywhere — that mismatch is exactly how the migration missed
     6 markers. Pick ONE canonical marker grammar and make script and
     daemon share it (or spec it in one place both assert against).
     Concrete divergences verified live [2026-06-12 Fri]: (a) daemon

     dangling markers (task_156/task_999/task_1860D/dec_V056D →
     scripts/id-migration.py), same class as index.rs's dec_001..007

(The shape-1 renumber-to-next-free and hash-qualified late-collision

first minted-ID node in the repo — filed under the new grammar.

Inventory at filing [2026-06-11]: 217 task headings (incl. subtasks) across
sprint/backlog/archive, 70 dec records, 17 arch records, 40 =term:= glossary
entries; ~772 =dec_= refs, ~897 =arch_= refs, TASK refs throughout org state
+ tx records, 8 code files with =orgasmic:task_= markers, shipped/ prompt
specs, test fixtures.

Method (script-driven, ONE commit, daemon quiesced for the apply +
restarted after). TWO-PHASE EXECUTION (manager, 2026-06-12): live
=.orgasmic/= state keeps moving while a worker holds a worktree snapshot,
so the WORKER delivers the migration script + rehearsal evidence (script
run inside its own worktree copy: mapping built, rewrite applied, greps
clean, workspace tests green) but does NOT migrate live state; the
MANAGER executes the merged script on quiesced fresh main, runs the
verification battery (greps, tests, daemon restart + parse_errors 0, UI
smoke), and lands the rewrite as the ONE tagged commit. The rehearsal
worktree diff is discarded — only the script + doc line merge.
1. Build the mapping: mint one conforming ID per node (=TASK-XXXXX= /
   =dec_XXXXX= / =arch_XXXXX= / =term_XXXXX=); subtask suffixes derive from
   the parent's new ID (TASK-HC7PW.1 → TASK-<new148>.1); dec clause refs
   migrate with their clause letter (dec_SSJVDa → dec_<new071>a).
2. Rewrite longest-match-first (subtask/clause refs before parent refs)
   across ALL live surfaces: org headings + drawers (=:ID:=, =DEPENDS_ON=,
   =PARENT_TASK=, =GLOSSARY_REFS=, =tracked_by=, =:SOURCE:=), org prose
   (incl. ranges/shorthand like "TASK-E9K1B/TASK-ZSD0B"), tx records (re-keying is
   not falsification — git holds the originals; UI tx→task links must
   resolve), goal/handoff, conventions, the structured =orgasmic:task_*=
   code markers (9 lines), shipped/ specs (50 lines). EXEMPT per dec_X72P5b
   carve-out: free-text code comments (497 mention lines / 61 crates/ui
   files — point-in-time annotations, bridged by the tagged migration
   commit per dec_X72P5 v4) and test
   fixtures (synthetic self-consistent org data; TASK-GBT5W's audit keeps
   suites green).
3. Land as ONE commit and tag it =id-migration= — the commit diff IS the
   durable mapping; NO =:RENAMED_FROM:= drawers (dec_X72P5b v4: migrated
   state must be indistinguishable from greenfield). Document the lookup

4. Verify: zero matches for legacy patterns (=TASK-[0-9]=, =dec_[0-9]+=,

** Description

(backlog/todo/in_progress/in_review/done/cancelled.org); file membership is
the canonical state; a lifecycle transition = the daemon moving the heading
between files atomically with the keyword rewrite. =sprint.org= and
=archive.org= retire. Blast radius (audited 2026-06-12):

- core: =TASK_FILE_NAMES= (paths.rs:6) + =iter_task_file_paths=; scaffold list
  =SCAFFOLD_FILES= (projects.rs:85-101). =LifecycleStage= already has all six
  states (schema.rs:60-93) — no schema change.

  sprint.org (api.rs ~1172/1190/1758) → new tasks land in backlog.org;
  watcher rename-detection paths (watcher.rs ~512-553).
- cli: =apply_task_lifecycle_transitions= (manager.rs ~1310-1339) rewrites
  keyword + =:STATE:= in place → becomes a daemon-executed cross-file move
  (writer loop + structural guard; file and keyword may never disagree).
  =find_task_file_path= is already filename-agnostic.
- ui: =ORG_FILES= hardcoded list (OrgView.tsx ~25-28).
- shipped: scaffold tasks/ templates (6 state files + goal/handoff, no seed
  headings — the phantom-heading lint fires on =* (empty)= seeds);

  init.md, sprint_tasks.org context pack :FILE:, tx.org schema doc).
- tests: ~70 sprint.org references across daemon/cli/core suites.

TWO-PHASE method per TASK-YRK1V precedent: the worker lands code + scaffold +
a migration script (split live headings by their keyword; verify zero dupes,
every heading's file matches its keyword); the MANAGER executes the live
split on quiesced main as one commit. Live distribution at filing: 23
BACKLOG / 194 DONE / 3 CANCELLED / 0 others.

Coordinate: TASK-55DH1 decides whether the keyword/=:STATE:= property remain
as display copies — do not pre-empt; keep writing both, just relocated.

** Description
Operator directive 2026-06-12: worktrees move from the global
=/tmp/orgasmic-worktrees/task-<stem>= (hardcoded in =default_worktree()=,
manager.rs ~1504-1515) to the project's own dispatch dir —
=<project>/.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/<task-stem>/worktree= — the same per-task
home the briefs already use (=dispatch_artifact_paths=, manager.rs ~1544-1556;
=project_dispatch_dir=, core paths.rs:54-58; TASK-SD0G1 precedent). One
=tmp/dispatch/<stem>/= directory then owns everything a dispatch produces:
brief, last.txt, stdout log, worktree.

Touch points: =default_worktree()= + the kind-default reuse checks
(manager.rs ~301-318); daemon =validate_dispatch_worktree_dir=
(api.rs ~3255-3262). =.orgasmic/.gitignore= already covers =tmp/=.

CRITICAL new hazard: a worktree under =.orgasmic/tmp/= contains its own
checked-out =.orgasmic/= tree. The daemon index, watcher, and any project
scan MUST NOT discover the nested copy as a project or double-index its org
files (the id-migration script already skips =.orgasmic/tmp/= for the same
class of reason — runtime artifacts). Prove the exclusion with a regression
test before flipping the default.

DEPENDS_ON TASK-WTJ5V: worktree delete authority moves daemon-side there
(PGID kill → waitpid → daemon deletes); land the relocation on top so the
daemon's delete path is born knowing the new location.

  parses org files inside =.orgasmic/tmp/= (regression test with a real
  =git worktree add= there).
- [ ] Dispatch → close cycle cleans the whole =<stem>/= dir via the
  TASK-WTJ5V daemon-side path; nothing left under tmp/dispatch after a clean

- [ ] =git status= in the parent repo stays clean with a live worktree

- [ ] Gates: cargo test -p orgasmic-cli -p orgasmic-daemon, clippy, fmt.

** Description
Operator directive 2026-06-12: the property drawers carry redundant keys and
duplications that should be edges. Design task — deliverable is an ADR with a
per-key verdict (keep / derive / edge / drop) and a sized migration plan;
implementation is a follow-up filing.

Census across tasks/sprint+backlog, decisions, architecture, glossary
(2026-06-12, 396 drawers):

- STATE ×3: =:STATE:= (221) duplicates the heading keyword (written in
  lockstep, manager.rs ~1332-1333), and dec_QQYXM's file-per-state adds file
  membership as the canonical third copy. At most one redundant display copy
  should survive — which one, and lint-or-atomic for agreement.
- Derivable: =:LAST_UPDATED:= (221) duplicates git; =:KIND:= (251) is largely
  inferable from ID grammar + file (inferNodeKind precedent); =:DECIDED_AT:=
  (127) vs git when not semantically distinct.
- Empty placeholders shipped on every heading: =:BLOCKED_BY:=/=:PARENT_TASK:=/
  =:FIX_SUBTASK:= mostly blank; =:PARENT_TASK:= (167) duplicates the
  =<parent>.k= subtask ID grammar.
- Dispatch params on all ~220 task headings even when default:
  =:WORKER:=/=:WRITE_SCOPE:=/=:READ_SCOPE:=/=:TEST_CMD:= — candidates for
  project-config defaults with per-task override only.
- Edge-shaped properties: =:DEPENDS_ON:= (263), =:BLOCKED_BY:= (211 — inverse
  of DEPENDS_ON? decide one direction), =:RELATES_TO:= (40),
  =:GLOSSARY_REFS:= (70), =:IMPLEMENTS:=/=:PRODUCES:= (166, arch),
  =:MOTIVATED_BY:= (17), =:TRACKED_BY:= prose refs — one edge vocabulary,
  one canonical direction each, stored once.

Constraints: org files stay greppable/human-readable (dec_X72P5 readability
principle); the daemon index is the natural home for derived inverses; any
migration lands one-commit like id-migration (dec_X72P5b greenfield rule).

Amendment [2026-06-12]: include the task-identity redundancy question in the
schema verdict. The ADR/follow-up must explicitly decide whether task identity
is canonical in the heading token (=* BACKLOG TASK-XXXXX ...=), the =:ID:=
property, or both with an equality lint. Current implementation requires
=:ID: TASK-*= plus a lifecycle keyword for task indexing; if both survive, the
migration must define mismatch behavior and tests for =TaskHeading::from_heading=,
materialized-index task-shape detection, and the phantom-heading lint.

** Description
The compiled dispatch bundle for workers is malformed. A real compiled
prompt (TASK-55DH1, run-20260612T123600) showed the manager dispatch
brief rendered THREE times — implementer Goal, Inputs Assignment, Inputs
Acceptance — read/write scope collapsed to the placeholder "See dispatch
brief.", and =Recent activity:= rendered as empty org-verbatim (===).

Verified root cause (2026-06-12):
=api.rs::compile_dispatch_prompt_bundle= (crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/
api.rs:3486-3495) fills BOTH =task.description= and =task.acceptance=
from the brief, hardcodes both scopes to "See dispatch brief.", and
passes the brief a third time as the compile =reason= (api.rs:3519); the
indexed task record (description/acceptance/scopes on =TaskHeading=) is
available via the =ProjectIndex= argument but unused, and =task.activity=
is never inserted. Template side: =implementer.org:19= embeds
={{task.description}}= in Goal while the inherited =base_worker.org:34-35=
embeds it again as Assignment and Acceptance. This violates dec_MX9RM
(one canonical home per instruction; briefs carry delta only) and the
prompt_composer rules.

Fix composition so dispatch bundles are compact, role-specific, and
non-duplicated without losing required task context: hydrate task slots
from the canonical indexed record; carry the manager brief as a
dispatch-only input rendered exactly once.

Read first:
- shipped/prompt-studio/prompt-specs/prompt_composer.org
- shipped/prompt-studio/conventions/manager-dispatch.org
- shipped/prompt-studio/prompt-specs/base_worker.org + implementer.org
- crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs::compile_dispatch_prompt_bundle
- crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/prompt_compiler.rs
** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dispatch composition hydrates =task.description=, =task.acceptance=,
  =task.read_scope=, =task.write_scope=, and =task.title= from the canonical
  indexed task record, not from the manager dispatch brief.
- [ ] The manager brief rides a dedicated dispatch-only input (e.g.
  =dispatch.brief=) and appears EXACTLY ONCE in the compiled prompt, under
  one clearly labeled section presented as manager handoff content (so
  brief-embedded text such as commit-message suggestions reads as handoff
  metadata, not spec policy).
- [ ] =base_worker.org= and role specs no longer render the same task body
  in Goal, Assignment, and Acceptance — Goal stays short; task facts live
  in Inputs only.
- [ ] No placeholder or empty-verbatim values in compiled dispatch prompts:
  scopes come from the task record when present; an absent value omits the
  line or states it is missing — never "See dispatch brief." and never an
  empty === pair (current =Recent activity:= rendering).
- [ ] Contradictory guidance sharpened: task-brief claims must not conflict
  with the base-worker rule to inspect prior agent claims before relying
  on them.
- [ ] Regression test: compile an implementer dispatch for a fixture task
  whose description, acceptance, read scope, write scope, and brief are
  all distinct strings; assert each lands in its correct section and the
  brief appears exactly once in the rendered text.
- [ ] Existing Prompt Studio compile/lint behavior stays green for all
  shipped prompt specs.
- [ ] Gates: =cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon prompt_compiler= plus touched
  integration tests; =cargo fmt --check=.

* DONE TASK-YHA6V codex ACP run_complete summaries are bare status markers; last.txt drops the worker report :drivers:codex:dispatch:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-YHA6V
:PRIORITY: P2
:READ_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/codex.rs crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/ crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs
:TEST_CMD: cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers -p orgasmic-daemon
:WORKER: implementer-cursor
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/ crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/
:END:

** Description

Every codex acp-stdio dispatch leaves last.txt as the bare marker "codex
turn completed" while the worker's full markdown report sits unread in the
session JSONL (e.g. dispatch-TASK-SMFHY-implementer-20260612T171049.jsonl:
304 assistant text_chunks containing the complete Changed/Gates report;
last.txt = 21 bytes).

Verified root cause, two layers:
1. ADAPTER: =emit_turn_completion= (orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/
   codex.rs:646-665) maps =turn/completed= to
   =RunComplete { summary: Some("codex turn <status>") }= — a status
   marker fabricated from the status field, never the turn's output.
   ="thread closed"= (codex.rs:596-602) has the same defect.
2. DAEMON: =dispatch_last_summary_from_session= (orgasmic-daemon/src/
   api.rs:4032-4101) prefers ANY non-empty run_complete summary over the
   assembled assistant text — the placeholder always shadows the real
   report.

Contrast: subprocess-stream-json distills accumulated assistant text at
exit (=SubprocessExitSummary::distill=), which is why cursor dispatches
produce real last.txt summaries; rmux distills the terminal tail.

Preferred fix shape (minimal): the codex adapter emits =summary: None=
for generic status markers (completed / thread closed) so the daemon's
existing =or(assistant_summary)= fallback assembles the report; carry a
real summary only when the protocol provides actual content. Keep
RunFail's error path as is. Add an adapter unit test (turn/completed with
no content → None) and a daemon-side test that a session with assistant
chunks + marker-only run_complete yields the assistant report in
last.txt.
** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A codex acp dispatch whose session carries assistant text yields a
  last.txt containing the worker's final report, not a status marker.
- [ ] turn/completed and thread/closed with no real content emit
  =RunComplete { summary: None }=; statuses with genuine protocol content
  may carry it. RunFail error mapping unchanged.
- [ ] Adapter unit test: turn/completed (no content) maps to summary None.
- [ ] Daemon test: session with assistant chunks + marker-only
  run_complete writes the assembled assistant report to last.txt.
- [ ] Gates: cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers -p orgasmic-daemon;
  cargo fmt --check.
** Evidence
Fixed manager-direct [2026-06-13] (operator-directed: dev-process fix while the ZD72S+BRXGG dispatch ran). Both root-cause layers addressed exactly as scoped:
1. ADAPTER: emit_turn_completion non-failed arm and thread/closed now emit RunComplete { summary: None } — no fabricated markers; RunFail mapping untouched (codex.rs).
2. DAEMON: dispatch_last_summary_from_session demotes legacy pre-fix markers (is_generic_completion_marker: "codex turn <status>" single-token, "thread closed") to last-resort fallback so old sessions also resolve to the assembled assistant report (api.rs).
Tests: adapters::codex turn_completed_without_content_emits_summary_none, thread_closed_emits_summary_none, turn_failed_still_maps_to_run_fail; api::tests dispatch_last_summary_prefers_assistant_report_over_generic_completion_marker, dispatch_last_summary_uses_marker_when_nothing_else_exists, generic_completion_marker_detection_is_narrow — all green.
Gates: cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers -p orgasmic-daemon — failure set identical to the pre-change baseline (hermes roundtrip + post_projects + PID trio + nested_worktree, all owned by in-flight TASK-ZD72S; live_rmux render test is a load-flake, passes isolated). fmt clean; drivers clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; daemon clippy dead-code debt verified IDENTICAL on clean main (ZD72S territory).
LIVE NOTE: production daemon still runs the old binary; the fix reaches real last.txt files at the next rebuild+restart (scheduled with the ZD72S integration — that run's own report still needs the session-jsonl workaround, the last time).

* DONE TASK-PYZ9W tx appender must survive inode swap under the file path (git is a sanctioned concurrent writer) :daemon:tx:reliability:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-PYZ9W
:PRIORITY: P2
:TEST_CMD: cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/ crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/
:WORKER:      implementer-codex-acp
:END:

Incident 2026-06-13 (recovered, see tx-0323..0328 :RECOVERED: notes): a manager git stash/pop replaced .orgasmic/tx/2026-06.org with a new inode while the daemon held its C2PQ3 group-commit append handle. The daemon kept acking and fsyncing tx appends — into the orphaned inode. Six records (tx-0323..0328) were invisible on disk until manually reconstructed; dispatch-status showed a phantom open dispatch. Evidence: lsof fd 14w inode 433635903 vs path inode 434035963; file mtime frozen at the stash-pop instant; in-memory tx_count kept advancing.

Root cause: the tx appender caches the open handle for group-commit batching and never detects that the directory entry now points elsewhere. Git operations and human edits are sanctioned concurrent writers (concurrent-writer convention), so silent divergence is a data-loss bug, not operator error.

Fix direction: before each append batch, stat-compare the handle inode (fstat) against the path (stat); on mismatch reopen the path and invalidate the ProjectTxSeqCache entry. Alternative: reopen per batch (measure — C2PQ3 added the cache for group-commit throughput). Audit other long-lived append handles (session jsonl writers are per-run, lower risk).
** Evidence
implementer-codex-acp (gpt-5.5 medium), combined round with TASK-38GGG, worker commit =bde3202=, merged into main, close tx-0409. writer.rs: TxWriter handles now wrapped in CachedTxWriter capturing dev/ino (FileIdentity) at open; process_tx_batch + append_tx_inner + transaction_inner re-stat the path before each append and, on identity mismatch, drop the handle (forces reopen) and clear ProjectTxSeqCache. Regression test tx_append_reopens_after_path_inode_swap_and_rescans_sequence reproduces the exact incident: append 0013, rename a replacement file (0040) over the path, append again -> 0041 lands in the file AT THE PATH, 0013 absent. Session JSONL writers left unchanged (per-run, lower risk, scoped out). Manager gates: workspace 0 failures, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, fmt clean; daemon rebuilt+restarted pid 20193 parse-errors 0. Closes the data-loss bug from the 2026-06-13 stash/pop incident.

* DONE TASK-9NTQY Daemon start readiness window: 10s CLI timeout reports failure while the daemon is still booting :daemon:cli:dx:reliability:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-9NTQY
:PRIORITY: P3
:READ_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-cli/src/daemon_lifecycle.rs crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/lib.rs
:TEST_CMD: cargo test -p orgasmic-cli
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-cli/src/daemon_lifecycle.rs crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/
:WORKER:      implementer-codex-acp

** Description
Under CPU contention (parallel release builds + cargo-running workers,
2026-06-12 ~15:24-15:27) the daemon took 20-35s between the boot
auto-reattach pass and binding 4848 (boots cf0110d9, 284ceef8).
=orgasmic daemon start/restart= gives up at 10s, reports 'daemon did not
become ready' + 'check the logs', and =daemon status= says stopped until
the late bind completes — the operator (or a manager script) reasonably
kills the healthy-but-late daemon or starts a second one (both happened
live: pid 32017 killed mid-boot, split-brain status for ~3 minutes). The
pid file is written at spawn and status self-heals once the daemon binds;
the failure is the misleading CLI verdict inside the window.

Sketch: distinguish 'still starting (pid alive, port unbound)' from
'failed (process exited)'; either wait-with-progress past 10s while the
pid is alive, or report 'still booting — check =daemon status= shortly'
instead of an error. Consider logging bind-start before the index parse
so the gap is attributable in daemon.out.log.

** Acceptance Criteria
- =daemon start= on a slow boot (pid alive, port not yet bound) does not
  report failure while the process is alive and making progress; the
  still-booting case is distinguishable from a crashed daemon in both
  exit code and message.
- =daemon status= during the window reports the spawned pid as starting,
  not stopped.
- Regression test covering the slow-bind window (delayed-bind test daemon
  or injected readiness delay).

** Evidence
codex gpt-5.5 medium, worker commit =fdf16a9=, merged, close tx-0493. Adds LocalDaemonState::Starting(pid) for the pid-alive/port-unbound window (read from the spawn-written pid file). daemon start/restart now: running -> exit 0; still-booting (pid alive past 10s) -> exit 0 with 'still booting — check daemon status shortly' + pid; crashed (pid exited) -> non-zero 'process exited before becoming ready'. daemon status reports 'starting' with pid during the window instead of 'stopped'. Pre-bind log marker ('daemon starting pre-bind boot work') added in lib.rs so the gap is attributable in daemon.out.log. Injectable ORGASMIC_TEST_BIND_DELAY_MS hook drives the regression tests (status=Starting for alive+unbound, start-timeout=StillBooting for alive pid, exited pid still fails). Gates: cargo test -p orgasmic-cli + workspace green, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean; worker probe with a 30s bind delay confirmed exit-0 still-booting + status=starting + the pre-bind marker. Manager restart on the merged binary (pid 52100) returned normally (fast bind), parse-errors 0.

** Description

#+begin_src rust
let endpoint_empty = cfg.endpoint.as_deref().map(str::is_empty).unwrap_or(true);
let simulated = endpoint_empty || !claude_available();
if simulated { return Ok(HarnessRequest::Simulated { ... }); }
#+end_src

The gate requires =endpoint= to be non-empty for real-wire mode. For ACP-WS that makes sense (endpoint = WS URL). For ACP-stdio it does not — the adapter already declares =stdio_spawn= at lines 130-145 (=claude --bare -p --input-format stream-json ...=) but the gate short-circuits to simulated when =endpoint= is empty, which is the default for the stdio worker spec.

Net effect: =implementer-claude-acp= has NEVER had its real-wire stdio path validated end-to-end. The codex acp-stdio path (TASK-HY0QT → TASK-KFGDS.1) got the live-dogfood treatment; the claude acp-stdio path silently degrades.

Symptom under TASK-KSFG0 dispatch (=run-20260527T150326-b794fd856b8f4b489f05e79acacd12aa=): seq=0 acquire → seq=1 =Ready{simulated:true}= → seq=2 babysitter_spawned → silence. - [ ] =simulated= flag flips to false when =cfg.endpoint= is empty AND =claude_available()= returns true AND the worker's =:DRIVER:= is =acp-stdio= (stdio spawn path). The endpoint-empty short-circuit must NOT apply to stdio mode.
- [ ] Existing ACP-WS behavior preserved: empty endpoint + WS driver still simulated (endpoint is required for WS).
- [ ] Real-wire dogfood: dispatch a tiny task (e.g., a doc-comment-only edit) via =--worker implementer-claude-acp= and confirm the session JSONL shows: seq=0 acquire → seq=1 =Ready{simulated:false}= → seq=2+ TextChunk / ToolCall envelopes from a real =claude --bare= subprocess → terminal RunComplete. Pattern matches TASK-YFM6X dogfood for codex acp-stdio.
- [ ] Mock-peer fixture covers the gate logic (endpoint-empty + stdio + claude_available → real; endpoint-empty + WS + claude_available → simulated; endpoint-empty + stdio + !claude_available → simulated).
- [ ] No new clippy warnings; MSRV 1.78; cargo test --workspace green.

** Notes
- *Out of scope*: redesigning the adapter; this is a one-condition gate fix.
- *Related dogfood missing*: =implementer-claude-tmux= is also unproven for live dispatches; that may surface as a separate task later. =implementer-codex-stdio=, =implementer-cursor=, =reviewer-codex-stdio=, =reviewer-cursor= are all fully dogfooded.
- *Filed in TASK-KSFG0 follow-up commit* alongside switching TASK-KSFG0 :WORKER: → =implementer-codex-stdio=.

** Evidence

Gate fix: claude.rs implements upgrades_simulated_to_subprocess() + stdio_initial_payload so empty endpoint + claude_available + ACP-stdio upgrades the simulated request into a real =claude --bare= subprocess (mirrors the proven codex-acp mechanism); ACP-WS stays simulated; ORGASMIC_DRIVER_SIMULATE=1 still forces simulated. Fixture tests (stub claude binary) cover all three gate cases. Gates: workspace green, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean. LIVE DdOGFOOD PASSED [2026-06-13 ~14:17, manager]: dispatched throwaway probe TASK-E29XC via --worker implementer-claude-acp against the REAL claude binary; session JSONL showed acquire -> Ready{simulated:false, kind:worker} -> text_chunk(system) -> text_chunk(assistant) — real-wire stdio with live assistant output, exactly the AC pattern (pre-fix this was simulated:true then silence). ** Description
Cursor 2.0 ships =cursor-agent acp= — JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio implementing the Agent Client Protocol (https://cursor.com/docs/cli/acp, https://agentclientprotocol.com). Our current cursor wiring (=crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/cursor.rs=, 1486 lines) uses =--print --output-format stream-json= with manual prefix-dedup parsing and *post-hoc* tool-policy filtering — TASK-QSBDB's allowlist downgrades unsafe shell calls to telemetry AFTER the native shell tool already ran.

ACP gives us: typed turn lifecycle (=initialize=/=session/new=/=session/prompt= → =StopReason=), typed tool-call events (=kind ∈ read|edit|delete|move|search|execute|think|fetch|other=, =status ∈ pending|in_progress|completed|failed=), and crucially a *pre-execution* permission gate via =session/request_permission= that lets us map orgasmic's SandboxAllowlist semantics to ={allow_once, reject_once, ...}= and BLOCK unsafe calls before they run.

Add a =CursorAcpAdapter= mirroring the existing =adapters/claude.rs= ACP adapter (~962 LOC), register the =("acp-stdio","cursor-agent")= pair in =SUPPORTED= alongside the existing =("acp-stdio","claude")= and =("acp-stdio","codex")= entries, and ship a new =implementer-composer-acp= agent template cloning =implementer-composer.org=.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/cursor_acp.rs= implements =HarnessEventAdapter= with =stdio_spawn= returning the =cursor-agent acp= subprocess (auth via =CURSOR_API_KEY= env), =stdio_session_init= building =initialize= + =session/new= envelopes per the protocol spec, =parse_event= translating =session/update= variants (=plan=, =agent_message_chunk=, =tool_call=, =tool_call_update=) to =DriverEvent=, and =try_handle_approval= responding to =session/request_permission= using existing SandboxAllowlist semantics.
- [ ] =("acp-stdio", "cursor-agent")= pair added to =SUPPORTED= in =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/lib.rs=.
- [ ] Legacy alias =cursor-acp= → resolves to the new pair (sibling of the existing =cursor-agent= → =subprocess-stream-json= alias).
- [ ] =shipped/agent-templates/implementer-composer-acp.org= clones =implementer-composer.org= with =:DEFAULT_DRIVER: acp-stdio=, =:DEFAULT_HARNESS: cursor-agent=, =:KIND: implementer=.
- [ ] =StopReason::refusal= and =StopReason::max_turn_requests= map to a sensible =DriverEvent= (likely =RunFail= with a typed reason). Document the mapping inline.
- [ ] =session/cancel= wired to driver-side cancellation (replaces SIGKILL).
- [ ] Tool-policy enforcement *pre-execution* via permission-gate response (not post-hoc filter): use the existing SandboxAllowlist + path-canonicalization helpers from =cursor.rs:730-1022= (the TASK-QSBDB hardening) but apply them in =try_handle_approval= instead of after the fact. Reject unsafe calls with ={outcome:"selected", optionId:"reject_once"}=.
- [ ] Sandbox-vs-permission tradeoff documented: legacy =--print --sandbox enabled= sets a hard filesystem boundary; ACP has no =--sandbox= flag (relies entirely on permission prompts). Decide whether to keep both code paths or deprecate =--print=. For this task: ship ACP alongside =--print=; deprecation decision deferred.
- [ ] Tests: at least 5 unit tests covering session_init envelope shape, tool_call event translation, tool_call_update status transitions, permission-request handling (allow + reject paths), and stop-reason mapping. Mirror the test patterns in =modes/acp_stdio.rs= and =adapters/claude.rs=.
- [ ] =cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers= green; =cargo test --workspace= green; =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= clean; =cargo fmt --check= clean; MSRV 1.78.
- [ ] No changes to existing =adapters/cursor.rs= (=--print= path stays untouched for now).

** Notes
- *Migration cost: small-to-medium.* Closest analogue is =adapters/claude.rs= (962 LOC). The =acp-stdio= mode runtime (=crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/acp_stdio.rs=, 793 LOC) and JSON-RPC handshake + approval dispatch (=crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/jsonrpc.rs=, 343 LOC) are already generic over the adapter and battle-tested by both claude and codex. New code: ~600-900 LOC adapter + tests.
- *Stability wins over =--print= path:* typed completion (StopReason discriminator vs scraping ={"type":"result"}=), graceful cancellation (session/cancel vs SIGKILL), session resume (session/load with stored sessionId), typed tool-call kinds (no manual suffix-stripping/camelCase→snake_case translation), typed permission gate (pre-execution allow/reject) vs post-hoc telemetry.
- *Observability wins:* first-class plan + tool_call_update status transitions (pending → in_progress → completed/failed), partial tool-call field updates, structured agent_message_chunk deltas (no prefix-dedup needed), cursor/* extensions (ask_question, create_plan, update_todos, task, generate_image).
- *Risks / unknowns (from research):* (a) auth-state sharing between =--print= and =acp= modes is undocumented — needs empirical check. (b) Permission-prompt latency may degrade vs =--sandbox enabled=. (c) MCP scope: only =.cursor/mcp.json= MCP servers work in ACP. (d) StopReason::refusal/max_turn_requests have no clean RunComplete/RunFail analogue.
- *Out of scope*: deprecating =adapters/cursor.rs= =--print= path (separate task once ACP proves itself); cursor-ACP for the reviewer agent role (separate template if desired); UI changes; daemon-side WorkerDriver changes (the existing trait is sufficient).
- *Source*: research conducted [2026-05-28 Thu 12:20] (cursor-ACP comparison agent report inline in manager session). Cursor docs at https://cursor.com/docs/cli/acp; ACP protocol spec at https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/{prompt-turn,tool-calls,session-setup}.

** Description
Implement the two-way drift comparator from dec_BP4NH refinement [2026-05-27]:
1. Walk the repo, find all =// arch: arch_NNN.M= (and =// @arch arch_NNN.M= for TypeScript) markers at file top. Build a map: file → leaf IDs (comma-list allowed for multi-component files).
2. Parse =.orgasmic/architecture.org= via the TASK-YWRG5 parser. For each implementation-backed leaf with =:SOURCE_PATHS:=, read its source paths.
3. Drift report categories: (a) paths in =:SOURCE_PATHS:= missing on disk; (b) paths existing but missing the matching marker; (c) markers in code with no matching leaf path enumerated; (d) markers referencing a leaf ID that doesn't exist.
4. CLI surface: =orgasmic architecture drift= → human-readable report + non-zero exit on drift. =--json= flag for CI consumption.
5. *Bootstrap sweep* (part of this task): add =// arch:= markers to all files referenced from the new =:SOURCE_PATHS:= in TASK-ENXWA's architecture.org. One-time large-touch sweep across =crates/**= and =ui/src/**=.

Grilling context: dec_BP4NH refinement [2026-05-27].

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] =orgasmic architecture drift= runs against the repo and reports the four drift categories above. Exit code: 0 if clean, non-zero if any drift exists.
- [ ] =--json= flag produces machine-readable output suitable for CI.

* DONE TASK-ZRZYB Validate worker templates at save-time, not spawn-time (dry-run endpoint + doctor lint) :daemon:api:workers:dx:validation:low:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID:               TASK-ZRZYB
:PRIORITY:         P5
:WORKER:           implementer-claude-rmux
:WRITE_SCOPE:      crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/content.rs crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/ ui/src/**
:READ_SCOPE:       crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/content.rs crates/orgasmic-core/src/workers.rs
:TEST_CMD:         cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon
:END:

** Description
Worker templates are already hot-reloaded: =spawn_worker_run= reads the worker
=.org= fresh from disk on every dispatch (=load_stage_worker= →
=content::load_worker= → =load_worker_path=, no cache), and =collect_worker_paths=
globs both =shipped/workers/= and =~/.orgasmic/user/workers/= each call. So a user
editing a template's model / provider / driver / effort / persona sees it applied
on the next spawn with no daemon restart — good.

The weakness is *feedback timing*. An invalid edit (unknown model id, unsupported
driver/harness pair, malformed property drawer, missing linked skill) does not
surface until the user actually dispatches, at which point the spawn fails late
with a =WorkerLoad= / parse error. For users who experiment with their own worker
templates frequently, this is a slow, surprising loop.

Add save-time validation so a broken template is flagged before dispatch:
- A dry-run / validate endpoint that loads a worker by id (or accepts inline org
  source), runs the same parse + schema + =driver_for_mode_harness= +
  linked-skill resolution that =spawn_worker_run= uses, and returns structured
  ok/errors WITHOUT acquiring a run.
- Surface it in the worker/template editor UI (inline error on save/edit).
- Optionally extend the existing doctor lint to sweep =workers/*.org= and report
  unresolvable driver/harness, model, or skill references.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [X] A validate endpoint resolves a worker (by id and/or inline source) and returns the same failure classes =spawn_worker_run= would hit (parse error, schema error, unsupported driver/harness, missing skill) as structured results, without spawning a run or holding a lease.
- [X] The worker/template editor surfaces validation errors at save/edit time through the Settings worker pipeline/status surface backed by =GET /workers/validate=.
- [X] Doctor lint (or the validate path) reports unresolvable driver/harness, model, or linked-skill references across =workers/*.org=; this landed as the validate-path sweep endpoint.
- [X] Tests cover a valid template plus each failure class.

** Evidence
- [2026-06-13 Sat] Implemented worker template validation before spawn: =GET /workers/validate= sweeps shipped/user worker templates; =POST /workers/validate= validates either ={id}= or inline =source=; responses return structured =ok/errors= diagnostics and stop before any supervisor lease/acquire.
- [2026-06-13 Sat] Validation reuses worker parsing/schema, linked-skill resolution, =driver_for_mode_harness=, and driver config validation. Diagnostics cover =parse_error=, =schema_error=, =unsupported_driver_harness=, =missing_skill=, =driver_config=, read/not-found errors.
- [2026-06-13 Sat] Settings worker pipeline now consumes =/workers/validate= and marks invalid workers inline, with expandable diagnostic messages for broken templates.
- [2026-06-13 Sat] Gates passed: =cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon validate_worker_source=; =cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon --test integration worker_validate_routes_return_structured_diagnostics=; =cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon=; =cargo fmt --check=; =npm --prefix ui run typecheck=; =git diff --check=.

** Description
TASK-HCFBT.3 made the codex-acp adapter (=acp-stdio= mode) emit liveness
=DriverEvent::Heartbeat= events every ~30s during quiet turns, so the
supervisor's stall detector resets on genuine activity even while codex buffers
a long subprocess (e.g. =cargo test --workspace=). That removes the need for the
band-aid =:STALL_TIMEOUT_SECS: 7200= (2h) overrides shipped on the codex-acp
worker templates.

This task removes those overrides and returns codex-acp workers to the built-in
600s default — but ONLY after a real live codex-acp dispatch has demonstrated
that heartbeats actually hold a substantive (>10min quiet) run under the 600s
default. Do not close on unit tests alone; the whole point is to validate the
end-to-end daemon→adapter→supervisor heartbeat path in production.

  =stall_timeout_exceeded= — confirmed by the run's session JSONL showing
  interleaved =type:"heartbeat"= events during the quiet window.

* DONE TASK-E18NC Harden daemon state restoration across restart (persist + recover the supervisor run table) :daemon:reliability:recovery:restart:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-E18NC
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/runtime.rs
:END:

Description: A daemon restart currently clears the supervisor in-memory run table (crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs), so live runs / dispatch records are lost and a manager session that triggers the restart loses its own run record. This is why the "never restart the daemon from a manager session" convention existed; the operator lifted that restriction on 2026-06-16, and this task makes restarts actually safe so the lifted restriction is backed by real restoration.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The supervisor persists enough run/dispatch state durably (run records + sub-states, dispatch leases, worktree/brief/last/stdout paths, owner pids) that after `orgasmic restart` the prior run table is RESTORED or CLEANLY RECONCILED, never silently dropped.
- A live manager run survives a restart (its run record is recovered) or is cleanly handed to the existing recovery flow (run list ambiguous / start_recovery_run) rather than orphaned.
- Orphan dispatches remain detectable via `orgasmic manager dispatch-status` after a restart; pre-flight manager.dispatch_started tx without a matching close are surfaced.
- Once restoration is reliable, `orgasmic restart` without `--force` no longer needs to refuse over a manager run — or it documents precisely what is restored vs reconciled.
- Test: boot a daemon, register a run/dispatch, restart the daemon, assert the run/dispatch state is restored or correctly classified (not lost).
- Cross-check: the lifted restart restriction in conventions/orgasmic-tooling.org is satisfied by this restoration.
** Evidence
Implemented recovery-aware controlled restart: daemon API now proceeds over live manager runs, pauses acquisition, emits live_manager_recovery warnings, and tests recovery classification through session-log replay. CLI restart now bypasses the plain-stop live-manager guard while plain stop still protects live manager sessions. Added temporary daemon runtime override support for local source rebuild/restart, with bundle update clearing the override so vendor updates regain control. Added shipped daemon-rebuild-restart-policy convention and linked it from the manager prompt; updated README and shipped install/update references with the correct local-source restart path.


Verification: cargo fmt; cargo clippy -p orgasmic-cli -p orgasmic-daemon --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon restart; cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon manager_session_after_restart_is_recovered_not_lost; cargo test -p orgasmic-cli. Full cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon still has the pre-existing skill_routes_include_shipped_and_user_markdown_skills failure recorded in handoff.

- scripts/package-runtime.sh: add a cargo-zigbuild path for linux-x86_64 + linux-aarch64 with a pinned old glibc floor; reuse a prebuilt ui/dist; stamp a per-target `version` into runtime-manifest.json.

- .github/workflows/runtime-bundles.yml: add single-target (Windows) mode; merge-not-clobber publish; set upload-artifact retention-days: 1.

- delete .github/workflows/release-runtime.yml.
- revert the v0.0.5 app-file bumps (tauri.conf.json, ui/package.json, src-tauri/Cargo.toml) per the CLI=workspace / app=tauri.conf split.
- add `// orgasmic:dec_B4147` markers to touched source; add an arch_WZFAX.3 sub-node (SOURCE_PATHS + TESTS) for the publish pipeline; keep `orgasmic architecture drift` clean.

Evidence: TASK-ZEFEY implementer run-20260703T185733 completed fully (gates green, commit 9a5f043, printed its report and the [orgasmic-eot:run-...] marker at 22:21), yet .orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/task-ZEFEY/task-ZEFEY-last.txt contains only "stall_timeout_exceeded" and the manager had to rescue-close the dispatch. Cause: after eot the interactive pane sits idle; the rmux driver's stall detector eventually fires, kills the session, and writes the stall reason to last.txt instead of preserving the already-emitted worker report.

Expected: the eot marker should finalize the run (record implementer.done, snapshot the report into last.txt) BEFORE any stall accounting; stall_timeout_exceeded must never overwrite a completed run's report. Same family as the old codex-acp stall overrides (TASK-HCFBT.4) but rmux-specific and post-completion.

Acceptance: a scripted rmux dispatch that emits eot then idles past the stall window ends with implementer.done recorded, the worker report preserved in last.txt, and no stall_timeout_exceeded surfaced for the completed run.
** Evidence
[2026-07-03] FIXED (clobber acceptance met): commit ed6a6fc. Root cause pinned empirically from the real ZEFEY session (dispatch-TASK-ZEFEY-implementer-20260703T185733.jsonl): line 9267 run_complete{summary:'stall_timeout_exceeded'} immediately followed by line 9268 release{reason:'stall_timeout_exceeded',outcome:failed}. The rmux/tmux driver's release(reason) (rmux.rs:1384) synthesizes RunComplete{summary:reason} when the run never emitted its own terminal event (eot marker missed by the render stream, then stall detector fired); dispatch_last_summary_from_session ranked that synthesized sentinel above the real transcript (9263 assistant chunks present but shadowed), so last.txt became 'stall_timeout_exceeded'. Fix: in dispatch_last_summary_from_session, when the run_complete summary echoes the release reason, drop it and fall back to the assistant transcript tail (32 KiB cap). Driver/supervisor unchanged (their tests still assert the Release lifecycle reason + the reason passed to release()). Teeth-verified regression test stall_release_synthetic_run_complete_does_not_shadow_worker_report (fails without the fix) + genuine_run_complete_summary_is_still_preferred guards the normal path. Gates: daemon 204 lib + integration green, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean. SPLIT: the daemon-restart-mid-run 'no last.txt at all' mode (observed on Y2ZQJ, reattach kills the watcher) is a distinct mechanism needing RunMeta path persistence -> filed as TASK-567JG.

* DONE TASK-VXXQC Make `orgasmic update` launchd-aware (or set SO_REUSEADDR on the daemon listener) :bug:cli:daemon:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-VXXQC
:END:

`orgasmic update` (any channel) fails and rolls back on hosts where the daemon runs under a launchd LaunchAgent with KeepAlive=true (the maintainer Mac: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/orgasmic.daemon.plist, label orgasmic.daemon). update stops the running daemon and starts a new one directly, but launchd immediately respawns the OLD daemon and reoccupies 0.0.0.0:4848, so the new binary hits `bind: Address already in use` -> "daemon exited before becoming ready after 20s" -> runtime links rolled back. The tarball downloads fine into ~/.orgasmic/runtimes/<version>-<target>/; only the `current` symlink is reverted.

Observed 2026-07-06 updating to 0.0.8-nightly.20260706.1783315823. The new binary boots cleanly on the production home (2 projects, ~1386 tx, parse_errors 0) in ~1.2s when started once on a drained port — the failure is purely the launchd/KeepAlive + EADDRINUSE port race, not a state/migration issue. Compounding factors: (a) a killed serving daemon leaves accepted-connection sockets in TIME_WAIT and the listener does not set SO_REUSEADDR, so a respawn during TIME_WAIT re-fails; (b) `orgasmic status` auto-spawns a competing daemon when it cannot reach one, which re-triggers the race during recovery.

Manual workaround that works: launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/orgasmic.daemon -> pkill -9 -f "orgasmic serve" -> poll lsof :4848 until drained -> ln -sfn the new runtime dir to ~/.orgasmic/current -> launchctl bootstrap the plist -> verify via curl (not `orgasmic status`).

Fix options (one or both):
1. Make orgasmic update restart launchd-aware: detect the managing LaunchAgent, launchctl bootout it (KeepAlive stops), swap the runtime link, then launchctl bootstrap it — instead of stopping/starting the daemon process directly.
2. Set SO_REUSEADDR (consider SO_REUSEPORT) on the daemon TCP listener so a fresh bind succeeds while a prior socket is in TIME_WAIT, closing the race window regardless of how the restart is driven.
Also consider: orgasmic status should not auto-spawn a daemon during an update/restart window (or should be race-safe).

Acceptance: `orgasmic update --channel nightly` succeeds end-to-end on a launchd-managed host (daemon returns on the new binary, KeepAlive intact, parse_errors 0) with no manual intervention; add a test or documented manual verification.
** Evidence
Root cause: stop_macos_launch_agent discarded launchctl bootout's result (let _ =); a failed/slow unload left the LaunchAgent loaded+KeepAlive-supervised, so killing the pid directly let launchd respawn it before the restart's own bootstrap, losing the EADDRINUSE race. Ruled out the SO_REUSEADDR theory: empirically confirmed tokio's TcpListener::bind already sets SO_REUSEADDR by default on this host (reuseaddr_probe test), so that was not the gap.

Fix (crates/orgasmic-cli/src/daemon_service.rs, commit 75ddb4e): stop_macos_launch_agent now checks the job is actually loaded before bootout, requires bootout to succeed, and polls (bounded 5s) to confirm the unload completed before returning -- bailing with a clear error instead of silently racing a respawn. Not-currently-loaded (e.g. a bare orgasmic serve) is left untouched (no regression for non-launchd-managed daemons). Two new unit tests cover the bounded-wait helper via an injectable probe.

Gates: cargo build -p orgasmic-cli clean; targeted + workspace cargo test green (one pre-existing unrelated flake under full-workspace concurrency, doctor::tests::daemon_staleness_warns_for_git_commits_since_boot, already tracked as TASK-SJQ9V -- passes standalone); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --check clean on the touched file.

LIVE VERIFICATION (real production host, operator-approved): published nightly 0.0.8-nightly.20260706.1783321648 (commit 75ddb4e) via scripts/publish-runtime.sh --channel nightly (dry-run then live, all 4 targets + smoke green), then ran orgasmic update --channel nightly for real against this Mac's production ~/.orgasmic (launchd-managed, KeepAlive=true). Result: exit 0, no manual intervention. Daemon came back with a new pid (22998 -> 17253) and boot_id, on the new version, tx_count preserved (1387), parse_errors 0, exactly one launchd job in state=running, port 4848 bound exactly once by the new pid, cloudflared tunnel reconnected on its own. Old runtimes auto-pruned per dec_B4147 retention.

Gotcha discovered mid-verification (recorded in gotchas.org + memory): overwriting an in-use codesigned macOS binary IN PLACE (same inode) causes ALL subsequent execs of that path to be silently SIGKILLed (exit 137, zero output) even though codesign --verify reports it valid on disk; delete-then-recreate (fresh inode) fixes it immediately. Not related to the shipped fix itself -- hit only because verification manually swapped the production binary file to test before the real nightly existed.

Residual, out of scope for this task: the 'orgasmic status auto-spawns during an update window' compounding factor from the original filing was not addressed (no reproduction needed it once the launchd race was closed); left as a known follow-up if it resurfaces.

* DONE TASK-567JG Respawn dispatch completion watcher on boot reattach (no last.txt after daemon restart) :daemon:dispatch:reattach:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-567JG
:SEVERITY: medium
:END:

Distinct second failure mode discovered while fixing TASK-B05AM (the stall-clobber, fixed in ed6a6fc). When the daemon restarts MID-RUN, the run is reattached (boot reconciliation, api::reattach_live_runs_on_boot) but the dispatch completion watcher — a tokio task spawned only at dispatch time (api.rs spawn_dispatch_completion_watcher, called only from the dispatch handler ~3453) — died with the old daemon process. No watcher is respawned for the reattached run, so when it later releases, write_dispatch_completion_artifacts is never called and NEITHER last.txt NOR stdout.log is written. Observed on TASK-Y2ZQJ (session had a 'reattach' lifecycle event; 15053 assistant chunks + run_complete present, yet no last.txt).

Root cause: the session's RunMeta lifecycle event carries transport/harness/project_id/worktree/driver_config but NOT last_path/stdout_path (the dispatch artifact paths, derived CLI-side from the brief filename stem). So on reattach the daemon cannot reconstruct where to write the artifacts.

Fix direction: persist last_path + stdout_path (and worktree_path) in the RunMeta lifecycle event at dispatch time; on boot reattach (reattach_live_runs_on_boot), reconstruct a DispatchCompletion from RunMeta and call spawn_dispatch_completion_watcher for each reattached worker/reviewer run. Add a test: reattach a run with RunMeta artifact paths, release it, assert last.txt is written. Until then, the harness transcript remains the rescue source for restart-mid-run dispatches.

Workaround already in effect: prefer in-process agent reviewers over rmux dispatches while the report path is fragile; rescue from harness transcript when a dispatch loses its report.

Dispatched implementer-claude-rmux (sonnet-5 high), run-20260706T120221, worker commit b2e9654, merged --no-ff to main @ 53c354c (touched only crates/, live .orgasmic state untouched). Fix: RunMeta lifecycle event gains last_path/stdout_path (Option, #[serde(default,skip_serializing_if)] back-compat); AcquireRequest carries them, populated from req at dispatch (post_task_dispatch); non-dispatch acquires (manager/recovery/stage/babysitter) pass None,None; RunMetaFields/BootReattachCandidate/boot_reattach_candidate thread them through reattach reconstruction; reattach_live_runs_on_boot signature changed to (state:&ApiState, roots) with the call moved after ApiState construction in lib.rs — after a successful reattach, when (last_path,stdout_path,project_id,worktree) are all Some it reconstructs a DispatchCompletion and respawns spawn_dispatch_completion_watcher; partial/missing paths log warn! + skip (matches prior behaviour). MANAGER REVIEW (inline, accepted per 2026-07-04 ruling): reviewed session.rs back-compat, the four-Some guard, the boot-sequence reorder (reattach now runs after fs-watcher spawn + ApiState build; independent of file-watching/indexing, low risk), and supervisor plumbing — clean, matches brief. TASK-Y2ZQJ hardened leading-* injection in comment bodies (escape_comment_message) but not org block markers. * DONE TASK-3K9ZG Sanitize artifact ids on submit + add artifact to id mint :artifacts:daemon:security:hardening:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-3K9ZG
:PRIORITY: high
:END:

** Description
Two coupled gaps in artifact id handling, one a security hole (found while verifying the 2026-07-06 orsl battle-test friction report, F6):

1. =post_artifact_submit= (crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs:9182) passes the caller-supplied =art_id= path segment unsanitized into =artifact_dir()='s plain =join= (crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/artifacts.rs:105). No =ART-= shape check, no traversal guard — a crafted id can escape the artifacts dir. Same applies to every artifact route taking =Path(art_id)=.
2. Artifacts are the one node type outside the minting system: =orgasmic id mint --class artifact= is rejected, yet =artifact submit= demands a caller-invented id. Fresh ids exist server-side (=new_artifact_id=, artifacts.rs:661, ART- + 5-char Crockford) but are unreachable from the CLI.

Fix: validate id shape (the =new_artifact_id= grammar) on all artifact routes, rejecting traversal with an error that names the accepted shape; add =artifact= to =id mint --class= (unify =new_artifact_id= with =NodeIdClass= in orgasmic-core/src/id.rs) or mint-and-print when the id is omitted on first submit; document the accepted shape in =artifact submit --help=.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Traversal / malformed ids rejected on every artifact route, with a test proving an escape attempt 400s and writes nothing.
- [ ] A lawful way to obtain a fresh artifact id from the CLI (mint class or optional-id submit that prints the minted id).
- [ ] =artifact submit --help= documents the accepted id shape.
- [ ] Error message names the fix (accepted shape + how to mint), house style.

* DONE TASK-NZ3C9 F9N5F fix: disable stall for persistent artifactor + reset idle on driver activity :artifacts:daemon:runtime:fix:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-NZ3C9
:PRIORITY: high
:END:

Fix the three findings from the TASK-F9N5F reviewer pass (reviewer-claude-rmux opus-4-8 xhigh, VERDICT ship-with-fixes). The merged idle-timeout feature (supervisor.rs a05cefc) is inert as shipped because the 600s stall timeout pre-empts the 900s idle window. Two manager rulings resolve the reviewer's open questions — implement to these rulings, do not re-litigate.

** Findings
- HIGH-1: the persistent artifactor still carries its 600s stall timeout, but idle is 900s. Stall fires first, so (a) the 15-min idle window is dead code and (b) a hot session waiting on operator think-time still dies at 600s — the feature does not achieve arch_045Q0.2 session-lifetime intent.
- MEDIUM-1 (regression): idle resets ONLY on accepted send_input, not on driver output. A single artifactor generation that streams continuously for >900s with no user input is treated as idle and killed mid-generation. Real risk — artifactor runs of 56m are on record.
- LOW-1 (test gap): no production-shaped test that ages last_input_at AND last_driver_event_at together and asserts the release reason; the stall-vs-idle interaction is unexercised.

** Manager rulings (authoritative — build to these)
- RULING 1 (fixes HIGH-1): DISABLE stall for the persistent artifactor. At the Artifactor && rmux gate in api.rs (the same site that sets idle_timeout_secs and mirrors persistent:true), also set stall_timeout_secs: Some(0) so idle becomes the SOLE inactivity gate. Mirror the manager-launch pattern (api.rs ~2113). No other worker kind changes.
- RULING 2 (fixes MEDIUM-1): the idle reference is max(last_input_at, last_driver_event_at) in timed_out_run. This DELIBERATELY broadens the task's original "reset on send_input only" wording: with stall disabled, idle must mean "no accepted input AND no driver output for the idle window" = genuinely abandoned, which survives operator think-time and never aborts a live streaming turn. This ruling supersedes the strict reset-on-input-only semantics from the original F9N5F brief.
- Keep everything the reviewer verified correct: min-deadline fold, last_input_at seeding at run_started_at, the lock discipline, and the Artifactor && rmux gating (the only site idle should be ON). Do not touch those.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Artifactor && rmux runs get stall_timeout_secs: Some(0) (stall disabled); all other kinds unchanged. Test proves a persistent artifactor is NOT released at the old 600s stall point.
- [ ] Idle release fires only when BOTH last_input_at and last_driver_event_at are older than the idle window; a run streaming driver events within the window is never idle-released. Teeth test: aging only the input clock (fresh driver events) must NOT release; aging both must release with reason idle_timeout_exceeded.
- [ ] Production-shaped test ages both clocks together and asserts the release reason + lease freed (LOW-1).
- [ ] Gates: cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon green (redirect to file, do not pipe); clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; fmt --all --check clean. MSRV 1.87.

- [ ] Existing projects (shared =:ID:=) work without file migration.

** Description
Battle-test F1: a freshly registered project 404s ("project not found") on every daemon-backed call until =orgasmic restart=, while the file-backed =orgasmic board= lists it fine — a flat contradiction that cost 3 failed calls plus the time to form the stale-daemon hypothesis. Code confirms a narrow gap: =project init= is file-only (crates/orgasmic-cli/src/main.rs:1155 → orgasmic-core/src/projects.rs:335); the board file IS watched and =refresh_board= (crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/watcher.rs:343, index.rs:455) reloads the project list — but nothing calls =watcher.watch_project= for the new root (per-project watches registered only at boot, lib.rs:273-277), so the new project's files go unwatched/unloaded until restart.

Fix:
- On board refresh, register the filesystem watch + index load for newly appearing projects (canonicalize paths per the /private/var vs /var gotcha in gotchas.org).
- Make the 404 diagnostic for the residual window: when the id exists on the board but is not loaded, say so ("registered after daemon boot — reindex/restart") instead of a bare "project not found".

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Integration test: =project init= against a running daemon → immediate =task update= succeeds, no restart.
- [ ] File edits in the newly registered project trigger reindex (watch actually registered).
- [ ] Board-listed-but-unloaded id → diagnostic 404 naming the cause and fix.

** Description
Battle-test F5 (and the observability half of F4): =parse_errors= reaches agents only as a global opaque count in =/daemon/status= — aggregated across all registered projects, with no project/file/node/reason attribution and no way to tell whether it reflects live reindexing. - =orgasmic reindex [--project <id>]= verb triggering a rebuild and returning fresh per-project counts.

- [ ] An induced dangling ref is fully attributable (project/file/node/reason) from the CLI alone.
- [ ] =reindex= clears the count after a fix without a daemon restart; per-project counts in output.
- [ ] Identical WARNs emitted once per rebuild, not once per pass.

* DONE TASK-WFW1N Worker-driven dispatch finalize verb (orgasmic dispatch finalize) :daemon:cli:dispatch:hardening:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-WFW1N
:MOTIVATED_BY: dec_3M7M0
:PRIORITY: high
:END:

Implements dec_3M7M0. Replace inferred TUI-driver finalization (guess done + scrape scrollback + unconfirmed commit) with a worker-declared completion call over the existing worker->daemon write channel.

** Scope
1. CLI verb `orgasmic dispatch finalize` (worker-side counterpart to `manager dispatch-close`):
   - flags: --run <run-id> (or --task), --status done|failed, --commit (stage+commit the worktree), --summary-file <path> (authoritative report text; also accept stdin), --worker-commit passthrough.
   - Behavior via a daemon endpoint: record the terminal event; write last.txt from --summary-file (NOT scraped); if --commit, commit the worktree; emit implementer.done / reviewer.done (by run kind); release the lease. One daemon call, atomic finalize.
2. Prompt-spec contract: add "your contract ends by calling `orgasmic dispatch finalize --run $RUN_ID --status done --commit --summary-file <report>`" to the implementer + reviewer worker personas (shipped/prompt-studio/prompt-specs or the worker templates), so it is universal, not per-brief. Thread $RUN_ID into the worker env/prompt so the worker knows its run id.
3. Demote the scrape/stall path to FALLBACK: if a finalize event arrived for a run, the release path must NOT overwrite last.txt from scrollback; stall-detection only fires "no finalize within timeout -> mark orphan / rescue-needed", not "assume done + scrape".
4. (Optional, belt-and-suspenders) a harness stop-hook that calls finalize if the worker did not.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `orgasmic dispatch finalize` writes last.txt verbatim from --summary-file (test: content matches input exactly, no scrollback contamination).
- [ ] --commit produces the worktree commit as part of finalize; a finalize with uncommitted changes + --commit leaves a clean committed worktree (commit-stall impossible).
- [ ] finalize emits the correct terminal tx (implementer.done/reviewer.done) and releases the lease; manager dispatch-status shows the run closed.
- [ ] When finalize arrived, the driver release path does NOT scrape/overwrite the report (regression test).
- [ ] When finalize did NOT arrive within the stall window, the run is flagged orphan (not silently marked done) — verified by a test simulating a worker that never finalizes.
- [ ] Worker prompt specs carry the finalize contract; a dispatched worker calls it (verify on a live rmux smoke).
- [ ] gates: daemon + cli green, clippy -D, fmt.

** Notes
Does not fix host-kill-before-finalize (dec_3M7M0 residual): that path yields no finalize event + uncommitted worktree = detectable + rescuable, which is the intended bound. ACP drivers already have protocol finalize; this brings TUI drivers (rmux/tmux) to parity. Reuses manager dispatch-close plumbing where possible (same terminal-tx + lease-release, different caller/authority).

* DONE TASK-QKQ3R dispatch finalize commits wrong root when worktree lacks .orgasmic (greenfield silent work-loss) :dispatch:fix:hardening:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-QKQ3R
:PRIORITY: high
:RELATES_TO: TASK-SQE9P TASK-WFW1N
:END:

Found by the SQE9P live smoke (2026-07-08, isolated 0.0.8 daemon). cmd_dispatch_finalize resolves its commit target via find_project_root() (crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs:1595), which walks UP from cwd looking for .orgasmic/project.org. A dispatch worktree checkout does NOT contain .orgasmic/ whenever the project's .orgasmic is uncommitted (every greenfield project between 'orgasmic project init' and its first commit — the exact DHYXQ bootstrap window). The walk then ESCAPES the worktree (nested at <repo>/.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/<task>/worktree) and resolves the MANAGER'S live repo root. Observed consequence in the smoke: finalize --commit ran 'git add -A && git commit' in the manager repo (sweeping the unrelated uncommitted .orgasmic scaffold + AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md onto the manager's HEAD), stamped THAT sha into the implementer.done tx as SHA/MERGE_SHA, wrote last.txt claiming success — while scripts/greet.sh sat UNCOMMITTED on the dispatch branch (task-05cy5-impl still at base). Silent wrong-target write + fabricated durable-work claim: worst class. Production orgasmic is unaffected only because its .orgasmic/ IS committed (worktrees carry project.org).

Fix direction: the COMMIT boundary must be the git worktree toplevel, not the project-marker walk — use 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' from cwd (stops at the worktree boundary: .git file) for commit_worktree/current_git_branch/WORKTREE tx extra; keep find_project_root only for reading project id (or read it from the daemon's run record instead). Additionally cross-check: refuse --commit when the resolved commit root differs from the run's dispatched WORKTREE (daemon knows it; expose on RunSummary/LiveRunInfo if needed) — fail loudly, never commit a root that isn't the dispatched worktree. Regression test: dispatch-finalize fixture where the project .orgasmic is NOT committed (worktree lacks project.org) → finalize --commit commits ONLY the worktree, never the manager root. Minor bundled polish: finalize_commit_message uses the summary's first line verbatim — strip leading markdown heading markers ('# ') so subjects aren't 'TASK-X: # TASK-X (...)'.

Gates: cargo test -p orgasmic-cli (+ daemon if RunSummary changes), clippy -D, fmt.

* DONE TASK-70VV1 Fix: codex-tmux/rmux dispatch stubs — placeholder-swap gate is claude-only :bug:drivers:dispatch:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-70VV1
:PRIORITY: P1
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/tmux.rs crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/rmux.rs
:END:

** Description
Pre-existing driver bug (present since the initial public release c96f0f3, still in 0.0.10-dev; the live 0.0.9 daemon has it too). Any =implementer-codex-tmux= / =implementer-codex-rmux= dispatch silently stubs: the daemon stages every worker pane with a placeholder command =sh -lc "echo orgasmic pipeline stage acquired; exec sh"= (=api.rs:3221=, `stage_driver_config_with_overrides`), and the terminal driver is supposed to swap that placeholder for the real harness launch. But the swap gate only fires for claude:
- =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/tmux.rs:548-552= `should_use_default_command` returns true only if `cfg.command.is_none()` OR `harness == "claude" && is_dispatch_placeholder(...)`.
- =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/rmux.rs:289-292= same, gated on `(harness == "claude" || harness == "custom") && staged_placeholder`.
For =harness == "codex"= the placeholder is Some("sh") and the claude clause is false, so the driver runs the placeholder shell verbatim and types the compiled prompt into a bare =sh= → cascade of `sh: …: command not found` / `syntax error near unexpected token '('` → `stall_timeout_exceeded` → `outcome: failed`, no files touched. `default_command_for_harness` already maps `"codex" => ("codex", [])` (tmux.rs:584, rmux.rs; unit test `default_command_for_harness("codex").0 == "codex"` passes), so the launch capability exists — only the gate excludes codex.

Evidence: runs run-20260709T115632 (tmux) and run-20260709T121150/121151 (rmux) all failed identically with the placeholder pane command in their driver_config. Daemon is the genuine 0.0.9 release under launchd with codex on its PATH (~/.nvm/.../bin/codex) — not a PATH or binary-missing issue.

** Acceptance Criteria
- [X] `should_use_default_command` in tmux and the rmux equivalent swap the daemon dispatch placeholder for the real harness command for Codex and every known TUI harness.
- [X] Live Codex-rmux and Codex-tmux redesign dispatches launched real Codex turns and produced landed commits.
- [X] Existing Claude and custom behavior remains covered; focused placeholder regression tests pass for both terminal modes.
- [X] After rebuild and daemon restart, the TASK-74TA6 probe produced commit `8fe0c98` and was merged.

Blocks dispatching the entry/workflows redesign (TASK-VBZ24 tree) via codex. Until fixed, those dispatch via claude workers or manager-implement.
