* DONE TASK-WYSMM Mobile: selection-comment quote stuck on first word; extend-selection never updates the composer :ui:bug:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-WYSMM
:END:

On mobile browsers, long-press selects one word and touchend opens the inline comment composer quoting only that word. Dragging the native selection handles to extend the selection never updates the quote: handle drags do not dispatch pointerup/touchend to the page (only document.selectionchange fires), and ArtifactView captures the anchor exactly once on pointerup/touchend/keyup. Fix: keep the captured anchor in sync via a debounced document selectionchange listener while the composer is eligible, re-capturing when the selection is non-collapsed inside the artifact body and preserving the existing quote when the selection collapses (e.g. focusing the textarea).

* DONE TASK-VKP5T External manager self-registration via orgasmic CLI
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-VKP5T
:IMPLEMENTS: dec_3Y2E1
:END:

Implement dec_3Y2E1's registration feature so a manager started outside the app appears in Running Agents as a supervised run.

Scope:
- Daemon: registration endpoint that acquires a run with driver 'external' (no PTY) on the manager.launch:<project> lease, using the SAME lease kind the app's manager launch acquires with (currently kind=Worker per the lease-held error text) so collisions actually collide. Liveness loop: poll the registered terminal session-leader PID ~every 30s, release the run on death; TTL fallback (refreshed by re-register) when no PID was supplied. Same-session re-register = idempotent refresh; different holder = readable refusal naming the holder.
- Drivers: export ORGASMIC_RUN_ID into the environment of every launched PTY session.
- CLI: 'orgasmic manager register' (captures getsid; exits 0 as a no-op with a notice when ORGASMIC_RUN_ID is set) and 'orgasmic manager release'.
- Entry router (shipped/entry/router.org): add one unconditional Manager-startup step: run 'orgasmic manager register'.
- UI: RunningAgentsMenu renders driver 'external' as an info row — click explains that attach is unavailable, an inline End control releases the run. No dock tab.

Risk to test hardest: a stale external lease must never wedge the app's manager launch (the lease-held 500 class). Cover: PID death → release; daemon restart → registration does not survive and lease is free; refusal message paths.

* DONE TASK-2D0EJ Bound worker command-session polling after vanished subprocess :hardening:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-2D0EJ
:PRIORITY: high
:RELATES_TO: TASK-HQR91
:END:

Incident evidence: TASK-HQR91 run run-20260722T063313-f001018601c74ef1a4bc852fd0c9ce98 repeatedly polled unified-exec session 52872 after its OS process disappeared. ACP heartbeats and poll tool events kept daemon liveness fresh, so the run remained apparently healthy until manager intervention.

Harden the shipped worker contract and manager dispatch convention, without provider-specific daemon parsing:

- Long commands must redirect output to a log and expose an atomic status sentinel when practical.
- One owner polls a yielded command. Polling must be bounded: after repeated empty polls or no observable log/status progress, verify the concrete OS process/session instead of trusting a stale running token.
- If the process is gone while the tool session still reports running, stop polling, classify the attempt interrupted, preserve the log, and retry at most once with a single non-restarting detached runner and atomic exit status.
- Never launch a duplicate verification run; enumerate and stop only the manager-owned duplicate if overlap is detected.
- On a second interruption, finalize blocked with evidence rather than loop.
- Manager watchers must have an escalation bound and treat a live worker PID as insufficient proof of progress.

Add deterministic prompt-render/contract tests proving implementer and reviewer bundles inherit the rule. Keep supervisor timeout semantics unchanged in this scoped task; file a separate design task if runtime-level semantic-stall detection is still needed.

:ID: TASK-35TK4
:PRIORITY: high
:READ_SCOPE: .orgasmic/project.org .orgasmic/gotchas.org Cargo.toml crates/orgasmic-core crates/orgasmic-daemon crates/orgasmic-cli
:WRITE_SCOPE: Cargo.toml Cargo.lock crates/orgasmic-daemon crates/orgasmic-cli
:TEST_CMD:    cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon && cargo test -p orgasmic-cli
:END:

Evidence (2026-07-23, operator Mac): launchd-spawned daemons hung forever in pre-bind boot because index.rebuild() runs before bind (lib.rs "AC #1") and git_remote_origin_url (index.rs:1350) spawns `git config --get remote.origin.url` with .output() and no timeout — the child wedged in getcwd/open on a ~/Documents project (launchd-context TCC Files-access stall). Meanwhile launchd respawned instances that each spent minutes in boot work and only then died on EADDRINUSE (the lib.rs:194 retry budget covers only a releasing predecessor), and CLI autostart spawned additional racers; daemon.err.log filled with bind failures across two days. Fix set: (1) wrap the git spawn in tokio::time::timeout (2-5s), kill the child on expiry, degrade repo_url to None; better, resolve repo_url lazily/async after bind and cache it — boot must never depend on spawning git. (2) On macOS, when a scan under ~/Documents, ~/Desktop or ~/Downloads times out, log an actionable hint naming the path and likely missing Files-and-Folders (TCC) access. (3) Take an exclusive flock on $ORGASMIC_HOME/daemon.lock BEFORE any boot work; if held, probe the incumbent over HTTP: healthy incumbent means exit 0 "already running" (keeps launchd quiet), unhealthy/stale means report, never race. Lock-first also moves port/instance conflict detection from after-minutes-of-rebuild to milliseconds. Regressions: hung-git fixture (a fake git that blocks), double-start under launchd KeepAlive, CLI autostart against a booting incumbent.
** Acceptance Criteria
- Acquire an exclusive $ORGASMIC_HOME/daemon.lock before index rebuild, project scanning, git probes, or bind work. A healthy incumbent makes a second start exit cleanly as already running; an unhealthy/stale incumbent produces a bounded actionable error and no racing daemon.
- Boot cannot block indefinitely on git remote discovery: the child has a 2-5 second bound, is killed and reaped on expiry, and repo_url degrades to None. Prefer post-bind lazy/async discovery when it stays inside task scope.
- A timed-out scan under macOS Documents, Desktop, or Downloads logs an actionable Files-and-Folders/TCC hint naming the affected path.
- Deterministic regressions cover a blocking fake git, double-start/KeepAlive behavior, and CLI autostart while an incumbent is still booting.
- cargo fmt --all --check, cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon, cargo test -p orgasmic-cli, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings pass.
** Notes
Independent Claude Opus 4.8/high review of b18808c..bd3d7bd returned SHIP. Focused daemon and CLI boot tests passed. The reviewer transport could not finalize because the daemon run-list endpoint hung, so the verdict was rescued from the completed Claude scratchpad and the dispatch was closed manually with tx evidence. Its one new medium lock-probe overlap finding was subsequently implemented by Codex gpt-5.6-terra/high under TASK-870YX in 4c0a151, merged as e4b6b7b, and independently reverified with focused daemon/CLI regressions.

* DONE TASK-KWSTJ P0 prove and finish bounded GET /api/runs plus exact-run terminal paths :daemon:recovery:bug:
:PROPERTIES:
:DEPENDS_ON: TASK-JN5Q1
:ID: TASK-KWSTJ
:PRIORITY: P0
:END:

Build on, do not discard, the existing uncommitted TASK-JN5Q1 patch. First preserve its diff and rerun its focused gates. Reproduce against a fresh curl output path and record time-to-headers, time-to-body-complete, HTTP framing headers, response counts, and inventory stage timings. Treat the report claim that a complete stale file proves response serialization as disproven unless a packet/wire probe reproduces it.

Implementation boundary:
1. `GET /api/runs` must never await unbounded driver work. Terminal tombstones do no attach probe; genuine attach probes share one absolute deadline, have capped concurrency, and are aborted/joined on timeout.
2. Inventory construction must not parse multi-megabyte transcript bodies to answer lifecycle questions. Read a bounded lifecycle summary/catalog representation; legacy fallback may inspect a capped prefix/tail and must classify uncertainty conservatively. No per-failed-run whole-board rescan.
3. Exact recorded run ids use `/runs/:id` and `/runs/:id/release`; `dispatch-close` and explicit-id finalize never enumerate `/runs`. Legacy records without a run id retain a safe reachability fence.
4. Add stage metrics/logs for file count, bytes inspected, attach count/timeouts, classification counts, and total inventory latency without logging transcript content or local secrets.

Required regression is wire-level: seed production-shaped terminal, failed, interrupted, missing-worktree, and one permanently hanging attach record, including at least one very large transcript fixture or sparse file. Perform an authenticated HTTP request with a hard deadline; assert headers arrive, the body reaches EOF, JSON parses, classification counts are correct, and a second request does not rescan transcript bytes. Also run direct-close and explicit-finalize tests through a proxy that rejects `/api/runs`.

Acceptance target: p95 warm inventory below 250 ms on 200 records; cold legacy reconciliation is bounded and cannot exceed the CLI request budget. Verify with the real 197-file/2.239-GiB shape using a non-mutating fixture or snapshot. Run daemon, CLI dispatch, fmt, clippy, and diff-check gates. Do not delete or rewrite operator session history in this task.
** Evidence
Wire reproduction against the live pre-fix daemon (0.0.14, pid 11674, 5 projects, 198 session files totalling 2.239 GiB), fresh curl output path:
- `GET /api/runs` -> HTTP/1.1 200, `content-type: application/json`, `content-length: 120579`, `size_download: 120579`.
- `time_connect` 0.000286 s, `time_starttransfer` (headers/first byte) *35.205 s*, `time_total` (body complete) 35.207 s.
- Framing is therefore correct and the body does reach EOF; the body transfers in 1.4 ms once it starts. The "complete stale JSON file proves serialization" claim is disproven as an explanation, and the earlier "no headers, zero bytes" observation is a client deadline expiring inside the 35 s time-to-first-byte, not a serialization defect.

Source-backed cause, measured on the same real corpus (release build, read-only, non-mutating):
- Whole-transcript enumeration read 2.239 GiB / 428,992 envelopes in 3.08 s per pass, and the recovery-origin index re-read the whole board again whenever a failed tombstone existed, on top of serial driver attach probes.
- Bounded lifecycle scan reads 26.67 MiB in 95.3 ms over the same 198 files (135 truncated, 0 parse errors): 86x fewer bytes, 32x faster, and inside the 250 ms warm target.

Fix, on top of the preserved TASK-JN5Q1 patch (its focused gates rerun green before any new edit):
- `orgasmic_core::scan_session_lifecycle` reads a prefix/tail byte window (128 KiB + 64 KiB by default) and retains only lifecycle-relevant envelopes, rejecting transcript lines from their raw bytes without parsing. Budget sized from the real corpus: the furthest a lifecycle-deciding line ever sat was 56 KiB from the start and 13 KiB from the end.
- Truncation is conservative: `final_envelope_retained` gates the terminal-release decision, so a still-writing run is never tombstoned from a stale retained lifecycle line, and a missing acquire still classifies `ambiguous`.
- Inventory (`classify_session_dir`), the recovery-origin index (through the same pinned-directory, device/inode-validated fd), and `resolve_run_session_path` all use the bounded scan. Boot auto-reattach deliberately still reads whole files; that is TASK-5P60H's slow-start scope.
- `InventoryStageMetrics` (file count, on-disk bytes, bytes inspected, truncated/unreadable counts, attach probes started/timed out, origin-index files and bytes, per-classification counts, duration) is emitted as a `tracing::debug!` and returned on `GET /api/runs` as `inventory`. Counts and byte totals only: no session paths, transcript text, prompts, or credentials.

Regression added, `crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/run_inventory_wire.rs` (raw HTTP/1.1 over TCP, `Connection: close` so EOF is observable, 5 s hard deadline):
- `runs_endpoint_completes_over_the_wire_with_a_hanging_worker_and_huge_transcripts` seeds terminal (32 MiB transcript), failed, interrupted, missing-worktree, and one record whose driver attach never answers (stub `tmux` that sleeps 600 s). Asserts the status line and JSON content-type arrive, the body reaches EOF non-empty and parses, per-bucket classification is exact, the hung probe is recorded as `exceeded inventory deadline` with `attach_probes_timed_out == 1`, and inspected bytes stay at the fixed per-record ceiling. A second request inspects exactly the same byte window, proving transcript bytes are never rescanned.
- `runs_endpoint_stays_bounded_across_two_hundred_records` seeds 200 terminal records (every 40th carrying a 4 MiB transcript) and asserts 200 classified, bounded bytes, and a warm response well inside the request budget.
- Direct-close and explicit-id finalize keep passing through the `/api/runs`-rejecting proxy (`dispatch_close_with_recorded_run_id_does_not_enumerate_runs`, `stage_grill_finalize_from_orgasmic_run_id_on_main`).

Gates: `cargo fmt` clean, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` clean, `git diff --check` clean, `npm run typecheck` clean. orgasmic-core 132 lib + 26 fixture tests pass (plus one opt-in ignored real-corpus measurement). orgasmic-daemon lib 500 tests and every integration binary pass. orgasmic-cli dispatch 39 tests pass. Pre-existing failures unrelated to this change, verified identical on clean `main` by stashing: `orgasmic-drivers` `simulated_acquire_emits_deterministic_flow`, and the three `dispatch_endpoint` tests that need a stub `codex` on PATH. Under full-parallel load the daemon and CLI suites also show load flakes (tmux/git/daemon-connect timing) that all pass when rerun serially; the same class of flake was present before this change. One stale assertion from the TASK-JN5Q1 patch was corrected: `manager_session_after_restart_is_recovered_not_lost` now expects the `does not support runtime reattach` reason that acp-stdio records instead of a driver probe.

No operator session history was deleted or rewritten.
** Reviewer pass
Production-shape verification, 2026-07-25, against an APFS copy-on-write clone of the real 200-file / 2.404 GB session corpus in an isolated scratch `ORGASMIC_HOME` on port 4899. The clone makes the measurement non-mutating by construction: writes cannot reach the originals, and the installed runtime was never involved.

Same corpus, same endpoint, three requests each:

| build | ttfb req1 | req2 | req3 |
| installed 0.0.14 (pre-fix) | 24.695 s | 24.809 s | 24.840 s |
| source build (fix)         | 0.105 s  | 0.096 s | 0.097 s |

Roughly 255x faster, and inside the 250 ms warm p95 acceptance target with margin. The endpoint's own reported metrics for the fixed build: 200 session files, 2,404,437,937 bytes on disk, 28,016,305 bytes inspected (86x reduction), 135 truncated scans, 1 attach probe started and 0 timed out, duration_ms 95.

Correctness, which matters more than the latency: the two builds were compared run-by-run across every classification bucket.

- runs classified: old 200, new 200
- present only in old: 0
- present only in new: 0
- classification differences: 0

So the bounded prefix/tail scan produces an identical classification of the entire production corpus while reading 86x fewer bytes, including across the 135 files where the middle region was skipped. This is the evidence the reviewer brief asked for under "attack the bounded-window premise" — the premise holds on real data, not just on fixtures.

* DONE TASK-9P810 Install the runtime to a stable, identity-checked path so TCC grants survive upgrades :install:runtime:macos:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-9P810
:PRIORITY: P0
:END:

Problem: every runtime version costs the operator a macOS permission approval. Measured 2026-07-25 on one machine: 16 distinct runtime paths have been granted, 37 TCC rows in total, since 2026-06-18 — 0.0.1, 0.99.601, 0.0.3, 0.0.6, 0.0.7, three separate 0.0.8 nightlies, and so on through 0.0.13 and 0.0.14. Each one is a System Settings dialog the operator had to find and click, and a daemon that does not work until they do.

Cause: TCC keys a grant to the resolved executable path. The install layout is `~/.orgasmic/runtimes/<version>/bin/orgasmic`, reached through `~/.orgasmic/bin/orgasmic -> ../current/bin/orgasmic -> runtimes/<version>/...`. TCC resolves the symlinks, so it records the versioned path and every release is a new client with no permissions.

The signature is not the problem, and that is the useful part. The designated requirement is identity-based, not byte-based:

  identifier "com.theaspirational.orgasmic" and certificate root = H"a70531007cd128ff081597cb27bee0816613d86d"

A rebuilt binary re-signed with the same `orgasmic dev codesign` certificate satisfies that requirement, so content changes at a fixed path should inherit the grant. The two halves together are the fix: hold the path still and hold the identity still, and one approval covers every future version.

Work:
1. Make the executed binary a real file at a stable path (`~/.orgasmic/bin/orgasmic`) that install/update replaces in place. Keep versioned directories as rollback artifacts, but stop routing execution through a per-version path.
2. Replace with a fresh inode, never overwrite in place — an in-use codesigned binary overwritten in place is silently SIGKILLed on every later exec (existing gotchas entry).
3. Re-sign each installed binary with the pinned identity, so the designated requirement continues to match.
4. Refuse the install when the incoming binary's designated requirement differs from the incumbent's, naming both. This is the guard for item 3: a mis-signed binary should be a rejected install, not a daemon that boots without permissions. Observed 2026-07-25 — an ad-hoc `codesign --force --sign -` replaced the certificate root and cost the operator two separate GUI grants to recover.
5. Decide what `update` does about the LaunchAgent's `ProgramArguments`, which currently names `~/.orgasmic/bin/orgasmic`. If that becomes the real binary the plist may not need rewriting at all, which is its own win.
6. Migration: existing installs already have grants against versioned paths. Decide whether the first stable-path install needs one final approval and say so in the update output, rather than letting the operator discover a dead daemon.

Not in scope: Developer ID signing and notarization. That would anchor the requirement to Apple and a Team ID and is the right answer for distributing to other people, but the operator has deliberately deferred it; this task must work with the existing self-signed identity.

Acceptance:
- upgrading between two runtime versions requires no new permission approval
- a binary signed by a different identity is refused at install time with both requirements named
- the executed binary is replaced by fresh inode, never overwritten in place
- rollback to a prior version still works

Implemented manager-direct. New =crates/orgasmic-cli/src/managed_binary.rs= owns
the single publish path; =update.rs=, =path_env.rs=, =doctor=, =daemon_service=
and =scripts/install.sh= all route through it.

Root cause confirmed, and it differs from the one assumed when this was filed.
The LaunchAgent already named =~/.orgasmic/bin/orgasmic=, so the plist was never
the problem: =env::current_exe()= on macOS returns the *invocation* path (probed
directly), and the kernel resolves the symlink at =exec=. =codesign -d= on the
link confirms it, printing =Executable=.../runtimes/0.0.14-darwin-aarch64/...=.
So item 5 resolves to "no plist rewrite needed" — but =service_spec= now names
the managed binary explicitly, because starting the daemon from a versioned path
would have pinned the service to a directory that retention later prunes.

Item 3 also resolves differently. A release bundle is already signed with the
pinned identity by =package-runtime.sh=, and the signature is embedded in the
Mach-O, so copying preserves it — verified: installing the real 0.0.14 binary
into a scratch home reproduces
=identifier "com.theaspirational.orgasmic" and certificate root = H"a705...d86d"=
byte for byte, and a second install of the same identity reports grants as
preserved. Re-signing at install time is therefore opt-in
(=$ORGASMIC_CODESIGN_IDENTITY=) and exists for contributor source builds, which
carry a linker signature that would otherwise be refused. Operators do not need
the signing key.

A real bug was caught before shipping. The first requirement parser missed
ad-hoc signatures, which =codesign= prints *commented out* (=# designated =>=),
reading them as "identity unknown" and waving them through — i.e. it would have
permitted the exact 2026-07-25 accident this guard exists to stop. Covered now
by a hermetic test that ad-hoc-signs a Mach-O and asserts the refusal end to
end, including that a refused install leaves the incumbent byte-identical.

=codesign= is invoked as =/usr/bin/codesign=, not through PATH: it decides
whether a binary keeps the operator's grants, so a shadowing binary must not be
able to answer for it.

Acceptance:
- no approval between versions — proven at the identity level: same requirement
  in and out, =preserves_grants()= true on re-install
- different identity refused with both requirements named — hermetic test
- fresh inode never in-place — inode compared across an upgrade
- rollback still works — restores from the previous runtime dir and bypasses the
  guard by design, since it restores what the operator already approved

* DONE TASK-KKGKM A project the daemon cannot read must not prevent it from binding :daemon:boot:resilience:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-KKGKM
:PRIORITY: P0
:RELATES_TO: TASK-3R3EZ TASK-5P60H
:END:

Problem: when the daemon lacks filesystem permission for a registered project's path, it does not degrade — it dies. Reproduced 2026-07-25 after a runtime binary swap invalidated the macOS TCC grant for `~/Documents`:

- boot logged `starting pre-bind boot work`, then only `project scan timed out` warnings, then nothing
- the process sat at 0% CPU for minutes, never reaching `listening`
- `lsof` showed no project files open at all, only its own log, lock and binary — consistent with a permission-gated `open()` blocking in the kernel before a descriptor exists
- launchd `KeepAlive` kept spawning replacements, each refusing with `daemon instance lock is held, but the incumbent is not healthy`, so the machine churned without recovering
- the only operator-visible signal was a WARN line in a log file nobody was watching; `orgasmic status` simply hung

The daemon never bound, so every CLI verb, the UI, and the app were dead. A permission problem affecting a subset of projects took down the whole runtime.

The scan timeout works as designed — it logs "omitting project so daemon boot can continue" — but something after it blocks anyway. Find that, and make the whole class non-fatal.

Work:
1. Bind first, or at minimum guarantee that no per-project filesystem work can prevent binding. An operator must always be able to reach `status` and the UI to learn why the runtime is unhealthy.
2. Give a project whose files cannot be read a durable `unavailable` state with the reason, rather than retrying it into a hang. This is the same state TASK-3R3EZ introduces for missing project roots; reuse it rather than inventing a parallel one.
3. Report the condition where an operator will actually see it: `orgasmic status` and `orgasmic doctor` should name the affected projects and the exact remedy, not just emit a WARN into `daemon.out.log`.
4. Identify what blocks after the index scan completes. Boot reattach reads every session JSONL and is the leading suspect, but it was not confirmed — no fd was open at the time of sampling. Confirm before fixing.
5. Bound the launchd churn: repeated replacements refusing on the instance lock is noise that hides the real fault. Relates to TASK-5P60H's backoff work.
6. Regression: a registered project whose path is unreadable must still leave the daemon bound, reporting that project as unavailable.

Acceptance:
- an unreadable project cannot prevent the daemon from binding
- `status` and `doctor` name the affected project and the remedy
- the daemon stays useful for every other project
- a regression covers the unreadable-project case

ITEM 4 CONFIRMED (2026-07-25) — the task said confirm before fixing, so it was
reproduced rather than assumed.

Built an isolated throwaway ORGASMIC_HOME with two registered projects and
planted a FIFO where a session JSONL belongs. A FIFO with no writer blocks
inside open() before a descriptor exists, which is the same shape as the
permission-gated open in the original incident, and it is deterministic without
touching TCC.

Baseline with both projects healthy: bound in 44 ms.
With the blocking session file present:
- never reached listening; curl exit 7 (connection refused) indefinitely
- daemon.boot froze at {"phase": "reattaching runs", "seq": 7}, refreshed_at
  stuck at the boot instant while wall clock advanced 33 s
- 0% CPU, and lsof showed zero descriptors on the blocking file — exactly the
  "no fd was open when the process was sampled" observation from the incident,
  now explained: the process is blocked *inside* open(), before an fd exists
- stack sample:
    tokio::runtime::park::CachedParkThread::block_on
      orgasmic_daemon::api::reattach_live_runs_on_boot
        orgasmic_core::session::read_session_file
          std::fs::read_to_string

So the leading suspect was right, and there is a second finding the task did not
anticipate: the scan runs synchronously on the main thread inside block_on, so
it also starves the boot-progress refresh task. That is why the operator's only
liveness signal froze and `orgasmic status` simply hung — the heartbeat could
not advance even to report the phase it was stuck in.

FIX
1. Boot auto-reattach now runs after the listener is bound, in a spawned task.
   It is best-effort recovery; answering status is what an operator needs in
   order to diagnose anything at all.
2. Its file reads moved to spawn_blocking, so a wedged read costs one blocking
   thread instead of a runtime worker.
3. Session paths that are not regular files are refused by shape with a named
   warning, rather than discovered by hanging.

Verified end to end on the same isolated home: binds in ~50 ms with the
blocking file still present, /api/daemon/status answers in 1.6 ms, and the
warning names the offending path.

REGRESSION
crates/orgasmic-daemon/tests/boot_resilience.rs covers both the blocking-open
case and an unreadable project directory. Both were verified to fail against the
reverted fix, not merely to pass against the current one.

The first version of that test used tokio::time::timeout and hung forever
instead of failing: a synchronous block inside a future stalls the task
mid-poll, so the timer fires but the task can never be woken to observe it. It
now boots on an owned thread and waits on a channel deadline, and a reverted fix
reports itself cleanly at 20.02 s with a message stating the invariant.

NOT DONE HERE, and why:
- Item 2 (durable `unavailable` project state) is the state model TASK-3R3EZ
  introduces. The task says to reuse it rather than invent a parallel one, and
  3R3EZ has not landed, so inventing it here would be something 3R3EZ has to
  unpick.
- Item 3 (status/doctor naming the affected project) depends on that state
  existing to report.
- Item 5 (bounding launchd churn) belongs with TASK-5P60H's backoff work.
- Boot reattach still reads whole session files. That is cost, not a hang, now
  that it is off the critical path; filed as TASK-7QM8M with the correctness
  subtlety that blocks a naive swap to the bounded scanner.

Findings, as filed: tx-20260726-orgasmic-2942 through -2946.

HIGH 1 — the salvage commit is not anchored to the recorded dispatch branch.
manager.rs:1432-1445 and api.rs:4496-4551 commit whatever HEAD the worktree
currently has; neither helper is told which branch was recorded. The later
retention guards keep the RECORDED branch merely because salvage.is_some().

MANAGER-CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY, not taken on the reviewer's word. In a scratch
repo: worktree on task-probe-impl, dirty file, `git checkout --detach`, then
add+commit exactly as commit_worktree does. Result — the salvage sha is NOT an
ancestor of the recorded branch, and `git for-each-ref --points-at` returns
nothing. The commit is unreferenced and prunable by `git gc`. So the close tx
advertises a recovery path that git is free to delete.

HIGH 2 — a late writer between the dirty check and `--force`. The CLI's last
clean check is manager.rs:1414-1440 and removal is manager.rs:2080-2084; the
daemon has the same gap at api.rs:4534-4551 vs 4569-4573. Anything writing in
that window produces a dirty worktree that `--force` then deletes silently. No
lock, and removal is not fail-closed.

MEDIUM 3 — a concurrent CLI close can delete another close's salvage branch.
manager.rs:2268-2273 checks only whether THIS invocation salvaged, then runs
unfenced `git branch -D`. Two concurrent `--branch-delete` closes: one salvages
and removes, the other sees salvage=None and deletes the branch now pointing at
the first salvage. The daemon path is already fenced with an expected OID; the
CLI is not.

LOW 4 — the CLI dirty + --branch-delete path is untested. Confirmed: the three
new CLI tests all pass branch_delete=false. This was the manager's own finding
and the reviewer ranked it correctly BELOW the three above.

LOW 5 — SALVAGE_FILE_COUNT under-reports. manager.rs:1381-1385 and
api.rs:4504-4507 count porcelain records, and default `git status --porcelain`
collapses an untracked directory into a single `?? dir/` entry. The tx promises a
file count and records a status-entry count.

FIX DIRECTION, from the reviewer and endorsed:
1. Pass the expected dispatch branch and OID into both salvage helpers. Require
   symbolic HEAD to match, or atomically move the intended ref from its
   pre-salvage OID to SALVAGE_SHA. Fail BEFORE removal on mismatch. Consider the
   reviewer's open question: a dedicated durable ref under refs/orgasmic/salvage/
   would make the tx sha independently reachable and simplify --branch-delete.
2. Stop using unconditional `--force` after salvage. Fail-closed removal plus a
   cleanup lock spanning final validation through removal, and a deterministic
   late-writer test.
3. In CLI close, never delete a branch after worktree missing/failure, and
   replace `git branch -D` with expected-OID `update-ref -d` fencing.
4. Tests: dirty + --branch-delete, detached HEAD / switched branch, removal
   failure after salvage, duplicate close, nested untracked directory. Mirror
   branch-identity and late-writer coverage on the daemon side.

Verified 2026-07-26 by reading the cleanup paths after the operator asked
whether a stuck dispatch can end with its work unrecoverable. It can, and the
destructive behaviour is the default.

THE PATH

`orgasmic manager dispatch-close` declares `--worktree-remove` with
`default_value_t = true` (crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs:124) and
`--branch-delete` with `default_value_t = false`. Removal is
`git worktree remove --force` (manager.rs:2007; the daemon does the same at
crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs:4438). `--force` is exactly the flag that makes
git delete a DIRTY worktree instead of refusing.

No dirty check guards it. `worktree_has_uncommitted_changes` exists at
manager.rs:1331 but is only consumed by `commit_worktree` on the worker-driven
`dispatch finalize --commit` path. Nothing consults it before removal.

The two guards that do run before removal —
`validate_dispatch_cleanup_targets` and `verify_dispatch_worktree_identity` —
protect against deleting the WRONG worktree. Neither protects against deleting
UNSAVED WORK.

THE SCENARIO, WHICH IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL

1. A worker does real work and never reaches `dispatch finalize --commit`,
   because its harness dies. Observed today: the TASK-STWVB run emitted
   `run_complete` at 09:54:47 and `claude exited with status exit status: 143`
   at 09:54:48.
2. The run can then sit live for a long time (80 minutes, observed).
3. The manager reaches for the documented cleanup verb,
   `dispatch-close --status aborted`.
4. Default flags delete the worktree with `--force`. Uncommitted work is gone,
   with no prompt, and no tx entry recording that anything was discarded.
5. The branch survives, because branch-delete defaults false. If the worker never
   committed, that branch sits at the base commit and holds nothing — so the
   surviving branch creates a false impression of recoverability.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG, so nobody widens this

There is no automatic or background pruning of dispatch worktrees. No retention
sweep touches them. The loss always requires an explicit manager action. The
problem is not a daemon deleting things unasked; it is that the verb the manager
is instructed to use is destructive by default, at exactly the moment a worker
has failed and its output is most likely to be uncommitted.

In practice the opposite failure dominates: 17 worktrees are on disk right now,
including several from 2026-07-23. Cleanup usually is not run at all. That makes
the risk distribution the worst possible shape — litter for the careless, silent
data loss for the conscientious.

FIX

`commit_worktree` already exists, so the cheap fix loses nothing and needs no
judgment call:
1. Before removing a worktree, test it with `worktree_has_uncommitted_changes`.
   If dirty, make a salvage commit on the dispatch branch (which already survives
   by default) with a message naming the task and that it was manager-salvaged,
   then remove.
2. Record the salvage in the close tx — sha and file count — so the recovery
   story is discoverable from state rather than from memory.
3. Consider making `--worktree-remove` default false for `--status aborted`
   specifically. A done close follows a worker that committed; an aborted close
   is by definition the case where it did not.
4. Say what happened in the CLI output. "worktree removed" should distinguish
   clean removal from salvaged-then-removed.

Related: TASK-TJKFC already states the right principle for the other half of this
("once startup has been accepted and meaningful work has occurred, later failures
retain normal failed-run history and inspection artifacts"), and that half is
unimplemented.

Acceptance:
- closing a dispatch whose worktree is dirty never loses the diff
- the salvage is recoverable from tx alone, without knowing the branch name
- a clean close behaves exactly as it does today

dominant failure (17 worktrees on disk). Accepted.

FINDING 1 (HIGH, the ship blocker) — crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/rmux.rs:1319. The liveness source observes newline-terminated LINES, not pane output BYTES. DriverEvent::PaneActivity is documented at orgasmic-core/src/session.rs:264 as proof the pane "wrote bytes", but spawn_pane_exit_watch subscribes to PaneLineStream and only calls the throttle after lines.next() returns (rmux.rs:1818-1824). The pinned rmux-sdk 0.9.0 buffers bytes until LF (or a 1 MiB partial-line safety flush), so ANSI/cursor/carriage-return redraws of an in-place status line produce NO item. A healthy full-screen TUI can write for the entire stall window while last_driver_event_at stays frozen — recreating TASK-RWCRN exactly. The production smoke does not catch this because its fixture is `while :; do echo tick; ...` (rmux.rs:3248-3251), which guarantees an LF per update. FIX: consume PaneOutputStream raw byte chunks, persisting only a bounded count and never content. Add a live smoke whose pane writes CHANGING NON-NEWLINE output for longer than the coalescing interval.

Both rmux codex reviewer panes survived past 600s (12.4 min and 10.2 min, 16 and 12 pane_activity events, terminal run_complete not a stall release), but codex emits newline output. That evidence is real and does not generalise to a redraw-only TUI. Treat the acceptance as unproven for full-screen harnesses.

An rmux TUI worker emits no driver events while it works, so the supervisor's
600-second stall detector fires on a healthy, actively-working run and kills it.
Every rmux dispatch dies at exactly ten minutes. This makes the standing worker
matrix (operator-set 2026-07-26: every dispatch runs in an rmux pane)
unusable as written.

MEASURED, first rmux dispatch under the new matrix. TASK-6AYEJ,
implementer-claude-rmux (rmux / claude / claude-opus-5 / high), run
run-20260726T193954-5ce5327e7b854438843e7f592f66dc4d. Its whole event stream,
from .orgasmic/tmp/sessions/dispatch-TASK-6AYEJ-implementer-20260726T193954.jsonl:

    seq 0-2  19:39:54.697-.717  lifecycle
    seq 3    19:39:54.752       driver_event  ready
             ...600 seconds of silence...
    seq 4    19:49:54.786       driver_event  run_complete
    seq 5    19:49:54.798       lifecycle     released

`manager.dispatch_orphaned` (tx-20260726-orgasmic-2979) landed at 19:49:55 with
"worker never called `orgasmic dispatch finalize` before the run was released".
The worker's own transcript shows it editing crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/dispatch.rs
at 19:49:51 — one second before the kill — and its claude process was left as a
zombie (pid 37956, STAT Z). It had produced 266 insertions across two files and
the tree compiles. It was not stalled by any definition except the daemon's.

MECHANISM. supervisor.rs:3410 computes
`last_activity_at = rec.last_input_at.max(rec.last_driver_event_at)`, and
DEFAULT_STALL_TIMEOUT (supervisor.rs:65) is 600s. In acp-stdio the driver
streams events continuously, so this is at worst too lenient — that is
TASK-VZMZE, where 30-second heartbeats defeat the timeout entirely. In rmux the
opposite holds: the pane is a terminal, not an event source, so
`last_driver_event_at` freezes at `ready` and the timeout is guaranteed to fire
at exactly 600s no matter what the worker is doing. Same line of code, two
opposite failures, and the pair should probably be fixed together.

THE MECHANISM FOR THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS AND IS DOCUMENTED. `stall_timeout_secs:
Some(0)` disables the detector, described at supervisor.rs:149-152 as being for
"interactive, operator-paced runs (the manager) that legitimately idle at a
prompt". supervisor.rs:1732 already applies exactly that to manager tasks via
`is_interactive_manager_task`. An rmux worker has the same shape: no driver
events, attachable, operator-paced.

DO NOT JUST SET IT TO ZERO AND STOP. Disabling the detector for rmux removes the
only thing that catches a genuinely wedged pane, leaving DEFAULT_MAX_RUN_DURATION
(14400s = 4 hours) as the sole backstop. A wedged rmux worker would then burn
four hours before anyone noticed. TASK-RRT4T's first attempt wedged for 60
minutes with 0 tool calls and 6.77s of CPU, so this is a real shape, not a
hypothetical. Whatever lands must still be able to distinguish "working" from
"wedged" for a pane. Candidates worth weighing in the report: pane output
activity as a liveness signal, the worker's own tool-call cadence in the session
jsonl, sampled CPU time of the pane's process group, or a periodic driver_event
emitted by the rmux driver itself. Argue the choice; do not silently pick the
cheapest.

Interim workaround, already in use: pass
`--governance-json '{"stall_timeout_secs": 0}'` on rmux dispatches. Record it in
the manager-dispatch convention until this lands, and remove it after.

Acceptance:
- an rmux dispatch that works continuously for well over 10 minutes is not
  released, proven by an actual long dispatch rather than a unit test alone
- a genuinely wedged rmux pane is still detected and released, with the
  detection signal named and tested
- the acp-stdio path is unchanged, or changed only in coordination with
  TASK-VZMZE
- a released rmux run does not leave a zombie harness process or an orphaned
  rmux session behind

The new default sentinel works and is not in question. Independently probed on
current HEAD with a stripped PATH and both `ORGASMIC_RUN_ID` and
`ORGASMIC_ALLOW_MISSING_TOOLS` unset, the daemon sentinel exited 101, named
`rmux (gates 7 tests)` and `tmux (gates 6 tests)`, stated the gated tests did not
run, and printed the per-tool opt-out. The original hidden-PATH scenario is
fixed. `ORGASMIC_ALLOW_MISSING_TOOLS` is set nowhere in the tree, so the opt-out
cannot be inherited accidentally.

What blocks is that "a compatible binary is on PATH" was treated as equivalent to
"a live session was really acquired", and three false-green paths survive that
gap.

** 1. HIGH — four live-rmux tests still accept an inert session (in this diff)

`crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/rmux.rs:3171-3175,3244-3249,3357-3360,3402-3404`.

`f894a7a` converted each test's missing-binary guard to `skip_test_if_missing`
and introduced `assert_not_degraded`, but left the pre-existing
inert-success branches in place. `run_live_session` converts **every** SDK or
daemon startup error into an inert `Ready` (`rmux.rs:765-810`), while the binary
sentinel (`modes/tmux.rs:2532-2542`) only proves a compatible executable exists.

So a compatible `rmux` **plus** an SDK/daemon connection failure makes the
sentinel pass while `live_rmux_session_lifecycle_when_available`,
`live_rmux_streams_output_and_completes_on_exit`,
`live_rmux_session_exports_orgasmic_run_id` and
`live_rmux_process_exit_emits_run_complete_without_text_chunks` all report success
without exercising their named behaviour. That is the false-green class this task
exists to remove, surviving in the very tests it was filed about.

Required: route all four retained inert branches through `assert_not_degraded`.
A live test must fail when acquisition degrades to inert.

** 2. HIGH — `rmux_release_reaps_session` is a default-running binary with no
   sentinel (pre-existing, missed by the audit)

`crates/orgasmic-drivers/tests/rmux_release_reaps_session.rs:60-77,109-119`.

It still prints `SKIPPED` and returns success when `rmux` is unavailable or
acquisition degrades to inert. It has no `required_test_tooling_is_present`
sentinel and is not `#[ignore]`.
`git diff --exit-code f894a7a^1 f894a7a -- <that file>` returns 0, so the
tree-wide audit missed it. `cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers --test
rmux_release_reaps_session` can still print a clean pass with no live release or
reap assertion — contradicting the one-sentinel-per-affected-binary design.

Note this is the same file TASK-69CW6 (the TASK-6FNAY fix round) must also
change, for the adjacent reason that `ORGASMIC_REQUIRE_LIVE_RMUX` is set nowhere.
**Coordinate: these two rounds must not be dispatched concurrently.**

Required: put it under the shared per-binary sentinel contract, or make it an
explicit `#[ignore]` live smoke that fails loudly when invoked without a usable
live session.

** 3. HIGH — the shared environment lock does not cover every availability probe
   (pre-existing)

`crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/adapters/claude.rs:1863-1874,1926-1935`.

`gate_simulates_for_empty_endpoint_stdio_when_claude_missing` holds the shared
lock and sets process-global `PATH=""`.

returns through `skip_test_if_missing`, then the library sentinel waits for PATH

Required: acquire `test_environment_lock` before **every** availability probe
that can race with process-environment mutation, and hold it through the guarded
test.

The task's stated mechanism — "launchd does not carry `~/.local/bin`" — does not
hold on this machine, measured 2026-07-28 (tx-20260728-orgasmic-3134): the plist

Eight rmux-dependent tests in `crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs` silently
return (and therefore PASS) when `rmux` is not on PATH:

    if !rmux_available_for_test() {
        eprintln!("skipping <name>: rmux binary not found");
        return;
    }

`rmux_available_for_test()` is `probe_rmux_binary().found`, which resolves
`rmux` from PATH only (crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/rmux.rs:197-210). The
skip prints to stderr, which `cargo test` swallows without `--nocapture`. The
run then reports `504 passed; 0 failed` — literally true, and completely
misleading.

MEASURED 2026-07-26, manager-direct, on main at the TASK-STWVB merge, same
machine, same commit, one variable changed:

| PATH                             | result          | wall   | syspolicyd CPU |
|----------------------------------|-----------------|--------|----------------|
| normal (rmux on ~/.local/bin)    | 502 passed, 2 failed | 106.5 s | +281 s |
| /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin... | 504 passed, 0 failed |  22.3 s | + 32 s |

The second row reproduces, to the second, what the TASK-STWVB round-2
implementer reported as proof its fix worked: 504/0 at 24.9 / 27.5 / 26.1 s.
Its fix did not green those tests; its environment skipped them.

WHY THIS IS P0

This is the mechanism behind three consecutive over-reports today:
- TASK-8W30B: worker measured +5 leaked sessions/run, manager measured +1
- TASK-6FNAY: worker reported 504/0, manager measured 502/2 three times
- TASK-STWVB r2: worker reported 504/0 x3, manager measured 502/2 four times

Every one is the same shape, and the shape is not worker dishonesty — each
phrased its claim carefully. A dispatched worker inherits the daemon's PATH.
The daemon runs under launchd, which does not carry `~/.local/bin`, so `rmux`
is absent for workers and present for the operator. Worker green on this crate
therefore does not mean what it says, and no amount of brief discipline fixes
it.

Corroborating evidence in the round-2 report itself: it recorded
`orgasmic-rmux-run-*` sessions as 7 before / 7 after three runs. A real run of
`post_artifact_regenerate_hot_path_reuses_live_run_id` creates rmux sessions,
and the manager's runs grew 7 -> 10 (+1 per run, the known panic-abandon).
Zero growth was the tell that the test never ran.

FIX

1. A skipped test must be visible in the default `cargo test` summary. Options,
   in preference order: (a) make the guard `panic!` unless an explicit
   `ORGASMIC_ALLOW_SKIP_RMUX_TESTS=1` opt-out is set, so the default is loud;
   (b) mark them `#[ignore]` and run them via an explicit filtered gate, so the
   summary counts them as ignored rather than passed.
2. Whatever the mechanism, `cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon --lib` must not be
   able to print `504 passed; 0 failed` while eight tests did nothing.
3. Give dispatched workers a PATH that finds the tools their gates need, OR
   make the worker persona report the skip count with every test claim. Prefer
   the first; the second is a documentation fix for an environment defect.
4. Audit for the same pattern elsewhere: any `if !X_available() { return }` in
   a test is the same trap. tmux and cursor-agent guards are the likely
   siblings.

Acceptance:
- with rmux absent, the daemon suite cannot report a clean all-passed summary
- the count of skipped-for-missing-tooling tests is visible without --nocapture
- a manager reading a worker's test claim can tell whether the scoped test ran

Found by the TASK-6AYEJ.2 reviewer (run-20260728T063207-654ec2af0d5140ffbb091ed15de786d1, finding 2, HIGH). Filed separately because it is a defect in stage outcome computation, not in the dispatch-close generation work that review was scoped to.

It was previously written off as a test-stub artifact. It is not: the reviewer traced the production ordering and the false failure is user-visible.

** The path
The production-path test acknowledges that real finalize records architect.failed and declines to assert completion (cli/tests/dispatch.rs:5223-5230). That test launches the real ACP stage and invokes real finalize (dispatch.rs:4911-4979, 5124-5221).

1. ACP release interrupts/closes the active turn (drivers/src/adapters/codex.rs:479-496).
2. Teardown reaps the harness process group (drivers/src/modes/acp_stdio.rs:817-833).
3. subprocess_stream_json.rs:315-360 synthesizes a FATAL driver error for the resulting non-success exit, because no terminal event preceded it.
4. The supervisor drains that error before appending the authoritative finalized_by_worker release (daemon/src/supervisor.rs:2181-2239).
5. But stage_outcome_from_session returns Failed IMMEDIATELY on the earlier fatal error (daemon/src/api.rs:5889-5924) and never reaches the finalized-tombstone handling at api.rs:5937-5949.

So the session contains BOTH a teardown-induced fatal driver error AND an authoritative worker-finalize release, and the outcome function honours the wrong one because it short-circuits on the first.

** Why it matters
A worker finalizing from its still-active turn is the NORMAL contract, not an edge case - that is what orgasmic dispatch finalize does. So a successful architect stage can be recorded as failed on the ordinary path.

The daemon unit at api.rs:21758-21833 synthesizes only a clean release, so it never exercises the production ordering and cannot catch this.

** Fix direction (reviewer)
Parse the COMPLETE stage session and make an authoritative Lifecycle::Release { finalized_by_worker: true } DOMINATE teardown-induced driver errors. Retain genuine pre-finalize failure semantics - an error that precedes any finalize must still fail the stage. Extend the production CLI stage test to REQUIRE architect.completed and FORBID architect.failed, and add a session-order regression with a fatal driver error immediately before the finalized release.

** Note
Check whether the same short-circuit affects non-architect stage kinds and the implementer/reviewer outcome paths, or whether stage_outcome_from_session is architect-only. The reviewer did not state this either way.

Fix round for the reviewer BLOCK on TASK-8W30B (merged d60c4ed / d3fae4d).
Reviewer: reviewer-codex-acp-stdio (acp-stdio / codex / unknown / unknown),
run-20260726T110214. Findings are also in tx as reviewer.finding
tx-20260726-orgasmic-2872..2876. The merged change is NOT reverted: measured
release growth did go from +8 to 0 on the happy path. What follows is the
failure path it did not make reliable.

1. HIGH — the reaper can be cancelled before its fallback ever runs.
`run_live_session` builds the SDK facade with a 5s default timeout;
`reap_rmux_session` awaits `Session::kill()` before starting a separately
bounded 5s CLI fallback; and `stop_and_join_driver_producer`
(supervisor.rs:3983-3989) wraps the whole `release` in a third 5s timeout. A
transport that is gone but does not fail fast eats the entire outer budget in
the SDK attempt, and the fallback gets no guaranteed opportunity to start.

The severe part is what cancellation costs. `release` sets `released = true` and
does `self.session.take()` BEFORE the await, so when the outer timeout drops the
future the only `Session` handle drops with it. The following `drop(control)`
sees `session == None` and the Drop backstop cannot retry. That reproduces the
original production symptom exactly: session, pty and harness survive release.
Fix: one authoritative release budget with the SDK attempt strictly shorter than
the total and time reserved for the CLI fallback, or a caller budget large enough
for both. Do not `take()` the only handle before a cancellable await without a
durable retry owner.

2. MEDIUM — the reap error is still invisible. `release` returns `reap_result`,
but supervisor.rs:3988 assigns the nested timeout result to `_`, discarding both
`Ok(Err(DriverError::Transport(..)))` and `Err(Elapsed)`. `release_one` then
removes the record, writes `Lifecycle::Release` and returns success. The
invisible warn became an invisible Result. Fix: inspect both layers; keep
producer/drain/lifecycle cleanup unconditional so an error can never strand a
run, but emit an error with run and transport context after cleanup.

3. MEDIUM — the CLI fallback can address the wrong daemon. It shells out to bare
`rmux kill-session -t <stored string>`, but rmux-sdk 0.9.0 stores the resolved
endpoint AND the sanitized protocol-owned name on `Session`, and its builder
honours `RMUX_SDK_ENDPOINT`, while the CLI resolves `-S`/`-L`/`$RMUX`/default
instead. A session acquired via a custom endpoint falls back against a different
daemon: usually it just leaks, but if that daemon holds the same target name it
kills the wrong session. The name happens to match today only because
`make_run_id`/`RuntimeIdentity::new` emit safe components —
`RuntimeIdentity::planned` accepts arbitrary strings and `run_live_session`
copies `session_target` before `SessionName::new` sanitizes `.` and `:`. Fix:
capture `session.name()` and `session.endpoint()` from the handle before the
primary kill and pass the endpoint explicitly. Do not maintain a second, weaker
identity.

4. MEDIUM — a cancelled release loses its `RunComplete`. Confirmed, with the
manager s no-strand reasoning upheld: explicit release keeps the RunRecord until
the drain joins, then removes it and writes `Lifecycle::Release`, and a
terminal-event-driven release already persisted its terminal event first. So no
run is stranded — but the latch is set before the reap, Drop aborts the competing
watcher, and the driver summary is simply lost. Fix: publish the release-owned
`RunComplete` claim before the fallible reap, or make terminal publication
cancellation-safe.

5. MEDIUM — the regression test cannot gate anything. It returns success when the
binary is missing/incompatible and again when acquire reports inert, and it calls
`control.release` directly, so it cannot reach any of the four failures above.
Keep it as a live smoke and add deterministic coverage for SDK failure, CLI
fallback, cancellation, and endpoint/target propagation — including a
supervisor-path regression that stalls the SDK request and proves the fallback
runs and the session is gone after `Supervisor::release`.

Out of scope: the known-red trio, and TASK-099T6.

Acceptance:
- a stalled SDK kill still results in a reaped session via the CLI fallback,
  proven by a supervisor-path test that goes through the real 5s caller timeout
- a reap failure appears in the daemon log with run and transport context, and
  cleanup still happens unconditionally
- the fallback targets the endpoint and name owned by the SDK handle
- a cancelled release does not silently drop its RunComplete
- at least one test fails, rather than skips, when rmux is absent in a lane
  designated as a gate

Production defect, root-caused by the TASK-STWVB implementer while diagnosing a
test flake. It is not a test problem.

THE DEFECT

`RmuxControl::release` (crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/rmux.rs:1760) aborts
its lifecycle task and its startup task BEFORE calling `Session::kill()`. The
kill is then issued over a torn-down SDK transport and fails. Instrumented probe:

    PROBE rmux Session::kill -> Err(Transport { operation: "complete
      `kill-session` request/response exchange with rmux daemon",
      source: BrokenPipe: "rmux SDK request was cancelled while its ordered
      response was pending" })

The session survives. The only report is a `tracing::warn!`, invisible under
`cargo test` and easy to miss in a daemon log.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TESTS

Every released rmux run leaks a session, a pty and a harness process into the
per-user rmux daemon — a singleton on `$TMPDIR/rmux-$uid`, shared across every
run and every test binary, started by launchd and therefore inheriting a 256-fd
soft limit (`launchctl limit maxfiles` → `maxfiles 256 unlimited`, confirmed
independently on this machine 2026-07-26).

Once saturated the daemon cannot create sessions, and the rmux driver degrades
to INERT — silently. A developer's machine reaches that state on its own, and
from then on every rmux dispatch quietly does nothing useful.

MEASURED

- 8 leaked sessions per `--lib artifact` run (109 → 189 across 12 runs; 7 still
  present 15 s after the process exited)
- 236 stale `orgasmic-rmux-run-*` sessions and 69 orphaned
  `artifactor-test-harness.sh` processes found accumulated, oldest predating the
  dispatch that found them
- at 236 sessions the daemon held 253 open fds against the 256 limit
- dose-response over 10 consecutive full-suite runs: green at 204/210/217/221/226
  leaked sessions, failing at 233/236/236/236/236. The count stopped growing
  exactly when failures began — the daemon could no longer create sessions.
- the resulting symptom is `409 capability_unsupported: send_input` on all 40
  retries, not a deadline that wanted lengthening

SUGGESTED FIX

`RmuxControl` already carries `rmux_bin` and `session_target`. Either kill the
session before aborting the tasks, or add a CLI `kill-session` fallback for when
the SDK transport is already gone. Prefer both: the CLI path also cleans up
sessions leaked by earlier builds.

Also make the failure visible. A kill that fails is currently a warn on a path
nobody watches; it should be an error the release path surfaces.

NOTE ON CURRENT MACHINE STATE: the accumulation was cleared incidentally during
this session (rmux servers were killed during unrelated cleanup), so a check
right now reports 0 sessions and no running daemon. That is not the defect being
fixed — it will re-accumulate from the next rmux run.

Downstream: this is the production root cause of
`api::post_artifact_regenerate_hot_path_reuses_live_run_id` flaking, which is why
TASK-STWVB deliberately did not patch that test.
INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED [2026-07-26] by the manager, on different runs than the
implementer's, from a known-empty daemon.

23 leaked `orgasmic-rmux-run-*` sessions before one
`cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon --lib` run, 31 after: **+8 per run**, matching the
implementer's 8/run exactly. rmux-daemon fds 47/256. The 23 had accumulated from
three earlier verification runs in the same hour (~7.7/run) starting from zero,
so this is a clean growth curve rather than an inherited pile.

CONSEQUENCE FOR MEASUREMENT, not only for users: at 8 sessions per run,
saturation (~236 sessions / 253 fds) arrives after roughly 29 more full-suite
runs. Any 'N consecutive green runs' gate on this crate therefore measures a
monotonically degrading environment — later runs are strictly likelier to fail
than earlier ones for reasons unrelated to the change under test. That is why
TASK-STWVB's implementer saw its only green streak in runs 1-2 of a 10-run gate
and none after, and why that gate should be re-run only once this lands.
** Evidence
Implemented by implementer-codex-acp-stdio, run-20260726T102724, commit d60c4ed, merged --no-ff to main.

THE FIX (both halves kept)
Ownership hypothesis confirmed by the implementer: Session and the lifecycle
watcher pane retain clones of ONE ordered SDK transport after the local Rmux
facade drops, so aborting a pending pane request poisons the later kill.
release() now reaps first, then aborts/joins. A bounded 5s `rmux kill-session -t`
CLI fallback covers a transport that is already gone. The Drop backstop shared
the same ordering defect and was fixed the same way; kill_on_drop == false still
takes the no-kill branch, so reattached and system-wide sessions are never
implicitly reaped.

IMPLEMENTER MEASUREMENT (controlled)
Unfixed: 31 -> 36 sessions across one `cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon --lib`
(+5). Fixed: 36 -> 36 (+0), before/after session-name set difference empty.
Regression test fails (exit 101, "rmux session survived explicit release") on
restored unfixed ordering and passes 1/1 with the fix.

MANAGER MEASUREMENT (independent, on the merged tree, different runs)
Before 37, after 38 (+1). The single new session is
orgasmic-rmux-run-20260726T105347-034ff6ca..., which is the exact run_id the
FAILING api::post_artifact_regenerate_hot_path_reuses_live_run_id asserted on
("left: run-20260726T105347-034ff6ca..."). It is a run abandoned by a panicking
test, not a leak on the release path. Production release growth is 0, down from
the +8/run recorded in the heading.

GATES ON THE MERGED TREE
- cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers: lib 231/231, cursor_agent 5/5,
  rmux_release_reaps_session 1/1 (ran for real, did not print SKIPPED)
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: PASS
- cargo fmt --all --check: PASS
- cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon --lib: 500 passed, 2 failed, both declared
  known-red and untouched

WHAT THIS DID NOT FIX, contrary to the hypothesis in the heading
api::post_artifact_regenerate_hot_path_reuses_live_run_id STILL FAILS on the
merged tree (two consecutive rounds got different run_ids). The implementer saw
it pass once in a fixed run and reported that; the manager then saw it fail. The
heading calls this defect the production root cause of that flake — that claim is
now disconfirmed, not confirmed. Do not close TASK-STWVB on the assumption the
flake is gone; it needs its own root cause.

UNRELATED DEFECT SURFACED BY THESE GATES
driver_modes::legacy_drivers_and_explicit_pairs_emit_equivalent_start_events now
fails on a claude session-id collision. Filed as TASK-099T6. It is fallout from
TASK-SGRTX making --session-id actually reach the process, not from this task.

RESIDUAL RISK (manager review of the diff)
1. supervisor.rs:3988 wraps release in its own 5s timeout and discards the
   result (`let _ = tokio::time::timeout(...)`). The new Err return therefore
   reaches no caller on the production path, so "make the failure visible" is
   only half met — the value is returned but nothing reads it.
2. Nested 5s budgets: the outer timeout equals the CLI fallback timeout, so a
   slow SDK kill leaves the fallback no room to run.
3. release() now latches terminal_emitted BEFORE the reap. If the outer timeout
   cancels release mid-reap, RunComplete is never emitted by anyone. The drain
   still writes Lifecycle::Release (supervisor.rs:3976-3981), so the run is not
   stranded, but its summary event is lost.
These three are for the reviewer to rule on; none blocked the merge.

Repeated close is TASK-bound, not dispatch-generation-bound, so a stale retry can close and clean up a SUCCESSOR dispatch instead of no-oping. cmd_dispatch_close selects any currently open dispatch covering the task before it consults closed records (593-602). The normal workflow closes the implementer, moves the task to IN_REVIEW (manager.rs:2958-2966), then opens a reviewer for the SAME task. Replaying the implementer close at that point selects the reviewer record: the extra --merge-sha is accepted, done_tx_type becomes reviewer.done, lines 677-714 release the live reviewer and enter worktree/branch cleanup, and 735-767 append the wrong close and apply reviewer lifecycle. The existing test at crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/dispatch.rs:3164 only replays IMMEDIATELY, before any successor exists, so it misses the acceptance-breaking edge. FIX: bind close/retry identity to the intended manager.dispatch_started tx (preferred --started-tx, or an equally stable generation token), derive a deterministic request id from it, and make a retry a no-op against that exact closed generation even when another dispatch for the task is open. CLOSED_TX already names the stable generation in terminal records, so exposing the corresponding started tx as a close precondition is the clearest identity. ADD TESTS: implementer-close -> reviewer-open -> stale implementer-retry; and abort -> redispatch -> stale retry.

FIX DIRECTION: require --started-tx whenever an open matching dispatch exists. Preserve tokenless compatibility only as a no-op when there is no open record and a historical closed record exists - historical records never need to act on a LIVE record by task. ** Finding 2 - LOW correctness
manager.rs:3701-3720 and daemon/src/api.rs:7543-7909. The fail-closed RUN_ID rule leaves a legitimate fresh recovery run permanently [unreported]. Initial CLI dispatches write a run.created association carrying RUN_ID and DISPATCH_TX (api.rs:5109-5200), and attach_run_created_to_dispatch stores that original run id (manager.rs:3655-3697). But resume_native_fork and start_recovery_run acquire a REPLACEMENT run and return a new id while preserving the task and terminal contract - and never call the sole record_dispatch_created site, so no replacement association is emitted. dispatch finalize then reports the live replacement id (manager.rs:1218-1221), which cannot equal the open generation's original id, and mark_matching_dispatch_reported now returns without task fallback. Reattach-in-place is unaffected because it preserves the id.

So the answer to the brief's adversarial probe is YES: fresh recovery/resume is a valid mismatch shape, and its manager status never becomes [reported]. The wrong-marking bug was traded for a never-marking bug in this one shape.

FIX DIRECTION: persist a replacement-run-to-manager.dispatch_started generation association for fresh recovery/resume, and match *.reported by that generation rather than by task overlap. Add an end-to-end dispatched-run -> interruption -> recovery -> finalize status test.

** Finding 3 - LOW test
daemon/src/api.rs:21416-21485. The added architect-stage test does not prove a stage run creates no manager.dispatch_started record. It opens a synthetic session, appends a Lifecycle::Release and calls spawn_stage_completion_watcher directly. The tombstone-driven architect.completed assertion is useful, but the negative dispatch assertion is TAUTOLOGICAL because the production stage launch/recording path never ran.

FIX DIRECTION: drive the assertion through the real stage launch endpoint / shared production spawn path, then finalize-tombstone it and inspect both project and home ledgers.

** Finding 4 - LOW test
tests/shipped_conventions.rs:49-71. The forced-cleanup guard is both syntax-brittle and blind to realistic dangerous variants. It matches only the adjacent substring 'worktree remove --force', while the ORIGINAL dangerous instruction read 'git worktree remove <path> --force' - which would evade the needle entirely, alone or paired with a generalized 'git branch -D <branch>'. Conversely it requires exactly one occurrence and the exact phrase 'destroys exactly that', so innocent rewording fails it. The convention at manager-dispatch.org:205-227 is currently safe; the guard is the problem. A brittle guard gets deleted the first time it fails spuriously, and then protects nothing.

FIX DIRECTION: replace exact prose matching with a semantic guard that rejects 'git worktree remove' combined with '--force' regardless of intervening arguments, and rejects 'git branch -D' regardless of branch spelling. Permit zero warning literals, or anchor any allowed warning to an explicit structured marker rather than a sentence.

* DONE TASK-6AYEJ manager dispatch-close is unreachable after a worker finalize, so success-path cleanup never runs :dispatch:lifecycle:defect:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-6AYEJ
:PRIORITY: P1
:TEST_CMD: cargo test -p orgasmic-cli
:END:

The worker's own success signal closes the dispatch record, so the manager's
`dispatch-close` can never run on a successful dispatch. Found while trying to
close TASK-D0GA3 after merging it.

REPRODUCED, not inferred:
- TASK-D0GA3 merged at 0daa77c. `orgasmic manager dispatch-close --task
  TASK-D0GA3 --status done --merge-sha 0daa77c ... --worktree-remove
  --branch-delete` fails with "no open manager.dispatch_started tx for
  TASK-D0GA3".
- `orgasmic manager dispatch-status` prints nothing — zero open dispatches —
  while `git worktree list` shows 17 live dispatch worktrees and their branches.

MECHANISM, read from code: scan_open_dispatches (crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs:3316)
pairs each manager.dispatch_started with the first terminal tx it sees, and
manager.rs:3338-3341 counts `implementer.done` / `reviewer.done` /
`architector.done` / `manager.dispatch_aborted` as terminal. Per dec_3M7M0 the
worker's `orgasmic dispatch finalize --commit` is the SOLE success signal and it
emits `implementer.done` itself. So the dispatch is closed by the worker before
the manager has even read the report.

The tx history shows the switchover cleanly. Every terminal tx up to 2026-07-23
carries ACTOR theaspirational@users.noreply.github.com (the manager, via
dispatch-close). Every one from 2026-07-26 carries ACTOR agent.implementer or
agent.reviewer (the worker, via finalize). Not one manager-recorded close since.

WHAT IS LOST, per successful dispatch:
1. Worktree and branch cleanup never runs. cleanup_dispatch — and with it the
   whole salvage path just hardened by TASK-2BPWM and TASK-D0GA3 — is dead on
   the success path. 17 stale worktrees is the accumulated evidence.
2. MERGE_SHA in the close tx is the WORKER's commit, not the manager's merge.
   TASK-D0GA3's implementer.done (tx-20260726-orgasmic-2967) records
   SHA = MERGE_SHA = e7837f1; the actual merge is 0daa77c. Any later audit that
   trusts MERGE_SHA is looking at a commit that was never on main as such.
3. REVIEWED_DIFF, worker-session, tokens and wall are never recorded, because
   only dispatch-close accepts them.
4. The manager's verdict is not the closing record. The worker's self-report is.
   That inverts the "treat worker summaries as claims" rule at the tx layer.

NOT AFFECTED, so scope this correctly: the salvage machinery still runs on the
failure paths, which is where it matters most — cleanup_created_resources
(dispatch rollback), the daemon POST cleanup endpoint, and dispatch-close on an
orphan dispatch that never finalized. TASK-2BPWM and TASK-D0GA3 are not wasted
work.

DIRECTION, to be argued rather than assumed:
- The likely fix is that `finalize` should record worker completion WITHOUT
  closing the dispatch — a distinct tx type (implementer.reported?) that
  scan_open_dispatches does not treat as terminal — leaving implementer.done to
  the manager. That preserves dec_3M7M0's "finalize is the sole success signal"
  for the WATCHER while restoring the manager's close.
- Whatever shape is chosen, closing must stay idempotent and must not strand a
  dispatch open forever when the manager dies mid-integration.
- Backfill is out of scope, but the fix must not choke on the ~10 dispatches
  already closed this way.

Acceptance:
- after a worker runs `dispatch finalize --commit`, `manager dispatch-status`
  still lists the dispatch as open
- `manager dispatch-close --status done --merge-sha <real merge>` succeeds and
  records the manager's merge sha, and removes the worktree and branch
- a dispatch that is never finalized still closes via dispatch-close, unchanged
- double-close is a clean no-op, not an error
