may legitimately take `ShutdownBudgets::default().total()` = 40s.

"launchd still reports … loaded 5s after bootout". That is the same operator
experience TASK-QRB8S just fixed on the start path: a failure message for
something that was working.

`stop_timeout()` (TASK-WGXKD.2), `start_timeout()` (TASK-QRB8S). This is the
last one that is not.

`daemon_service.rs:448-451`: the `bootout` of the **rmux** agent is
fire-and-forget (`let _ = …`), unlike the orgasmic agent's verified unload. A
slow-exiting previous `rmux-daemon` can therefore race the subsequent
`bootstrap`. This predates TASK-ATAXN and is bounded by rmux's own exit, but it
is an unverified teardown on the path that cycles the rmux LaunchAgent — the

carrying a name that is never written.

Root cause, two halves that hid each other:

1. `seed_worker` wrote worker templates to `$ORGASMIC_HOME/user/workers/`.
   Templates were retired — `lib.rs:454` logs "legacy user/workers directory
   ignored" at boot and reads nothing. 33 call sites were seeding a directory
   with no reader.
2. The tests sent `"worker_id"` in the dispatch body. `DispatchRequest`
   (api.rs:3787) has no such field and does not deny unknown fields, so serde
   dropped it silently. The daemon derives the label from the address alone,
   via `addressing::compatibility_worker_id(kind, mode, harness)`.

So the tests asked for a worker by a name with no reader, over a field with no
receiver, and asserted a result nothing produces. Each half looks deliberate on
its own; together they are inert.

Cost: the suite has been red on this crate on every full run, so it could not
answer "did my change break something?" — TASK-TJKFC's evidence had to carry
"dispatch_endpoint has 3 failures, identical on HEAD" as a manual caveat, and
every future change to this crate would have repeated that stash-and-compare.

Fix: delete `seed_worker`/`seed_worker_kind` and all 33 call sites; correct
the label literals to the ids the daemon actually mints; stop sending the
dropped `worker_id` field; assert on the pinned-worker test that a task's
stale `:WORKER:` property does NOT override the dispatch address (the real
current contract, and a stronger claim than the one it replaced); add
`asserted_worker_labels_match_the_daemons_naming_rule`, which pins all four
labels to `compatibility_worker_id` so the rule cannot drift silently again.

Related but distinct: TASK-STWVB (four daemon --lib tests that fail only under
full-suite parallelism). This one fails deterministically, alone or not.

* DONE TASK-VZMZE Heartbeats reset the stall timer, so a wedged run that never starts a turn is immortal for four hours :daemon:supervisor:dispatch:reliability:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-VZMZE
:PRIORITY: P1
:TEST_CMD: cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon --lib
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs
:END:

Measured 2026-07-26 on a real dispatch that produced nothing for 60 minutes and
was never released by the daemon.

THE ARITHMETIC
- Heartbeats arrive every 30 s (observed: 118 of them, seq 0..115, exactly 30 s
  apart).
- `DEFAULT_STALL_TIMEOUT` is 600 s (supervisor.rs:65).
- Stall is computed from `last_activity_at = rec.last_input_at.max(rec.last_driver_event_at)`
  (supervisor.rs:3410) and the drain updates `last_driver_event_at` for EVERY
  drained event, variant-agnostically. The crate's own test says so:
  `heartbeat_is_non_terminal_so_drain_never_releases_on_it` — "The event drain
  resets last_driver_event_at for every drained event (variant-agnostic)".

So a harness that is alive and emitting heartbeats can never trip the 600 s stall
timeout, no matter how long it does no work. The only backstop is
`DEFAULT_MAX_RUN_DURATION` at 14_400 s — four hours of a billed session producing
nothing before the daemon acts.

THE OBSERVED RUN
run-20260726T144430-aa47b867840f42f282b30d3469949731 (TASK-RRT4T implementer,
acp-stdio / codex / gpt-5.6-sol / xhigh). Session event tally against the healthy
run that preceded it on the same harness and model:

| event       | TASK-2BPWM (healthy) | TASK-RRT4T (wedged) |
|-------------|----------------------|---------------------|
| ready       | 1                    | 1                   |
| tool_call   | 243                  | 0                   |
| tool_result | 135                  | 0                   |
| text_chunk  | 211                  | 12 (all stderr logs)|
| heartbeat   | 7                    | 118                 |
| lifecycle   | 3                    | 2 (no terminal)     |

It reached `ready`, never began a turn, wrote zero bytes into its worktree, and
consumed 6.77 s of CPU in 60 minutes. Its 12 text chunks are all harness stderr:
`codex_models_manager::cache: failed to load models cache: missing field
'supports_reasoning_summaries' at line 88 column 5`, repeated `failed to renew
cache TTL` with the same message, and three
`rmcp::transport::worker: worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed` for
`http://localhost:8080/_agent-native/mcp`.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE HARNESS BUG
The harness fault may be transient — the reviewer run dispatched seven minutes
later on the same binary and model worked fine. What is not transient is that the
daemon could not tell the difference. A run with zero tool calls and 118
heartbeats is, to the supervisor, exactly as healthy as one with 243 tool calls.

The manager-dispatch convention already states the correct rule for humans:
"A live PID alone is not proof of progress, and heartbeat-only/session-token
activity must not reset the deadline." The supervisor does the opposite of what
we tell managers to do. The manager's shell watcher caught this in 60 minutes
because it was told to; the daemon would have taken four hours.

FIX DIRECTION
Distinguish liveness from progress. A heartbeat should keep the run from being
declared dead, and should NOT count as progress against the stall timer. Track a
separate `last_progress_at` advanced only by events that represent work —
tool_call, tool_result, text_chunk from stdout, turn boundaries — and evaluate
stall against that. Keep `last_driver_event_at` for liveness, since a harness
that stops heartbeating is a different failure.

Second, a run that reaches `ready` and never starts a turn deserves its own
shorter deadline. "Started but never began work" is a distinct and much cheaper
failure to detect than a mid-turn stall, and it is the one that keeps happening.

Related: the handoff already records a run that stayed live ~40 minutes after its
worker exited. Same family, and this is the mechanism.

Acceptance:
- a run emitting only heartbeats trips the stall timeout at the configured
  threshold, not at max_run_duration
- a heartbeat still prevents a "harness is gone" classification
- a test asserts a heartbeat-only run is released, using fake time rather than a
  600 s sleep
- the reason recorded distinguishes "no progress" from "no liveness"

CORRECTION, same session, before this task is worked. The harness stderr listed
above is NOT the cause and must not be treated as a lead.

The healthy TASK-2BPWM reviewer run, dispatched seven minutes after the wedged one
on the same binary, model and effort, contains the SAME errors: 6 occurrences of
`missing field 'supports_reasoning_summaries'` and the same 3
`_agent-native/mcp` transport fatals. It then made 41 tool calls and finalized
normally.

So those messages are ambient noise on every codex run here, and the wedged run's
cause is UNKNOWN. What is established is only this: it reached `ready`, never
emitted a single tool_call or a turn, and the supervisor could not tell.

That does not weaken this task. The defect filed here is the detection gap, which
is proven from the code and the arithmetic (30 s heartbeats against a 600 s
variant-agnostic stall timer), not from any theory about why the harness stalled.
If anything the correction strengthens it: the trigger is unidentified and may
recur at any time, so the daemon cannot rely on knowing the cause in advance.

Worth filing separately if it happens again: a run that reaches `ready` and never
starts a turn, with no explanation in its session events.
HARD COMPATIBILITY GATE added 2026-07-27 by the TASK-RWCRN reviewer (finding 2, MEDIUM). TASK-RWCRN landed DriverEvent::PaneActivity, a content-free per-30s event emitted while an rmux pane writes; it is the ONLY driver event an rmux worker produces after ready, and the rmux stall clock now depends on it. This task's recorded fix direction — move stall onto a progress-only clock advanced by tool/text/turn events — will kill every rmux dispatch at 600s again if implemented literally, because a pane produces none of those. The RWCRN author deliberately did NOT reuse DriverEvent::Heartbeat precisely so this task can classify the two independently: Heartbeat means the harness produced no substantive output, PaneActivity means the pane demonstrably wrote. That reasoning is sound, but the only warning it left was a doc comment in orgasmic-core/src/session.rs, which is outside this task's declared supervisor.rs write scope and outside this task record — so an implementer routed here would never see it. Hence this note. REQUIRED ACCEPTANCE, both regressions, cross-transport: (a) an acp-stdio run emitting only heartbeats and no substantive progress MUST time out, which is this task's whole point; and (b) a working rmux run emitting only pane_activity MUST continue to reset its stall deadline and MUST NOT be released. Treat (b) as a gate, not a note. Related: TASK-RWCRN's own reviewer also filed a HIGH that pane_activity is line-based and misses a redrawing TUI; if that lands as a raw-byte observation the event may change shape, so re-read the variant before building on it.

* DONE TASK-GQPGR manager/task/tx CLI run from a dispatch worktree reports frozen snapshot state as fact and writes can silently not apply :cli:agent-ergonomics:hardening:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-GQPGR
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Filed 2026-07-28 from three measured false readings in one session, all caused
by one mechanism: the CLI resolves the project from the cwd, and a dispatch
worktree contains a FROZEN `.orgasmic/` snapshot from the commit the worktree
was created at. Run from inside one, state commands answer confidently from
stale data, and some writes report success without applying.

=== Measured, 2026-07-28 (all after `cd` into
`.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/task-z8wej-review/worktree` to inspect a commit)

1. `orgasmic manager dispatch-status` returned EMPTY while three workers were
   live and healthy (`rmux ls` showed both sessions; `git worktree list` showed
   all three worktrees). Briefly read as "all workers died".
2. `orgasmic manager dispatch-close --started-tx tx-...-3305` failed with
   "no manager.dispatch_started tx in the tx log" — the worktree's snapshot
   predates that tx.
3. `orgasmic task update --property BLOCKED_BY=...` RETURNED A TX ID and
   silently did not apply to the live project. A write verb that succeeds
   against a frozen snapshot is the worst variant: no signal, wrong state.

The failure is plausible rather than loud, which distinguishes it from
TASK-HXSW0's argument-level silent drops (same disease, different organ: this is
PROJECT RESOLUTION, not flag parsing).

=== The fix

The CLI created these worktrees; it can recognize them. Detect that the resolved
project root is a dispatch worktree — by path shape
(`.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/*/worktree`), or better, by a marker the dispatch
machinery already writes (or should write) into the worktree at creation.

Then, for every verb that reads project state or writes the tx/ledger surface
(`manager *`, `task *`, `tasks *`, `tx *`, `node *`, `board`, ...):

- REFUSE with an error naming the situation and the primary project root
  ("this is the dispatch worktree for TASK-X; run from <root> or pass
  --project"), OR auto-resolve to the primary root and say so on stderr.
  Choose one policy, record why. Refusal is the conservative default; a worker
  legitimately operating inside its own worktree (the `dispatch` verb group,
  dec_3M7M0) must keep working — the worker-facing surface is the carve-out
  that must be explicitly decided and tested.
- Daemon-routed verbs with explicit `--project` are already safe and must keep
  working from anywhere.

=== Acceptance

- From inside a dispatch worktree: `manager dispatch-status` either reports the
  LIVE project's state or refuses naming the primary root — proven by a test
  that creates a real dispatch worktree shape and runs the verb from it.
- From the same location, `task update` on a live task either applies (visible
  from the primary root) or errors; it must never return a tx id that does not
  land in the live ledger.
- The worker-authority `dispatch` verb group still functions from inside its
  own worktree (regression test).
- Injection proof per project standard: with the guard removed, show the stale
  EMPTY dispatch-status reading red against the new test; restore, green.

=== Non-goals

- Do not change how snapshots get into worktrees or what workers may read.
- Do not implement TASK-HXSW0's help/arg-validation items here; cross-reference
  only.

Related: TASK-HXSW0 (silent no-ops on write verbs), the recorded gotcha
"Manager commands run from a dispatch worktree report stale state as fact".

* DONE TASK-TCTTD Injection proofs are re-authored at merge time against the fixed tree; ship them as artifacts replayed by one verb :cli:verification:mechanism:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-TCTTD
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Filed 2026-07-28 after a session in which the manager's own re-injection probes
were malformed four times, every time failing toward FALSE GREEN: an org-verbatim
span tested against a backtick extractor, a std-Mutex API probe against a tokio
Mutex, a "removed" lock that was still one shared static, and a genuine removal
run after the ambient load that reproduced the race had gone. A broken probe
that passes looks identical to a working fix. Each was caught only by manual
suspicion, which does not scale and fails silently.

Root cause: the injection proof is a RITUAL, re-authored from scratch at merge
time against the ALREADY-FIXED tree — which is precisely where false green
lives. The worker demonstrated red once, pre-fix, when red was cheap; that
demonstration is then thrown away and the manager improvises a new probe.

=== The mechanism

Make the injection a shipped ARTIFACT, authored once at the moment the defect
demonstrably exists, then replayed — never re-authored.

1. The implementer, while the defect still reproduces (pre-fix), captures:
   - a patch that reintroduces the defect onto the fixed tree (reverse of the
     fix, or a minimal hand-written defect patch),
   - the exact test command (single line, with the mandatory
     `--skip legacy_drivers_and_explicit_pairs_emit_equivalent_start_events`
     baked in where the drivers suite is involved),
   - the expected RED signature: a substring/regex of the failure output plus
     the nonzero exit class.
2. These live in the repo with the fix (suggested: `verify/TASK-<id>/` with
   `injection.patch`, `cmd`, `expect-red`), so they survive worktree removal
   and travel with the merge. The task drawer records the path.
3. A new verb `orgasmic verify TASK-<id>` replays it: assert clean tree, apply
   patch, run cmd, ASSERT RED MATCHING SIGNATURE (a green or wrong-red run
   fails verification loudly), revert patch byte-clean, run cmd, assert green.
   Machine-readable result; nonzero exit on any deviation.

The property this buys: probe authorship happens exactly once, against a
known-broken state, with its red output pinned. Replay cannot silently degrade
into false green — a probe that no longer bites fails the replay itself.
It also makes merge verification delegable (reviewer or manager runs one verb)
instead of a manager-serial bespoke step.

=== Design points the worker must decide and record

- Patch application on a moved tree: if `injection.patch` no longer applies,
  verify must FAIL (stale artifact), not skip.
- Where the verb lives (`orgasmic verify` vs `orgasmic task verify`) and how it
  finds the artifact (drawer property vs path convention). Prefer drawer
  property `verify_artifact` set by the implementer, validated at close.
- Safety: refuse to run on a dirty tree; always restore (RAII/temp-worktree ok,
  but note dispatch worktrees already exist — do not invent a second worktree
  mechanism if `git stash`-discipline suffices).

=== Acceptance

- One real, already-merged fix (suggested: TASK-R74E8's drain-budget defect) is
  re-expressed as a verify artifact, and `orgasmic verify` shows the full
  red-then-green replay with output.
- A deliberately malformed artifact (patch that does not change behavior, or
  wrong expected signature) makes verify FAIL loudly — demonstrated, with
  output. This is the false-green detector and the core of the task.
- Replay leaves the tree byte-identical (`git status` clean, `git diff` empty).
- `verify --help` documents the artifact layout.

=== Non-goals

- Do not retrofit artifacts onto historical merges beyond the one exemplar.
- Do not gate `manager dispatch-close` on verify yet — that is a follow-up
  decision once the verb has been used in anger.
- Do not touch the billed harness test in any way; its name appears here only
  inside the mandatory skip flag.

Related: TASK-S2KM0 (a CI lane could run `orgasmic verify` per merged task),
TASK-MFJZ7 (mechanism-over-prose for the billed test, same philosophy).

* DONE TASK-MFJZ7 the billed harness test is guarded only by a flag people must remember, and it already fired
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-MFJZ7
:PRIORITY: P1
:TAGS: drivers,tests,cost,safety
:END:
** Description
`legacy_drivers_and_explicit_pairs_emit_equivalent_start_events`
(`crates/orgasmic-drivers/tests/driver_modes.rs:1662`) spawns the real `claude`
binary and can submit a real, billed turn. It is declared as a plain
`#[tokio::test]` with **no `#[ignore]` and no environment gate**, so a bare
`cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers` runs it.

The only thing standing between a contributor and a charge is remembering to
pass `-- --skip legacy_drivers_and_explicit_pairs_emit_equivalent_start_events`
on every invocation. That is prose in briefs and one entry in `gotchas.org`
("Asking a harness to prove it can work costs real money"), enforced by nothing.

=== It already fired

2026-07-28, the TASK-QRB8S worker. Its brief carried the constraint in bold and
it still ran `cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers` without the skip, twice — once on
its branch and once on a stashed baseline to classify the failure. It reported
the result honestly, which is how this was caught.

Cost was probably nil that time: the run failed with the real binary answering
`Error: Session ID … is already in use`, which is a pre-turn rejection. **That is
luck, not a control.** A clean session id would have submitted the turn.

This is the same shape as the defects this project keeps finding: a guarantee
that lives in a document rather than in the code. A worker who is told the rule
and breaks it anyway is evidence the rule needs a mechanism, not a louder brief.

=== Ask

1. Gate the test so the **default is safe**. `#[ignore]` plus an explicit
   opt-in env (e.g. `ORGASMIC_ALLOW_BILLED_TESTS=1`) is the obvious shape: a
   bare `cargo test` then skips it and says so, and `--include-ignored` alone is
   not enough to run it.
2. Make the skip unnecessary rather than mandatory. Once gated, briefs and
   `gotchas.org` should stop telling people to pass `--skip`; update both, and
   say what the new instruction is.
3. Audit for any other test that can spend money or quota — any test that
   spawns a real harness and submits a turn. Report the full list and gate each,
   or state why it cannot bill. `real_claude_stream_json_bridge_reports_auth_error`
   and the `live_rmux_*` family are the obvious places to start; several are
   already availability-gated but availability is not the same as billing.
4. Make the sentinel account for it. The `required_test_tooling_is_present`
   contract counts gated tests; a billed test that is skipped by default must not
   silently change that count in a way that hides it.

=== Acceptance

- `cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers` with no extra flags does not run the billed
  test, and prints something that names why it was skipped.
- Prove it by injection: remove the gate, show the test being collected and
  attempted, restore it, show it skipped — with output. Do **not** let the
  injected run actually submit a turn; assert on collection, not on execution.
- The opt-in path works: with the env set, the test runs.
- `gotchas.org` and every brief template no longer instruct `--skip`, and the
  audit list from ask 3 is recorded on this task.

=== Non-goals

- Do not delete the test. It is the parity check between legacy drivers and
  explicit pairs and it has real value when someone deliberately opts in.
- Do not change what the test asserts.

* DONE TASK-ZYWZD node body set silently drops nested headings: a write verb that lost 92 percent of a body and reported success :cli:daemon:hardening:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-ZYWZD
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Filed 2026-07-28. `orgasmic node body set` replaces only the free prose between
the property drawer and the first nested heading. A body containing `**`
sub-headings is silently truncated at the first one — TASK-ATAXN was filed with
300 of its 3959 characters and nobody was told. The read side compounds it:
nested `**` sections are NOT returned in the JSON `description` field, so the
loss is invisible through the same surface that caused it. A write verb that
can drop 92% of its payload and report success is the single worst surface in
the CLI.

=== The principle (shared with TASK-HQ970, defect 2)

A writer must not commit what it cannot read back. TASK-HQ970 states it for
`tx record` (re-parse before reporting success); this task applies the same
round-trip guarantee to the node body surface. If the fix grows shared
machinery (compose -> re-parse -> diff-against-intent -> refuse on loss), use
it for both.

=== Work

1. WRITE: `node body set` must either persist the full submitted body
   (including nested `**` headings, correctly re-depthed under the task
   heading) or REFUSE, naming exactly what would be lost ("body contains 3
   nested headings starting at '** The gap'; this verb replaces prose only —
   use ... or restructure with ==="). Never a silent partial write. Same audit
   for `node body append` and any sibling that composes org content.
2. READ: `task get` / `node` reads must expose the full body, or explicitly
   mark elision ("+ 3 nested sections not shown") — never present a truncated
   body as complete. Pick and record one; full exposure preferred.
3. Post-write verification: after composing the new file content, re-parse and
   assert the submitted body round-trips before the write is committed
   (mirrors HQ970's acceptance "a write that would not round-trip is rejected
   rather than committed").

=== Acceptance

- Setting a body containing `** Section` either persists it fully (verified by
  reading the raw org node) or errors naming the offending heading — proven
  both ways in tests.
- The ATAXN shape is the regression fixture: a ~4000-char body with three `**`
  sections survives set + get with zero loss, or is refused up front.
- No silent partial write remains on any `node body` verb (enumerate them in
  the report).
- Injection proof per project standard: restore the truncating behavior, show
  the round-trip test red with output, restore the fix, green.

=== Non-goals

- Do not implement TASK-HQ970 (tx record validation) here; share machinery if
  natural, cross-reference regardless.
- Do not redesign the org body/section model; make the existing surface honest
  about it.

Related: TASK-HQ970 (same round-trip principle on tx record), TASK-XPYRR
(title, the other unwritable field), the recorded gotcha "`node body set`
replaces prose only, so `**` headings in a body are lost".

* DONE TASK-DJ1WV Red classification is manual folklore; a runner wrapper must retry failures in isolation against a signed flake registry :testing:mechanism:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-DJ1WV
:PRIORITY: P2
:END:

Filed 2026-07-28. Five tests fail on full-suite runs under load and pass in
isolation. Today every full run therefore ends with a MANUAL classification
step: a human (or manager agent) rereads the failure list, recalls which names
are "known", reruns them alone, and decides whether red means anything. That
step was performed from memory at least four times today; once a failure was
misattributed to the wrong owning task (the 5HBST/STWVB mislabel — one test
name, two distinct failure modes) and was caught only by reading the panic
text. Standing red that requires folklore to interpret trains everyone to
discount red, which is exactly how the next TASK-Q07Y5 walks through a green
gate.

=== Mechanism

1. A machine-readable flake registry in the repo (suggested:
   `verify/flake-registry.toml` or similar): per entry the exact test name, the
   owning open TASK id, the failure SIGNATURE (substring/regex of the panic —
   this is what makes the 5HBST/STWVB confusion impossible: one test may carry
   two entries with different signatures and different owners), the evidence
   ("fails under load, green in isolation, N/M runs on <date>"), and the date
   filed. An entry whose owning task is done must fail a check — a registry
   that only grows is a graveyard.
2. A test-runner wrapper (script or cargo alias the whole project adopts —
   workers, manager, and the future TASK-S2KM0 CI lane) that: runs the suite,
   reruns each failure IN ISOLATION, and emits a final verdict block that
   separates `REAL:` failures from `FLAKE (green in isolation, owner
   TASK-STWVB, signature matched):` ones. Exit code nonzero iff REAL is
   nonempty OR a failure matched no registry entry.
3. A failure that matches a registered NAME but not its SIGNATURE is REAL —
   that is the mislabel detector.
4. The wrapper must bake in the mandatory
   `--skip legacy_drivers_and_explicit_pairs_emit_equivalent_start_events`
   default for the drivers suite so the safe invocation is the short one
   (until TASK-MFJZ7 lands the in-test gate; then keep both).

=== Seed entries (verify signatures before recording, do not copy blindly)

`poll_direct_child_pid_prefers_worker_server_over_generic_sibling`,
`recovery_reattaches_tmux_session_when_handle_exists`,
`recovery_inventory_waits_for_atomic_claim_commit`,
`git_resolves_quoted_included_origin_from_linked_worktree` — owner TASK-STWVB;
`production_resume_native_fork_uses_pinned_claude_not_path_shim` — owner
TASK-STWVB with the `resume_native_fork recover: 500` signature ONLY (its env
race signature was fixed by TASK-5HBST and must NOT be registered).

=== Acceptance

- A full-suite run under induced load ends with the verdict block; the five
  seeds classify as FLAKE with owners named; an injected genuine failure (any
  deliberately broken test) classifies as REAL and the wrapper exits nonzero.
- A failure matching a registered name with a different panic signature is
  reported REAL — demonstrated.
- Registry entries pointing at a done/cancelled task fail a check.
- The wrapper never runs the billed test by default — demonstrated by output.

=== Non-goals

- Not fixing the flakes themselves (TASK-STWVB, TASK-QCG6J, TASK-Y9BY6 own
  those). This task makes red mean something while they are being fixed.
- Not the CI lane itself (TASK-S2KM0 consumes this — its work item 2, "decide
  what to do about known-red tests before the lane goes required", is answered
  by this registry).

* DONE TASK-WE0Q7 No gate runs a daemon longer than ten seconds; add a scheduled soak that would have caught Q07Y5 :daemon:testing:mechanism:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-WE0Q7
:PRIORITY: P2
:END:

Filed 2026-07-28. No test in this repository runs a daemon longer than about
ten seconds, so any defect that needs uptime to express passes every gate.
That is not hypothetical: TASK-Q07Y5 shipped fully green and killed the
operator's daemon 10.00s after every boot. TASK-R74E8 fixed it and added
`daemon_serves_far_beyond_its_connection_drain_budget` — one test, watching one
instance of the class (drain-budget misapplication, 8x budget ~ seconds). The
CLASS — anything that expresses only with minutes of uptime: timers, budgets,
watchers, leaks, heartbeat/stall interactions (see TASK-VZMZE), fd/session
accumulation — still has nothing watching it.

=== Mechanism

A scheduled soak gate, not a per-merge one (minutes of wall clock do not belong
in the merge path):

1. A self-contained script (suggested `scripts/soak.sh` or a subcommand) that:
   boots a REAL daemon from the tree under test with an isolated
   `ORGASMIC_HOME` and random port (the isolated smoke-daemon recipe in
   gotchas/memory — never `daemon start`, never the LaunchAgent, never the
   installed runtime), runs it for a configurable duration (default >= 5
   minutes; >= 10x any derived budget), under light periodic traffic (status
   probes, a task read, a tx list — hit real surfaces), then SIGTERMs it.
2. Asserts across the whole window: one pid and one boot_id throughout; zero
   parse errors; memory/fd growth bounded (record; alert on gross growth, do
   not tune thresholds finely); clean exit within
   `ShutdownBudgets::default().total()` + margin (derived, not a literal —
   the R74E8/ATAXN/QRB8S standard); marker/lock files retracted after exit.
3. Wire it into a schedule: the repo already has `nightly-macos` /
   `nightly-runtime` workflows — add it there, and/or a local launchd schedule
   for the operator machine. Decide and record which; a soak that exists but
   never runs is the same blindspot with extra steps.

=== Acceptance

- The soak runs green on current HEAD for the full default duration, output
  showing the single pid/boot_id assertion sampled across the window.
- Injection proof: reintroduce the Q07Y5-class defect (apply the drain budget
  to the server's whole life instead of the drain phase) and show the soak
  catches it — daemon dies mid-window, soak exits nonzero with a message
  naming when it died. Restore, green. This proves the gate watches the class,
  not the code path R74E8 already guards.
- A second, different uptime defect class is demonstrated caught (suggested: a
  short-interval timer/watcher misbehavior injected artificially) — one

* DONE TASK-HQ970 tx record accepts a multi-line --reason and bricks the append-only ledger :tx:data-integrity:defect:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-HQ970
:PRIORITY: P1
:TEST_CMD: cargo test -p orgasmic-core
:END:

`orgasmic tx record --reason "<multi-line text>"` writes the newlines verbatim
into the org property drawer, returns success with a tx_id, and leaves the
append-only ledger unparseable. Every subsequent CLI read fails, so no verb —
including the ones you would use to repair it — can run. The only way out is a
hand-edit of the file the manager is forbidden to hand-edit.

REPRODUCED [2026-07-26], not inferred. `orgasmic tx record --type manager.action
--project orgasmic --task TASK-D0GA3 --reason "$(cat multi-line-file)"` returned

    {"tx_id": "tx-20260726-orgasmic-2973", "tx_path": ".orgasmic/tx/2026-07.org"}

and the next command failed with

    Error: parse .orgasmic/tx/2026-07.org
    Caused by: ...:29850: malformed property drawer entry: blank line inside
    property drawer

The remaining `--extra KEY=VALUE` properties were appended AFTER the injected
prose, so they landed outside the drawer too. A second, subtler failure mode:
once the blank lines were removed the parser then rejected the entry with "tx
entry has trailing content after property drawer" — tx entries are drawer-only
and carry no body at all, which is not stated anywhere in `tx record --help`.

BLAST RADIUS. The write is accepted, so a manager has no signal until the next
read. Both ledgers were hit in one session: the project ledger and, because
`tx record` is not project-scoped by default (TASK-HXSW0 instance 6),
`$ORGASMIC_HOME/state/tx/2026-07.org` as well. A daemon that cannot parse its
tx file cannot dispatch, cannot close, cannot update a task.

THREE SEPARATE DEFECTS, all in this one path:
1. No validation. A value containing a newline must be rejected at the API
   boundary with a clear error, before anything is written.
2. No atomicity or verification. The writer should re-parse what it produced
   before reporting success — a ledger that only accepts what it can read back
   cannot be bricked by its own writer.
3. No documented body support. If long prose belongs in a tx (and
   `tx-scannable-bodies` implies it does), the entry format needs a body region
   the parser accepts, or `--reason` needs to be documented as single-line and
   the convention corrected.

Acceptance:
- `tx record --reason` with an embedded newline fails with a clear message and
  writes nothing
- a tx write that would not round-trip through the parser is rejected rather
  than committed
- `tx record --help` states the single-line constraint, or a body region exists
  and is tested with multi-paragraph prose
- a regression test asserts the ledger still parses after each supported write

If either fix grows shared compose->re-parse->refuse machinery, use it for both.

* DONE TASK-XPYRR a task title cannot be corrected through any CLI surface, so a retracted claim outlives its correction
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-XPYRR
:PRIORITY: P1
:TAGS: cli,daemon,org-surface
:END:
** Description
A task heading's title cannot be changed through any CLI surface. `task update`
takes `--state`, `--priority`, `--reason` and `--property`, and rejects
`--title` with `unexpected argument`. `node body set` edits prose and named
sections, never the heading line. `node prop set` edits the drawer. Nothing
edits the title.

=== Why it matters, concretely

TASK-0RCRY was filed on 2026-07-28 with a diagnosis that was **retracted the
same day** (tx-20260728-orgasmic-3226): the claim that workers inherit the
daemon's `$TMUX`. The body was rewritten around the one surviving fact and now
opens with an explicit correction. **The title could not be rewritten**, so the
board still reads:

  "Workers inherit the daemon's $TMUX, so tmux tests talk to the rmux server
   and six gated tests never run"

The title is the most-read field on the board — it is what `dispatch-status`,
the task lists and every survey print. A retracted claim sitting in a heading
outlives the correction in the body, and the only reader guaranteed to see the
correction is one who opens the task.

The manager cannot fix this by hand: `.orgasmic` is daemon-owned and hand-edits
are forbidden. So the wrong title is currently unfixable by any sanctioned path.

=== Same class as TASK-JQARS

JQARS was about a documented command that did not exist. This is the inverse:
a field the product plainly owns, with no surface to write it. Both leave an
operator with a state they can observe and cannot change.

=== Ask

1. Add title editing to the task surface, through the daemon with the same OCC +
   structural guard as the other node writes. `task update --title` is the
   obvious shape given the flag already suggested by clap's own "a similar
   argument exists" tip.
2. Decide and record whether a title edit is allowed to change the org tags on
   the title line, or whether tags stay a separate concern. Do not let a title
   write silently drop tags — the heading line carries both.
3. Check the same question for the other node kinds that have titles (decision,
   architecture, glossary, goal). Report which already have a write path and
   which do not; fix only the ones in scope and file the rest.
4. Fix TASK-0RCRY's title as the acceptance demonstration, to:
   "No tmux call site passes -L/-S, so every probe and test session shares one
    server — on a dev box, the operator's own"

=== Acceptance

- `orgasmic task update <id> --title "..."` rewrites the heading, preserves the
  drawer, the body, all named sections and the org tags, and records a tx.
- Prove it by injection: a test that rewrites a title and asserts tags and body
  survive fails if the tag-preserving path is removed. Show it red, then green.
- A title containing org-significant characters (`*` at line start, `:tag:`
  shapes, trailing colons) either round-trips or is rejected with a reason — say
  which you chose and why. A silently corrupted heading is worse than a refusal.
- TASK-0RCRY reads correctly on the board afterwards.

=== Non-goals

- Do not add a general "edit any org line" escape hatch. The structural guard is
  the reason these surfaces are narrow.

* DONE TASK-EP3H1 dispatch-close tears under load: tx appended, lifecycle stranded, and a timed-out request can succeed invisibly :cli:daemon:hardening:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-EP3H1
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Measured 2026-07-29 at load average ~190 (a worker deliberately inducing load).
`orgasmic manager dispatch-close --task TASK-G7E4R --status done` produced:

  warning: close tx appended but lifecycle update failed: daemon request
  failed ... is the daemon reachable?
  closed: TASK-G7E4R implementer.done tx=tx-20260728-orgasmic-3500

State afterwards: close tx recorded, dispatch record closed, task stranded at
`in_review`. The warning is loud (good — this is not a silent tear), but the
operator is left to repair the lifecycle by hand.

The repair then hit the second half of the defect: a follow-up
`task update --state done` returned `"changed": {}` with an EMPTY tx_id —
because the "failed" lifecycle request had actually landed server-side after
the client gave up. Client timeout is not server failure. Two consequences:

1. `dispatch-close` is not atomic across its two writes (tx append +
   lifecycle update) and does not retry or reconcile the second on failure.
2. A timed-out request can succeed invisibly, so naive retry logic can
   double-apply or mis-read state. The `{"changed":{}, "tx_id":""}` no-op
   response was correct here, but nothing documents that contract.

=== Ask

1. Make dispatch-close's task-state transition part of the same daemon
   operation as the close tx (single request, single commit), or make the CLI
   reconcile on startup of the next manager command ("close tx tx-N exists but
   task is in_review -> finish the transition").
2. Idempotency: closes and state updates should carry the started-tx (they
   already do) and the daemon should treat a re-submitted close/transition for
   an already-closed dispatch as a clean no-op with a response that SAYS it was
   already applied, distinguishable from "nothing to do".
3. While in the file: the CLI's timeout error text "is the daemon reachable?"
   misdiagnoses scheduler starvation as daemon death (three occurrences on
   2026-07-29, all with the daemon healthy and answering raw HTTP in 0.4s).
   Say "request timed out after Ns; the daemon may be healthy but the system
   is under load" and name the load if cheaply readable.

=== Acceptance

- A close whose lifecycle leg is injected to fail leaves a state the NEXT
  manager command repairs automatically, proven by test.
- A re-submitted close is a labelled no-op, proven by test.
- Injection per the TCTTD standard; verify artifact `git apply`-clean.

* DONE TASK-0RCRY No tmux call site passes -L/-S, so every probe and test session shares one server — on a dev box, the operator's own :daemon:drivers:tmux:testing:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-0RCRY
:PRIORITY: P1
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-drivers/**,crates/orgasmic-daemon/**,.orgasmic/gotchas.org
:END:

**This task was filed on 2026-07-28 with a wrong diagnosis and rewritten the same
day.** The original claim — that workers inherit the daemon's `$TMUX` and so
reach the rmux server — is false and is recorded as such in
tx-20260728-orgasmic-3226. What survives is a narrower, measured problem.

=== What was measured, and what it ruled out

Filed after a TASK-1T3FZ dispatch reported six daemon failures with
`tmux new-session failed (exit 1): server exited unexpectedly` and
`required test tooling is missing: tmux (gates 6 tests)`.

Ruled out, each by direct measurement:

- *The daemon does not carry `TMUX`.* `ps eww 32814` shows none. (The earlier
  contrary reading came from `pgrep` matching a worker's prompt text instead of
  the daemon; the pid was a claude worker, not the daemon.)
- *A worker's tmux calls are not broken.* rmux creates the worker's pane, sets
  `TMUX=/private/tmp/rmux-501/default,...`, and prepends a shim directory in
  which `tmux` is a symlink to `rmux`. Under the exact worker `PATH` + `TMUX`,
  `tmux new-session -d -s … -- sleep 1` exits **0**.
- *It is not environmental at all.* `supervisor::tests::required_test_tooling_is_present`
  passes in isolation in both the manager environment and a replicated worker
  environment (0.04 s / 0.03 s).
- *It is not worker-specific.* A full `cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon --lib` in
  the **manager** environment — no shim, no `TMUX` — reproduced three of the
  worker's six failures identically: `production_resume_native_fork_uses_pinned_claude_not_path_shim`,
  `recovery_reattaches_tmux_session_when_handle_exists`, and
  `two_recovery_chain_second_resume_uses_first_fork_session_id`
  (528 passed, 5 failed, 451 s).

So these are **full-suite concurrency failures — the TASK-STWVB family** — and
this task is not about a worker/manager divergence. The RRT4T/R2HDN open question
is still open, and is now *more* open, because the leading candidate is gone.

=== The real, narrower defect

No tmux call site anywhere passes `-L` or `-S`
(`crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/tmux.rs:1506`, `:2489`, `:3730`). Every
probe, every test session, and every production call therefore shares **one tmux
server** — whichever the environment selects. Concurrent tests create, query and
reap sessions on that single shared server, and on a developer machine it is the
same server the operator's own sessions live on.

`server exited unexpectedly` under a full-suite run, from a server that was
verified alive throughout (pid 32723, up since 13:32, still running at 15:1x), is
consistent with contention on that shared server rather than with a missing or
broken tmux.

=== Ask

- Give the test path an owned server: an explicit `-L <socket>` per test binary
  (or per test), so no test can reach a server it did not create, and so a
  developer's own tmux sessions are never touched by a test run.
- Decide separately, and state, whether production call sites should pin a
  socket too. An operator running the daemon inside tmux is the mirror image of
  this and would be a product bug, not a test bug.
- Make the diagnostic name the cause. `tmux test session should start` and
  `required test tooling is missing: tmux` are both true and both useless when
  tmux is installed, on PATH, and working — the message should name the server it
  tried and how that server was selected.

=== Acceptance

- The tmux-gated daemon tests use a server the test run owns, and a concurrent
  full-suite run does not produce `server exited unexpectedly`.
- Reproduce first: show the contention on the shared server before the fix.
  If it cannot be reproduced, say so plainly rather than shipping a speculative
  isolation change — that is precisely the mistake this task's first version made.
- Sessions created on the owned server are reaped. TASK-Z3093's guard covers
  rmux sessions, not a new tmux socket; say which mechanism reaps this one.
- The three failures that reproduce in the manager environment are re-run after
  the change and their status reported honestly, whether or not this fixes them.

=== Relationship to TASK-STWVB

STWVB is "four daemon tests fail on every full-suite run and pass alone". This
measurement says the set is at least five and includes the tmux-session-start
failures. If the socket isolation here does not fix them, that is a genuine
result and STWVB keeps them; do not widen this task into STWVB's investigation.

=== Non-goals

- Do not weaken the TASK-RRT4T sentinel to make the red go away. The red is
  correct — the tests really did not run.
- Do not use `ORGASMIC_ALLOW_MISSING_TOOLS` to paper over this. A contended
  server is not a missing tool, and the waiver would recreate the silent skip.

** Measured, one variable, 2026-07-28

The daemon runs inside an rmux pane and therefore carries rmux's `TMUX` in its
own environment:

```
$ ps eww 30834 | tr ' ' '\n' | grep ^TMUX=
TMUX=/private/tmp/rmux-501/default,32723,751
```

Every dispatched worker inherits it. A tmux client with `$TMUX` set and no
`-L`/`-S` connects to the socket named in `$TMUX` — which is the **rmux**
server's socket, and rmux is a tmux fork with an incompatible protocol version.

```
$ TMUX=/private/tmp/rmux-501/default,32723,751 tmux new-session -d -s p -- sleep 1
server exited unexpectedly
EXIT=1

$ env -u TMUX tmux new-session -d -s p -- sleep 1
EXIT=0
```

Same binary (tmux 3.6a), same host, same user, same TMPDIR. The only difference
is the inherited variable.

** Scope, measured rather than assumed

- `rmux` under the same inherited `TMUX` exits **0** — matching binary, matching
  socket. So the 7 rmux-gated tests do run in workers, and the rmux half of the
  RRT4T story was never the problem.
- The class is **tmux-only: 6 gated tests**
  (`crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs:6941`,
  `ToolRequirement::new("tmux", 6, tmux_spawn_usable_for_test().await)`).
- Observed live in the TASK-1T3FZ dispatch: `required test tooling is missing:
  tmux (gates 6 tests); gated tests did not run`, with
  `recovery_reattaches_tmux_session_when_handle_exists`,
  `failed_terminal_with_live_tmux_never_offers_reattach`,
  `boot_reattach_respawns_dispatch_completion_watcher_without_artifacts`,
  `production_resume_native_fork_uses_pinned_claude_not_path_shim` and
  `two_recovery_chain_second_resume_uses_first_fork_session_id` all failing on
  `tmux test session should start`. Before TASK-RRT4T's sentinel these skipped
  **silently** — which is precisely the historical divergence.
- No probe and no production call site passes `-L` or `-S`
  (`crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/tmux.rs:1506, 2489, 3730`), so all of them
  inherit whatever server `$TMUX` names.

** Ask

1. **Isolate the tmux server the tests use.** A test that means to exercise tmux
   should not be able to reach whatever server happens to host the daemon. Give
   the test path an explicit `-L <socket>` (or clear `TMUX` for the spawn), so
   the probe and the tests it gates talk to a server they own. Decide and state
   whether production tmux calls should do the same — an operator running the
   daemon inside tmux hits the mirror image of this, and that is a product bug,
   not a test bug.
2. **Make the diagnostic name the cause.** `tmux test session should start` and
   `required test tooling is missing: tmux` are both true and both useless here:
   tmux is installed, on PATH, and working. The failure text should say the
   server it tried, and that `$TMUX` selected it.
3. Reconcile `.orgasmic/gotchas.org`. R2HDN correctly demoted the PATH claim to a
   simulation and recorded the open question. Replace the open question with this
   measurement.

** Acceptance

- The 6 tmux-gated daemon tests pass inside a dispatched worker. Prove it by
  dispatching, not by reasoning — that is the whole point of this task.
- Reproduce first, the way it was found: set `TMUX` to a foreign server's socket,
  show the probe failing, apply the fix, show it passing.
- The manager path stays green; isolating the socket must not make tests reach a
  server they then leak. Whatever sessions the tests create are still reaped —
  TASK-Z3093's guard covers rmux sessions, not a new tmux socket.
- State whether production call sites were changed and why.

** Why this matters beyond the six tests

Every dispatched worker has been reporting a green tmux lane it never ran, for
as long as the daemon has been hosted in an rmux pane. The sentinel from
TASK-RRT4T is what made it visible; this is the first dispatch where a worker
reported the failure honestly instead of a silent skip. Any conclusion drawn from
a worker's daemon-suite count before 2026-07-28 should be treated as excluding
these six tests.

** Non-goals

- Do not weaken the sentinel to make the red go away. The red is correct.
- Do not change `ORGASMIC_ALLOW_MISSING_TOOLS` semantics; a foreign tmux server
  is not a missing tool, and papering over it with the waiver would recreate the
  silent skip this task exists to end.

* DONE TASK-K4G1D Run the mux-dependent daemon tests under tmux as well as rmux, so 'is rmux at fault' becomes a measurement :testing:daemon:drivers:rmux:
:PROPERTIES:
:DEPENDS_ON: TASK-RRT4T
:ID: TASK-K4G1D
:PRIORITY: P1
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs
:END:

Filed after the operator asked whether rmux, being far less mature than tmux,
might itself be the defect behind the recurring artifact-test failures.

It cannot currently be answered, and that is the problem worth fixing.

WHAT IS KNOWN
rmux 0.9.0 (crates.io, pinned `=0.9.0` in crates/orgasmic-drivers/Cargo.toml) is
a pre-1.0 third-party tmux clone with a tmux-compatible CLI. Measured 2026-07-26
against tmux on the same machine: 15 create+kill cycles cost 12.1 ms each against
tmux's 13.1 ms, 20 pane spawns of a warm script cost 12.8 ms against tmux's
6.9 ms, neither leaves a session behind, and neither costs syspolicyd anything.
So at the level that can be measured from outside, rmux is leak-free and merely
about 2x slower per pane spawn.

WHAT IS NOT KNOWN
Every artifact-regenerate test in crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs runs only
under rmux. There is no tmux counterpart, so when one fails there is no way to
tell whether the defect is in our driver, in rmux, or in the test's deadline.
Two of the three worker rounds on TASK-STWVB attributed that failure to a
different cause and both attributions were later withdrawn.

The one confirmed rmux-adjacent defect so far was OURS, not rmux's: TASK-8W30B,
where RmuxControl::release aborted its lifecycle task before Session::kill and
poisoned the shared ordered SDK transport. Worth noting the structural asymmetry
it exposed, though — the tmux driver drives tmux through its CLI, one process per
command and no shared state, while the rmux driver holds a persistent socket with
an ordered transport shared between Session and the lifecycle watcher. The second
design has failure modes the first cannot have, and every hang and leak this week
has been on that side. That is an argument about our integration, not about rmux's
correctness, and the two keep getting conflated.

WHAT TO DO
Parameterize the artifact-regenerate tests (and any other mux-dependent daemon
test) over both rmux and tmux, running the same assertions through each mode.

- red under rmux, green under tmux -> rmux is indicted, with a reproducer we can
  file upstream or route around by defaulting to tmux
- red under both -> the defect is ours, and we stop suspecting the dependency
- green under both -> the deadline is the defect

Depends on TASK-RRT4T: a mode that is unavailable must make the test fail or
report as ignored, never silently pass. Without that this change would just
double the number of tests that can quietly do nothing.

Acceptance:
- at least post_artifact_regenerate_hot_path_reuses_live_run_id runs under both
  modes
- a failure names which mode it failed under
- the answer to "is rmux at fault" is a test result, not a judgement call

* DONE TASK-HXSW0 Make the CLI self-documenting for agents: real help per verb and flag, no silent no-ops, a drivers listing verb :cli:agent-ergonomics:docs:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-HXSW0
:priority: P1
:write_scope: crates/orgasmic-cli/src/
:PRIORITY:    P1
:END:

Filed 2026-07-26 after a session in which the manager guessed wrong CLI verbs
four times, and one shipped convention was found instructing a hallucination.

The operator framing, which sets the constraint: fix this with better CLI help
that agents are told to consult, NOT by pasting a command cheat sheet into every
prompt. Prompt space is scarce and a stale cheat sheet is worse than none.

MEASURED FAILURES, all from one session

1. `orgasmic manager drivers` does not exist in any command group — and
   `shipped/prompt-studio/conventions/manager-dispatch.org` instructed the
   manager to run it to choose `--mode`/`--harness`. The valid pairs live only in
   `orgasmic_drivers::SUPPORTED` (crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/lib.rs:74) with no
   CLI surface at all. The convention was corrected the same day, but the
   underlying gap stands: the one fact needed on EVERY dispatch has no listing
   verb. The only discovery path is to submit a bogus pair and read the
   rejection, which does helpfully name all sixteen.
2. `orgasmic task show` — guessed repeatedly. The real verb is `task get`, and
   listing lives in a SEPARATE top-level group, `tasks list`. A singular/plural
   split where both exist and neither mentions the other is a hallucination
   generator.
3. `orgasmic run release` — a prior manager asserted it existed, corrected
   itself in the handoff, and the correction itself was then wrong. Two wrong
   records about one nonexistent verb.
4. `orgasmic worker list` — guessed, does not exist.

5. WORST CLASS — a silent no-op on a write verb.
   `orgasmic task update TASK-X --property "WRITE_SCOPE=..." --property
   "TEST_CMD=..."` returned `{"changed":{"STATE":"in_progress"}}` and dropped
   both properties without a word. The same call with lowercase `write_scope`
   and `test_cmd` worked. An unrecognised property key must be an error: a write
   verb that reports success while discarding two of three arguments is worse
   than a missing feature, because the caller has no reason to re-check.

6. Flags on the primary agent verb have NO help text. `orgasmic manager dispatch
   --help` renders `--task <TASK>`, `--kind <KIND>`, `--brief <BRIEF>`,
   `--from <FROM>`, `--model <MODEL>`, `--effort <EFFORT>`, `--worktree`,
   `--branch`, `--reason` with blank descriptions. An agent cannot learn from
   that whether `--from` is a git ref or a path, or that `--worktree-remove`
   on `dispatch-close` defaults to TRUE and force-deletes uncommitted work
   (TASK-2BPWM).

WHAT ALREADY WORKS, and should be the template

Two errors in the same session were excellent and cost zero follow-up:
- `manager dispatch` from the wrong lifecycle: "task TASK-X is in lifecycle
  stage in_progress; implementer dispatch is allowed only from BACKLOG or TODO"
  — names the rule and the allowed set.
- `node body append --section Evidence` on a node lacking it: "no section
  \"Evidence\"; sections: [] (use `set --section` to create one via add)" —
  names the fix verb.
Contrast `node body append gotchas ...` → "glossary file not found", which names
the wrong file entirely (already a recorded gotcha).

WORK

1. Give every command and every flag a one-line description that says what it
   does and what it returns. Blank `#[arg]` descriptions on agent-facing verbs
   should be treated as a bug, not a style nit.
2. State destructive defaults in the help text where the operator reads them,
   not only in the code.
3. Make unrecognised `--property` keys a hard error listing accepted keys.
   Audit for other silent-drop paths in the same shape.
4. Add a real listing verb for mode/harness pairs, sourced from
   `orgasmic_drivers::SUPPORTED` so it cannot drift.
5. Make near-miss verbs self-correcting: an unknown subcommand should suggest
   the real one (`task show` -> `task get`; `worker list` -> ?) and cross-
   reference the singular/plural split between `task` and `tasks`.
6. Audit shipped prompts and conventions for commands that do not exist. One was
   found by accident; nobody has checked the rest. A test asserting that every
   `orgasmic ...` invocation appearing in `shipped/**` parses against the real
   clap surface would make this class permanently impossible.

Item 6 is the highest-leverage item here — it converts "an agent hallucinated"
into a build failure.

Acceptance:
- an agent can discover any verb and flag it needs from `--help` alone, in at
  most three calls, without reading Rust source
- no write verb silently ignores an argument
- every command string in shipped prompts/conventions is checked against the
  real CLI surface by a test
- mode/harness pairs are listable
CONFIRMED INSTANCE, found while filing these very tasks [2026-07-26].

`orgasmic task create` has no `--priority` flag at all. Every task filed this
session used `--property "priority=P1"` on create, which was accepted silently
and discarded. ALL SEVEN tasks created today came out with priority None:
TASK-099T6, TASK-A55J7, TASK-VSWZT, TASK-S2KM0, TASK-6FNAY, TASK-2BPWM,
TASK-HXSW0. They were repaired afterwards with `task update --priority`, which
does have a real flag and works.

This sharpens item 3 beyond "unknown property keys should error". Two distinct
defects compose here:

1. The property allowlist differs between `create` and `update`. `update`
   accepts `--priority` as a first-class flag; `create` accepts neither the flag
   nor the property. The same field is settable, unsettable, or silently ignored
   depending on which verb you reach for.
2. The silent drop makes the divergence invisible. `create` returned a normal
   success object with `id` and `tx_id` and no indication that an argument had
   been thrown away.

The result is a whole session of P1 work filed as unprioritised, which is exactly
the kind of state error that later reads as "nobody triaged this" rather than
"the CLI dropped it".

Note the failure is silent in BOTH directions worth testing: an unknown key
(`WRITE_SCOPE` uppercase, dropped) and a known-but-unsupported-on-this-verb key
(`priority` on create, dropped). Fixing only the first would leave this case
intact.

TWO MORE CONFIRMED INSTANCES [2026-07-26], both found while filing a fix subtask.

4. `task create` accepts and silently discards property keys that `task update`
   accepts and persists. Reproduced on TASK-D0GA3: the same
   `--property "PARENT_TASK=TASK-2BPWM" --property "FIX_SUBTASK=t"` pair was
   dropped by `create` (drawer contained only ID, PRIORITY, TEST_CMD,
   WRITE_SCOPE) and then written verbatim by `update`, whose response echoed both
   keys under "changed". PRIORITY, TEST_CMD and WRITE_SCOPE survived `create` in
   the same invocation, so this is a per-key filter on create, not a general
   restriction. The user-visible effect is that the same command produces
   different state depending on which verb you happen to use.

5. `:PARENT_TASK:` is never read by anything. `parent_task` is derived purely
   from the id grammar — `derive_task_parent_id` (crates/orgasmic-core/src/id.rs:319)
   splits `TASK-<stem>.<digits>` and returns `TASK-<stem>`. So the property is
   accepted by `update`, stored in the drawer, echoed as changed, and ignored by
   every reader. `orgasmic task get TASK-D0GA3` still reports
   `parent_task: null` with `:PARENT_TASK: TASK-2BPWM` sitting in the file.

   This one had a downstream cost: the shipped `manager-dispatch` convention
   instructed managers to file fix subtasks with a `:PARENT_TASK:` back-edge, so
   the documented mechanism produced no edge at all. Corrected in the convention
   the same day — parentage must be minted into the id as `TASK-<parent>.N`.

The pattern across all five instances is one defect: `--property` is an untyped
passthrough with no schema, so every layer is free to accept, store, filter or
ignore a key independently, and every combination reports success. The fix is not
five special cases. It is (a) validate keys against the schema at write time and
reject unknown or miscased ones with a message naming the correct key, and
(b) make `create` and `update` accept the same set, or say why they differ.

INSTANCE 6 [2026-07-26]. `orgasmic tx record` is the only mutation verb that is
NOT project-scoped by default. Without `--project`, it writes to
$ORGASMIC_HOME/state/tx/YYYY-MM.org — the global home file — and reports success
with a differently-shaped tx id (tx-20260726192932-05e34dce) rather than the
project's tx-20260726-orgasmic-NNNN. Every sibling verb (`task update`, `node
body append`, `task create`) resolves the project from the cwd and needs no
flag. The help text for --tx-path says "defaults to $ORGASMIC_HOME/state/tx/
YYYY-MM.org", which is accurate and is the only warning you get; nothing in
`tx record --help` suggests --project is load-bearing.

Cost: one manager.action for TASK-D0GA3 was written to the home tx file and had
to be re-recorded with --project. The stray entry is still there. A manager
following the obvious invocation silently loses every tx it records off the
project ledger and cannot tell from the exit code.

Fix direction: default `tx record` to the cwd project like its siblings, and
keep --project / --tx-path as explicit overrides.

:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-GEZHQ

`an_unusable_credential_leaves_no_lease_no_session_and_no_run`

ACCEPTING a dispatch whose claude credential the test intends to be unusable:

  created: {"run_id":"run-20260728T221637-…","driver":"acp-stdio",
  "harness":"claude",…}
    left: 200
   right: 400

The `left: 200` body shows a REAL RUN was created. The assertion text names the
stake: the CLI relies on the 400 to roll back the worktree it created, so a 200
here leaves a worktree behind for a dispatch that should never have started.

This is deliberately NOT filed into the load-flake class: the EP3H1 worker's
read is that it is environment-dependent rather than timing-dependent — a
usable claude credential exists on the dev machine, and parallelism changes
which credential the preflight probe observes. A preflight that PASSES when it
should refuse is a product defect surface, not a test-timing defect. Green in
isolation, so the gate does not catch it.

=== Ask

1. Diagnose how the probe found a usable credential when the test constructs an
   unusable one — fixture bleed (real ~/.claude reachable from the test env?),
   probe fallback order, or a race in credential selection.
2. Fix so the test's intent holds under parallel load: an unusable credential
   yields 400, no lease, no session, no run, no leftover worktree — regardless
   of what else is on the machine.
3. If the root cause is the test env leaking the operator's real credentials
   into the probe, treat that as the defect (isolation), not the assertion.

=== Acceptance

- The test survives >=5 consecutive full-suite loaded runs (pre-fix red count
  pinned for A/B if reproducible).
- Injection per TCTTD standard, `git apply`-clean, self-tested with
  `orgasmic verify --artifact` before reporting.

* DONE TASK-JGHNC Seven tmux-gated daemon tests accept the rmux shim and have been measuring rmux while reporting tmux
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-JGHNC
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

From TASK-K4G1D (2026-07-29), measured, not inferred: inside an orgasmic
worker, `tmux` on PATH is the rmux shim, and a `-L`-pinned call through the
shim creates an RMUX server (the socket lands in /private/tmp/rmux-501/, and
the real tmux cannot connect to it). The 0RCRY owned-server mechanism does not
protect against this — the isolation holds, but the multiplexer is the wrong
one.

Consequence: seven tmux-gated daemon tests gate on `tmux_on_path()`, which
accepts the shim, so IN EVERY WORKER-RUN SUITE they have been measuring rmux
while reporting tmux:

  boot_rehydration_reattaches_tmux_session,
  explicit_reattach_tmux_session_endpoint,
  pending_plan_reattach_existing_session,
  boot_reattach_respawns_when_session_gone,
  failed_terminal_with_live_tmux_session_is_not_resurrected,
  production_resume_native_fork_uses_pinned_claude_not_path_shim,
  two_recovery_chain_second_resume_uses_first_fork_session_id

(names as listed in K4G1D's report §6.2; verify against HEAD before acting).

K4G1D added the strict availability rule (`tmux_mode_availability_for` — a
shimmed tmux counts as ABSENT, loudly) but deliberately did NOT widen
`tmux_on_path()`: regating seven tests is a decision, not a fix — it would
newly fail the tmux sentinel in every worker environment, and it partly
reframes the worker-vs-manager failure comparisons recorded on TASK-STWVB.

=== Ask

1. Decide: should these seven tests demand REAL tmux (strict rule), or is
   testing-through-the-shim acceptable for some of them (in which case they
   should SAY they ran rmux)? Record the decision and its reason.
2. Apply it: either regate on the strict rule (accepting that worker-run
   suites will report tmux NOT RUN via the honesty manifest — that is the
   truth), or split tests into genuinely-mode-agnostic (rename/parameterize per
   K4G1D's pattern) vs really-tmux-specific (strict gate).
3. Re-examine any STWVB comparison that relied on "the worker ran these under
   tmux" — it ran them under rmux.

=== Acceptance

- No daemon test can report mode=tmux while executing rmux: proven by test
  (K4G1D's strict rule is the template; its verify artifact pins the
  silent-GREEN failure mode).
- The honesty manifest names whatever is gated out in a worker environment.
- Injection per TCTTD standard, self-tested before reporting.

* DONE TASK-HAREX A worker that exits without finalize stays live for tens of minutes instead of being released :daemon:supervisor:dispatch:recovery:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-HAREX
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Observed 2026-07-26 on run `run-20260726T080801-79056fdb262348afb3e0eb6633d3cab2`
(TASK-STWVB, acp-stdio/claude, installed runtime 0.0.15-dev.1).

The worker wrote a complete report to `last.txt` and exited WITHOUT calling
`orgasmic dispatch finalize`. Roughly forty minutes later the run was still
`sub_state: implementer.working`, `live`, with its process long gone. It was
only released when a manager ran `manager dispatch-close`, which releases
explicitly (`release_dispatch_run`, crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs:627).

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A MISSING FEATURE

The rescue-policy convention is explicit that this is the daemon's job:

  "A failed agent run (protocol-end without terminal declaration, fatal driver
  error, stall / max-duration / idle timeout) ends after the daemon writes the
  authoritative release tombstone and, for dispatches, a
  manager.dispatch_orphaned tx."

So the intended sequence for a vanished worker is: daemon detects protocol-end
or stall, writes the Release tombstone with
`reason = protocol_end_without_finalize`, emits `manager.dispatch_orphaned`, and
only then does the manager choose a rescue action via `orgasmic run recover`.
None of that happened here. There was no orphan tx, and the manager had to
close the record for the run to go away.

Deliberately NOT the fix: adding an `orgasmic run release` verb. Release is not
a manager-authorized action in this model — `run recover` is — and a manual
release verb would paper over the daemon failing to write its own tombstone.

LIKELY ALREADY FIXED, NEEDS CONFIRMING

The running daemon is 0.0.15-dev.1 and predates f80b577,
"a declared failure ends the run instead of waiting for the harness" (TASK-TJKFC),
whose message says `terminal_event_releases_transport` allowlisted
`tmux | tmux-tui | rmux`, so on every OTHER transport a terminal event set the
outcome and released nothing, leaving release to stream end. acp-stdio is
exactly such an 'other transport'. That is a strong candidate for the whole
explanation.

So the first step is confirmation, not code: re-run this scenario on a daemon
built from current main — dispatch acp-stdio/claude, let the worker exit without
finalize, and check whether a Release tombstone and `manager.dispatch_orphaned`
appear on their own within the stall window. If they do, close this against
f80b577 with the evidence. If they do not, the stall detector is not reaching
this state at all and that is the bug.

Either way the observable acceptance is the same: a worker that exits without
finalize produces a daemon-written release tombstone and an orphan tx without
any manager action.

* DONE TASK-6HJYT Split the liveness question out of the recovery inventory :daemon:api:architecture:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-6HJYT
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Problem: =GET /api/runs= answers three unrelated questions with one full pass
over every session file on disk.

1. "Is anything live?" — the CLI's fence before restart, update, and
   dispatch-close (=daemon_lifecycle.rs::live_manager_runs=). It reads the
   response, keeps =live=, and filters to =task_id= starting =manager.launch:=.
2. "What should the UI badge show?" — =ui/src/hooks/useTaskRuns.ts=.
3. "What needs recovery?" — the actual crash-recovery inventory, which is the
   only one of the three that genuinely requires reading durable history.

Question 1 needs no disk at all. Live runs are supervisor-local: the daemon
already holds them in memory, with their identities. Answering it through the
recovery inventory means a restart fence pays for classifying every historical
run on the board.

The codebase already contains this reasoning, applied to the singular endpoint
and never to the plural one. =get_run= (api.rs, "Exact active-run lookups are
supervisor-local") checks =state.supervisor.snapshot()= first and only falls
back to =recovery_status= when the id is not live, with the comment: "Worker
finalize and manager close must not scan unrelated durable recovery history
before they can act on a live run whose id they already know." That is exactly
the argument for splitting the list endpoint too.

Why this is worth doing even though the scan is now cheap: the coupling, not the
duration, is the defect. Measured on the operator's board 2026-07-25 after
TASK-KWSTJ: 224 session files, 2.42 GB on disk, 31.4 MB inspected, 0.24 s to
first byte — down from 41.9 s. Before that fix the same fence failed outright:
=manager dispatch-close --status aborted= died after 10.03 s against the CLI's
10 s deadline, so a dispatch that failed at startup could not be closed by the
documented verb. Two defects multiplied — startup left the mess, enumeration
prevented cleaning it. A control-path check that cannot fail for reasons
belonging to unrelated historical runs removes that whole class.

Work:
1. Give the liveness question its own answer sourced from the supervisor
   snapshot, with no session-file reads. The CLI fence and any other
   "is something running right now" caller move onto it.
2. Keep =GET /api/runs= as the recovery inventory it actually is. Decide
   explicitly whether the UI badge path belongs on the live source, the
   inventory, or a third shape — it wants live state per task, not history.
3. Do not duplicate classification logic. If the live bucket is derived in two
   places it will drift; the supervisor snapshot should be the single source for
   "live" and the inventory should consume it rather than recompute it.
4. Naming should stop implying that =/api/runs= is a general run list. It is a
   recovery inventory and reads as one only after reading the handler.

Acceptance:
- the restart/update/dispatch-close fence performs no session-file reads
- that fence still refuses correctly while a manager terminal is live, and
  still permits when only historical runs exist
- =GET /api/runs= keeps its current classifications and bounded-scan metrics
- a regression proves the fence answers on a board whose session files are
  unreadable or absent, since its correctness no longer depends on them

* DONE TASK-MRJRK A registered project can be missing from the index, and the 404 blames the wrong thing :P1:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-MRJRK
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Problem: a project can be registered on the board, listed by `orgasmic project
list`, and still be absent from the index snapshot, at which point every route
that addresses it by id fails with a 404 that names the project as though it
were unregistered. The operator's only signal is an error that points at the
wrong thing, and the only known remedy is `orgasmic reindex` - which nobody
tries, because nothing suggests the index is the problem.

Two things need fixing, and they are separable.

1. The diagnosis. `select_project` (api.rs) reports a missed lookup as
   `not_found("project {id}")`. That message is indistinguishable from a genuinely
   unknown project, so it sends the reader to check registration - the one thing
   that is definitely fine, since `project list` just showed it. The message
   should distinguish "no such project on this board" from "registered but not
   in the current index snapshot", and the latter should name the remedy
   (`orgasmic reindex`). This is cheap and is most of the operator-visible value.

2. The underlying gap. A project that is registered but missing from the
   snapshot is a state the daemon can sit in indefinitely: nothing retries, and
   nothing reports it. Whatever the cause, the daemon should either converge on
   its own or say plainly that it has not. A `status` field naming registered-
   but-unindexed projects would make the condition self-reporting rather than
   something an operator stumbles into through an unrelated 404.

Do not start by assuming a cause. What is actually established is thin, and one
plausible-sounding explanation has already been checked and ruled out.

EVIDENCE, 2026-07-25, live on the operator's daemon
Found incidentally while trying to record gotchas during TASK-TJKFC.

- Daemon booted 17:53:31Z (pid 10647, boot_id a6fdd006). It had restarted on its
  own during the session; the previous instance was pid 71878 from 16:49.
- At ~18:03Z - ten minutes after that boot, so this is NOT a boot race -
  `orgasmic node body append <anything> --project orgasmic` returned
  `404 {"error":"project orgasmic"}`. Same for ddd.
- The same command with `--project orsl`, `--project lynx-auth` and
  `--project rare` got PAST project resolution (they failed later, on the node
  id or the glossary file). So exactly two of five were missing.
- `orgasmic project list` showed all five with clean ids at that moment. Ids
  were checked through `cat -v` for hidden characters: clean.
- `orgasmic reindex` at ~18:04Z fixed it immediately. The retry of the same
  command then failed at the *next* stage instead, which is how we know project
  resolution had started succeeding.
- Corroborated in ~/.orgasmic/logs/daemon.out.log: the first `glossary file not
  found` warnings for ddd appear at 18:04:23Z - i.e. only after the reindex,
  because before it the request never got far enough to touch a file.

RULED OUT, so nobody re-runs it
- Not a boot race. Ten minutes elapsed, and the boot log shows a completed
  reattach pass at 17:53:35 with no scan-timeout or partial-load warnings.
- Not "`status` reads a different source". `status.projects` is
  `snap.projects.len()` (api.rs:5753) - the same map the lookup missed. So
  `status` should have reported 3, not 5, during the window. It was simply never
  run at that moment, which is the one piece of evidence this report is missing
  and the first thing to capture if it recurs.

STILL OPEN
Whether the two projects were dropped after a successful load, never loaded at
all, or present under a different key. Note `load_project` inserts under
`board_entry.id`, and the two affected projects are the two with the largest and
most actively written `.orgasmic/` trees - both were being written continuously
by this session while the others were idle. That is a correlation, not a cause.

REPRODUCTION NOTE
If this recurs, capture in this order before reindexing, because reindex
destroys the evidence: `orgasmic status` (the projects count is the decisive
missing datum), `orgasmic project list`, and the failing node call for each of
the five project ids.

ACCEPTANCE
- A lookup miss for an id that IS registered on the board reports that
  distinctly from an unknown id, and names `orgasmic reindex` as the remedy.
- The condition is visible without provoking it: an operator can see that a
  registered project is not in the current snapshot without first hitting an
  unrelated 404.
- A test drives a snapshot that is missing a registered project and asserts the
  error text distinguishes the two cases. The test must construct the state
  directly rather than wait for whatever produced it here, since the cause is
