* DONE TASK-Z3093 LiveSessionGuard serializes but never reaps, so every failing live-session test leaks an rmux session :testing:rmux:leak:production:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-Z3093
:PRIORITY: P1
:test_cmd: cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon
:END:

`LiveSessionGuard` serializes live-session tests and reaps nothing. Every one of
its 9 copies is the same flock-only type whose `Drop` calls `fs2::FileExt::unlock`
and returns. Cleanup of the rmux session the test created is a *trailing
statement* in the test body, so a panic anywhere above it skips the reap and the
session, its pty and its harness process survive the test binary.

This is the open source of the TASK-8W30B leak that a production-path fix cannot
close. TASK-6FNAY hardened `RmuxControl::release` (merged 83ea420) and the leak
still reproduced afterwards: two orphan sessions found 2026-07-28 at 13:20,
ages 3h18m and 2h46m, both running
`orgasmic_daemon-e5f5d4f31537ab72.fixture.sh artifact-ready`, both 404 to the
daemon and absent from every ledger, i.e. from test fixtures rather than from a
dispatch (tx-20260728-orgasmic-3117). Earlier the same day three more were found
at 09:57 (tx-20260728-orgasmic-3103, refiled onto 8W30B by
tx-20260728-orgasmic-3110).

** Measured inventory

- 9 definitions of `struct LiveSessionGuard(std::fs::File)`, byte-identical in
  behaviour, across 3 crates:
  - `crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs:15772`
  - `crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs:5478`
  - `crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/rmux.rs:2329`
  - `crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/tmux.rs:2481`
  - `crates/orgasmic-drivers/tests/rmux_release_reaps_session.rs:23`
  - `crates/orgasmic-cli/src/test_support.rs:37`
  - `crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/dispatch.rs:38`
  - `crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/list_output.rs:33`
  - `crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/bootstrap_smoke.rs:46`
- 85 `live_session_guard()` call sites. Heaviest: `cli/tests/dispatch.rs` 30,
  `daemon/src/api.rs` 19, `drivers/src/modes/rmux.rs` 12,
  `drivers/src/modes/tmux.rs` 12.
- All 12 artifactor tests in `api.rs` that call `seed_test_artifactor_harness` /
  `seed_busy_artifactor_harness` spawn a real rmux session. 11 end with a
  trailing `supervisor.release(..)` or `release_with_finalization(..)`; one,
  `launch_artifact_generation_persistence_failure_releases_run`
  (api.rs:27530), has no release in the test body at all and relies on the
  production path releasing for it — confirm that it actually does.
- The fixture never exits on its own. `artifact-ready` loops
  `echo '> ready'; read -r line || exit 0`, and inside an rmux pane stdin never
  closes, so an unreaped session runs until something kills it
  (`crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/test_fixtures.rs:20`).

** Why this compounds

TASK-STWVB records four daemon tests that fail on every full-suite run and pass
alone, and the TASK-C0XMR merge note (`0860861`) says that family gained two more
members under load. A load-induced failure is a panic, and a panic is exactly the
path that skips the trailing release — so **the flake and the leak are the same
event**. Every dispatched worker runs the full suites, so leak rate scales with
dispatch volume, which is what the two-per-day observation shows.

A leaked session also outlives its worktree: pid 42520 still named
`.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/task-C0XMR/worktree`, a directory `dispatch-close` had
already removed.

** Fix

One shared guard that owns cleanup, not nine that own a file lock.

- Give the guard a registration surface (`guard.owns(run_id)` /
  `guard.owns_session(name, endpoint)`) and reap on `Drop`, unconditionally,
  before releasing the flock. Drop runs on the panic path, which is the whole
  point.
- The reap must not itself depend on a live SDK transport — reuse the CLI
  fallback shape TASK-6FNAY established (`rmux_session_reap_args(endpoint,
  name)`, rmux.rs:1505), addressed at the endpoint the handle owned. A `Drop`
  cannot await, so the reap has to be a blocking call or a spawned-and-joined
  helper; pick one and say why.
- De-duplicate: one definition in a shared test-support location that all three
  crates use. Nine copies is how a fix to one of them silently misses the other
  eight.
- Keep the flock behaviour exactly as it is. Serialization is load-bearing and
  independent of the leak.

** Acceptance

- A live-session test that panics mid-body leaves no session behind — proven by
  a test that deliberately panics inside the guard's scope and then asserts the
  session is gone.
- `rmux ls` is empty after a full `cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon` and after
  `cargo test -p orgasmic-cli` on a machine that started with no sessions.
- One `LiveSessionGuard` definition remains in the tree.
- `launch_artifact_generation_persistence_failure_releases_run` either releases
  through the production path (demonstrated) or gains a guard registration.

** Non-goals

- Do not change `RmuxControl::release`; TASK-6FNAY owns the production path and
  is in review.
- Do not fix the TASK-STWVB flakes themselves. This task makes their cost
  bounded, not zero.
- Do not run `legacy_drivers_and_explicit_pairs_emit_equivalent_start_events`
  (TASK-099T6) — it bills real money. Skip it explicitly on the drivers suite.

** HIGH — a genuine terminal failure followed by a worker finalize is turned green

`crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs:6098,6141-6149`.

`DriverEvent::RunFail` is a real failure: the production drain maps it to
`ReleaseOutcome::Failed` and stores it on the run
(`supervisor.rs:3429-3463`). Explicit release deliberately waits for that drain
and persists the stored terminal outcome, so a finalize racing a queued `RunFail`
produces the authoritative shape
`Release { outcome: Failed, finalized_by_worker: true }`
(`supervisor.rs:2181-2228`).

The new scan sets `pending_failure` and then clears it **unconditionally** on
`finalized_by_worker`, inspecting neither the failure kind nor the release
outcome, and returns `StageOutcome::Completed`. The stage watcher then writes
`<stage>.completed` for a run the supervisor classified as failed.

The added negative test does not cover the claimed case:
`stage_outcome_fails_when_a_fatal_driver_error_has_no_worker_finalize_after_it`
uses `finalized_by_worker: false`, while the adversarial case is failure **plus**
finalize.

Required (reviewer's direction 1): make semantic failure sticky across worker
finalize. At minimum `RunFail` must survive a later finalize. For fatal driver
errors, persist enough release-boundary or classification data to suppress only
the errors *caused by* the finalize teardown, rather than clearing every earlier
failure. Add a regression for
`RunFail -> Release { outcome: Failed, finalized_by_worker: true }`, plus a
production-path race test.

** Open question the reviewer raised, and it is the crux

What durable session event should identify the finalize-admission boundary? The
trailing release cannot distinguish a queued genuine `RunFail` from a fatal error
caused by teardown, because **both are drained before that release**. Answer this
explicitly before writing the fix; a suppression rule that cannot name its
boundary will get one of the two cases wrong. Record the answer in the task or a
decision, not only in a code comment.
The reviewer is right that the trailing release cannot carry the boundary, and
the evidence is stronger than "cannot distinguish": the two cases produce a
byte-identical release. `terminal_outcome_for_event` maps `RunFail` and fatal
`DriverError` to the same `ReleaseOutcome::Failed`
(`supervisor.rs:3429-3436`), both are drained before `release_one` freezes
`rec.terminal_outcome.unwrap_or(outcome)`, so a genuine queued `RunFail` and a
teardown-induced fatal error both write
`Release { outcome: Failed, finalized_by_worker: true }`. The release is not a
weak discriminator; it is not a discriminator at all. Asserted directly by the
production-path test pair
`worker_finalize_does_not_clear_a_run_fail_drained_during_teardown` and
`worker_finalize_still_suppresses_the_error_its_own_teardown_caused`, which
assert the identical release shape and opposite stage outcomes.

The boundary is two rules, not one, because no single durable event answers
both halves.

1. KIND, for semantic failure. `RunFail` is only ever emitted from a harness
   protocol result — Claude `is_error`, a failed codex turn, a cursor stop
   reason. Teardown reaps the process group, and every transport classifies
   that as a fatal `DriverError` (`classify_pane_exit`,
   `orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/rmux.rs:1901-1959`); nothing synthesizes a
   `RunFail`. So `RunFail` is sticky across a later worker finalize,
   unconditionally and regardless of position. Position must not matter: a
   `RunFail` still queued when the finalize is admitted is drained AFTER the
   admission marker, so a marker-only rule would clear exactly the case this
   task exists to fix.

2. A durable ADMISSION MARKER, for driver errors. The supervisor appends a
   `SessionEventKind::Note` carrying `{"note": "worker_finalize_admitted"}` at
   the instant it grants finalize admission — after
   `explicit_release_in_progress = true`, before
   `stop_and_join_driver_producer`, awaited so it is on disk first
   (`supervisor.rs`, `release_one`). Teardown cannot produce anything before
   it. A fatal driver error after the marker is one this finalize caused and
   stays suppressed; one before it was already there and is sticky.

Why a new event rather than an existing one: the release is the only other
durable session event on this path, and it is appended after the drain, so
every candidate discriminator is already behind it. This is a session-schema
addition, but not a `Lifecycle` variant change — `Note` is the existing
free-form supervisor channel, so `orgasmic-core` is untouched and every reader
that filters by kind ignores it.

Backward compatibility: sessions with no marker (written before this change, or
where the append failed and logged) keep the TASK-C0XMR reading for driver
errors — dominance by the following finalize. Rule 1 still applies to them, so
the reported HIGH is fixed for old sessions too.

If a third case appears later, the question to ask is which of the two rules it
belongs to: is the failure semantically declared by the harness (rule 1, sticky
by kind), or is it a transport/process artifact whose blame depends on whether
this finalize caused it (rule 2, sticky unless after the marker)? A signal that
fits neither means a new durable event is needed, not a new heuristic on the
existing ones.

** Acceptance

- A run with a queued `RunFail` that is then finalized by its worker is recorded
  as failed, not completed.
- A teardown-induced error after a clean finalize is still suppressed — the
  original C0XMR symptom must not regress.
- Both cases have regressions, and the failure case exercises
  `finalized_by_worker: true`.
- The finalize-admission boundary is named and durable, not inferred from
  ordering alone.

** Non-goals

- Do not revert `0533735`.
- Reviewer finding 2 (a live stage loses its completion watcher across daemon
  restart) is **out of scope** and filed separately. It is pre-existing and
  outside this diff.

* DONE TASK-K5NDR ORGASMIC_RUN_ID leaks into test subprocesses, so the CLI suite fails inside a dispatch :tests:defect:dispatch:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-K5NDR
:PRIORITY: P1
:TEST_CMD: cargo test -p orgasmic-cli
:END:

`ORGASMIC_RUN_ID` leaks from the operator's (or a worker's) environment into
test subprocesses, so every `dispatch finalize` test in
`crates/orgasmic-cli/tests/dispatch.rs` resolves the AMBIENT run id instead of
the one its fixture created, and fails with `no live run ...`.

Reported by the TASK-6AYEJ implementer, and it reproduced the failure on
UNMODIFIED code before touching anything —
`dispatch_finalize_commit_flag_leaves_clean_committed_worktree` fails when run
from inside a live dispatch and passes outside one. All of that task's gates had
to be run as `env -u ORGASMIC_RUN_ID cargo test -p orgasmic-cli`.

This is the same class of defect as TASK-RRT4T (tests that silently skip when
tooling is absent) and TASK-STWVB (tests that pass alone and fail in-suite): the
suite's result depends on who is running it and from where, rather than on the
code. It is worse than either in one respect — it makes the CLI suite
UNRUNNABLE from inside a dispatch, which is exactly where every dispatched
worker runs it. A worker that does not know the incantation reports a red suite
it cannot explain, or worse, works around it.

The manager's own runs of this suite pass because a manager shell has no
ORGASMIC_RUN_ID set (verified: unset). So the manager and the worker see
different results from the same command on the same tree, and the manager's
green is the misleading one.

Fix direction: the test harness must not inherit ambient orgasmic run identity.
Clear `ORGASMIC_RUN_ID` (and audit sibling `ORGASMIC_*` variables that steer
resolution) in the fixture that builds the command, not in a wrapper the caller
has to remember. A test whose correctness depends on the operator's environment
is not a test.

Acceptance:
- `cargo test -p orgasmic-cli` passes with `ORGASMIC_RUN_ID` set to an arbitrary
  value in the environment
- the fixture, not the caller, is responsible for the isolation
- an audit of other `ORGASMIC_*` variables that can steer CLI resolution is in
  the report, with each one either cleared or explicitly justified as safe

:PROPERTIES:

From TASK-Z7VQK (2026-07-29), measured and causally confirmed: a fast-exiting
harness on subprocess-stream-json LOSES ITS TRANSCRIPT and its run_complete —
the run is flagged protocol_end_without_finalize and orphaned with an empty
transcript. Product-visible data loss, not a test defect.

Mechanism (subprocess_stream_json.rs:418 at Z7VQK's base): the driver's select
loop covers stdout, stderr and a command channel; the command branch `break`s
on release OR channel-close WITHOUT draining stdout, and tokio::select! picks
at random among ready branches. A harness that runs to completion quickly (the
fixture ran 9.5ms, printed all 16 lines) can have its entire output pending
when the loop exits; finalize_subprocess_exit then distills an empty summary
(`exit_code=Some(0) distill_is_some=false assistant_len=0 system_chunks=0`).

Causal confirmation: identical build plus a 200ms sleep before the harness
body (the latency Gatekeeper used to supply) suppresses most failures — fixed
4 failures vs delayed-start 1 in one window. The effect scales with load.
Historically masked because every fresh fixture paid ~160ms first-exec
evaluation; TASK-Z7VQK's shared pre-warmed fixture removes that sedative, which
is why its branch is held unmerged pending this fix.

Candidate shape (from Z7VQK's report, verify by reading): `biased;` with
stdout first, plus a bounded drain of stdout after `released` before
finalize_subprocess_exit. Adjacent precedents: TASK-HAREX's DrainGate bounds a
release-requested drain in the SUPERVISOR; this is the DRIVER-side sibling —
do not conflate them, but the derived-bound discipline applies.

=== Ask

1. Fix the drain so a harness's produced output is never lost to loop-exit
   ordering: whatever it wrote before exit reaches the session and run_complete
   synthesis. Bounded (derived) so a harness that never stops producing cannot
   wedge a release — state the bound and its derivation.
2. Audit the OTHER stream-consuming drivers (acp-stdio bridge, anything with a
   select over child stdout + command channel) for the same break-without-drain
   shape; fix or report per instance.
3. Prove end-to-end with Z7VQK's un-sedated fixtures (your worktree is based on
   its branch): the six-test dispatch_endpoint family green suite-concurrently
   — the acceptance BOTH tasks share. Pin A/B counts (Z7VQK's report has the
   baseline table).

=== Acceptance

- The family (all six named tests) survives >=3 suite-concurrent rounds green
  with the fast shared fixture, counts pinned.
- A deterministic test pins the property: a harness that exits immediately
  after printing N lines yields all N in the session (no sleep-masking — the
  Z7VQK report's warning: a fixture-side delay would hide the defect, never
  add one).
- Injection per TCTTD standard, git apply-clean, self-tested with
  `orgasmic verify --artifact` before reporting.

* DONE TASK-KPMFK A live stage loses its completion watcher across daemon restart, so no terminal tx is ever emitted :daemon:stage:boot:defect:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-KPMFK
:PRIORITY: P1
:test_cmd: cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon
:END:

Found 2026-07-28 by the TASK-C0XMR reviewer (reviewer-codex-rmux,
run-20260728T103249) as finding 2. Pre-existing and outside the C0XMR diff, so it
did not block that round — but it falsifies the cross-restart guarantee that
review asked C0XMR to prove, so it belongs to the same family.

** The defect

`crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs:3321-3330,8973-9020`.

`post_stage` keeps `stage`, `target` and completion ownership **only** in the
spawned in-process `StageCompletion`. Boot reattach reconstructs the run but
respawns only `DispatchCompletion`, and only when both `last_path` and
`stdout_path` exist.

Stage runs carry `last_path: Some` and `stdout_path: None`
(`api.rs:3239-3267`), so they land in the partial-artifact warning branch and **no
stage watcher is recreated**.

Consequence: if the daemon restarts while `grill`, `plan` or `architect` is live,
a later worker finalize is persisted but no `<stage>.completed` or
`<stage>.failed` tx is ever emitted. The C0XMR outcome rule is never called at
all. The stage silently has no terminal record.

No restart test exercises a stage watcher, which is why this survived.

** Fix, per the reviewer

Persist stage completion metadata — `stage`, project/task, and `target` — in
recoverable lifecycle state, and have boot reconciliation respawn or directly
reconcile `StageCompletion`.

Note the partial-artifact branch is doing real work for dispatch runs; the fix is
to stop treating `stdout_path: None` as "incomplete" for a run shape that legitimately
never has one, not to weaken the branch for everybody.

** Acceptance

- A daemon-restart test for each shared stage path (`grill`, `plan`, `architect`).
- The `architect` case must cover its report-only terminal tx specifically —
  `architect` is a STAGE kind whose worker finalize emits `architector.reported`
  rather than `architector.done` (recorded near `api.rs:22475`, TASK-6AYEJ.1), so
  a watcher keyed on `.done` would pass the other two and still miss this one.
- A stage live across a restart emits its terminal tx.

** Non-goals

- Do not fold this into the C0XMR fix round (TASK-QSSQH). That round owns the
  failure-stickiness rule; this one owns watcher recovery. They touch the same
  file and must not be dispatched concurrently.

* DONE TASK-VSWZT A run can appear live with no release surface able to clear it, blocking the update fence :runtime:supervisor:recovery:bug:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-VSWZT
:priority: P1
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Observed 2026-07-26 clearing run-20260726T080801-79056fdb262348afb3e0eb6633d3cab2
(TASK-STWVB implementer). The run showed as `implementer.working` in
`orgasmic run list` .live for ~80 minutes after its worker died, and NO surface
could clear it.

THE DEAD END

- `POST /api/runs/:id/release` returned 404 `{"error":"active run <id>"}` — even
  though the same run was present in `GET /runs` .live. Both the snapshot lookup
  (api.rs:6173) and `SupervisorError::RunNotFound` (api.rs:6197) return that same
  string, and `.live` is fed from `supervisor.snapshot()` (api.rs:7651), so the
  run was in the snapshot while `release_with_finalization` could not find it.
  Those two views of the supervisor disagreed.
- `orgasmic manager lease-release` refuses while a live run holds the lease.
- `orgasmic run recover` offers only reattach_tmux / resume_native_fork /
  start_recovery_run. The rescue-policy convention lists *abandon* as one of four
  manager judgments, but no verb implements it.
- `orgasmic manager dispatch-close` had already run; the dispatch record was
  closed and the run stayed live regardless.

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC

`refuse_if_live_runs` (crates/orgasmic-cli/src/update.rs:436-462) reads exactly
`GET /runs` .live and refuses the runtime update for any entry. One phantom run
therefore blocks `orgasmic update` and any publish behind that fence, with no
documented way out. The only route that worked was a full daemon restart.

WHY THE SESSION NEVER CLOSED

The session JSONL ends at seq 1657 `run_complete` ("worker finalize for
TASK-STWVB") and seq 1658 fatal `driver_error` ("claude exited with status exit
status: 143"), with no `Lifecycle::Release`. The supervisor kept its entry; the
tombstone was never written. On the next boot the classifier read the same file
and correctly returned terminal_noop ("session ended with terminal driver
event") via `session_driver_terminal_event` (api.rs:9104), so the durable
evidence was sufficient all along — only the live supervisor disagreed.

Note this is the second wrong answer recorded about this same run. The prior
handoff asserted it had been released and that `run list` reported 0 live; it had
not been, and did not.

WORK

1. Reconcile the two supervisor views, or make `POST /runs/:id/release` able to
   clear anything that `GET /runs` .live reports. A run the fence refuses to
   ignore must be releasable by the surface documented to release it.
2. Implement abandon as a first-class manager verb so the fourth branch of
   rescue-policy is executable, not just describable.
3. Write the release tombstone when a driver reports a fatal terminal event.
   `run_complete` followed by a fatal `driver_error` should end the run rather
   than leave it working; the boot classifier already treats that pair as
   terminal, so the two paths disagree about the same evidence.
4. Consider having `refuse_if_live_runs` name the escape hatch in its error text.
   It currently says "Close them or use the existing force path deliberately"
   without saying how, which is what sent this session looking for a verb that
   does not exist.

Acceptance:
- a run reported in `GET /runs` .live can always be cleared without restarting
  the daemon
- a worker whose harness dies after run_complete leaves a release tombstone
- `orgasmic run list` .live and the release path never disagree about whether a
  run exists

SCOPE RETARGETED [2026-07-29, after TASK-HAREX merged]: HAREX diagnosed and fixed the producer of this task's first symptom. The 404-from-release while live-in-snapshot disagreement has exactly one producer — a release that started (explicit_release_in_progress set) and could not finish because the event drain awaited an unbounded recv() held open by a stray driver-internal sender. HAREX's DrainGate bounds the drain once a release is requested (RELEASE_DRAIN_BUDGET, derived, 20s), so that window is now at most one budget and self-clearing. WHAT REMAINS THIS TASK'S SCOPE: (1) the missing *abandon* judgment in `orgasmic run recover` (the rescue-policy convention lists four manager judgments; abandon has no verb); (2) the update-fence consequence and its documentation (a phantom live run blocking `orgasmic update` with no documented way out — partially eased by TASK-6HJYT's liveness split if that lands); (3) if desired, a regression proving the 404/live disagreement stays impossible (HAREX's tests cover the drain; a direct two-views-agree test would pin the property itself).

NUANCE FROM TASK-6HJYT [2026-07-29]: the 404/live disagreement verdict is narrowed-not-closed. post_run_release and /runs .live read the SAME supervisor snapshot at two different times — HAREX removed the persistent producer (a wedged release, self-clearing within RELEASE_DRAIN_BUDGET now), and 6HJYT removed the staleness amplifier (liveness no longer waits behind a whole-board classification pass). What remains is the structural TOCTOU of two reads of one map; closing it means reading liveness under the supervisor lock as one step with the action (the TASK-1T3FZ close-guard pattern). Fold that into this task's remaining scope if a direct two-views-agree regression is wanted.

* DONE TASK-5P60H Harden launchd boot backoff and prove single-owner slow startup :daemon:launchd:recovery:
:PROPERTIES:
:DEPENDS_ON: TASK-KWSTJ
:ID: TASK-5P60H
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Treat the crash-loop report as a regression audit of the now-present lock-first boot protocol, not as proof that all suggested redesigns are still needed. Current source already acquires the home lock before project scanning, publishes boot-state heartbeats, makes explicit start return `StillBooting` after 20 seconds, lets autostart follow live heartbeats up to a finite backstop, retries bind for 8 seconds, and the current 3,118-tx daemon reached listening in about 8.45 seconds. Preserve those semantics.

Work:
1. Add a deterministic service-level test with an artificially slow project scan longer than the old readiness timeout and concurrent `daemon start`/autostart attempts. Assert exactly one lock owner and one eventual listener, callers observe the same pid/boot phase, no competitor reaches bind, and no healthy boot is killed/restarted.
2. Add an explicit `ThrottleInterval` to the generated macOS LaunchAgent and verify install/update rewrites existing plists. Keep restart policy intentional and test repeated abnormal exits use launchd backoff.
3. Correlate `daemon.lock`, boot-state owner, pid liveness, and authenticated status in diagnostics. A lock-held pre-bind owner with fresh heartbeat is `starting`, not unhealthy; a dead owner is stale and may be replaced only after the OS lock is actually released. Never break a live file lock based only on HTTP failure.
4. Capture phase durations and tx/project counts for config, project scan, session migration/catalog load, watcher attach, reattach, and bind. Optimize or make replay incremental only if measurement still exceeds the accepted startup budget after the run-catalog work; do not expose normal API reads from a partially rebuilt index merely to make health green. A tiny early health responder is allowed only if it cannot serve normal routes and tests prove the handoff to the full router.
5. Make the no-progress/absolute readiness budgets configurable only if production measurement shows current heartbeat behavior insufficient; preserve a finite backstop.

Acceptance: the slow-start matrix produces no alternating Address-in-use/instance-lock errors, launchd does not hot-loop, one daemon becomes ready, and normal routes see a fully rebuilt index. Include a real generated-plist assertion and a macOS smoke or launchctl transcript where available.
** Notes
Handoff from TASK-KWSTJ: `GET /api/runs` now classifies from a bounded prefix/tail lifecycle scan, but `reattach_live_runs_on_boot` still calls `read_session_file` on every session JSONL — on the reported board that is 2.239 GiB read at boot before the daemon can serve. It was left alone deliberately: boot reattach takes the *last* Acquire/RunMeta rather than the first, so switching it to the bounded scan is a semantic change that belongs with the slow-start work, not with the request-path repair. `orgasmic_core::scan_session_lifecycle` is ready to reuse.

`crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs:6849,7118-7141`.

`terminal_tx` is optional on the release payload. A `finalized_by_worker` release
carrying `terminal_tx: None` releases the run and returns success with
`terminal_tx_id: None`. An old CLI then still owes the separate `POST /tx`.

On acp-stdio the release reaps the old finalize process's own setsid group
**before** that POST is made, leaving a released run with no terminal tx. That is
exactly the loss TASK-WGXKD exists to prevent, arriving through the skew
direction the capability handshake does not cover.

** What is already correct — do not redo it

The other direction is fail-closed and proven: new CLI against an old daemon is
refused by the TASK-WGXKD.1 capability handshake, and its regression passed under
review. Only old CLI → new daemon is open.

** Fix, per the reviewer

Two shapes, choose and record which:

A. Fail closed before releasing when `finalized_by_worker: true` arrives with no
   `terminal_tx`, and tell the operator to upgrade or restart the CLI. Keeps the
   lease held rather than releasing into a known-lossy path.
B. Reconstruct the terminal tx server-side from what the daemon already knows,
   so the old CLI's missing POST stops mattering.

A is the safe one and matches the handshake's existing posture; B removes the
skew concern entirely but has to be correct about what the daemon can reconstruct
without the worker's own report.

** Acceptance

- An old-payload / new-daemon acp-stdio regression that proves either the lease
  stays held, or the terminal tx lands atomically with the release.
- The chosen shape is recorded, not just implemented.
- TASK-WGXKD's version-skew claim is restated to match what is actually true.

** Non-goals

- Do not touch the capability handshake's new-CLI/old-daemon direction; it works.
- Do not fold this into the TASK-WGXKD.2 fix round (TASK-Q07Y5) — the reviewer
  scoped them apart deliberately, and Q07Y5's writer-budget work is unrelated.

The acp-stdio claude adapter isolates its worker from the operator's MCP

different blast radii — and rmux is now the standing default for every dispatch
(manager-dispatch, standing worker matrix, 2026-07-26).

MEASURED ON A LIVE WORKER, not read from code alone. TASK-6AYEJ dispatched as
implementer-claude-rmux (rmux / claude / claude-opus-5 / high), pid 37956:

    claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --model claude-opus-5 --effort high
           --session-id a3c31a76-... -- <compiled prompt>

No --strict-mcp-config. Compare adapters/claude.rs:361-365, where the acp path
pushes it deliberately, with the comment "without it this machine loaded nine
MCP servers into a worker that wants none". `claude mcp list` on this machine
today returns exactly nine: Figma, Google Drive, Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion,
plugin:svelte, syncntn, ray-exomem-dev, ray-exomem. Six connect.

The rmux argv is built at modes/rmux.rs:550-575 and pushes only
--dangerously-skip-permissions, --model, --effort, --session-id.

DO NOT REACH FOR --bare. It skips hooks, LSP, plugin sync, auto-memory and
CLAUDE.md discovery, but it also makes Anthropic auth strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
or apiKeyHelper — OAuth and keychain are never read. Our workers run on
subscription auth, so --bare would break them. That is precisely why the acp
adapter branches on ClaudeCredentialMode and, for NativeLogin, rebuilds "what
--bare would have given us, minus its credential policy" from
--strict-mcp-config alone. rmux is NativeLogin. Use the same narrow flag.

SIZE THE WIN HONESTLY — it is an isolation win, not a context win. Measured with
two `claude --print` runs in this repo, identical but for the flag: prefix
tokens 26528 without, 26284 with. A 244-token difference. Nine servers' worth of
tool schemas would cost far more than that if they were loaded eagerly, so the
harness appears to defer MCP tool schemas and charge only for names. Anyone
justifying this task on token savings is quoting a number that no longer holds.

The real argument is blast radius. A dispatched implementer working on a Rust
CLI has no business holding live, authenticated handles to the operator's Gmail,
Google Drive, Google Calendar and Notion. Nothing in the worker persona forbids
calling them, the run is --dangerously-skip-permissions, and the operator is not
watching every pane. TASK-6AYEJ's worker invoked no MCP tool, which is luck
rather than a control.

  today. Codex reads MCP from ~/.codex/config.toml. Determine whether it has a
  comparable flag and either use it or record plainly that it does not exist.
- one test per harness asserting the flag is present by default and absent when
  the operator supplied it

Out of scope: changing --dangerously-skip-permissions, touching the acp path,
and any CLAUDE.md / plugin / hook suppression. Those are separate arguments and
at least one of them (CLAUDE.md discovery) we actively want.

Acceptance:

A second leak class, measured 2026-07-28 11:35Z and **not** covered by
TASK-Z3093. That task made `LiveSessionGuard` reap rmux *sessions* on the panic
path. It does not own *spawned child processes*, so tests whose fixture forks a
process tree still leak it exactly as before.

SIGHTING [2026-07-29, TASK-TZKAC harness round 8]: after ~50 minutes of 4x64-thread daemon-suite load, the machine held 31 leaked /bin/bash driver-shim children accumulating zero CPU, and the round wedged at 552-560 of 566 tests per copy with no further output (killed by hand). Distinct from the tmux sentinel gate; makes long loaded rounds unreliable as evidence. Same class as this task's premise: fixtures leak process trees the session-level guard does not reap.

SIGHTING [2026-07-29 ~07:40 local]: orphan session orgasmic-rmux-run-20260729T030752-0e4f153badef4e93b93350da8b8ce35e on the LIVE rmux default server — no dispatch record, not in /runs/live, created 06:07 local during a worker's test window. A test created a real orgasmic-rmux-run-* session on the default endpoint and never reaped it. Manager reaped by exact name after confirming non-liveness. Same class as this task's premise, now on the live server rather than an owned one — whichever test binary did this needs the owned-endpoint treatment (the KPMFK/QRTT8 rmux stage tests are the recent suspects; their sessions are supposed to ride LiveSessionGuard).

** Measured

Three orphaned `cursor-worker-sibling` fixture trees, all reparented to PPID 1,
each holding a `/bin/sleep 3600` child:

| fixture pid | child pid | age    | executes from |
|-------------|-----------|--------|---------------|
| 5770        | 8260      | 10 min | `target/debug/deps/` (main checkout) |
| 13734       | 14957     | 42 min | `.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/task-z3093/worktree/target/debug/deps/` |
| 24454       | 26030     | 39 min | `.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/task-z3093/worktree/target/debug/deps/` |

Two of the three run from a worktree `dispatch-close` had **already removed** —
the binary keeps executing from an unlinked path, which is the same signature the
rmux leak showed (tx-20260728-orgasmic-3117) and is why neither is visible to a
`git worktree list` audit. Reaped by hand; recorded in
tx-20260728-orgasmic-3182.

** Mechanism

`crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/test_fixtures.rs`, the `cursor-worker-sibling` arm:

```
cursor-worker-sibling)
    ready=$2
    /bin/sleep 300 &
    (exec -a worker-server /bin/sleep 300) &
    /usr/bin/touch "$ready"
    /bin/sleep 3600
    ;;
```

It backgrounds two sleeps and then sleeps an hour in the foreground, so it never
exits on its own. The owning test,
`supervisor::tests::poll_direct_child_pid_prefers_worker_server_over_generic_sibling`,
kills it as a **trailing statement** — the same shape TASK-Z3093 fixed for
sessions, unfixed for processes.

And, once again, **the flake and the leak are the same event**: that test
panicked with `fake cursor-agent did not start children` in the manager's own
gate at 11:35Z, and the TASK-QSSQH worker independently recorded it failing on
the pristine tree under load. Every load-induced failure of this test leaks a
process tree that survives for an hour.

** Fix

Extend the same ownership idea from sessions to processes, in the one shared
guard TASK-Z3093 established (`orgasmic_drivers::modes::rmux::test_tooling`).

- A registration surface for spawned pids — `guard.owns_process(pid)` or a
  fixture handle that registers itself — reaped on `Drop`, before the flock
  releases, exactly as sessions are.
- Kill the **process group**, not the pid. The fixture's children are backgrounded
  subshells; killing only the parent orphans `sleep 3600` to init, which is
  precisely what two of the three observed cases show. Spawn the fixture in its
  own group so the group id is knowable.
- Audit every fixture arm that outlives its foreground command:
  `cursor-worker-sibling` (`sleep 3600`), `artifact-busy` (`sleep 120`),
  `claude-capture` (`exec sleep 600`), and `config` (`exec sleep 30`). Each is a
  candidate leak on its own test's panic path; say which ones are already covered
  by an existing kill and which are not.

** Acceptance

- A test that registers a fixture process and panics mid-body leaves no process
  behind — proven by injection the way TASK-Z3093 was: remove the reap, watch the
  new test fail naming the survivor, restore it, watch it pass.
- After a full `cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon`, no `fixture.sh` process and no
  `sleep` child of one remains.
- The fixture arms listed above are each classified as covered or fixed.

** Non-goals

- Do not change the rmux session reap; it is merged, verified and orthogonal.
- Do not fix `poll_direct_child_pid_prefers_worker_server_over_generic_sibling`'s
  flakiness itself. That belongs to TASK-STWVB. This task makes its cost bounded.
- This is **not** TASK-Z9C73. That one is a zombie harness child under the rmux
  daemon on the production release path; this is a test fixture's own process
  tree and involves no rmux at all.

* DONE TASK-7QM8M Bound the bytes boot auto-reattach reads per session file :daemon:boot:performance:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-7QM8M
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Boot auto-reattach reads every session file whole. It calls
=read_session_file= -> =std::fs::read_to_string=, so a project with large TUI
transcripts pays their full size at every daemon start. This is the same
unbounded read TASK-KWSTJ removed from =GET /api/runs=, still present on the
boot path; measured there, a 2.4 GB board cost 24.7 s and the bounded scanner
reduced it to 28 MB inspected.

TASK-KKGKM moved this scan after bind and onto a blocking thread, so it can no
longer stop the daemon serving, and it is no longer on the critical path. What
remains is cost and latency: reattachment of the operator's live manager
terminal is delayed by however long the read takes.

=boot_reattach_candidate= consumes only lifecycle-class events — acquire,
run_meta, release, the terminal driver event, and the external-registration
marker — which is exactly what =scan_session_lifecycle= retains, so the
substitution should be direct.

One correctness subtlety must be handled explicitly rather than assumed. The
function calls =latest_run_segment=, which picks the newest contiguous run
segment by run_id. On a truncated scan the prefix may hold one segment's
acquire while the tail holds a later segment's end, so the two windows can
describe different runs. =classify_session_files= already guards this with
=scan.final_envelope_retained= before trusting =release_outcome=; reattach needs
an equivalent rule. Getting it wrong means a live run is silently not
reattached, which looks like the run vanished.

Acceptance:
- boot reattach inspects bounded bytes per session file, not file size
- a truncated scan cannot combine two run segments into one candidate
- a still-live run in a multi-segment session file is still reattached
- measured against a production-shaped board, as TASK-KWSTJ was

* DONE TASK-RKTH1 Deliver oversized tmux worker prompts without hitting the imsg ceiling
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-RKTH1
:PRIORITY: P1
:TEST_CMD: cargo test -p orgasmic-drivers --lib
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-drivers/**
:END:

** Description

The tmux mode delivers the worker's compiled prompt as an argv element
(=push_initial_prompt_argv=, =modes/tmux.rs=) and hands the whole command line
to =tmux new-session=. tmux packs an entire command line into ONE imsg to its
server, and imsg's payload ceiling is =MAX_IMSGSIZE= (16 KiB) less the header.
A dispatch whose brief pushes the packed argv past that ceiling dies with
tmux's own =command too long=, surfaced to the operator as an opaque
=500 failed to acquire worker run=.

Measured 2026-07-30 on tmux 3.6a: a 16 000-byte argv spawns, 20 000 does not.
Typical compiled prompts here are 4-5 KB, which is why this stayed hidden until
TASK-3NJ9K was dispatched with a 5.5 KB brief.

The ceiling is tmux's own compile-time constant. It cannot be raised from
outside tmux, and refusing the dispatch with "shorten your brief" pushes a
tool limit onto the operator. The prompt must instead reach the pane by a route
that is not the imsg command line.

=modes/rmux.rs= drives its panes through the rmux SDK socket
(=ProcessSpec=), not the CLI, so it does not share this ceiling; the rmux CLI
does (same fork), which is why a CLI probe shows the same limit.

** Acceptance

- A tmux dispatch whose compiled prompt is far larger than the imsg ceiling
  (100 KB+) spawns and reaches the harness with the prompt intact.
- Prompt bytes are preserved exactly, including trailing whitespace and
  newlines, embedded single quotes, and non-ASCII.
- Dispatches under the ceiling keep their current, direct argv route; the
  fallback engages only when the packed argv would not fit.
- No operator-facing refusal that asks for a shorter brief.
- The Claude launch gate (=native_resume_mode=) and the pinned-executable
  identity check keep working when the fallback engages.
- Nothing that carries the prompt is left readable by other users, and the
  spawn failure path does not leak the artefact.
- Unit tests cover the size accounting and the escaping; a live tmux test
  proves an oversized prompt actually spawns, gated the way every other
  tmux test in the binary is.

** Prior Evidence

Failure captured in =~/.orgasmic/logs/daemon.out.log= 2026-07-30T13:41:32Z:
=driver transport unavailable: tmux new-session failed (exit 1) on the default
shared server (no -L/-S and no TMUX_TMPDIR): command too long=. Workaround at
the time was shortening the TASK-3NJ9K brief from 5476 to 2724 bytes.

* DONE TASK-CB6GQ Sections can be created by typo and never removed: give node body an inverse verb and explicit creation
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-CB6GQ
:PRIORITY: P2
:TEST_CMD: cargo test -p orgasmic-cli -p orgasmic-daemon -p orgasmic-core
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-cli/**,crates/orgasmic-daemon/**,crates/orgasmic-core/**
:END:

** Description

=orgasmic node body set --section <TITLE>= routes to
=Rewriter::upsert_section_text=, which **appends the section when it is
missing** (=orgasmic-core/src/org.rs=). Any string becomes a permanent heading:
a typo, or a section name borrowed from the wrong node kind. That is how
=handoff-current= acquired a task-shaped =** Description= section, whose own
body reads "superseded — this section was created in error".

It cannot be removed through supported tooling, and not because removal is
hard. Every layer below the CLI implements it:

| layer | create | remove |
|-------|--------|--------|
| =orgasmic-core= | =upsert_section_text= / =append_section= | =remove_section= (round-trip tested) |
| daemon =NodeEditOp= | =AddSection= / =SetSectionBody= | =RemoveSection= |
| route =POST /api/org/node/:id/edit= | yes | yes |
| =orgasmic-cli= | =node body set --section= | **nothing** |

The neighbouring surface is symmetric — =node prop= has =set= and =unset=.
=node body --section= has only the creating half. =node delete= cannot stand in:
it addresses nodes by =:ID:= and a =**= section has none.

So there are two defects, and fixing only the first would make the mistake
easier to clean up rather than harder to make:
1. no inverse verb, though the op exists and is already wired to the route;
2. creation is implicit, so nothing catches the moment the wrong name is
   written — which is when the error is cheap.

** Acceptance

- =orgasmic node body unset --section <TITLE> <ID>= removes a named section
  through the existing =RemoveSection= op. =--section= is required; the verb
  never clears a node's free prose body by omission.
- Removing a section that does not exist is refused by name, listing the
  sections the node does have. It is never a silent no-op.
- =node body set|append --section= **refuses to create** a section that does not
  yet exist unless =--create= is passed. The refusal names the title and lists
  the existing sections, so a typo shows itself as a typo.
- Writes to sections that already exist are unchanged — no new flag needed for
  the ordinary case, and no existing caller breaks.
- A round trip is byte-exact: =--create= a section, write it, =unset= it, and
  the org file matches its pre-creation bytes.
- A parity test asserts every =NodeEditOp= variant the daemon accepts is either
  reachable from the CLI or listed in one place as deliberately not exposed.
  This asymmetry existed because nothing compared the two surfaces.
- Finish by removing the dead =** Description= section from =handoff-current=
  with the new verb, so the fix is demonstrated on the node that motivated it.

** Prior Evidence

Section-creating write path: =crates/orgasmic-core/src/org.rs= =upsert_section_text=
falling through to =append_section=. Unexposed removal: =NodeEditOp::RemoveSection=
in =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs=, =Rewriter::remove_section= in
=orgasmic-core=. CLI surface: =crates/orgasmic-cli/src/node.rs= =NodeBodyCmd=
(=Set=, =Append=) versus =NodePropCmd= (=Set=, =Unset=). =NodeKind= in
=orgasmic-core/src/node_kind.rs= already carries a CLI/daemon parity test and is
the precedent for asserting two surfaces agree.

Related gotcha already recorded (=0a054b3=): =node body set= replaces prose only,
so =**= headings inside a body are refused or silently truncated.

* DONE TASK-95SGV finish_dispatch_cleanup releases by a recomputed worktree key, so a removed directory leaks the reservation forever :daemon:supervisor:hardening:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-95SGV
:PRIORITY: P1
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-daemon/**
:END:

Found by the TASK-1T3FZ worker while building the close-guard reservation, in a
path that round deliberately did not touch.

=== Evidence (manager, 2026-07-29)
Merged bf555ae. Rescued after a host reboot killed the dispatch mid-flight: the
worktree held one clean commit (277fd49) and the run had already reported, so
nothing was lost.

Manager-replayed proof, not the worker's account of it:
=orgasmic verify TASK-95SGV= PASS — injection applied, red at exit 101 matching
the pinned signature ("the reservation must be released even though the
worktree directory is gone"), tree byte-identical after revert, green at exit 0.
Replayed again against fully-merged main (after JQ8AV and FZB6T landed on the
same files) and PASSED again.

Gates on merged main: =cargo fmt --all --check= clean; =cargo clippy -p
orgasmic-daemon --all-targets -- -D warnings= clean.
=cargo test -p orgasmic-daemon --lib= 617 passed / 7 failed under a 4-job
concurrent load (1m avg 18.8); all 7 re-ran green in isolation in under 0.4s
each, including both close-guard tests inside this change's blast radius
(=explicit_reattach_{rmux,tmux}_is_fenced_out_of_a_worktree_a_close_guard_holds=).

NOT independently reviewed: manager integration review + injection replay only.

** The defect

`finish_dispatch_cleanup` — the TASK-NW4WV rollback path — looks its reservation
up by a **worktree key it recomputes after the directory has been removed**.
Path normalization on macOS resolves `/var` → `/private/var` only while the path
exists; once the directory is gone the recomputed key can differ from the one
installed, the lookup misses, and the reservation is never released.

A leaked reservation is not inert. `Supervisor::acquire_impl` blocks on
`cleanup_reservations`, so a stale entry silently refuses every future acquire on
that worktree path — and dispatch worktree paths are deterministic per task, so
the task becomes permanently undispatchable with no diagnostic naming why.

** Why the new path is immune, and why that is the fix to copy

TASK-1T3FZ's `reserve_dispatch_close` / `finish_dispatch_close` release by
`close_guard_id` — an opaque handle minted at install time — precisely so that
release never depends on recomputing a key from a path that may no longer exist.
Reservations also gained `owner_pid`, swept when an out-of-process holder dies.

`finish_dispatch_cleanup` should adopt the same shape: release by handle, and
carry an `owner_pid` backstop. This is a port of a verified fix, not a new
design.

** Ask

- Reproduce first. Install a reservation against a path under a symlinked
  prefix (`/var/...` on macOS), remove the directory, then call the existing
  release and show the lookup missing. If it does not reproduce on this
  platform, say so and say what would be required — that is a useful finding and
  should not be replaced by a speculative fix.
- Port the guard-id release and `owner_pid` sweep from the close path.
- Make a leaked reservation diagnosable: an acquire refused by a reservation
  should name the reservation, its owner pid, and whether that pid is alive.
  Today the operator sees a refusal with no way to tell a live cleanup from a
  stale entry.

** Acceptance

- A regression that removes the directory between install and release and shows
  the reservation released anyway; it must fail if the release reverts to the
  recomputed-key lookup.
- An acquire blocked by a reservation whose owner is dead is swept rather than
  refusing forever, and the refusal message names the owner either way.
- The TASK-1T3FZ close-guard tests still pass unmodified.

** Non-goals

- Do not restructure `cleanup_dispatch` or move it behind the daemon endpoint.
  TASK-1T3FZ considered that and recorded it as the larger follow-on if the
  daemon-state-only boundary is ever rejected; it is not this task.

** Description

The three injection proofs cover their narrow predicates, but the reviewer
found nine remaining acceptance and safety gaps:

1. History maintenance implements dry-run only; no confirmed recoverable
   archive/compaction transaction exists.
2. History inspection marks every =text_chunk= reclaimable, including
   structured ACP/subprocess evidence, and exact byte accounting misses
   torn/blank records.
3. A failed-recoverable run restores per-poll board/session rescans, and all
   terminal records are classified before paging.
4. Semantic retention bounds individual strings rather than the serialized
   event/subtree, allowing unbounded many-small-string or deep payloads.
5. A tombstoned run can become attachable again when its old path is reused.
6. Snapshot dirty/throttle state is global instead of per project, and cold
   boot rebuilds are not persisted by the production path.
7. Semantically corrupt in-root snapshot entries can survive refresh without a
   real direct-child session file.
8. The synchronous catalog holds its global mutex across blocking filesystem
   work from async request and writer paths.
9. Exact =run show <id>= cannot resolve terminal runs older than the default
   list window.

** Acceptance

- Implement a confirmed, dry-run-first maintenance transaction with a stable
  manifest, transport-aware reclaimability, recoverable archive or atomic
  rewrite, explicit confirmation, rollback, corruption and partial-write tests.
- Preserve structured ACP/subprocess evidence; reclaim only proven rendered
  pane payloads and account every input byte exactly, including blank and torn
  final records.
- Bound the serialized semantic event/subtree as a whole and replace over-budget
  or over-depth content with digest, byte count and a truthful source reference.
- Make recovery links catalog-authoritative, page/filter before classification,
  avoid per-poll session rescans, and make exact-id lookup direct.
- Make tombstones terminal for a run identity unless a durable worktree
  identity proves continuity; add remove-plus-recreate coverage.

  session-directory authority and current file identity.

* DONE TASK-4CSMY.1 Fix reviewer findings: glyph/role-aware marker recognition and a bounded stdout drain
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-4CSMY.1
:IMPLEMENTS: TASK-4CSMY
:PRIORITY: P1
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs, verify/TASK-4CSMY/, verify/TASK-JQ8AV/

:END:

** Description

Second review round on the pane evidence channel. Reviewer verdict NEEDS FIXES —
BLOCK SHIP (=tx-20260802-orgasmic-4104=). Two findings land in
=supervisor.rs=; the third is TASK-T7KSH and is NOT in this scope.

*FINDING 1 — HIGH, BLOCKS SHIP.* =supervisor.rs:5126-5131,5148-5171,5182-5197=.

The hardened classifier still accepts a COMPLETED assistant row as a live status
row. TASK-JQ8AV.1 measured that transcript bodies, tool results and footers are
indented two spaces and made column 0 the discriminator — but the measured
Claude assistant bullet =U+23FA= is ITSELF at column 0
(=supervisor.rs:10121-10130=), and:

- =spinner_status_row= accepts ANY punctuation glyph, not a known status glyph;
- =interrupt_hint_status_row= accepts ANY at-most-two-token label.

So an at-rest final assistant line of the shape =<bullet> Considering… (2s)= or
=<bullet> Working (7s • Esc to interrupt)=, inside the last 12 non-blank rows,
returns =Some=; the subtree CPU probe then credits the wedge =Working= on every
expired sweep until the four-hour ceiling. This is precisely the
wedge-dies-on-schedule violation the FIRST block (=tx-4055=) was raised about,
surviving the fix that was supposed to close it.

WHY THE SHIPPED REGRESSIONS MISS IT, which is the part worth reading before
writing new ones (=supervisor.rs:10675-10718=): the existing at-rest arms put
their exact marker ABOVE the region, indent their tool echoes, and prefix their
assistant quote with prose. Every one of them avoids the forged-IN-region case
by construction. That case is what the previous block asked for and it is still
untested.

*FINDING 2 — MEDIUM, does not independently block.*
=supervisor.rs:4949-4986=. =probe_command_stdout= enforces its deadline only
until the DIRECT child exits. If that child exits successfully after spawning a
descendant that inherited stdout, line 4985 joins the reader thread with no
deadline and never kills the stored process group. The supervisor returns
=Unknown= after its outer timeout, but the blocking task, the reader thread and
the descendant all survive — the same leak class TASK-JQ8AV.1 set out to close,
through the one door it left open. The existing group test
(=supervisor.rs:9911-9966=) covers a direct child that NEVER exits, not a
successful parent whose descendant holds the pipe.

** Acceptance

- Marker recognition is glyph- and ROLE-aware, not punctuation-shaped. Reject
  the measured assistant/action bullets (Claude =U+23FA=, codex transcript
  bullet) and admit only measured status combinations. Note the reviewer
  MEASURED a live codex status row during this review — =-o- Working (4m 11s
  esc to interrupt)=, flush left, third from the non-blank bottom — so codex is
  now a confirmed true positive that must keep working, not an unmeasured guess.
- Regressions for the forged-IN-region case on BOTH real transports: a bare
  =<bullet> Considering… (2s)= and a bare =<bullet> Working (7s Esc to
  interrupt)= inside the final 12 non-blank rows of an at-rest pane, proving the
  run dies on the FIRST expired sweep rather than surviving to the ceiling.
- Stdout draining shares the probe absolute deadline. If the direct child exits

** Description

Second review round on the compact run catalog. Reviewer verdict NEEDS FIXES —
five HIGH findings block ship, two MEDIUM remain actionable
(=reviewer.done= tx =tx-20260802-orgasmic-4111=; findings
=tx-4096=..=tx-4102=).

The unifying defect, and the thing to fix rather than patch around: DELETION
AUTHORITY IS DERIVED RATHER THAN REPROVEN. The catalog documents itself as
disposable derived state, and compaction then treats its cached semantics as
permission to destroy session evidence.

*1. HIGH, BLOCKS SHIP* — =run_catalog.rs:1523-1547=, =run_history.rs:587-602=.
=classify_history_line= takes the FIRST byte occurrence of =type= anywhere in
the first 64 KiB instead of proving =event.type=. A valid pane semantic event
whose nested payload contains =type=text_chunk= BEFORE its outer type is
classified =rendered_tui=, and =build_compacted= then drops the whole record.
The regression at =run_catalog.rs:2636-2689= only covers minimal events whose
first =type= happens to be the outer discriminator. Impact: explicit
maintenance destroys tool and result evidence.
FIX: identify the envelope and outer discriminator with a bounded STRUCTURAL
streaming parser; if it cannot be proven, classify unparsed and FAIL CLOSED.
Add nested-type collision regressions and assert byte-for-byte preservation.

*2. HIGH, BLOCKS SHIP* — =run_history.rs:379-436,513-531,683-755=.
=apply_compaction= mutates a session file, appends the result in memory, and
IGNORES every per-file =write_manifest= failure. A crash or ENOSPC after the
live rename but before a durable manifest update leaves the archived original
and the rewritten live file absent from =manifest.results=, and rollback
iterates only =results= — so it cannot restore them. Manifest and live-directory
renames are not followed by mandatory directory fsyncs.
FIX: a durable per-file state machine, propagated journal failures, parent
directory fsyncs, and a rollback reconstructable from PLANNED archive identities
even when the final result record is missing. Fault-inject after archive, stage,
rename, and result-journal boundaries.

*3. HIGH, BLOCKS SHIP* — =run_history.rs:465-531,574-620,683-755=,
=writer.rs:748,790-845,938-943=. Forward compaction does ONE pre-read
fingerprint check, compares only reclaimable record and byte COUNTS, never
compares the planned =reclaimable_sha256=, builds from one read and archives
from a SECOND read. There is no maintenance lock and no session-writer fence.
An append landing after the check is omitted from the replacement, and the
rename leaves the cached append handle writing to an ORPHANED INODE. Rollback
then overwrites the current path without proving it still holds the compacted
generation.
FIX: serialize maintenance per project, fence or close the writer handle,
compact and archive ONE proven byte generation, compare the planned digest,
revalidate immediately before commit, and refuse rollback unless the destination
matches the recorded post-compaction fingerprint and digest.

*4. HIGH, BLOCKS SHIP* — =run_catalog.rs:608-666,787-820,1039-1060=,
=run_history.rs:208-245=. Snapshot admission checks JSON shape, version, session
path and file fingerprint — then accepts =lifecycle=, =terminal=, =driver= and
=transport= VERBATIM. A steady-state refresh treats the unchanged fingerprint as
a cache hit and never rederives those semantics, and =plan_compaction= trusts
=entry.is_terminal= and =entry.transport= as deletion authority. So a valid-JSON
but semantically corrupt snapshot can present a LIVE or ACP file as terminal
rmux data and authorize its deletion. Note =semantically_corrupt_snapshot_entries_are_refused=
(=run_catalog.rs:2115-2202=) tests PATH and FINGERPRINT corruption, not semantic
field corruption — the name overclaims what it proves.
FIX: never use the derived catalog as sole deletion authority. Rederive terminal
state and transport from the CURRENT session generation during planning and
apply, or cryptographically bind every semantic field to verified source bytes,
and fail closed.

*5. HIGH, unmet acceptance, BLOCKS SHIP* — =session.rs:175-200,574-595,1595-1660=.
=SessionWriter= has no transport context and ACCEPTS =DriverEvent::TextChunk=
from a pane transport, retaining a bounded head plus digest. The lock test
injects a 4 MiB repaint but asserts only that the file grows by LESS THAN 8 KiB.
So one repaint is bounded — not forbidden — and repeated redraw events still
grow the JSONL linearly, contrary to the zero-persisted-redraw acceptance
criterion and to the test comments themselves.
FIX: reject pane =text_chunk= at a transport-aware writer/supervisor boundary,
and make the regression assert ZERO =text_chunk= envelopes and no
repaint-derived growth. A real tmux/rmux production-path test is still needed.

*6. MEDIUM* — =run_catalog.rs:787-833,883-915=. Rebuild and authority updates
capture and compare a per-path invalidation counter, but STALE paths capture no
generation and commit with an unconditional remove — and the commit deletes the
counter too. A refresh that observed a path absent can commit after another
refresh or the writer recreated it, evict the newer entry and RESET the
generation: a lost-update/ABA window. The stress test at
=run_catalog.rs:2415-2474= hides it behind a final quiet refresh.
FIX: plan stale eviction with a monotonic generation and remove only if it is
unchanged and no newer entry exists. Do not delete the path generation.

*7. MEDIUM* — =run_catalog.rs:1097-1141=. A tombstone revives when the current
directory has the recorded device and inode. Inode numbers ARE reusable, so an
unrelated checkout can eventually satisfy it; conversely a legitimate returned
volume with renumbered inodes never revives, and a tombstone that never had an
identity can never recover. The recreated-path test assumes a fresh directory
gets a different inode, which is an assumption about the filesystem rather than
a guarantee.
FIX: either make tombstones truly terminal, or model temporary unavailability as
its own state and verify continuity with immutable worktree/dispatch authority
rather than dev+inode alone.

** Open questions the reviewer raised, which need a DECISION before coding

- Is =run-catalog.json= trusted authority or disposable derived state? The
  module docs say derived and rebuildable; compaction treats cached semantics as
  deletion authority. These cannot both be true.
- Should a pruned worktree ever revive? If yes, the design needs a stronger
  persistent identity and a distinct unavailable state. If no, the same-inode
  revival path should be removed outright.
- What component owns maintenance exclusion against the writer and against
  concurrent compact/rollback requests? No such owner exists on the reviewed
  route.

Answer these in the task or in =decisions.org= before writing code — findings 3,
4 and 7 all resolve differently depending on the answers.

** Acceptance

- Every fix direction above, with the fail-closed rule applied throughout:
  where authority cannot be proven from current bytes, refuse rather than
  delete.
- Fault-injection coverage at the archive, stage, rename and result-journal
  boundaries, plus crash and full-disk cases for both forward and rollback.
- The redraw lock asserts ZERO persisted pane =text_chunk=, not a byte ceiling.
- Nested-type collision, semantic-field snapshot corruption, and stale-eviction
  interleaving each get a regression that fails without the fix.
- All four FZB6T injection artifacts keep replaying red-then-green. RE-CUT any
  artifact whose hunks this round rewrites and SAY SO explicitly.
- fmt, clippy -D warnings, and focused crate tests green. Do NOT run the billed

*THE FIX ROUND REINTRODUCED THE DEFECT IT WAS PROTECTING AGAINST.* TASK-4CSMY.1
replaced "any punctuation glyph" with the =STATUS_SPINNER_GLYPHS= allowlist to
stop a completed assistant row rescuing a wedge. That closed the false-RESCUE
hole and opened a false-KILL one, which is the direction no at-rest test can see.

*THE MEASUREMENT*, taken from the INSTALLED Anthropic Claude Code 2.1.220
binary — not from a fixture, not from a billed harness run:

: if(process.env.TERM==="xterm-ghostty")
:   return ["\xB7","✢","✳","✶","✻","✻"];
: return   ["\xB7","✢","✳","✶","✻","✽"];

So the real frame sequences are:
- normal:  =·= U+00B7, =✢= U+2722, =✳= U+2733, *=✶= U+2736*, =✻= U+273B, =✽= U+273D
- ghostty: same first five, =✻= repeated in the last slot

=STATUS_SPINNER_GLYPHS= (=supervisor.rs:5205-5214=) currently holds
=● ✽ · ∗ ✢ ✳ ✻ ◦=. Against that measurement:

- *U+2736 =✶= IS MISSING, and it is a real frame in BOTH sequences.* A
  provider-bound claude turn that freezes on that frame is REJECTED by the
  tightened classifier; subtree CPU stays below threshold, no new pane bytes
  arrive, and the supervisor stall-releases a healthy worker at the budget
  boundary. That is exactly the TASK-JQ8AV incident.
- U+2217 =∗= is present and appears in NEITHER sequence. It was labelled a
  "frame sibling" and is not one. Harmless in the false-kill direction, but it
  is an unmeasured entry in a table whose whole purpose is to be measured.

Manager independently re-ran the same extraction against the same binary and
confirms the reviewer byte for byte.

*WHY THE TESTS DID NOT CATCH IT*, which is the more important half. Both
real-pane acceptance arms hard-code a single glyph, =✽ Quantumizing…=
(=supervisor.rs:10767=, =10922=), and the unit loop at =10413-10419= only proves
that every entry ALREADY IN the table is accepted. A table that is missing an
entry passes both. The suite cannot distinguish a complete allowlist from an
incomplete one, so the next drift in claude''s frame set will land silently too.

** Acceptance

- *The completeness gap is the real deliverable.* Adding one glyph fixes today;

=== WIDENED at filing (manager, 2026-07-29): the primary channel is missing too

Further measurement while scoping the tmux default switch. The gap is not only
JQ8AV's rescue channel — the PRIMARY pane-liveness channel is absent on tmux:

- =pane_activity= is emitted by =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/modes/rmux.rs=
  and by nothing else. A grep for the event across =crates/orgasmic-drivers/src/=
  returns rmux hits only.
- =modes/tmux.rs= (4668 lines) sends =DriverEvent::Ready=,
  =TransitionState=, =ToolCall= and the fatal-error paths. There is no
  continuous pane-output event of any kind.

So on a tmux transport the stall clock sees driver events only when the worker
happens to call a tool or change state. Between those, evidence falls back to
the subtree CPU probe alone. A CPU-hot stretch (a long =cargo test= under the
pane) is still classified Working, so the common long-tool case survives. The
fatal case is the provider-bound think: low CPU, no tool calls, no pane event,
and — because JQ8AV's consult is gated on =transport == "rmux"= — no rescue
either. That is a 600s kill of a healthy worker with every channel blind.

This is why TASK-RWCRN's history matters: rmux only became safe when it grew
=pane_activity=. tmux has never had that, so it is where rmux was BEFORE the
fix, not merely missing the JQ8AV refinement.

ORDERING CONSEQUENCE. The operator has directed that tmux become the shipped
default driver, on the sound reasoning that a first-time user may have only
tmux. That makes this task a SHIP BLOCKER rather than a hardening nicety: with
the default flipped and this unfixed, the users least equipped to diagnose it
get healthy workers killed at ten minutes. Land this before the default flips;
dogfood on tmux in the meantime with
=--governance-json '{"stall_timeout_secs":3600}'= on every long-thinking
dispatch.

Work item 0, ahead of the others: give the tmux driver a coalesced
=pane_activity= equivalent to rmux's, with rmux's live tests ported
(=live_rmux_pane_publishes_pane_activity_while_it_writes= and the
newline-free-redraw variant) onto a test-owned tmux server. Only then does the
open-turn-statusline consult of items 1-3 become a refinement rather than the
sole channel.
PRODUCTION CONFIRMATION [2026-08-03], and this is what closes the loop the task
was opened for.

The runtime was rebuilt at =05e1813= and a TASK-8ED6V implementer dispatched on
*tmux* — the first tmux dispatch on a daemon that actually contains this channel.
Its session JSONL carries:

: driver_event/pane_activity   {"bytes": 10867, "seq": 3, "type": "pane_activity"}

Counted 2 events at +45s and 4 at +105s, increasing, with the run =[run-live]= and
=DRIVER=tmux=. So the channel is not merely compiled in — IT REPORTS, on the
transport it was written for, in production.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE TASK. Until this measurement, tmux dispatches on this
host had no progress signal at all, and a provider-bound think was released at the
stall budget regardless of how much work it was doing. That is what destroyed the
TASK-FZB6T.1 worker report on 2026-08-02: it committed 4,004 good lines and was
killed eight minutes later with its entire report unwritten.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE STANDING MITIGATION. The mandatory
=--governance-json {"stall_timeout_secs":3600}= on long tmux dispatches existed
only because the channel was blind. It now reports, so the override can be
retired for tmux — but retire it DELIBERATELY: the measurement above proves the
channel emits, and does not yet prove that a genuinely at-rest wedge still dies on
schedule under the new classifier in production. A short confirmation run that
lets a stall budget actually expire on a live tmux pane would close that half.
Until someone does it, keeping the override costs nothing.

** Description
TASK-JQ8AV landed a third work-evidence channel: at the stall deadline, when
subtree CPU is below the work threshold, the probe captures the pane and looks
for the TUI's open-turn statusline. A provider-bound turn is then classified
=Working= instead of being stall-killed.

That channel is gated on =target.transport == "rmux"= (supervisor.rs, in
=ProcessSubtreeCpuProbe=). On a =tmux= transport the consult never runs, so the
classification falls back to CPU alone — which is exactly the state that killed
FZB6T, RB1ZN and SZJ2B at 600.1s during long claude-opus-5 high-effort thinks.

This matters now because the operator has directed that orgasmic ship =tmux= as
the default driver (first users may have only tmux installed, so tmux is what
must be hardened). Dispatching opus-5 high-effort work over tmux before this
lands reproduces the original incident.

=== Work
1. Generalise the pane consult from rmux to any pane transport. =rmux= and
   =tmux= share the =capture-pane -p -t <session>= surface, so the marker
   classifier (=pane_open_turn_marker=) is reusable verbatim; what differs is
   the binary, the session-name derivation, and the socket/endpoint flag.
2. Keep the fail-closed ordering JK66P set and JQ8AV preserved: pane unreadable
   must never rescue a run, only report =pane capture unavailable=. The channel
   may flip Idle->Working and nothing else.
3. Extend the acceptance test to the tmux transport. JQ8AV's
   =a_network_waiting_provider_turn_survives_the_stall_window_and_a_wedge_dies=
   drives a REAL pane on a test-owned server; the tmux half needs the same
   shape on a test-owned tmux server, not a stubbed capture.
4. Do NOT widen the rescue to non-pane transports. acp-* transports already
   stream turn events into the stall clock and need no pane channel.

=== Acceptance
- A network-waiting provider-bound turn on a =tmux= transport survives repeated
  expired stall budgets, proven with a real tmux pane.
- An at-rest, connectionless wedge on =tmux= still dies on schedule, with a
  reason naming both empty channels.
- The rmux behaviour JQ8AV shipped is unchanged (its verify artifact still
  replays red-then-green).
- A shipped injection proof under verify/, per the project bar.

* DONE TASK-YGB1R Replace workflow tier adjectives with derivable escalating triggers :workflow:runtime:process:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-YGB1R
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Problem: `shipped/workflows/default.org` classifies work with bare adjectives — "trivial", "ordinary", "risky". Those are subjective enough that an agent already in execution momentum resolves them in whichever direction keeps it moving. On TASK-KWSTJ a P0 daemon-recovery change touching ~900 lines across orgasmic-core, orgasmic-daemon, orgasmic-cli and the UI read as manager-direct without the classification ever being contested.

Replace the adjectives with triggers a reader cannot argue with, while keeping the three-tier shape.

Work:
1. Define concrete escalating triggers, at minimum: task priority (P0/P1 is never trivial); blast-radius paths (daemon recovery, supervisor, boot, auth, dispatch lease, writer durability); breadth (crate count / file count / net line count over a stated threshold); and presence of a `depends_on` chain or an umbrella parent.
2. Any trigger firing means the work is at least `ordinary`; two or more, or a safety/auth path, means `risky`.
3. Keep the tiers as guidance for *how much process*, not a hard gate — the point is to remove the judgement call about which tier applies, not to remove judgement about how to work.
4. Where a trigger is derivable from the task heading itself (priority, tags, depends_on), surface it: an agent reading `orgasmic task get` should see the floor tier without recomputing it.
5. Reconcile with the manager-implementer clause in `shipped/entry/router.org` so router and workflow do not drift.

Non-goal: an exhaustive rubric. Four or five unambiguous triggers beat twenty debatable ones, and long prose dilutes the instruction it is meant to strengthen.

Acceptance:
- two agents reading the same task heading reach the same floor tier
- the P0/multi-crate/recovery-path shape that produced this task classifies as at least `ordinary` with no interpretation
- the fast path for genuinely small work stays fast

* DONE TASK-TW3N3 Document and guard the committed-history precondition for worker dispatch :workflow:dispatch:docs:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-TW3N3
:PRIORITY: P1
:END:

Problem: the workflow tells a manager to delegate ordinary work and to run an independent reviewer pass on risky work, but never says that delegation only works on committed history. `orgasmic manager dispatch` builds the worker a git worktree from a ref, so a dispatched implementer or reviewer sees exactly nothing of the manager's uncommitted edits. A reviewer dispatched against an uncommitted patch reports a clean review of code it never read.

This compounds a known sibling trap already recorded for `.orgasmic/` state: a worker in its own worktree also cannot see the live daemon's uncommitted writes to the manager's `.orgasmic/tx`, tasks, and decisions, so reviewers give false negatives on graph changes too.

The two together mean delegation is quietly useless at exactly the moment a manager-implementer reaches for it — after doing the work, wanting a second opinion before landing.

Work:
1. State the precondition explicitly in `shipped/entry/router.org` and `shipped/workflows/default.org`: commit to a branch before dispatching any worker that must see your changes, and pass that ref as `--from`.
2. Document the `.orgasmic/` blindspot in the same place, with the verification workaround (check graph state through the daemon CLI rather than through the worktree's files).
3. Consider a guard rather than only prose: when `manager dispatch` is invoked with a dirty worktree in the project root, warn (or refuse without an explicit override) naming the uncommitted paths the worker will not see.
4. Add the reviewer-specific case to whatever grill/review dispatch guidance exists — a review dispatch with nothing committed is the highest-cost version of this mistake, because it returns a confident wrong answer.

Acceptance:
- an agent following the router can dispatch a reviewer that actually reads the intended diff, without discovering the constraint by being surprised
- a dispatch that would silently review the wrong tree is either blocked or loudly flagged
- the `.orgasmic/` blindspot and the uncommitted-source blindspot are documented as one coherent constraint, not two folk facts

* DONE TASK-4YX1K Default to proceeding; confirm only for irreversible or outward-facing actions :workflow:runtime:process:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-4YX1K
:DEPENDS_ON: TASK-YGB1R
:PRIORITY:   P1
:END:

Problem: the runtime tells a manager what work to do and how much process to apply, but says nothing about when to stop and ask a human. Agents fill that vacuum with timidity. Observed 2026-07-25: a manager finished TASK-KWSTJ, correctly identified that a reviewer cannot see uncommitted source, and then asked the user for permission to commit to a local branch — a reversible, machine-local step that was already the precondition for a review the user had asked for. The question contained no decision. It cost a round-trip and stalled the work.

This is the mirror image of TASK-3CM0Q. That task stops an agent from silently proceeding through a decision that is genuinely the user's. This one stops an agent from interrupting on something that is not a decision at all. An agent without an explicit line between them oscillates: the same session skipped a real tier decision, was corrected, then over-corrected into asking about a mechanical step. Both failures are the human checkpoint landing in the wrong place, and neither is fixed by telling the agent to "use judgement".

Work:
1. State the default in `shipped/entry/router.org` and `shipped/workflows/default.org`: proceed. Asking is the exception and needs a reason that names which property of the action triggers it.
2. Define confirmation triggers by property, not by feeling. Confirm when an action is hard to reverse, leaves the machine, or spends someone else's resources — pushing to a remote, publishing a release or artifact, force-pushing or rewriting history, deleting or rewriting operator session/run history, touching the LaunchAgent or a live production daemon, or anything that mutates a shared or external service.
3. Name the proceed class just as explicitly, because a bare "proceed by default" will not survive contact with a cautious agent: committing to a local branch, creating and removing worktrees, running gates and test suites, reading anything, and `.orgasmic/` state writes through the CLI.
4. Cover the standing-authorization case: once a user has approved a plan, the mechanical steps that plan obviously entails do not each need their own approval. Re-asking inside an approved plan is itself the defect.
5. Say what to do instead of asking when an agent is unsure but the action is in the proceed class: act, then report what was done plainly enough to be reversed.

Non-goal: expanding autonomy on the confirm class. This narrows *where* the human is asked, it does not reduce *whether* they are asked about the things that matter.

Acceptance:
- committing to a branch, creating a worktree, or running gates never produces a permission question
- pushing, publishing, force-pushing, or touching the live daemon still does
- the router text distinguishes the two classes by a stated property, so an agent reaching an unlisted action can classify it rather than guess
- reads coherently against TASK-3CM0Q: one task puts a checkpoint where a decision exists, this one removes checkpoints where none does
