CONSEQUENCE: THE RUNTIME REINSTALL IS NO LONGER BLOCKED. The verb refuses by construction rather than by manager discipline, so reinstalling now makes the TASK-YN5FJ review gate and the TASK-M47E5 relocation live without arming the prune.

* DONE TASK-YN5FJ.1 fix-subtask: the review gate's refusal names a remedy that does not satisfy it — promote VERDICT to a real flag :cli:manager:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-YN5FJ.1
:PRIORITY: P1
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-cli/**
:END:

** Description
From the TASK-YN5FJ manager review, section "Manager review and verdict".
CONFIRMED against production, not reasoned.

The default-branch gate requires a =reviewer.done= carrying a non-empty
=VERDICT=. =VERDICT= has NO FLAG — it is settable only through the generic
=--property VERDICT=...=, and it was previously optional, read by
=reviewer_done_stage= only to choose the task's next stage (=.unwrap_or(false)=).

So the refusal text — "Dispatch and close a reviewer for that reported
generation, or re-run with --no-review-required --reason <why>" — names a first
branch that DOES NOT WORK. Follow it exactly and you are refused again with the
same message.

*Production evidence.* =tx-20260803-orgasmic-4401=, the =reviewer.done= this
manager wrote for TASK-XCJYC, carries =REASON=, =REVIEWED_DIFF=, =CLOSED_TX=,
=MODEL=, =EFFORT= and lifecycle properties and NO =VERDICT=. It is an ordinary,
correctly-formed reviewer close that the new gate rejects. Every historical
reviewer close is the same shape.

** Fix
1. Add a first-class =--verdict= flag to =dispatch-close= for reviewer closes,
   so the value the gate depends on is a documented part of the surface rather
   than an incantation through =--property=. Keep accepting the existing
   =--property VERDICT= spelling so nothing already written breaks.
2. Consider a typed value set (approve / approve-with-follow-ups / reject)
   rather than free text. This also answers the implementer's own declared
   residual risk that any non-empty verdict — including a negative one —
   currently satisfies "a verdict exists". Decide deliberately whether a REJECT
   should unlock a default-branch merge; there is a real argument either way
   (a REJECT the manager then resolved is exactly what happened on TASK-XCJYC),
   so state the reasoning rather than picking silently.
3. Name the verdict requirement IN the refusal text, so the remedy is
   self-contained.

** Ordering
Land this BEFORE any runtime reinstall. The gate is not live until the runtime
is rebuilt, so there is no live breakage today — but the first reinstall after
TASK-YN5FJ without this fix hands the operator a refusal they cannot clear
except by =--no-review-required=, which defeats the feature.

** Acceptance
- A reviewer close can record its verdict through a documented flag.
- Following the refusal's stated remedy actually clears the refusal — pin this
  with a test that walks the full loop: refuse, follow the remedy verbatim,
  succeed.
- Existing =--property VERDICT= closes still work.
** Evidence
Landed =bb2fb24= (merge) / =036b1d9= (worker commit) on main, base =739e3b8=.

Implementer: =implementer-claude-tmux= — driver tmux, harness claude, model claude-opus-5, effort high. Run =run-20260805T124037-ad04be2d00694da9929573ba9c7865c1=, started_tx =tx-20260805-orgasmic-4429=.

Manager rulings implemented as decided, with the reasoning carried in code comments rather than only in this record:
- RULING 1 — every verdict clears the gate, =reject= included. The gate asks whether an independent review happened, not whether it approved; blocking on a reject would force =--no-review-required=, stamping a bypass on a dispatch that WAS reviewed. A bad verdict already has its consequence in =reviewer_done_stage=.
- RULING 2 — =--verdict= takes a typed set (=approve= / =approve-with-follow-ups= / =reject=) that is a strict superset of the legacy free-text vocabulary; =clean= / =ship= / =has-issues= stay reachable through =--property VERDICT== unchanged.
- RULING 3 — passing both spellings is a hard error naming both, rather than last-wins.

Integration gates, re-run by the manager on the MERGED tree, not taken from the worker report:
- =scripts/run-tests.sh -p orgasmic-cli= — GREEN, 0 failures, 1 ignored, "environ: complete — no tool requirement was waived".
- =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= — exit 0.
- =cargo fmt --all --check= — exit 0.
- =orgasmic verify TASK-YN5FJ.1= — PASS, red-then-green replay, tree byte-identical. Injection is a full revert of the manager.rs fix.
- =orgasmic verify TASK-YN5FJ.1-remedy= — PASS. Second, narrower injection removing ONLY the =close_done_request= push that writes the flag value: the flag still parses and the refusal still prints the corrected remedy, yet the loop still fails. That is the proof a prose-only fix would not have been a fix.

Ordering requirement met: this landed BEFORE any runtime reinstall, so the first operator to meet the gate meets the fixed version of it.

One failure was seen and classified, not swallowed: =sigterm_exits_through_graceful_shutdown_rather_than_default_disposition= (daemon_lifecycle.rs:319) failed on the worker first run, passed in isolation, passed as a whole binary, and passed on a second full run — and on the manager own gate run it did not fail at all. It races a window its own =orgasmic:TASK-Q07Y5= comment says is "invisible on an idle machine"; this change touches dispatch-close argument handling only and cannot reach =orgasmic serve=. It is NOT in =verify/flake-registry.toml= and remains unowned.

is real — do this first.

** Description
Reviewer REJECT on TASK-M47E5 (merged =ffead86=) from =reviewer-codex-tmux=
(codex / gpt-5.6-sol / high), tx =tx-20260805-orgasmic-4474=. The RELOCATION half
of M47E5 is correct and stays. The PRUNE half cannot ship as written.

All three were verified against the code by the manager before filing — none is
taken on the reviewer word.

*** FINDING 1 (P0) — a symlinked managed root redirects =remove_dir_all= outside it
=scan_managed_worktrees= calls =std::fs::read_dir= on the project managed root
without first proving that root is a real directory. =read_dir= FOLLOWS a symlink.
Each CHILD is then checked with =symlink_metadata=, which is correct but too late:
the children enumerated are real directories inside whatever the root points at.

The direct-child fence in =remove_orphaned_worktree_dir= does not catch it, and
this is the part worth understanding rather than patching blind: =path= is built
as =<managed_root>/<child>= from =entry.path()=, so =path.parent()= is literally
=managed_root=. The comparison passes trivially — and =normalize_path=
canonicalizes BOTH sides through the same symlink, so it passes under either
reading. The final =symlink_metadata= sees a real directory, because it IS one; it
just belongs to the victim.

Net: if =~/.orgasmic/worktrees/<project-id>= is replaced by a symlink, a bare
=worktree-prune= recursively deletes real directories somewhere else. The root is
user-writable and this codebase runs AI workers with filesystem access, so
same-user replacement is not a hypothetical threat model.

*** FINDING 2 (P0) — prune bypasses the reservation this project already built
=RunSummary= deserializes =run_id= AND NOTHING ELSE, so the CLI cannot match a
live run to a worktree at all; =scan_managed_worktrees= makes the tx ledger the
sole ownership decision and uses live-run data only to decorate an
already-held record. Under the cleanup lock, prune re-reads only that ledger, then
removes.

So a live run whose open dispatch record is absent or torn classifies as
UNCLAIMED, and a recovery acquired in the classification-to-removal gap is not
fenced either. The local file lock is shared with CLI =dispatch-close=, but the
daemon acquire/recovery path does not take it.

THIS EXACT RACE IS ALREADY SOLVED, one path over. =Supervisor::reserve_dispatch_close=
(=crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/supervisor.rs= ~:3984) installs a cleanup reservation
and decides liveness UNDER THE SAME LOCK, and =admit_live_run= (~:543) reads that
fence last so no run can be admitted into a reserved worktree. Its own doc comment
says why a CLI-side audit cannot substitute: "a concurrent POST /runs/:origin/recover
acquires in *another process*, so no audit of await points in the CLI can close
that window — the authority has to sit where the supervisor lock already is."

Prune reproduces precisely the defect TASK-1T3FZ was filed to close. Do not
re-solve it in the CLI; route through the existing authority.

*** FINDING 3 (P1) — "repo gone" fails OPEN on I/O error, into the only unsalvaged delete
=worktree_repo_gone= treats ANY =read_to_string(.git)= error as evidence the
repository is gone: the =else= branch falls through to =(!dot_git.is_dir())=,
which is false for an unreadable regular file, yielding "no .git link". A
permission, ACL or transient I/O failure therefore selects =RepoGone= — the one
disposition that deliberately SKIPS SALVAGE and calls =remove_dir_all=.
=resolved.exists()= collapses errors the same way.

Classification also happens before the multi-GB size walk and before the cleanup
lock, and the under-lock re-check looks only at open dispatches, never at whether
the gitdir became reachable again. So an unreadable-then-restored repository can
lose dirty work with no salvage attempted.

** Fix
1. Anchor the managed root with no-follow semantics BEFORE scanning or deleting —
   refuse a symlinked root (and unsafe symlinked ancestors), or traverse and remove
   relative to a directory handle so a later rename cannot redirect the target. Add
   a tempdir regression in which the managed root points at a victim directory and
   every sentinel file survives.
2. Route each reclaim through the daemon existing cleanup reservation before
   salvage or removal, hold it across the whole mutation, release after. Match live
   runs by CANONICAL WORKTREE and project, which means =RunSummary= must carry
   =worktree= and =project_id=. Add tests for a live run with no open tx, and for a
   recovery acquired in the classification-to-removal gap.
3. Make repository classification FALLIBLE. Only a =NotFound= on the =.git= link or
   the admin directory may yield =RepoGone=; permission and other I/O errors become
   an explicit kept/skipped reason with that reason printed. Re-check repository
   state immediately under the guard, right before the unsalvageable direct delete.

** Acceptance
- A symlinked managed root cannot cause anything outside the real root to be
  removed, proven by a regression whose sentinels survive.
- A live run is never reclaimed, including one with no open dispatch record and one
  acquired during the classification-to-removal gap, enforced through the daemon
  reservation rather than a second CLI-side scheme.
- An I/O error never classifies as =RepoGone=; it is kept and named.
- The relocation half is unchanged and its tests stay green.
- =scripts/run-tests.sh -p orgasmic-cli= and =-p orgasmic-daemon= green;
  =cli_parity= green.
** Evidence
Landed =b20fba5= (merge) / =f6f1ca2= (worker HEAD) on main, base =0f8e364=.

Implementer: =implementer-claude-tmux= — driver tmux, harness claude, model claude-opus-5, effort high. Run =run-20260805T150600-dfd05d136f1f4e4c984c960570bceb06=, started_tx =tx-20260805-orgasmic-4479=.

THE FIX IS THE RIGHT SHAPE, NOT THE CHEAP ONE. =remove_orphaned_worktree_dir= was DELETED rather than repaired: all three of its guards were statements about a PATH, and a path ancestors are re-resolved by every syscall. =AnchoredManagedRoot::open= opens the root once with =O_NOFOLLOW | O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC= — which refuses a symlinked root outright — and the resulting DIRECTORY HANDLE, not the path, is what enumeration (=fdopendir=/=readdir=) and removal (=openat=/=unlinkat=) resolve against thereafter. A rename of the root path afterwards cannot redirect a removal because no removal consults the path again, and a test proves exactly that by renaming the real root aside mid-prune and moving a victim into its place.

FINDING 2 WAS ROUTED THROUGH THE EXISTING AUTHORITY, AND THE API DID NOT NEED EXTENDING — the implementer said so plainly instead of dressing it up as work. Reclaim goes through =POST /projects/:id/tasks/:task/dispatch/close-guard= onto =Supervisor::reserve_dispatch_close=, which is already keyed on the canonical worktree. Prune request differs from a close in two fields and both say prune is entitled to nothing: =releasing_run_id: None= and =owned_run_ids: []=, so EVERY live occupant blocks it. CLI =RunSummary= now deserializes =worktree=/=project_id=/=task_id= (the daemon side always carried them; only this mirror was blind, which is why the CLI could not match a live run to a worktree at all), each =#[serde(default)]= so an older daemon degrades to "unknown" and unknown refuses to reclaim. An unreachable daemon now FAILS CLOSED, where it previously fell back to "nothing is live".

FINDING 3: =worktree_repo_gone -> Option= became =worktree_repo_state -> {Present|Gone|Undetermined}=. Only =NotFound= may yield =Gone=; permission/ACL/stat failures become =Undetermined=, never reclaimed, reason printed, and reported as =KEPT_WORKTREE= distinctly from =HELD_WORKTREE= because "nobody could tell" is not "somebody owns it". State is re-checked under the guard immediately before the unsalvaged removal.

THE INJECTION PROOF DEMONSTRATES REAL DESTRUCTION, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH HAVING. Replayed by the manager on the merged tree: =orgasmic verify TASK-M47E5.2= PASS, and the red log shows the pre-fix code ACTUALLY DELETING =victim/task-precious/keep-me.txt= outside the root, and reclaiming an unreadable-git worktree with =BYTES=1880= of unsalvaged worker output. Exactly 2 panics, both the pinned assertions, =0 passed; 2 failed=.

ALL FOUR REQUIRED REGRESSIONS WERE CONFIRMED RED ON THE UNFIXED TREE, including the hardest one: a recovery acquired in the classification-to-removal gap, made DETERMINISTIC rather than raced via a post-guard pause file (mirroring the existing =ORGASMIC_DISPATCH_CLOSE_PAUSE_FILE=). Pre-fix it failed after 120.75s with "prune never reached its post-guard pause; it does not take a daemon reservation at all".

Integration gates, re-run by the manager on the MERGED tree:
- =scripts/run-tests.sh -p orgasmic-cli= — GREEN, 0 failures (see the flake note below).
- =cargo test -p orgasmic-cli --test cli_parity= — 3 passed.
- =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= — exit 0. =cargo fmt --all --check= — exit 0.
- =orgasmic verify TASK-M47E5.2= — PASS, tree byte-identical.
- The DAEMON suite was not re-run by the manager: the daemon diff against base is COMMENT-ONLY, verified by filtering the diff to non-comment lines and getting an empty result. The implementer ran it twice, red both times with NO OVERLAP between the failing tests, all green in isolation.

THE FIRST GATE RUN WAS RED, AND THAT RED WAS USEFUL. =sigterm_exits_through_graceful_shutdown_rather_than_default_disposition= failed as REAL — unregistered. It is TASK-37WN7, filed earlier the same day and deliberately left out of the registry for want of a captured signature. The gate handed one over. Registered in =898c7e3= with the signature pinned to the =status.signal()= assertion only, so a failure on the deadline or exit-code branch still reads REAL.

* DONE TASK-4WKNX.1.1 Make manager-owned close-tx keys win by construction, not by enumeration
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-4WKNX.1.1
:PRIORITY: P1
:FIX_SUBTASK: t
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-cli/
:END:

** Description

Round 3 on the manager-owned close-tx key namespace. The finding and its
confirmed mechanism are on TASK-4WKNX.1 under "Review round 1 — REJECT
(confirmed, and the severity is higher)". Read it there; do not re-derive it.

In one line: =MANAGER_OWNED_CLOSE_PROPERTIES= names three keys, but
=close_done_request= appends =CLOSED_TX=, =LIFECYCLE_FROM=/=LIFECYCLE_TO=,
=CLEANUP_STATUS=, =SALVAGE_*= and =GOAL_ID= AFTER the caller's =--property=
loop — and =extra()= is first-wins, so a forged caller value is the one every
reader sees.

** These keys are consumed, so this is not an audit problem

- =close_matching_dispatch= (=manager.rs:7033=) picks WHICH open dispatch a close
  terminates from =CLOSED_TX=.
- =close_tx_ran_cleanup= (=:7059=) sets =cleanup_already_run= from
  =CLEANUP_STATUS= — and cleanup is the path that SALVAGES uncommitted worker
  output before removing a worktree.
- =cleanup_status_reports_failure= (=:7158=) scans for cleanup failures a forged
  =ok= would hide.

** The ruling: two layers, and neither alone is sufficient

*Layer 1 — ordering, which covers keys nobody has written yet.* Push the
manager's own extras BEFORE the caller's =--property= loop. Measured and
verified by the manager: EVERY tx-extra reader in the workspace is first-wins
(=manager.rs:7101=, =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/index.rs:2008=, and the test
helpers) — there is no last-wins reader. So manager-first makes a forged
duplicate inert for consumption, for every key including future ones, with no
list to maintain.

*Layer 2 — refusal, which covers the deliberate bypass keys.* Ordering alone is
not enough and the reason is not cosmetic: an inert duplicate still sits in the
ledger where a person reads it, and for =FIX_ROUND_FINAL= / =NO_REVIEW_REQUIRED=
a silent no-op is the wrong answer. Forging a bypass key should be a loud
refusal.

*Explicitly rejected: extending the denylist to enumerate every structural key.*
That is a longer list with the same defect — a new key is protected only if
someone remembers to add it, which is precisely what this round exists to fix.

** Keep, do not rebuild

The round-2 work is good and most of it survives: the =const fn reserved(...)=
default, the =AliasedVerdict= exception, the byte-identical =VERDICT= refusal
text, the placement before release/cleanup/append/mutation, and the production
tests. This round changes the SHAPE of the coverage, not the policy.

** Acceptance

- A manager-owned key added in future is protected WITHOUT being added to any
  list, and a test demonstrates that rather than asserting it in prose.
- Forging =CLOSED_TX= or =CLEANUP_STATUS= through =--property= cannot change what
  =close_matching_dispatch= or =close_tx_ran_cleanup= decide.
- =FIX_ROUND_FINAL= and =NO_REVIEW_REQUIRED= still refuse loudly, before run
  release, worktree cleanup, tx append and lifecycle mutation.
- =VERDICT='s three behaviours are unchanged and its refusal text stays
  byte-identical: property-only accepted, typed-only accepted, both refused.
- An injection proof pinning a CONSUMED key, not just a refused one.

** Not in scope

TASK-3HR8R (the parked-=in_review= diagnostic). The reviewer re-confirmed it is
out of scope here.
** Landed and verified by the manager
** Review round 1 — APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS

* DONE TASK-4WKNX.1 Reserve manager-owned close-tx keys from the generic --property channel
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-4WKNX.1
:PRIORITY: P1
:FIX_SUBTASK: t
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-cli/
:END:

** Description

Fix round for the one BLOCK SHIP on TASK-4WKNX's review, confirmed by the manager
against the code. The full mechanism is on the parent under "Review round 1 —
REJECT (confirmed)"; read it there rather than re-deriving it.

In one line: ~close_done_request~ pushes caller ~--property~ entries before it
pushes its own typed keys, and ~parse_close_property~ accepts any uppercase key,
so a bypass-audit key can be forged or contradicted by the caller it is meant to
audit.

** The class, not the instance

The reviewer found it on ~FIX_ROUND_FINAL~. The manager found the same hole on
~NO_REVIEW_REQUIRED~ (manager.rs:4720), which is PRE-EXISTING — 4WKNX did not
introduce it, it introduced a second instance of it. ~VERDICT~ is the only key of
this class currently fenced (TASK-YN5FJ.1 RULING 3), and it is fenced by a
hand-written one-off ~if let (Some, Some)~ pair.

Three keys, two unfenced, one bespoke fence: the fix is a rule about
manager-owned tx keys, not a third copy of the same ~if~.

** Acceptance

- A caller cannot forge or contradict any manager-owned close-tx key through
  ~--property~. Covers at minimum ~FIX_ROUND_FINAL~, ~NO_REVIEW_REQUIRED~ and
  ~VERDICT~.
- ~VERDICT~'s existing behaviour is preserved exactly: ~--property VERDICT=~ is a
  supported legacy free-text spelling and must keep working alone, while
  flag-plus-property still refuses by name. Whatever rule replaces the one-off
  must reproduce this, not flatten it.
- The refusal happens with the other early close refusals — before run release,
  worktree cleanup, and any tx append.
- Tests pin property-only forgery AND typed-flag/property collision on the
  production path, and assert the close was refused before the worktree was
  cleaned up.

** Not in scope

The reviewer's usability suggestion (a close-time next-action line, or a
~dispatch-status~ diagnostic for a ~FIX_SUBTASK~ parked ~in_review~ with no
reviewer dispatch). That is a follow-up on a workflow that now works. File it
separately if it earns a task.
** Landed and verified by the manager
** Review round 1 — REJECT (confirmed, and the severity is higher)
Reviewer =reviewer-codex-tmux= (tmux/codex/gpt-5.6-sol/high) on merge =caf06ae=
vs base =f60af0a=. Verdict REJECT, one BLOCK SHIP. Manager confirmed it against
the code and confirmed the severity is HIGHER than the report states.

=== The finding, confirmed

=MANAGER_OWNED_CLOSE_PROPERTIES= is a three-key denylist, not the class rule the
task asked for. =close_done_request= pushes caller properties (=:4751=) and THEN
appends manager-derived structural keys — =CLOSED_TX= (=:4763=),
=push_lifecycle_extra=, =push_cleanup_extra=, =GOAL_ID= — none of which are in
the table. With =extra()= first-wins, the caller's forged value is the one every
reader sees.

=== Why this is worse than the report says: these keys are CONSUMED

The report frames the risk as forged audit data. Manager checked the consumers
and it is not only audit:

- =close_matching_dispatch= (=:7033=) selects WHICH open dispatch record a close
  terminates by matching =CLOSED_TX=. A forged value marks the WRONG generation
  closed and leaves the real one open.
- =close_tx_ran_cleanup= (=:7059=) sets =record.cleanup_already_run= from
  =CLEANUP_STATUS=. A forged =ok= makes a close that never ran cleanup look like
  it did — and cleanup is the path that SALVAGES uncommitted worker output before
  removing a worktree. This project has already destroyed a worker's work once
  (TASK-2BPWM, TASK-D0GA3).
- =cleanup_status_reports_failure= (=:7158=) scans the ledger for cleanup
  failures; a forged =ok= hides a real one from that report.

So the vector is state corruption and suppressed salvage, not a false record.
BLOCK SHIP stands and the severity is right.

=== This is MY scoping failure, not the implementer's

The round-2 brief said "a rule about manager-owned close-tx keys, not a third
copy of the same =if=" — and then named exactly three keys, in a table, in the
brief's own markdown. The implementer built precisely what was described. The
table it produced is good work: the =const fn reserved(...)= default and the
verbatim =VERDICT= text are both right and both survive into round 3. What was
missing was in the specification.

=== The structural answer, found while verifying

*Every tx-extra reader in the workspace is first-wins.* Verified:
=manager.rs:7101=, =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/index.rs:2008=, and the assertion
helpers — all =.iter().find(...)=. No last-wins reader exists.

So pushing the manager's own extras BEFORE the caller's =--property= loop makes
every forged duplicate INERT for consumption, for every manager-owned key
including ones nobody has written yet, with no list to maintain and no drift to
detect. That is the property the acceptance actually wants and it costs a
reorder.

It is not sufficient alone, and saying why matters: an inert duplicate still sits
in the ledger where a human reads it, and for the three deliberate bypass keys a
silent no-op is the wrong answer — forging =FIX_ROUND_FINAL= should be a loud
refusal, not a shrug. Hence two layers in round 3.

=== Accepted from the review, no action

- Placement verified independently: validation at =:1010= precedes merge
  verification (=:1022=), reservation/release (=:1096=), cleanup (=:1163=), tx
  append (=:1201=) and lifecycle mutation; the only mutating call before it is
  the explicitly accepted =reconcile_torn_closes_best_effort=.
- =VERDICT= collision text is byte-for-byte identical to base =f60af0a:969-971=;
  =reviewer_done_stage= and =close_verdict_value= unchanged, still reading either
  spelling. Independently exercised typed-only, property-only and collision.
- Duplicate handling for the three listed keys is sound: the =Reserved= arm
  refuses regardless of value, so duplicates cannot slip past.
- =parse_close_property= rejects lower-case, padded and non-ASCII-uppercase keys.

=== The =NO_REVIEW_REQUIRED= judgement is SETTLED, with a better argument

The brief asked for a real opinion including "the author was wrong". The reviewer
said Reserved is right and gave a stronger reason than the implementer's
absence-of-callers evidence: =project.org:12-18= records an explicit greenfield
bias — do not assume backward compatibility absent an explicit requirement.
And unlike =VERDICT=, whose property form preserves free-text values outside the
typed enum, a =NO_REVIEW_REQUIRED= alias adds no vocabulary and no capability
except bypassing the mandatory reason. Reserved, and the reasoning is now on the
record instead of in a report.

* DONE TASK-4WKNX FIX_SUBTASK closes straight to done, so a fix round that the goal requires to be reviewed cannot be dispatched a reviewer without a manual stage flip :cli:manager:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-4WKNX
:PRIORITY: P2
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-cli/**,crates/orgasmic-daemon/**
:END:

** Description
Found by running into it, 2026-08-05, closing TASK-YN5FJ.1.1.

=close_lifecycle_transitions= sends an implementer close to =Done= when the task
carries =:FIX_SUBTASK: t=, and to =InReview= otherwise. That encodes one-round
fix semantics, which the manager-dispatch convention states deliberately.

The ACTIVE GOAL says something else, and it is not reconcilable by reading
harder: "Fix subtasks minted from reviewer findings count as tasks: a BLOCK SHIP
is not closed until its fix round lands and passes a fresh review."

So for a fix round minted from a BLOCK SHIP, the two rules point opposite ways.
What happens in practice: =dispatch-close= flips the task to =done=, and the
reviewer dispatch then refuses with

: task TASK-YN5FJ.1.1 is in lifecycle stage done; reviewer dispatch is allowed only from IN_REVIEW

The refusal is CORRECT — a done task should not accept a reviewer. The defect is
upstream: the close had no way to say "this fix round still owes a review", so the
manager has to flip =done= -> =in_review= by hand afterwards to get the review the
goal demands. A state the board cannot express is a state managers will fake.

** Why this matters beyond one flip
The manual flip records a =task.state_transitioned= that reads like a correction,
not like policy. Anyone auditing later sees a task moved backwards out of done
with no way to tell whether that was process or panic. And a manager who does NOT
know the goal clause will simply not review the fix round at all — the tooling
actively steers them away from it.

** Fix directions, not yet decided
1. Let the close say it: a flag on =dispatch-close= (or a property on the task)
   that means "fix round, still owes review", so the close lands =in_review=
   without the manual flip.
2. Or derive it: a fix subtask minted from a reviewer finding labelled BLOCK SHIP
   goes to =in_review=; one minted from a non-blocking finding goes to =done=.
   That matches the goal clause exactly and needs no new operator input, but it
   requires the finding severity to be recorded somewhere the close can read —
   today it is prose in the reviewer report.
3. Or change the convention and the goal to agree on one rule. Cheapest, and it
   is a real option: decide that one-round fix semantics win and the goal clause
   is wrong.

Pick deliberately; do not implement all three.

** Acceptance
- A fix round minted from a BLOCK SHIP reaches its reviewer without a manual
  backwards stage transition.
- Whatever rule is chosen is stated in ONE place that both the convention and the
  close read from, so the next manager cannot find two answers.
- Existing one-round fix behaviour for non-blocking fix subtasks is preserved or
  its removal is explicit.
** Evidence
Landed =2d9d8b8= (merge) on main. Implementer: =implementer-claude-tmux= (tmux / claude / claude-opus-5 / high), run =run-20260805T184048-efc1a81d6ebb47439ce722ca7b4edbc2=, started_tx =tx-20260805-orgasmic-4519=.

THE MANAGER RULED THE POLICY, THE IMPLEMENTER CHOSE THE MECHANISM, and the split held. A =FIX_SUBTASK= implementer close now lands =in_review= like any other; the opt-out is =--fix-round-final=, which requires =--reason= and stamps =FIX_ROUND_FINAL=true= on the close tx.

THE RULING WAS MADE ON THIS SESSION OWN EVIDENCE, not taste. Five fix rounds ran 2026-08-05. One of them — TASK-M47E5.2, the fix round for three data-loss findings — was itself REJECTED with three MORE BLOCK SHIP findings, two P0. Under the old default it would have closed straight to =done= and six confirmed defects would be sitting on main unreviewed. The only thing that caught it was the manager flipping =done= -> =in_review= by hand, three separate times in one day, which nobody who had not read the goal would know to do. The asymmetry decides it: the old default fails as "a fix for a data-loss finding lands unreviewed"; the new one fails as "a trivial fix waits for a cheap review".

THREE IMPLEMENTER DECISIONS, all defensible and all stated:
- A FLAG, NOT A TASK PROPERTY. A property would describe the task forever, when what is recorded is a judgement about ONE round outcome, made at close time by the manager who read the diff.
- NAMED =--fix-round-final=, NOT another =--no-*=. The brief warned the two bypasses must not read as one concept; a near-homonym of =--no-review-required= would have invited exactly that. The flag names the state of the round rather than negating the word "review".
- REASON REQUIRED. Stronger here than for =--no-review-required=: this bypass is INVISIBLE IN THE OUTCOME — a task at =done= looks identical whether it was reviewed or declared not to need it — so the ledger has to carry the difference.

THE RULE NOW LIVES IN ONE PLACE: =implementer_done_stage(fix_subtask, fix_round_final)=, a four-row table with a unit test enumerating all four rows. =close_lifecycle_transitions= encodes nothing itself. Both shipped docs describe it by NAMING the flag, and =cli_parity= resolves shipped invocations against the real binary, so prose that lags the code is a gate failure.

A SECOND SHIPPED FILE WAS EDITED OUTSIDE THE DECLARED WRITE SCOPE, DECLARED RATHER THAN BURIED, and the manager accepts it: =shipped/schema/state-machine.org= still restated the old mapping ("transitions IN_PROGRESS -> DONE"). Leaving it would have preserved exactly the two-answers state this task acceptance forbids, so fixing it was the task, not scope creep.

Integration gates, re-run by the manager on the MERGED tree: =scripts/run-tests.sh -p orgasmic-cli= GREEN 0 failures; =cli_parity= 3 passed; =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= exit 0; =cargo fmt --all --check= exit 0; =orgasmic verify TASK-4WKNX= PASS.

THE INJECTION PROOF PINS THE END-TO-END SYMPTOM, NOT THE STAGE. The test reads the stage into a variable and lets the REVIEWER DISPATCH be the first assertion allowed to fail, so the pinned red is =task TASK-FIX-DECL is in lifecycle stage done; reviewer dispatch is allowed only from IN_REVIEW= — the thing an operator actually hits. Verified by the manager: exactly ONE panic in the red log, and it is that one. A proof pinned on the stage assertion would have passed while the workflow stayed broken.
** Review round 1 — REJECT (confirmed)
Reviewer `reviewer-codex-tmux` (tmux/codex/gpt-5.6-sol/high) on merge `2d9d8b8` vs first parent `a4199ed`. Verdict REJECT, one BLOCK SHIP. Manager confirmed the finding against the code rather than taking it on report, and found a third instance the reviewer did not.

**Confirmed — the new audit key is spoofable through the generic `--property` channel.**

`close_done_request` pushes caller properties (manager.rs:4718-4720) BEFORE it pushes the typed key (manager.rs:4726), and `parse_close_property` (:7183) accepts any uppercase key. Two concrete failures, both traced through the code path end to end:

1. `--property FIX_ROUND_FINAL=true` with no `--fix-round-final`: `validate_fix_round_final` returns `Ok` on its first line (`if !args.fix_round_final`), so neither `--reason` nor the `:FIX_SUBTASK:` check runs. The tx is stamped as a declared-final round; the task actually lands `in_review`. The ledger says one thing, the state machine did another.
2. `--fix-round-final --property FIX_ROUND_FINAL=false --reason <why>`: both land as duplicate keys. `extra()` (:7027) is `.find()` — FIRST-wins — so a reader sees `false` while the close really went to `done`.

Note the asymmetry that makes this easy to miss: `close_property_value` (:5790) reads ARGS last-wins (`.rev()`), while `extra()` reads the TX first-wins. The two readers disagree about which duplicate is authoritative.

**Why this is BLOCK SHIP and not a nit.** The entire argument for requiring `--reason` was that this bypass is invisible in the outcome — a `done` task looks identical whether it was reviewed or declared not to need review — so the ledger has to carry the difference. An audit key any caller can forge, without the reason the design demands, does not carry it. And this is the same shape already fenced for `VERDICT` under TASK-YN5FJ.1 RULING 3, decided hours earlier: a new key of the same class shipped without the fence its sibling has.

**Third instance, not in the report: `NO_REVIEW_REQUIRED` has the identical hole** (manager.rs:4720). `--property NO_REVIEW_REQUIRED=true` stamps the default-branch-gate bypass on the ledger while skipping the `--reason` that `--no-review-required` requires. That one is PRE-EXISTING, not introduced here — which is why the fix should be a reserved-key rule covering the class, not a one-off for `FIX_ROUND_FINAL`.

**Mitigating, and stated so the fix is not over-scoped:** nothing READS either key today; both are write-only ledger records. This is a false-record defect, not a live workflow break.

**Accepted from the review, no action:**
- `implementer_done_stage` is genuinely single-source in executable code; repository search found no surviving copy of the old mapping.
- `validate_fix_round_final` runs before run release, worktree cleanup, close-tx append, and lifecycle mutation. (The reviewer noted `reconcile_torn_closes_best_effort` still precedes all close validation — deliberate TASK-EP3H1 behaviour, repairing an unrelated owed close, not a regression. Agreed.)
- `--fix-round-final` and `--no-review-required` are coherent together: distinct gates, distinct keys.
- Both shipped doctrine files match the code; no third file states the old rule.
- Independent re-verification by the reviewer: `orgasmic verify TASK-4WKNX` PASS, `cli_parity` 3 passed.

**Deferred, not folded in:** the reviewer suggests a close-time next-action line or a `dispatch-status` diagnostic for a `FIX_SUBTASK` parked `in_review` with no reviewer dispatch. That is a usability follow-up on a workflow that now works; it does not belong in a fix round for an audit hole.
** Follow-up filed from the review's Open Questions
The reviewer's second open question — a close-time next-action line or a =dispatch-status= diagnostic for a =FIX_SUBTASK= parked =in_review= with no reviewer dispatch — is filed as TASK-3HR8R, and it was UPGRADED from the usability follow-up the manager first called it.

A board-hygiene sweep the same day found TASK-M47E5.1 merged at 18:09 and never reviewed, stalled in exactly this shape. So the reviewer reasoned FORWARD from a design change and the sweep reasoned BACKWARD from a real miss, and both landed on the same gap. It is a review the goal requires going missing silently, not polish.

** Description

Fix round for the BLOCK SHIP on TASK-M47E5.1.1's review. The finding and its
confirmed chain are on that task under "Review round 1 — REJECT (confirmed; two
findings land on the manager's brief)". Read it there; do not re-derive it.

In one line: round 3 fixed the finalize PREDICATE and left its INPUT unvalidated,
so a degenerate dispatch stem makes =dispatch_artifact_dir= equal to the dispatch
ROOT and the cross-stem grant returns.

** The chain, confirmed by the manager

1. =dispatch_artifact_stem= (=manager.rs:6442=) strips =-brief.md= with no
   emptiness check: a brief named =-brief.md= gives =stem == ""=, =.-brief.md=
   gives =".".
2. =dispatch_artifact_paths_for_attempt= (=:6631=) joins that stem to the
   dispatch dir, so =dir= IS the dispatch root.
3. =api.rs:4764= persists =last_path.parent()= — the dispatch root — as
   =dispatch_artifact_dir=.
4. =path_is_under= accepts EQUALITY (=cursor_acp.rs:1530=), so both halves of
   =path_under_own_dispatch_artifacts= pass for every sibling stem.

** The ruling: fix it at BOTH ends

*The adapter must not trust its input.* Require the artifact dir to be a STRICT,
shape-validated child of the resolved dispatch root — preferably
=resolved_artifact_dir.parent() == resolved_dispatch_root=, which matches the
real stem layout and rejects equality, =stem/..=, and deeper-shape surprises in
one condition rather than three.

*The CLI must not mint a degenerate stem.* Reject empty, =.= and =..= stems in
=dispatch_artifact_stem=. This is a real defect independently of the grant — a
dispatch whose artifact dir IS the dispatch root would also collide artifacts
across dispatches. *Scope is explicitly expanded to the CLI for this.*

Neither alone is sufficient: the adapter fix is the security boundary and must
hold against any input, while the CLI fix removes the only known route to that
input and is cheap.

** Acceptance

- =dispatch_artifact_dir= equal to the dispatch root is REFUSED by the finalize
  grant, and so is a traversal-equivalent value that resolves to it.
- A brief path that would produce an empty, =.= or =..= stem is refused by name
  at the CLI, before any dispatch artifacts are created.
- The paired authority test is EXTENDED with the root-equivalent case: sibling
  READ still allowed, sibling FINALIZE still refused. Keep the existing cases.
- A daemon test that derives the config from a =last_path= rather than passing an
  expected directory straight to the config helper. The current test only proves
  serialization of an already-correct value, which is why this got through.
- The injection proof covers the root-equivalent case.

** Also in scope, small

Correct the =ORGASMIC_PROBE_SESSIONS= example: it points at
=$PWD/.orgasmic/tmp/sessions=, which does not exist in a dispatch worktree, so
the documented command cannot provide the route it advertises. And either add the
sixth parent so the restored candidate really reaches the old =<stem>/worktree=
layout, or narrow the comment to the shallow custom layout the five-parent form
actually supports — from the manifest it currently expands to
=.orgasmic/tmp/tmp/sessions=, one parent short.

** Baseline correction, so it is not repeated

The TASK-M47E5.1.1 brief asked for a no-widening comparison against =d4922f7= as
"pre-M47E5". That was WRONG: =d4922f7= already contains the managed-worktree
move, at which point the old predicate was dead and the normal allowset was
worktree-only. *The true pre-move comparison point is =103ed7e=*, where the
intended shape was worktree plus =worktree.parent()= when that parent is under
the dispatch root. Compare against =103ed7e=.
** Landed and verified by the manager
** Review round 1 — REJECT (test-only; production confirmed correct)
Reviewer =reviewer-codex-tmux= (tmux/codex/gpt-5.6-sol/high) on merge =77b5e90=
vs base =7ffbe73=. REJECT, one BLOCK SHIP — *test-only; the production fix is
confirmed correct*.

=== The finding, confirmed by the manager

The daemon test computes the derivation itself:

: let last_path = FsPath::new(".../task-attempt-7/task-attempt-7-last.txt");
: let cfg = stage_driver_config_with_overrides(..., last_path.parent(), ...);
: assert_eq!(cfg.0["dispatch_artifact_dir"], json!(last_path.parent().unwrap()));

That asserts =parent() == parent()=. The production derivation —
=req.last_path.and_then(FsPath::parent)= at =api.rs:4770= — is exercised by NO
test. Swapping it for a grandparent derivation yields the DISPATCH ROOT, restores
the cross-stem finalize grant, and leaves this test green.

*This is the same acceptance criterion failing twice.* Round 4's brief demanded
"a daemon test that derives the config from a =last_path=, rather than passing an
expected directory straight to the config helper", precisely because round 3's
test only proved serialization. Round 4 moved the =.parent()= call into the test
and passed the result straight to the helper — satisfying the criterion's letter
and not its substance. The blind spot survived the round written to close it.

=== What the review CONFIRMED, independently — all of it accepted

- *The manager's daemon-suite skip was valid.* Checked directly:
  =git diff 3a825cb..77b5e90 -- crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs= changes only
  code inside =#[cfg(test)]=. Production daemon code is unchanged from the
  twice-run tree. The manager asked for this to be checked rather than trusted,
  and it held.
- *The stale-proof narrowing was right.* "Re-cutting the retired half would
  assert the widening already ruled defective." Both narrowed and new proofs
  replayed independently: PASS, byte-identical revert.
- *The no-widening comparison against =103ed7e= holds*: the grant retains the
  worktree path and restores the old one-attempt-directory shape without granting
  the dispatch tree.
- *=resolve_policy_path= makes the strict rule sound*: it canonicalizes, or
  recursively canonicalizes the nearest existing parent, so the
  =parent() == dispatch_root= check refuses equality, root-equivalent traversal,
  deeper resolved shapes and symlink escape. Where a path cannot be resolved the
  comparison *fails closed*.
- *The =Option= propagation from the fallible stem is safe*: it is confined to
  best-effort legacy Codex PID recovery when a record has no authoritative
  =last_path=, where =None= is the pre-existing fail-soft contract.
- *The CLI refusal lands early*: reservation propagates the error before
  =create_dir_all= and before artifact-file reservation.
- *The transcript-probe fix is real*:
  =git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir= resolves a dispatch
  worktree to the live checkout, and the six-parent fallback does reach the old
  =<stem>/worktree= layout as claimed.

=== The judgement worth carrying forward

Four rounds, four reviews, and the recurring failure is not in the production
reasoning — it is that each round's TEST proved something adjacent to the claim
rather than the claim. The widening survived because the matrix checked sibling
worktrees and not sibling stems; the input gap survived because the test
hard-coded a well-formed directory; this gap survives because the test does
production's arithmetic for it.

The remedy adopted for round 5 is a mutation-shaped acceptance criterion: the
test must FAIL if production derives the grandparent, the file itself, or =None=.
Naming the mutations a test must catch is stronger than naming the value it
should assert, and every round of this chain would have been caught by it.

** Description

In one line: the finalize command grant was widened from *this attempt's stem
directory* to *the whole project dispatch tree*, so a worker on TASK-A can name
another dispatch's report and have it become TASK-A's own terminal record.

** The manager was wrong, and the reason matters for the fix

The widening was DECLARED by the implementer and ACCEPTED by the manager on the
argument that =read_args_allowed= already reaches those paths, so no new surface
appears. That argument does not hold: =dispatch finalize --summary-file X= reads
X, may COMMIT the worktree, writes X's bytes verbatim as this run's =last.txt=,
and emits the terminal tx. A read grant and a finalize grant are different
authorities over the same path.

*The principle to build to: the criterion governs the command/path pair, not the
transitive closure of separately granted actions.*

** Direction: pass the authoritative stem, do not re-derive it

The daemon already knows this run's artifact directory — the CLI's own finalize
resolves =run.last_path= from the live run record (=manager.rs:1934=). So the
adapter should be TOLD its attempt's artifact directory in persisted driver
config and authorize exactly that, rather than inferring anything.

This restores the pre-move semantics precisely: the old predicate allowed
=worktree.parent()=, which WAS =last_path.parent()= before TASK-M47E5 moved
worktrees out of the project.

Rejected alternative: waiting on TASK-A1KJW (task-derived dispatch stem) and
deriving from =ctx.task_id=. A1KJW is a good change and would simplify this
later, but making a security fix wait on an unrelated refactor is the wrong
order. Note in the fix that A1KJW can supersede the plumbing.

*This crosses crates.* Unlike TASK-M47E5.1, the write scope has to include the
daemon and the driver-config type, because the daemon is where the authoritative
value lives.

- A summary file inside the CURRENT attempt's artifact directory is accepted.
- A summary file inside a SIBLING project dispatch stem is REFUSED. This is the
  newly-permitted pair the merged code allows and the existing matrix never
  tested.
- Nothing that was refused before TASK-M47E5 is newly permitted. State explicitly
  what the grant allows now versus at =d4922f7=.
- The brief-read grant (=path_under_dispatch_artifacts=) keeps working unchanged.
- With no artifact directory configured, the grant REFUSES rather than falling
  back to anything broader. Fail closed, as the sibling
  =a_dispatch_artifact_grant_refuses_when_no_project_root_is_configured= already
  does for the project root.
- The injection proof's pinned red/green contract INCLUDES the sibling-stem

  behaviours it claims and does not cover the no-widening criterion at all; that

- Add =ORGASMIC_PROBE_SESSIONS= to the probe's documentation alongside

Merged =3a825cb= (worker =9f7028b=, base =b4ca343=, +190/-39 across 6 files).

=== The fix restores the ORIGINAL shape with an authoritative input

The daemon persists =dispatch_artifact_dir= from
=req.last_path.and_then(FsPath::parent)= — the per-attempt directory it already
owns — and =path_under_own_dispatch_artifacts= returns, keyed on that configured
value instead of =worktree.parent()=.

Note it kept BOTH halves of the original predicate:
=path_is_under(artifact_dir, dispatch_root) && path_is_under(path, artifact_dir)=.
The daemon supplies the value and the adapter still re-checks it sits under the
project dispatch root. That is defence in depth the brief did not ask for and is
right to have.

=== The strongest line in the diff

One test asserts, in a single pair, that a sibling project dispatch stem is
*refused by finalize* AND *allowed by read*. That pins the DISTINCTION between
the two authorities rather than either grant separately — so a future collapse of
the predicates fails loudly, instead of passing the way the old matrix did.

The old matrix is precisely what let the widening through: it refused a sibling
managed WORKTREE, the sessions dir and an unrelated =/tmp= path, and never a
sibling project dispatch STEM. Every assertion passed while the one
newly-permitted pair went unexercised.

=== The proof, and why it is tighter than its predecessor

=injection.patch= is a ONE-LINE swap: =path_under_own_dispatch_artifacts= ->
=path_under_dispatch_artifacts=. It restores exactly the merged-but-wrong
predicate, so the red cannot arise for an incidental reason.

=a summary file in a sibling project dispatch stem must be refused= FIRST, then
=a finalize artifact grant with no configured artifact dir must fail closed=. The
test names are =a_=/=b_= prefixed so alphabetical ordering puts the no-widening
assertion first deliberately.

That is the criterion the PREVIOUS proof never covered at all, which is how a
wrong decision survived to merge.

Reviewer =reviewer-codex-tmux= (tmux/codex/gpt-5.6-sol/high) on merge =3a825cb=
vs base =b4ca343=. Verdict REJECT, one BLOCK SHIP plus one non-blocking. Manager

=== The BLOCK SHIP: the predicate is right, its INPUT is widenable

=path_is_under= accepts EQUALITY — =path == root || path.starts_with(root)=
(=cursor_acp.rs:1530=). So if =dispatch_artifact_dir= is the dispatch ROOT
itself, both halves of =path_under_own_dispatch_artifacts= pass and every sibling
stem is reachable again.

That value is production-reachable, not a forged test config. Manager traced and
confirmed the full chain:

1. =dispatch_artifact_stem= (=manager.rs:6442=) does
   =file_name.strip_suffix("-brief.md")= with no emptiness check. A brief named
   =-brief.md= yields =stem == ""=; =.-brief.md= yields =".".
2. =dispatch_artifact_paths_for_attempt= (=:6631=) does
   =project_dispatch_dir(project_root).join(&stem)=, so =dir= IS the dispatch
   root.
3. =last_path.parent()= is therefore the dispatch root, and =api.rs:4764=
   persists exactly that as =dispatch_artifact_dir=.
4. Equality passes, and the widened grant is back.

*So round 3 fixed the predicate and left its input unvalidated.* The new paired
test hard-codes a well-formed child directory and the daemon test only proves an
already-supplied value is serialized — neither exercises production derivation.

Worth naming: this is the reviewer answering the exact judgement question the
brief asked ("is there a cheaper way to re-widen this without the test
noticing?"). The answer is yes, and it is not by collapsing the predicates —
which is what the test guards — but by feeding the surviving predicate a broader
input.

=== TWO OF THE CORRECTIONS ARE ON THE MANAGER'S BRIEF

*1. The brief was wrong about canonicalization.* It told the reviewer to check
whether =path_is_under= could be fooled by traversal or symlinks, "note this code
does not canonicalize". It DOES: =resolve_policy_path= (=:1513=) canonicalizes,
and recursively canonicalizes the nearest existing parent before normalizing
=.=/=..=. Traversal and symlink escape are genuinely rejected. The real gap was
the one the brief did not think of.

*2. The brief named the wrong baseline.* It asked for a comparison against
=d4922f7= as "pre-M47E5". =d4922f7= is IN the M47E5.2 lineage and already
contains the managed-worktree move, at which point the old own-artifact predicate
was already dead and the normal allowset was worktree-only. The true pre-move
point is =103ed7e=, where the intended shape was worktree plus =worktree.parent()=
when that parent sits under the dispatch root.

The implementer's report claimed "compared with pre-M47E5 commit =d4922f7=, the
grant allows the same path set". That claim was made in good faith against the
baseline the brief supplied, and the baseline was wrong.

=== The pattern, and what changes

Three rounds on this sub-chain, and a manager brief has contributed an error to
each: M47E5.1 declared a write scope excluding the =verify/= dir it demanded;
M47E5.1.1's brief asserted two facts about code the manager had not read closely.

The common cause is stating unverified specifics with the authority of verified
ones. Adopted going forward: *a brief either verifies a specific claim about code
before asserting it, or marks it explicitly as a claim to check.* Both errors here
would have been harmless if labelled.

** Description
Declared by the TASK-M47E5 implementer rather than buried, and confirmed by the
manager against the code before filing.

=path_under_own_dispatch_artifacts= (=crates/orgasmic-drivers/.../cursor_acp.rs=,
~:1038) derives the dispatch attempt directory as =worktree.parent()= and then
requires THAT to sit under =<project>/.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch=. After TASK-M47E5
the managed worktree lives at =~/.orgasmic/worktrees/<project-id>/<task>/=, so
=worktree.parent()= is =~/.orgasmic/worktrees/<project-id>= — never under the
project. The condition is now ALWAYS FALSE.

** Severity: fails closed, so this is correctness-of-intent, not a hole
The grant only ever ADDED permission. Losing it denies more, never allows more.
The common case still works: a summary file inside the worktree is allowed by
=path_under_worktree=, and the brief-read grant is unaffected because
=path_under_dispatch_artifacts= keys on the PROJECT ROOT rather than on
=worktree.parent()=.

What is actually wrong is that a cursor-acp worker passing =dispatch finalize
--summary-file= a path inside the project dispatch stem directory is now refused,
and that the function is dead logic asserting a state that can no longer occur.
Dead code that describes an impossible world is how the next reader learns
something false.

** Fix
Derive the dispatch artifact directory from the PROJECT ROOT, the way the sibling
=path_under_dispatch_artifacts= already does, instead of from =worktree.parent()=.
The worktree path stopped being a reliable route to the project the moment
worktrees left the project — so any other place in the drivers crate that infers
project location from the worktree needs the same read. Grep for it rather than
fixing only this one call site.

** Acceptance
- A cursor-acp worker can pass a summary-file path under the project dispatch
  stem directory again.
- No grant widens beyond what it allowed before TASK-M47E5.
- Any other worktree-to-project inference in =crates/orgasmic-drivers/**= is
  either corrected or shown not to exist.

DESIGN CHOICE: the "own" variant is GONE, not narrowed. The attempt stem is not identifiable from anything the driver holds — it comes from the operator-chosen brief FILENAME (=dispatch_artifact_stem=), while =DriverContext= carries run id, task id, worker id, project id and worktree but never the stem or attempt token. Nothing could narrow the predicate honestly, and a distinctly-named function with a body identical to its sibling was ruled out, so the one caller routes to =path_under_dispatch_artifacts=.

A GRANT WIDENING WAS DECLARED AGAINST AN EXPLICIT "never widen a grant" INSTRUCTION, AND THE MANAGER ACCEPTED IT after checking the argument in code rather than the summary. The grant went from "under this attempt own stem dir" to "under the project dispatch dir", so a sibling task stem dir is newly accepted for =--summary-file=. Verified: =read_args_allowed= (=cursor_acp.rs:827=) has ALWAYS allowed reading anything under =path_under_dispatch_artifacts=, so no file becomes reachable that was not already readable, and =dispatch_finalize_command_allowed= still pins =--task= and =--run-id= to this run own ctx. Bounded, and it adds no reachability. The alternative — drop the grant and require summary files inside the worktree — fails acceptance criterion 1 as written.

=== The BLOCK SHIP overturns the MANAGER's decision, not the implementer's

At close time the manager wrote on the tx: "declared grant widening verified
bounded against =read_args_allowed= before acceptance". *That reasoning was
wrong, and the error was mine rather than the worker's* — the implementer
DECLARED the widening plainly and the manager waved it through.

The argument was: =read_args_allowed= (=cursor_acp.rs:829=) already allows the
whole project dispatch dir, so keying finalize on the same predicate exposes no
NEW surface. The reviewer's counter is correct and is the more careful principle:
*the acceptance criterion governs the command/path grant itself, not the
transitive closure of separately granted actions.*

Confirmed by reading what =dispatch finalize --summary-file X= actually does:
reads X (=manager.rs:1804=), may COMMIT the worktree (=:1874=), writes X's bytes
VERBATIM as this run's =last.txt= (=:1943=), and releases the lease carrying the
terminal =*.done= tx (=:1985=). That is not a read. A worker on TASK-A can now
name =<project>/.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/task-b/report.md= and have another
dispatch's report become its own terminal record. The pre-move predicate refused
exactly that: it required the path to be under =worktree.parent()= AND that

* DONE TASK-M47E5 Move dispatch worktrees out of TCC-guarded directories, and give them a prune :daemon:cli:macos:dispatch:
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: TASK-M47E5
:MOTIVATED_BY: TASK-3X5AQ
:PRIORITY: P1
:WRITE_SCOPE: crates/orgasmic-daemon/**,crates/orgasmic-cli/**,shipped/**
:END:

** Description
Implements the fix decided on TASK-3X5AQ. Read that task's two measurement
sections first — "The cdhash measurement" and "Verification and recommended
placement (2026-08-05)". Everything below is already measured; do not re-derive
it, and in particular do NOT revive the shared =CARGO_TARGET_DIR= or the
stable-slot idea. Both are disproved there, with reproductions.

*Why the move works, in one line:* a TCC grant for a linker/ad-hoc-signed binary
is pinned to its CDHASH, so no path scheme can make a grant survive a rebuild.
The only durable answer is to stop needing a grant — put the worktree where
macOS does not guard.

=== Part 1 — move the managed worktree root
Change the DEFAULT managed worktree path from
=<project>/.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/<task>/worktree= to:

: ~/.orgasmic/worktrees/<project-id>/<task-id>/

- Key on PROJECT ID, not display name — the id is what the CLI and daemon
  already use (=--project <id>=) and names can collide or change.
- MOVE ONLY THE SCRATCH. The dispatch RECORD — brief, =last.txt=, stdout log
  under =.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/<task>/= — STAYS in the project. It is small,
  durable, written by the already-granted daemon, and leaving it keeps every
  existing brief-path reference in gotchas, briefs and memories valid.
- =orgasmic manager dispatch --worktree <PATH>= already exists as the override,
  so this changes the managed default only and adds no new surface.
- UNIVERSAL, not macOS-gated. Linux has no TCC, but the repo still stops
  accumulating multi-GB build trees and =git status= stays clean. One code path
  beats a platform branch.

Verified already (TASK-3X5AQ): a worktree there resolves its =.git= back into
the Documents-hosted repo, =status=/=log=/=remove= all work, the worktree's own
=.orgasmic/project.org= keeps project resolution working, it is on the same
filesystem, and the toolchain builds and runs from it.

Rejected alternative, for the record: =~/Library/Caches/orgasmic/...= is the
idiomatic macOS location and IS unguarded (zero TCC rows for Cache services) —
but macOS may PURGE it under disk pressure and destroy a worktree mid-dispatch.

=== Part 2 — pruning, which is NOT optional here
This is a REQUIREMENT OF THE MOVE, not a follow-up. Today a stray worktree sits
inside the repo where =git status=, =git worktree list= and the operator's own
eyes find it. After the move it is invisible, so the same leak becomes silent
multi-GB accumulation in =~/.orgasmic=. Shipping Part 1 alone trades visible
garbage for invisible garbage.

What exists today, measured 2026-08-05:
- =dispatch-close --worktree-remove= (DEFAULT TRUE) salvages uncommitted work to
  =refs/orgasmic/salvage/<sha>= and then removes WITHOUT =--force=, so git's
  clean check gates it.
- =dispatch-status --orphans-only= REPORTS dispatches whose run is gone.
- =dispatch-status --cleanup-failed= writes the orphan close tx and clears
  LEASES — not worktrees.

What does NOT exist: any call to =git worktree prune=, any age-based GC, any
boot-time or periodic sweep, any disk budget.

So three leaks survive close today, and all three become invisible after Part 1:
1. *A DIRTY worktree is never removed* — removal is deliberately non-forced.
2. *An ABANDONED dispatch* (worker died, manager never closed) keeps its
   worktree forever.
3. *Stale =.git/worktrees/<name>= metadata* accrues if a directory is removed
   out of band, which the move makes MORE likely because the new root is a
   plausible thing for an operator to =rm -rf=.

And Part 1 introduces a genuinely NEW failure mode to handle: a worktree whose
REPO no longer exists. Today worktrees die with the repo; afterwards they are
orphans pointing at a missing gitdir, and =git worktree remove= cannot help
because there is no git to run it from. Detect and handle this explicitly.

*Design constraints for the prune:*
- NEVER remove a worktree with an open dispatch or a live run. Reuse the
  existing health signals rather than inventing new ones.
- Salvage before removing, reusing the existing =refs/orgasmic/salvage/<sha>=
  path — do not add a second salvage mechanism.
- REPORT WHAT IT SKIPPED AND WHY, and how many bytes it reclaimed. Silent
  truncation reads as "cleaned everything" when it did not; this project has
  been bitten by that shape repeatedly.
- Prefer extending the existing orphan surface (=dispatch-status
  --cleanup-failed= and its health checks) over building a parallel reaper.
  Adding machinery where existing machinery can be made consistent is what took
  a sibling chain five fix rounds.
- Decide deliberately whether prune runs automatically (daemon boot and/or at
  close) or only as an explicit verb, and SAY WHY. An automatic reaper that
  deletes a worker's tree is a much sharper tool than a verb.

=== Acceptance
- A dispatch's managed worktree is created under
  =~/.orgasmic/worktrees/<project-id>/<task-id>/= and nothing under
  =~/Documents= is written by the worker's build.
- The dispatch record (brief, report, logs) still lands in the project.
- =--worktree <PATH>= still overrides.
- Closing a dispatch still removes the worktree, still salvages first, and still
  refuses to force-remove a dirty tree.
- A prune surface reclaims worktrees for closed or absent dispatches, refuses to
  touch live ones, names what it skipped and why, and reports bytes reclaimed.
- A worktree whose repo is gone is detected and removable.
- =git worktree prune= is run so stale =.git/worktrees= metadata does not
  accumulate.
- Gotchas, briefs and any shipped text naming
  =.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/<task>/worktree= are updated in the same change —
  =cli_parity= resolves shipped invocations against the real binary and is the
  gate that catches a doctrine edit that lags the code.
** Evidence
Landed =ffead86= (merge) / =e5ed186= (worker HEAD, 6 commits) on main, base =103ed7e=.

Implementer: =implementer-claude-tmux= — driver tmux, harness claude, model claude-opus-5, effort high. Run =run-20260805T140235-4e4f74ec8c154ad48115bf43d5bbc97a=, started_tx =tx-20260805-orgasmic-4458=.

NO DAEMON CODE CHANGED. The daemon worktree handling was already location-agnostic (=validate_dispatch_path= / =validate_dispatch_worktree_dir= check absolute + non-symlink + directory and nothing about the project), so the whole change is =orgasmic-cli= + =shipped/=.

MANAGER PRODUCTION PROBE on the merged tree, with the freshly built binary (the installed =orgasmic= on PATH is older and cannot answer this):
- default: =worktree: /Users/aspirational/.orgasmic/worktrees/orgasmic/task-stwvb= — outside Documents, keyed on project id.
- the dispatch RECORD still resolves under the project =.orgasmic/tmp/dispatch/=.
- =--worktree /tmp/override-probe= still wins.
- dry-run created nothing: neither =~/.orgasmic/worktrees= nor the override path existed afterwards.

Integration gates, re-run by the manager on the MERGED tree:
- =scripts/run-tests.sh -p orgasmic-cli= — GREEN, 0 failures, "environ: complete — no tool requirement was waived".
- =cargo test -p orgasmic-cli --test cli_parity= — 3 passed. This is the gate the task named, and it is what proves the shipped doctrine edit did not lag the code.
- =cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings= — exit 0.
- =cargo fmt --all --check= — exit 0.
- The DAEMON suite was NOT re-run by the manager, deliberately and stated rather than implied: no daemon code changed (=git diff --stat= is cli + shipped only), and this host has no trustworthy full-run signal for that suite. The implementer ran it, saw 2 =supervisor::tests::a_probe_child_*= failures, and took the second measurement the brief demanded — both passed alone against the already-built binary in <0.6s.

THE MANAGER RULING WAS IMPLEMENTED AND THEN SHARPENED BY THE IMPLEMENTER, correctly: prune refuses an open dispatch WHATEVER its run health, orphaned included, because reclaiming an abandoned dispatch tree would be a second way to end a dispatch. The skip line names the verb that actually releases it. That is a better reading of the ruling than the ruling itself had.

SAFETY OF THE DELETE PATH, reviewed by the manager line by line rather than taken on report: =remove_orphaned_worktree_dir= is the only =remove_dir_all=; it refuses any path containing =..=, refuses anything that is not a DIRECT CHILD of this project managed root, and re-stats immediately before removing to refuse a symlink or a non-directory. Removal of a live repo worktree still goes through =git worktree remove= WITHOUT =--force=, so git own clean check gates it, same as =dispatch-close=. =managed_worktree_root= refuses a project id that could escape the root.

NO INJECTION PROOF, and the reasoning is accepted. The defect needs live macOS TCC state, an operator prompt and a fresh cdhash per build — there is no assertion a test in this repo can make about it, which is exactly why TASK-3X5AQ measured it against the system TCC database instead. The remainder is relocation and new capability, not a bug with a red. Authoring a probe against the fixed tree would be a passing broken probe.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, by the implementer: =git worktree prune -v= writes its report to STDERR with stdout empty on git 2.52.0, so reading stdout would have silently reported "pruned nothing" every time; and =du= on this worktree real 7.6 GB target/ costs 0.084s warm, which is what justifies sizing reclaimable trees on the status path while deliberately NOT sizing held ones.

and *=# @arch=*. The manager's inventory grepped only =arch:= and reported it as

** Description

** The mechanism, confirmed by the manager

Stage C part 2 carved =arch_= out of =lint_dangling_graph_edges=. A SECOND,
independent path survives:

1. =index.rs:685= scans source markers and runs =lint_project_identity_state=;
   =index.rs:1172= pushes every finding into =parse_errors=.
2. =identity_lint.rs:253= collects architecture identities into the known-id
   universe *only while =.orgasmic/architecture.org= exists* — gated on
   =path.exists()=.
3. =identity_lint.rs:358= (=lint_dangling_references=) emits
   =dangling advisory marker `{id}` in {file}= for every scanned marker id not in
   that universe. There is no retired-=arch_= carve-out.

*Measured blast radius*: *59 scanned =orgasmic:arch_= marker lines naming 36
distinct ids* across =crates/=, =ui/= and =scripts/=.

The vivid case: =crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/index.rs:1= carries
=// orgasmic:arch_C87Z9=, which resolves today only because
=.orgasmic/architecture.org:572= defines it. After stage D, *the file that runs
the lint flags itself*.

** The ruling

Exclude retired =arch_= ids from *index-time* identity-lint dangling enforcement,
in BOTH branches of =lint_dangling_references= — the advisory-marker branch,
which is the measured blocker, and the reference-token branch.

The reviewer recommended both and the manager agrees: one canonical rule beats
two, and the second branch is a latent repeat in any project that does have
=arch_= values under a reference property. This repository currently has zero
such values under =RELATES_TO=, =GLOSSARY_REFS= or =PARENT= — so the second
branch is prevention, not repair, and should be stated as such.

*Keep the generic marker scanner and =/graph/markers= behaviour unchanged.* The
markers stay indexed and queryable; only their dangling ENFORCEMENT changes.

*Do not weaken write-time rejection of new unresolved references.* A retired id
should stop being an error to HAVE; it should not become a legal thing to ADD.
If that distinction is not expressible where the lint sits, say so rather than
guessing.

- *Task lifecycle*: =in_review=, not superseded by a newer dispatch.
- *Native transcript*: nothing produced.
- *Worktree*: clean — and it was a REVIEWER, whose contract is read-only, so there was never work to salvage.
- *Runtime liveness*: dead and not reattachable; the server is gone, not idle.

Judgment from the policy's menu: *abandon and re-dispatch under a fresh lease.* Reattach is impossible, resume/fork needs a trustworthy native session identity that does not exist here, and fresh recovery is pointless when the attempt produced nothing.

Closed =--status aborted= so the ledger records an orphan rather than a completion. The hard rule the policy states — never treat a failed release as silent success — is the reason this got a tx entry of its own instead of a quiet re-dispatch.
** Root cause of three orphans — codex workspace out of credits
Three consecutive reviewer dispatches orphaned. *Root cause is quota exhaustion, not transport.*

*The diagnostic*: dispatch, then =tmux capture-pane= within 30 seconds instead of waiting for the stall detector. The pane showed:

: ■ Your workspace is out of credits. Ask your workspace owner to refill in order to continue.
:   Usage limit reached
:   Request a limit increase from your owner to continue using codex. Request increase?
:   1. Yes (y)
: › 2. No (default) (n)

*The full chain, which is worth recording because every link looked like something else:*

1. Codex launches, hits the workspace quota, and blocks on an INTERACTIVE prompt.
2. It consumes no CPU and writes nothing — =last.txt= and the stdout log stay 0 bytes.
3. After 600s the stall detector releases: =stall_timeout_exceeded: no work
   evidence for 600s; 6 process(es) under pid 60457 at 0.0% cpu=.
4. The release kills the pane. That was the tmux server's only session, so *the
   server exits*.
5. =tmux ls= then reports =no server running=, which reads exactly like a
   transport failure — and that is what the first two orphans were misdiagnosed
   as.

*Two hypotheses were tested and killed before the right one*, both worth naming
so they are not re-tested: the manager's earlier =daemon restart= did NOT break
the environment (the running daemon has the correct =PATH=, =ORGASMIC_HOME=,
=USER=, =HOME=, =LOGNAME=), and tmux itself is healthy (a plain detached session
created from a shell survived 45s while orgasmic's died).

*The instrument that mattered*: capture the pane EARLY. The release tombstone
says "0.0% cpu, no work evidence", which is true and tells you nothing about
why. The pane says exactly why. For any future silent-hang orphan, capture before
the stall clock expires.

*Consequence*: every codex dispatch will orphan identically until the workspace
is refilled. The board's reviewers and implementers have both been codex today.
Claude remains available as a harness. Refilling is an operator action; the
manager cannot resolve it.
** Review round 2 — APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS; stage D cleared
Reviewer =reviewer-claude-tmux= (tmux / claude / claude-opus-5 / high — the first
dispatch after the harness switch). *APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS. Stage D: YES.*
Three NON-BLOCKING findings, no BLOCK SHIP.

=== It ran the experiment the manager botched, correctly

The manager tried to validate stage D by deleting =architecture.org= on the LIVE
repository against a daemon that predates the carve-outs — invalid, and it
perturbed operator state. The reviewer did it properly and *explicitly declined
to repeat the live version*:

a read-only probe running the *MERGED* lint against a *COPY* of this repository's
real state with =architecture.org= deleted, reproducing the daemon's own scanner
(=should_scan_marker_file=, =should_skip_marker_dir=, =should_skip_marker_path=,
=marker_node_ids_in_line=) line by line — *and with a pre-fix CONTROL*:

| repo copy | rule | findings |
|---|---|---|
| =architecture.org= absent (stage D) | merged | *0* |
| absent | pre-fix control | *78* |
| present (today) | merged | 0 |
| present | pre-fix control | 0 |

The control is what makes the 0 a real negative rather than a vacuous one. The
live repo was never touched: =git status --porcelain= empty throughout,
=architecture.org= still 119773 bytes.

*The 78 corroborates the mechanism from a second direction* — it is exactly the
residual count the manager measured after restoring the file.

=== It corrected the count WITH the mechanism

The brief said 59 marker lines naming 36 distinct ids. Measured against the
scanner's own normalisation: *57 lines, 14 distinct INDEXED ids*. The 36 counted
=.N= subtask suffixes separately; =normalize_marker_node_id= (=marker.rs:96=)
collapses =arch_X.1= -> =arch_X=. Nothing to fix — but *stage D's real surface is
14 ids, not 36*, and the manager's number was raw grep output rather than what
the indexer sees.

=== The producer enumeration went finer than the implementer's

*14 call sites* through the =push_parse_error= funnel plus 7 direct pushes,
versus the implementer's "seven semantic producers" — same conclusion, more
granular evidence, and it checked =api.rs= only READS =parse_errors=. *No eighth
producer.* It also established that =lint_dangling_references= has exactly one
production caller, which itself has exactly one, so the comment's "index-time
only" claim is literally true.

=== FINDING 1 is the one worth carrying into stage D

The comment credits the write-time boundary to =unresolved_reference_tokens=
staying prefix-agnostic. *That is accurate but not what actually holds the line.*
The guard resolves against =graph.nodes=, and =arch_= ids never enter it — which
is true only because =looks_like_structured_node_id= KEEPS =arch_=, so
=:PRODUCES: arch_X= is not materialised as an artifact node.

So the real invariant is "=arch_= is never materialised into =graph.nodes=", and
after stage D that one list entry becomes the SOLE thing preventing a retired id
from becoming addable again. Someone "cleaning up" that entry post-excision —
which reads like cosmetic tidying — would silently stop
=reject_unresolved_reference_token= firing on all four write handlers. *Nothing
fails; the guard just goes quiet.*

It verified the boundary holds today by code path (all four handlers call the
guard under =if !req.force=), and that existing values are not re-validated
unless re-set — so stage D creates no trap for the two live backlog tasks
carrying =:IMPLEMENTS: arch_RN73Z=.

=== The anti-vacuity check that could have cost the repo

It confirmed the marker-shaped STRING LITERALS the new tests embed
(=\"// orgasmic:arch_GONE99\\n\"=) are NOT picked up by the real scanner, because
=comment_region_from_slash_slash= (=marker.rs:120=) is quote-aware. It checked
this specifically because a false =dec_GONE99= marker would have injected three
parse errors into this repository's own index and broken the =parse_errors = 0=
criterion. That is checking whether the test can poison the thing it measures.

- *Findings 1 and 3 (test gaps)*: filed rather than fixed here; finding 1's
